zh.title: 面向智能体信息搜寻的嵌套式浏览器操作学习
zh.abstract: 信息寻觅（IS）智能体在各种广泛而深入的搜索任务中取得了显著性能，然而，它们的工具使用在很大程度上仍局限于 API 级别的片段检索和基于 URL 的页面获取，这限制了它们获取通过真实浏览可获得的更丰富信息。尽管完整的浏览器交互可以解锁更深层次的能力，但其细粒度的控制和冗余的页面内容返回给 ReAct 风格的函数调用智能体带来了巨大的复杂性。为了弥合这一差距，我们提出了嵌套式浏览器使用学习（NestBrowse），它引入了一个最小且完整的浏览器动作框架，该框架通过一种嵌套结构将交互控制与页面探索解耦。这种设计简化了智能体的推理，同时能够有效地获取深网信息。在具有挑战性的深层 IS 基准测试上的实验结果表明，NestBrowse 在实践中提供了明显的优势。进一步的深入分析强调了其效率和灵活性。

summary.summary: 由阿里巴巴集团通义实验室开发的 NestBrowse 引入了一个嵌套的浏览器使用框架，旨在增强信息搜索代理的能力。它通过从动态页面中提炼出与目标相关的内容，从而实现高效的网页交互，在深度信息搜索基准上表现出色，并降低了上下文开销。
originalProblem: 现有的信息搜索 (IS) 代理主要依赖于 API 级别的片段检索或静态 URL 获取，限制了它们对动态网页内容和页面内功能的访问。
将完整的网页内容注入大型语言模型 (LLM) 的上下文通常过于冗长，超出令牌限制，并且由于冗余而损害推理效率。
由于细粒度浏览器控制的复杂性和原始页面数据的庞大性，开发一个标准化且高效的真实浏览器交互模型仍然充满挑战。
solution: 设计了一个最小且完整的浏览器工具包，包含四个核心操作（搜索、访问、点击、填写），以平衡全面的网页访问和降低代理的工具复杂性。
一个嵌套的浏览器使用框架将交互解耦为用于工具集成推理的“外循环”和用于目标驱动页面探索的“内循环”，确保只有相关信息传递给 LLM。
通过利用质量过滤的监督，一个多任务模仿学习公式共同训练代理执行高级推理和从网页中提取与目标相关的低级证据。
keyInsights: 将浏览器操作空间简化为一套最小但功能完整的工具，对于代理在不造成认知负担的情况下有效与复杂网络环境交互至关重要。
将网页交互解耦为嵌套循环可以高效管理冗长的网页内容，通过仅提取和注入与目标相关的信息来防止上下文窗口溢出。
多任务学习方法使单一代理模型能够有效地内化高级战略推理和细粒度信息提取能力，这些能力对于复杂的浏览器使用是必需的。
results: NestBrowse-30B-A3B 在四个具有挑战性的深度 IS 基准（例如，BrowseComp 上 31.6，GAIA 上 75.7）上取得了强大表现，超越了许多开源代理并与专有系统竞争。
嵌套框架显著提高了上下文效率，通过仅将与目标相关的内容注入代理的推理上下文，防止了上下文过载，否则将提前终止 85% 的任务。
消融研究证实，工具包简化和与目标相关的内容提取都独立且累加地有助于性能提升，并且代理通过利用网页中嵌入的功能实用程序展示了“元工具使用”。

zh.overview:
## 理解 NestBrowse：一个用于高级网络AI代理的框架

当前在网络上搜索信息的AI代理在处理动态内容和交互式网络功能时面临显著限制。尽管它们可以通过搜索查询和基本的页面访问检索静态信息，但在需要填写表单、点击按钮或导航复杂多步骤流程的任务上却力不从心。NestBrowse 通过引入一个复杂的框架来解决这些挑战，该框架使AI代理能够像人类用户一样与网络交互，同时保持效率并避免信息过载。

![NestBrowse 与其他信息检索代理在 BrowseComp 基准测试上的性能比较，显示 NestBrowse-30B-A3B 取得了 31.6 的最高分](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-0.jpeg)

## 核心创新：嵌套浏览器交互

NestBrowse 引入了一种“嵌套”方法，将浏览器交互分为两个不同但相互关联的循环。**外层循环**处理高层推理和工具选择，遵循标准的 ReAct 风格函数调用范式，即代理进行思考、选择工具并处理响应。**内层循环**管理详细的页面探索和信息提取，确保只有相关内容到达代理的推理上下文。

这种分离解决了一个关键问题：网页包含大量文本，这些文本会迅速淹没AI代理的上下文窗口。传统方法要么截断内容（冒着丢失重要信息的风险），要么注入整个页面（导致效率低下并超出 token 限制）。NestBrowse 的内层循环充当智能过滤器，仅从每个页面片段中提取与目标相关的信息。

![NestBrowse 框架的详细插图，展示了用于代理推理的外层循环和用于页面探索的内层循环](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-1.jpeg)

该框架通过一个精心设计的浏览器工具包运行，该工具包仅包含四个操作：
- **search**：执行 Google 查询并返回前 10 个结果
- **visit**：从 URL 获取并提取相关内容
- **click**：与可点击元素交互并提取结果内容
- **fill**：在表单字段或可编辑元素中键入文本

这个最小而完整的工具包在功能覆盖性和简洁性之间取得了平衡，避免了更大动作空间带来的复杂性，同时仍然能够访问静态和动态网页内容。

## 通过多任务模仿学习进行训练

为了开发能够进行这种复杂浏览器交互的代理，NestBrowse 采用了多任务模仿学习方法。训练过程共同优化两个目标：

$$
L_{MT} = \lambda_{out} L_{out} + \lambda_{in} L_{in}
$$

其中 $L_{out}$ 训练外层循环的推理能力，而 $L_{in}$ 训练内层循环的信息提取技能。这种联合训练使单个模型能够执行高层战略推理和低层内容过滤。

训练数据通过拒绝采样进行质量过滤，如果轨迹表现出格式违规、工具调用幻觉或不正确的最终答案，则会被丢弃。这确保了在训练过程中只强化高质量的行为模式。

## 效率和上下文管理

NestBrowse 最显著的优势之一是它能够有效地管理上下文长度。分析表明，如果没有嵌套框架，在约 20 轮交互后，处理的总信息量将迅速超过典型的上下文限制（128K token），导致大约 85% 的复杂任务执行失败。

![上下文长度分析显示 NestBrowse 在处理大量信息的同时如何保持可管理的上下文大小](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-2.jpeg)

通过在将内容注入外循环之前，通过内循环对其进行过滤，NestBrowse 在整个执行过程中将推理上下文保持在可行的范围内。这使得其能够长时间持续运行，这对于传统方法来说是不可能实现的。

## 经验验证和性能

NestBrowse 在多个具有挑战性的基准测试中表现出强大的性能。该框架的有效性通过对 BrowseComp、GAIA、BrowseComp-zh 和 XBench-DeepSearch 等数据集的全面评估得到验证。值得注意的是，即使是较小的 NestBrowse-4B 模型也取得了具有竞争力的性能，这表明有效的工具设计和交互策略可能比原始模型规模更重要。

![内循环页面探索能力分析显示在原始快照保留和目标相关提取方面均有改进](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-3.jpeg)

消融研究表明，工具包简化和目标相关内容提取都独立地促进了性能提升，它们的结合提供了附加的益处。内循环的有效性通过在原始快照保留和目标相关提取任务上改进的性能得到证明。

## 超越信息检索：元工具使用

NestBrowse 实现了作者所称的“元工具使用”——即利用网络嵌入工具和功能进行计算任务的能力。这种能力超越了简单的信息检索，扩展到主动利用在线计算器、数据可视化工具和其他基于网络的实用程序。

![案例研究演示 NestBrowse 使用在线牛顿法计算器解决数学问题](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-4.jpeg)

一个引人注目的例子是代理通过导航到在线牛顿法计算器、填写所需函数和参数、点击计算按钮并使用结果进行后续推理来解决复杂的数学问题。这表明浏览器使用能力可以减轻代理自身的计算负担，同时扩展其解决问题的能力。

## 影响和未来方向

NestBrowse 代表了使 AI 代理成为更强大的网络用户方面的一项重大进步。通过提供一种平衡功能与效率的浏览器交互原则性方法，它为代理与现代网络的动态和交互式方面进行交互开辟了新的可能性。

该框架的设计原则——最小化而完整的工具包、嵌套交互范式和目标驱动的内容过滤——为开发未来的代理系统提供了宝贵的见解。多任务学习方法展示了如何将复杂的行为能力有效地内化到单个模型中。

当前的局限性包括只专注于文本内容，作者承认现实世界的浏览通常依赖于视觉线索和布局。将 NestBrowse 扩展到包含多模态信息代表了未来发展的一个有希望的方向，尽管这将在建模和系统设计中引入显著的额外复杂性。

NestBrowse-4B 等小型模型的成功表明，对代理能力的深思熟虑的设计可能比简单地扩展模型参数更具影响力，为实现更易访问和资源高效的、能够进行复杂真实世界交互的代理 AI 系统提供了途径。

en.title: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
en.abstract: Information-seeking (IS) agents have achieved strong performance across a range of wide and deep search tasks, yet their tool use remains largely restricted to API-level snippet retrieval and URL-based page fetching, limiting access to the richer information available through real browsing. While full browser interaction could unlock deeper capabilities, its fine-grained control and verbose page content returns introduce substantial complexity for ReAct-style function-calling agents. To bridge this gap, we propose Nested Browser-Use Learning (NestBrowse), which introduces a minimal and complete browser-action framework that decouples interaction control from page exploration through a nested structure. This design simplifies agentic reasoning while enabling effective deep-web information acquisition. Empirical results on challenging deep IS benchmarks demonstrate that NestBrowse offers clear benefits in practice. Further in-depth analyses underscore its efficiency and flexibility.

summary.summary: NestBrowse, developed by Tongyi Lab at Alibaba Group, introduces a nested browser-use framework to enhance information-seeking agents. It enables efficient web interaction by distilling goal-relevant content from dynamic pages, achieving strong performance on deep information-seeking benchmarks with reduced context overhead.
originalProblem: Existing information-seeking (IS) agents primarily rely on API-level snippet retrieval or static URL fetching, limiting their access to dynamic web content and in-page functionalities.
Injecting full web page content into a Large Language Model's (LLM) context is often verbose, exceeds token limits, and impairs reasoning efficiency due to redundancy.
Developing a standardized and efficient model for real browser interaction remains challenging due to the complexity of fine-grained browser control and the volume of raw page data.
solution: A minimally complete browser toolkit is designed with four core actions (search, visit, click, fill) to balance comprehensive web access with reduced tool complexity for the agent.

A nested browser-use framework decouples interaction into an 'outer loop' for tool-integrated reasoning and an 'inner loop' for goal-driven page exploration, ensuring only relevant information is passed to the LLM.

A multi-task imitation learning formulation, utilizing quality-filtered supervision, jointly trains the agent to perform both high-level reasoning and low-level goal-relevant evidence extraction from web pages.
keyInsights: Simplifying the browser action space to a minimal, yet functionally complete, set of tools is crucial for agents to effectively interact with complex web environments without cognitive overload.
Decoupling web interaction into nested loops allows for efficient management of verbose web content, preventing context window overflow by only extracting and injecting goal-relevant information.

A multi-task learning approach enables a single agent model to effectively internalize both high-level strategic reasoning and fine-grained information extraction capabilities necessary for sophisticated browser use.
results: NestBrowse-30B-A3B achieved strong performance on four challenging deep IS benchmarks (e.g., 31.6 on BrowseComp, 75.7 on GAIA), outperforming many open-source agents and competing with proprietary systems.

The nested framework significantly improves context efficiency, preventing context overload that would prematurely terminate 85% of tasks by injecting only goal-relevant content into the agent's reasoning context.

Ablation studies confirmed that both toolkit simplification and goal-relevant content extraction independently and additively contribute to performance gains, and the agent demonstrates 'meta tool-use' by leveraging web-embedded functional utilities.

en.overview:
## Understanding NestBrowse: A Framework for Advanced Web-Based AI Agents

Current AI agents that search for information on the web face significant limitations when dealing with dynamic content and interactive web features. While they can retrieve static information through search queries and basic page visits, they struggle with tasks requiring form filling, button clicking, or navigating complex multi-step processes. NestBrowse addresses these challenges by introducing a sophisticated framework that enables AI agents to interact with the web like human users while maintaining efficiency and avoiding information overload.

![Performance comparison of NestBrowse against other information-seeking agents on the BrowseComp benchmark, showing NestBrowse-30B-A3B achieving the highest score of 31.6](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-0.jpeg)

## The Core Innovation: Nested Browser Interaction

NestBrowse introduces a "nested" approach that separates browser interaction into two distinct but interconnected loops. The **outer loop** handles high-level reasoning and tool selection, following a standard ReAct-style function-calling paradigm where the agent thinks, selects tools, and processes responses. The **inner loop** manages detailed page exploration and information extraction, ensuring that only relevant content reaches the agent's reasoning context.

This separation addresses a critical problem: web pages contain enormous amounts of text that can quickly overwhelm an AI agent's context window. Traditional approaches either truncate content (risking loss of important information) or inject entire pages (causing inefficiency and exceeding token limits). NestBrowse's inner loop acts as an intelligent filter, extracting only goal-relevant information from each page segment.

![Detailed illustration of the NestBrowse framework showing the outer loop for agentic reasoning and inner loop for page exploration](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-1.jpeg)

The framework operates through a carefully designed browser toolkit consisting of just four actions:
- **search**: Performs Google queries returning top-10 results
- **visit**: Fetches and extracts relevant content from URLs  
- **click**: Interacts with clickable elements and extracts resulting content
- **fill**: Types text into form fields or editable elements

This minimal yet complete toolkit balances functional coverage with simplicity, avoiding the complexity that would come with a larger action space while still enabling access to both static and dynamic web content.

## Training Through Multi-Task Imitation Learning

To develop agents capable of this sophisticated browser interaction, NestBrowse employs a multi-task imitation learning approach. The training process jointly optimizes two objectives:

$$
L_{MT} = \lambda_{out} L_{out} + \lambda_{in} L_{in}
$$

where $L_{out}$ trains the outer-loop reasoning capabilities and $L_{in}$ trains the inner-loop information extraction skills. This joint training enables a single model to perform both high-level strategic reasoning and low-level content filtering.

The training data undergoes quality filtering through rejection sampling, where trajectories are discarded if they exhibit format violations, tool-call hallucinations, or incorrect final answers. This ensures that only high-quality behavioral patterns are reinforced during training.

## Efficiency and Context Management

One of NestBrowse's most significant advantages is its ability to manage context length effectively. Analysis shows that without the nested framework, the total information processed would quickly exceed typical context limits (128K tokens) after approximately 20 turns, causing execution failure for about 85% of complex tasks.

![Context length analysis showing how NestBrowse maintains manageable context sizes while processing substantially more total information](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-2.jpeg)

By filtering content through the inner loop before injecting it into the outer loop, NestBrowse keeps the reasoning context within feasible limits throughout execution. This enables sustained operation over long task horizons that would be impossible with traditional approaches.

## Empirical Validation and Performance

NestBrowse demonstrates strong performance across multiple challenging benchmarks. The framework's effectiveness is validated through comprehensive evaluation on datasets including BrowseComp, GAIA, BrowseComp-zh, and XBench-DeepSearch. Notably, even the smaller NestBrowse-4B model achieves competitive performance, suggesting that effective tool design and interaction strategies can be more important than raw model scale.

![Analysis of inner-loop page exploration capabilities showing improved performance in both raw snapshot retention and goal-relevant extraction](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-3.jpeg)

Ablation studies reveal that both toolkit simplification and goal-relevant content extraction independently contribute to performance improvements, with their combination providing additive benefits. The inner loop's effectiveness is demonstrated through improved performance on both raw snapshot retention and goal-relevant extraction tasks.

## Beyond Information Retrieval: Meta Tool-Use

NestBrowse enables what the authors term "meta tool-use" - the ability to leverage web-embedded tools and functionalities for computational tasks. This capability extends beyond simple information retrieval to active utilization of online calculators, data visualizers, and other web-based utilities.

![Case study demonstrating NestBrowse using an online Newton's method calculator to solve a mathematical problem](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.23647v1/img-4.jpeg)

A compelling example involves the agent solving a complex mathematical problem by navigating to an online Newton's method calculator, filling in the required function and parameters, clicking the calculate button, and using the results for subsequent reasoning. This demonstrates how browser-use capabilities can reduce the computational burden on the agent itself while expanding its problem-solving capabilities.

## Implications and Future Directions

NestBrowse represents a significant advancement in making AI agents more capable web users. By providing a principled approach to browser interaction that balances functionality with efficiency, it opens new possibilities for agents to engage with the dynamic and interactive aspects of the modern web.

The framework's design principles - minimal yet complete toolkits, nested interaction paradigms, and goal-driven content filtering - offer valuable insights for developing future agentic systems. The multi-task learning approach demonstrates how complex behavioral capabilities can be effectively internalized into single models.

Current limitations include the exclusive focus on textual content, with the authors acknowledging that real-world browsing often relies on visual cues and layouts. Extending NestBrowse to incorporate multimodal information represents a promising direction for future development, though it would introduce significant additional complexity in both modeling and system design.

The success of smaller models like NestBrowse-4B suggests that thoughtful design of agent capabilities can be more impactful than simply scaling model parameters, offering a path toward more accessible and resource-efficient agentic AI systems capable of sophisticated real-world interactions.

abstract: Information-seeking (IS) agents have achieved strong performance across a range of wide and deep search tasks, yet their tool use remains largely restricted to API-level snippet retrieval and URL-based page fetching, limiting access to the richer information available through real browsing. While full browser interaction could unlock deeper capabilities, its fine-grained control and verbose page content returns introduce substantial complexity for ReAct-style function-calling agents. To bridge this gap, we propose Nested Browser-Use Learning (NestBrowse), which introduces a minimal and complete browser-action framework that decouples interaction control from page exploration through a nested structure. This design simplifies agentic reasoning while enabling effective deep-web information acquisition. Empirical results on challenging deep IS benchmarks demonstrate that NestBrowse offers clear benefits in practice. Further in-depth analyses underscore its efficiency and flexibility.
title: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking

abstract: The early detection of pancreatic neoplasm is a major clinical dilemma, and it is predominantly so because tumors are likely to occur with minimal contrast margins and a large spread anatomy-wide variation amongst patients on a CT scan. These complexities require to be addressed with an effective and scalable system that can assist in enhancing the salience of the subtle visual cues and provide a high level of the generalization on the multimodal imaging data. A Scalable Residual Feature Aggregation (SRFA) framework is proposed to be used to meet these conditions in this study. The framework integrates a pipeline of preprocessing followed by the segmentation using the MAGRes-UNet that is effective in making the pancreatic structures and isolating regions of interest more visible. DenseNet-121 performed with residual feature storage is used to extract features to allow deep hierarchical features to be aggregated without properties loss. To go further, hybrid HHO-BA metaheuristic feature selection strategy is used, which guarantees the best feature subset refinement. To be classified, the system is trained based on a new hybrid model that integrates the ability to pay attention on the world, which is the Vision Transformer (ViT) with the high representational efficiency of EfficientNet-B3. A dual optimization mechanism incorporating SSA and GWO is used to fine-tune hyperparameters to enhance greater robustness and less overfitting. Experimental results support the significant improvement in performance, with the suggested model reaching 96.23% accuracy, 95.58% F1-score and 94.83% specificity, the model is significantly better than the traditional CNNs and contemporary transformer-based models. Such results highlight the possibility of the SRFA framework as a useful instrument in the early detection of pancreatic tumors.
title: Scalable Residual Feature Aggregation Framework with Hybrid Metaheuristic Optimization for Robust Early Pancreatic Neoplasm Detection in Multimodal CT Imaging

abstract: Large Video Language Models (LVLMs) have rapidly emerged as the focus of multimedia AI research. Nonetheless, when confronted with lengthy videos, these models struggle: their temporal windows are narrow, and they fail to notice fine-grained semantic shifts that unfold over extended durations. Moreover, mainstream text-based retrieval pipelines, which rely chiefly on surface-level lexical overlap, ignore the rich temporal interdependence among visual, audio, and subtitle channels. To mitigate these limitations, we propose TV-RAG, a training-free architecture that couples temporal alignment with entropy-guided semantics to improve long-video reasoning. The framework contributes two main mechanisms: \emph{(i)} a time-decay retrieval module that injects explicit temporal offsets into the similarity computation, thereby ranking text queries according to their true multimedia context; and \emph{(ii)} an entropy-weighted key-frame sampler that selects evenly spaced, information-dense frames, reducing redundancy while preserving representativeness. By weaving these temporal and semantic signals together, TV-RAG realises a dual-level reasoning routine that can be grafted onto any LVLM without re-training or fine-tuning. The resulting system offers a lightweight, budget-friendly upgrade path and consistently surpasses most leading baselines across established long-video benchmarks such as Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench, confirming the effectiveness of our model. The code can be found at https://github.com/AI-Researcher-Team/TV-RAG.
title: TV-RAG: A Temporal-aware and Semantic Entropy-Weighted Framework for Long Video Retrieval and Understanding

abstract: Neural ranking models have achieved remarkable progress and are now widely deployed in real-world applications such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). However, like other neural architectures, they remain vulnerable to adversarial manipulations: subtle character-, word-, or phrase-level perturbations can poison retrieval results and artificially promote targeted candidates, undermining the integrity of search engines and downstream systems. Existing defenses either rely on heuristics with poor generalization or on certified methods that assume overly strong adversarial knowledge, limiting their practical use. To address these challenges, we propose RobustMask, a novel defense that combines the context-prediction capability of pretrained language models with a randomized masking-based smoothing mechanism. Our approach strengthens neural ranking models against adversarial perturbations at the character, word, and phrase levels. Leveraging both the pairwise comparison ability of ranking models and probabilistic statistical analysis, we provide a theoretical proof of RobustMask's certified top-K robustness. Extensive experiments further demonstrate that RobustMask successfully certifies over 20% of candidate documents within the top-10 ranking positions against adversarial perturbations affecting up to 30% of their content. These results highlight the effectiveness of RobustMask in enhancing the adversarial robustness of neural ranking models, marking a significant step toward providing stronger security guarantees for real-world retrieval systems.
title: RobustMask: Certified Robustness against Adversarial Neural Ranking Attack via Randomized Masking

abstract:
Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) at billion scale is fundamentally an out-of-core problem: vectors and indexes live on SSD, so performance is dominated by I/O rather than compute. Under skewed semantic embeddings, existing out-of-core systems break down: a uniform local index mismatches cluster scales, static routing misguides queries and inflates the number of probed partitions, and pruning is incomplete at the cluster level and lossy at the vector level, triggering "fetch-to-discard" reranking on raw vectors.
  We present OrchANN, an out-of-core ANNS engine that uses an I/O orchestration model for unified I/O governance along the route-access-verify pipeline. OrchANN selects a heterogeneous local index per cluster via offline auto-profiling, maintains a query-aware in-memory navigation graph that adapts to skewed workloads, and applies multi-level pruning with geometric bounds to filter both clusters and vectors before issuing SSD reads. Across five standard datasets under strict out-of-core constraints, OrchANN outperforms four baselines including DiskANN, Starling, SPANN, and PipeANN in both QPS and latency while reducing SSD accesses. Furthermore, OrchANN delivers up to 17.2x higher QPS and 25.0x lower latency than competing systems without sacrificing accuracy.

abstract: As Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems evolve toward more sophisticated architectures, ensuring their trustworthiness through explainable and robust evaluation becomes critical. Existing scalar metrics suffer from limited interpretability, inadequate uncertainty quantification, and computational inefficiency in multi-system comparisons, hindering responsible deployment of RAG technologies. We introduce DICE (Discrete Interpretable Comparative Evaluation), a two-stage, evidence-coupled framework that advances explainability and robustness in RAG evaluation. DICE combines deep analytical reasoning with probabilistic $\{A, B, Tie\}$ scoring to produce transparent, confidence-aware judgments that support accountable system improvement through interpretable reasoning traces, enabling systematic error diagnosis and actionable insights. To address efficiency challenges at scale, DICE employs a Swiss-system tournament that reduces computational complexity from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$, achieving a 42.9% reduction in our eight-system evaluation while preserving ranking fidelity. Validation on a curated Chinese financial QA dataset demonstrates that DICE achieves 85.7% agreement with human experts, substantially outperforming existing LLM-based metrics such as RAGAS. abstract: Local railway committees need timely situational awareness after highway-rail grade crossing incidents, yet official Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) investigations can take days to weeks. We present a demo system that populates Highway-Rail Grade Crossing Incident Data (Form 57) from news in real time. Our approach addresses two core challenges: the form is visually irregular and semantically dense, and news is noisy. To solve these problems, we design a pipeline that first converts Form 57 into a JSON schema using a vision language model with sample aggregation, and then performs grouped question answering following the intent of the form layout to reduce ambiguity. In addition, we build an evaluation dataset by aligning scraped news articles with official FRA records and annotating retrievable information. We then assess our system against various alternatives in terms of information retrieval accuracy and coverage.

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in open-domain settings faces significant challenges regarding irrelevant information in retrieved documents and the alignment of generated answers with user intent. We present HiFi-RAG (Hierarchical Filtering RAG), the winning closed-source system in the Text-to-Text static evaluation of the MMU-RAGent NeurIPS 2025 Competition. Our approach moves beyond standard embedding-based retrieval via a multi-stage pipeline. We leverage the speed and cost-efficiency of Gemini 2.5 Flash (4-6x cheaper than Pro) for query formulation, hierarchical content filtering, and citation attribution, while reserving the reasoning capabilities of Gemini 2.5 Pro for final answer generation. On the MMU-RAGent validation set, our system outperformed the baseline, improving ROUGE-L to 0.274 (+19.6%) and DeBERTaScore to 0.677 (+6.2%). On Test2025, our custom dataset evaluating questions that require post-cutoff knowledge (post January 2025), HiFi-RAG outperforms the parametric baseline by 57.4% in ROUGE-L and 14.9% in DeBERTaScore.
title: HiFi-RAG: Hierarchical Content Filtering and Two-Pass Generation for Open-Domain RAG

abstract: Hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) pose a significant challenge, generating misleading or unverifiable content that undermines trust and reliability. Existing evaluation methods, such as KnowHalu, employ multi-stage verification but suffer from high computational costs. To address this, we integrate the Hughes Hallucination Evaluation Model (HHEM), a lightweight classification-based framework that operates independently of LLM-based judgments, significantly improving efficiency while maintaining high detection accuracy. We conduct a comparative analysis of hallucination detection methods across various LLMs, evaluating True Positive Rate (TPR), True Negative Rate (TNR), and Accuracy on question-answering (QA) and summarization tasks. Our results show that HHEM reduces evaluation time from 8 hours to 10 minutes, while HHEM with non-fabrication checking achieves the highest accuracy \(82.2\%\) and TPR \(78.9\%\). However, HHEM struggles with localized hallucinations in summarization tasks. To address this, we introduce segment-based retrieval, improving detection by verifying smaller text components. Additionally, our cumulative distribution function (CDF) analysis indicates that larger models (7B-9B parameters) generally exhibit fewer hallucinations, while intermediate-sized models show higher instability. These findings highlight the need for structured evaluation frameworks that balance computational efficiency with robust factual validation, enhancing the reliability of LLM-generated content.

abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming scientific discovery, enabling rapid knowledge generation and hypothesis formulation. However, a critical challenge is hallucination, where LLMs generate factually incorrect or misleading information, compromising research integrity. To address this, we introduce HalluMatData, a benchmark dataset for evaluating hallucination detection methods, factual consistency, and response robustness in AI-generated materials science content. Alongside this, we propose HalluMatDetector, a multi-stage hallucination detection framework that integrates intrinsic verification, multi-source retrieval, contradiction graph analysis, and metric-based assessment to detect and mitigate LLM hallucinations. Our findings reveal that hallucination levels vary significantly across materials science subdomains, with high-entropy queries exhibiting greater factual inconsistencies. By utilizing HalluMatDetector verification pipeline, we reduce hallucination rates by 30% compared to standard LLM outputs. Furthermore, we introduce the Paraphrased Hallucination Consistency Score (PHCS) to quantify inconsistencies in LLM responses across semantically equivalent queries, offering deeper insights into model reliability.

en.title: OxygenREC: An Instruction-Following Generative Framework for E-commerce Recommendation
en.abstract: Traditional recommendation systems suffer from inconsistency in multi-stage optimization objectives. Generative Recommendation (GR) mitigates them through an end-to-end framework; however, existing methods still rely on matching mechanisms based on inductive patterns. Although responsive, they lack the ability to uncover complex user intents that require deductive reasoning based on world knowledge. Meanwhile, LLMs show strong deep reasoning capabilities, but their latency and computational costs remain challenging for industrial applications. More critically, there are performance bottlenecks in multi-scenario scalability: as shown in Figure 1, existing solutions require independent training and deployment for each scenario, leading to low resource utilization and high maintenance costs-a challenge unaddressed in GR literature. To address these, we present OxygenREC, an industrial recommendation system that leverages Fast-Slow Thinking to deliver deep reasoning with strict latency and multi-scenario requirements of real-world environments. First, we adopt a Fast-Slow Thinking architecture. Slow thinking uses a near-line LLM pipeline to synthesize Contextual Reasoning Instructions, while fast thinking employs a high-efficiency encoder--decoder backbone for real-time generation. Second, to ensure reasoning instructions effectively enhance recommendation generation, we introduce a semantic alignment mechanism with Instruction-Guided Retrieval (IGR) to filter intent-relevant historical behaviors and use a Query-to-Item (Q2I) loss for instruction-item consistency. Finally, to resolve multi-scenario scalability, we transform scenario information into controllable instructions, using unified reward mapping and Soft Adaptive Group Clip Policy Optimization (SA-GCPO) to align policies with diverse business objectives, realizing a train-once-deploy-everywhere paradigm.

summary.summary: OxygenREC, developed by JD.com, is an instruction-following generative framework that seamlessly integrates LLM-based deductive reasoning through a "Fast-Slow Thinking" architecture for e-commerce recommendation. Deployed across diverse online scenarios, it achieved up to +11.80% GMV and +4.28% order volume in A/B tests while maintaining 50-80ms latency.
originalProblem: Existing generative recommendation models lack deductive reasoning, failing to interpret complex user intents and real-world knowledge, leading to "data" and "logic" gaps.
Integrating large language models (LLMs) for deep reasoning into real-time online recommendation systems is hindered by their high latency and computational costs.
Developing scalable recommendation solutions for numerous diverse e-commerce scenarios faces a dilemma: dedicated models are costly, while unified models often suffer from negative transfer.
solution: Introduces a "Fast-Slow Thinking" architecture that uses an offline LLM pipeline to generate contextual reasoning instructions, which then guide a high-throughput online encoder-decoder for real-time item generation.
Leverages multimodal quantized Semantic IDs (SIDs) and Instruction-Guided Retrieval (IGR) with Q2I loss to ensure semantic alignment between instructions and item representations.
Achieves multi-scenario adaptation through scenario instructions and a unified post-training framework using a novel reinforcement learning algorithm, SA-GCPO, optimized for multi-task objectives.
keyInsights: Decoupling LLM reasoning into a near-line slow path and a real-time fast path can effectively inject world knowledge and deductive capabilities without incurring online latency.

A unified generative model can effectively serve diverse e-commerce scenarios by employing scenario-specific instructions and a robust multi-task reinforcement learning approach, fostering synergistic knowledge transfer.
Multimodal quantized item representations (SIDs) provide compact, semantically consistent item tokens, crucial for efficient generation and instruction-guided retrieval in large-scale systems.
results: Online A/B tests at JD.com showed statistically significant increases across key business metrics, including up to +11.80% GMV and +4.28% order volume across diverse scenarios.
The unified instruction-following model consistently outperformed independently fine-tuned models across six core scenarios, demonstrating synergistic knowledge transfer and universal user modeling.
The system maintained low latency (50-80ms) while handling massive online traffic and billion-scale candidate spaces, proving its industrial scalability and efficiency.

en.overview:
## Introduction

E-commerce recommendation systems have evolved from traditional multi-stage pipelines to unified generative approaches, but significant challenges remain in bridging the gap between sophisticated reasoning capabilities and real-world deployment constraints. OxygenREC introduces an instruction-following generative framework that addresses two critical limitations in existing systems: the inability to perform complex deductive reasoning without prohibitive latency costs, and the difficulty of serving multiple recommendation scenarios efficiently within a single model.

![Traditional vs. Generative Recommendation Paradigms](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-0.jpeg)

The framework represents a strategic initiative within JD.com's next-generation e-commerce AI architecture, designed to handle billion-scale item catalogs and massive user traffic while maintaining sub-100ms response times across diverse recommendation scenarios.

## The Fast-Slow Thinking Architecture

OxygenREC's core innovation lies in its Fast-Slow Thinking architecture, which decouples reasoning from real-time generation to achieve both intelligence and efficiency. The "Slow Thinking" component operates offline using Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate contextual reasoning instructions, while the "Fast Thinking" component performs real-time item sequence generation using a lightweight encoder-decoder network.

The Slow Thinking pipeline analyzes diverse user signals including behavioral sequences, spatiotemporal context (location, date, holidays), and demographic profiles to generate "Contextual Reasoning Instructions" ($I_r$). These instructions capture complex user intents that traditional inductive approaches might miss, such as inferring winter clothing needs from "young parents in Chengdu during winter solstice." The generated instructions are converted to dense embeddings and stored in a Redis-based key-value store, updated daily for full refresh and incrementally for high-value user actions.

![Fast-Slow Architecture Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-1.jpeg)

The Fast Thinking component integrates these pre-computed reasoning instructions with real-time scenario instructions ($I_s$) to form a composite instruction prompt that guides the decoder's generation process. This separation ensures that complex reasoning enhances recommendations without impacting online latency.

## Unified Multi-Scenario Framework

Traditional recommendation systems face a fundamental dilemma: dedicated models for each scenario are computationally expensive, while unified models often suffer from negative transfer between scenarios. OxygenREC solves this through an instruction-following paradigm that treats scenario-specific information as controllable instructions rather than architectural modifications.

![Instruction-Following Framework](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-2.jpeg)

The framework introduces Scenario Instructions ($I_s$) that encode scenario-specific contexts (scenario ID, trigger items) into natural language prompts. During training, the model learns to associate different instruction patterns with appropriate recommendation behaviors across scenarios like Homepage feeds, Channel exploration, and Checkout add-ons. This approach enables a single model to serve diverse contexts while maintaining scenario-specific performance characteristics.

## Semantic Alignment and Item Representation

A critical component of OxygenREC is its multimodal quantized item representation system, which creates semantically meaningful item tokens for generation. Items are encoded using Qwen3 for textual features and CLIP for visual features, with the resulting 256-dimensional embeddings discretized into Semantic IDs (SIDs) using a hierarchical 3-layer codebook structure.

The system employs Instruction-Guided Retrieval (IGR) to ensure effective instruction control. An adapter mechanism projects instruction queries and item features into a shared embedding space, while a Query-to-Item (Q2I) loss function aligns instruction embeddings with target item representations during training:

$$
L_{Q2I} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(q, t)/\tau)}{\sum_{i} \exp(\text{sim}(q, i)/\tau)}
$$

where $q$ is the query embedding, $t$ is the target item embedding, and $\tau$ is a temperature parameter.

## Multi-Scenario Reinforcement Learning

To achieve optimal performance across scenarios, OxygenREC employs a novel reinforcement learning algorithm called Soft Adaptive Group Clip Policy Optimization (SA-GCPO). This approach addresses the challenges of multi-scenario, multi-task optimization through several key innovations.

The system uses a unified ranking model as a reward service, providing consistent ranking rewards across scenarios through Format (error penalties), Relative (relevance), Ranking (business objectives), and Diversity metrics. SA-GCPO incorporates a soft adaptive importance sampling function and asymmetric temperature control to enhance training stability:

$$
w(\rho) = \text{sigmoid}(\alpha \cdot (\rho - \beta))
$$

where $\rho$ is the importance sampling ratio, and $\alpha$, $\beta$ are adaptive parameters that provide smooth gradient decay for stability.

![Multi-Scenario Alignment](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-3.jpeg)

## System Implementation and Optimization

OxygenREC's implementation leverages a unified PyTorch-based training framework capable of handling terabyte-scale sparse embeddings and billion-scale dense parameters. The system achieves 40% Model FLOPs Utilization through distributed sparse optimization and custom attention kernels.

For inference, the xGR serving system (built on JD.com's xLLM framework) provides specialized optimizations for generative recommendation workloads. These include xSchedule for task parallelism, xAttention for efficient KV-cache management, and xBeam for optimized beam search with prefix-constrained decoding to enforce scenario-specific business rules.

## Experimental Validation and Results

Comprehensive ablation studies validated key design choices across multiple dimensions. The multimodal item encoder using Qwen3 and CLIP achieved over 30% relative improvement in HitRate@1 compared to heavier alternatives while providing 32x speedup in embedding inference. Scaling experiments from 0.1B to 3.0B parameters using Mixture-of-Experts showed monotonic improvements, with HR@10 increasing from 13.17% to 16.99%.

![Scaling Laws](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-7.jpeg)

The instruction-following capabilities were thoroughly evaluated, with "Fused Instruction" (combining scenario and trigger information) achieving the best HR@1 of 3.60%. The unified model consistently outperformed independently fine-tuned baselines across six core scenarios, demonstrating effective knowledge transfer and universal user modeling.

Post-training experiments confirmed SA-GCPO's superiority over established RL methods, achieving +1.73pp improvement in HR@1 and over +3pp in HR@10 compared to GRPO. The incorporation of synthetic data further enhanced performance, with SA-GCPO showing more consistent gains across varying data proportions.

![SA-GCPO Performance](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-8.jpeg)

## Industrial Impact and Deployment

OxygenREC was deployed across three critical scenarios in the JD App ecosystem, covering the complete user journey from interest triggering to conversion. Online A/B tests with 10% traffic allocation demonstrated statistically significant improvements across all business metrics:

- **Homepage Floor scenarios**: Up to +8.40% GMV increase
- **Channel Feeds**: +8.03% Order Volume with improved click quality
- **Checkout Path**: +11.80% GMV and +4.28% Order Volume gains

The system maintained strict latency requirements (50-80ms) while handling massive traffic volumes, proving its scalability and efficiency in demanding production environments.

## Significance and Future Directions

OxygenREC represents a significant advancement in bridging the gap between LLM reasoning capabilities and industrial recommendation system requirements. By successfully integrating deductive reasoning without compromising latency, it moves recommendation systems beyond pattern matching toward intelligent, context-aware assistance.

The unified multi-scenario approach validates the "train-once-deploy-everywhere" paradigm, drastically reducing operational overhead while maintaining high performance across diverse contexts. The demonstrated industrial impact at JD.com's scale provides strong empirical evidence of the framework's practical value and reliability.

Future research directions include exploring non-autoregressive generation for further latency optimization and enhancing multi-scenario user trajectory modeling for deeper intent discovery. These developments could further advance the field toward more efficient and intelligent generative recommendation systems.

zh.title: OxygenREC: 指令遵循的电商推荐生成框架
zh.abstract:
传统推荐系统存在多阶段优化目标不一致的问题。生成式推荐 (GR) 通过端到端框架缓解了这些问题；然而，现有方法仍然依赖于基于归纳模式的匹配机制。尽管响应迅速，但它们缺乏揭示需要基于世界知识进行演绎推理的复杂用户意图的能力。同时，大语言模型 (LLMs) 展示出强大的深度推理能力，但其延迟和计算成本对于工业应用而言仍是挑战。更重要的是，在多场景可扩展性方面存在性能瓶颈：如图1所示，现有解决方案需要为每个场景独立训练和部署，导致资源利用率低下和维护成本高昂——这一挑战在生成式推荐文献中尚未得到解决。

为解决这些问题，我们提出了 OxygenREC，一个工业级推荐系统。它利用快慢思维，在满足真实世界环境中严格延迟和多场景需求的同时，提供深度推理能力。首先，我们采用快慢思维架构。慢思考利用近线大语言模型流水线合成上下文推理指令，而快思考则采用高效编码器-解码器骨干网络进行实时生成。其次，为确保推理指令有效增强推荐生成，我们引入了语义对齐机制：通过指令引导检索 (IGR) 筛选意图相关的历史行为，并使用查询-物品 (Q2I) 损失来确保指令与物品之间的一致性。最后，为解决多场景可扩展性问题，我们将场景信息转化为可控指令，并利用统一奖励映射和软自适应组剪辑策略优化 (SA-GCPO) 使策略与多样化的业务目标对齐，从而实现了“一次训练，处处部署”的范式。

summary.summary: OxygenREC是京东开发的一个遵循指令的生成式框架，它通过“快慢思考”架构无缝集成基于LLM的演绎推理，用于电商推荐。它已部署在多样化的在线场景中，在A/B测试中实现了高达+11.80%的GMV增长和+4.28%的订单量增长，同时保持了50-80毫秒的延迟。
originalProblem: 现有的生成式推荐模型缺乏演绎推理能力，无法解释复杂的用户意图和现实世界知识，导致“数据”和“逻辑”鸿沟。
将大型语言模型（LLM）用于深度推理集成到实时在线推荐系统中，受到其高延迟和计算成本的阻碍。
为众多多样化的电商场景开发可扩展的推荐解决方案面临两难：专用模型成本高昂，而统一模型常遭受负迁移问题。
solution: 引入“快慢思考”架构，利用离线LLM管道生成上下文推理指令，然后指导高吞吐量的在线编码器-解码器进行实时物品生成。
利用多模态量化语义ID（SIDs）和指令引导检索（IGR）与Q2I损失，确保指令与物品表示之间的语义对齐。
通过场景指令和使用新型强化学习算法SA-GCPO的统一后训练框架实现多场景适应性，该算法针对多任务目标进行了优化。
keyInsights: 将LLM推理解耦为近线慢路径和实时快路径，可以有效注入世界知识和演绎能力，而不会产生在线延迟。
通过采用场景特定指令和稳健的多任务强化学习方法，统一的生成模型可以有效服务于多样化的电商场景，促进协同知识迁移。
多模态量化物品表示（SIDs）提供紧凑、语义一致的物品令牌，对于大规模系统中的高效生成和指令引导检索至关重要。
results: 京东的在线A/B测试显示，在不同场景下，关键业务指标显著增长，包括GMV增长高达+11.80%，订单量增长高达+4.28%。
统一的指令遵循模型在六个核心场景中持续优于独立微调的模型，证明了协同知识迁移和通用用户建模的能力。
系统在处理海量在线流量和亿级候选空间的同时保持了低延迟（50-80毫秒），证明了其工业级可扩展性和效率。

zh.overview:
## 引言

电商推荐系统已经从传统的多阶段流水线演变为统一的生成式方法，但在弥合复杂的推理能力与实际部署限制之间的鸿沟方面，仍存在重大挑战。OxygenREC 引入了一个遵循指令的生成式框架，解决了现有系统中存在的两个关键局限性：一是无法在不产生过高延迟成本的情况下执行复杂的演绎推理，二是在单个模型中高效服务多种推荐场景的困难。

![传统与生成式推荐范式](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-0.jpeg)

该框架是京东下一代电商 AI 架构中的一项战略性举措，旨在处理数十亿规模的商品目录和海量用户流量，同时在各种推荐场景中保持低于 100 毫秒的响应时间。

## 快慢思考架构

OxygenREC 的核心创新在于其快慢思考架构，该架构将推理与实时生成解耦，以实现智能和效率兼顾。其中，“慢思考”组件利用大型语言模型（LLM）进行离线操作，生成上下文推理指令，而“快思考”组件则使用轻量级编码器-解码器网络进行实时商品序列生成。

慢思考流水线分析多样化的用户信号，包括行为序列、时空上下文（地点、日期、节假日）和人口统计资料，以生成“上下文推理指令”（$I_r$）。这些指令捕捉了传统归纳方法可能遗漏的复杂用户意图，例如从“冬至时节成都的年轻父母”中推断出冬季服装需求。生成的指令被转换为密集嵌入并存储在基于 Redis 的键值存储中，每日更新以实现完全刷新，并针对高价值用户行为进行增量更新。

![快慢架构概览](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-1.jpeg)

快思考组件将这些预先计算的推理指令与实时场景指令（$I_s$）相结合，形成一个复合指令提示，指导解码器的生成过程。这种分离确保了复杂推理能够增强推荐效果，同时不影响在线延迟。

## 统一多场景框架

传统推荐系统面临一个根本性困境：为每个场景建立专用模型计算成本高昂，而统一模型则常常受到场景间负迁移的影响。OxygenREC 通过指令遵循范式解决了这一问题，该范式将场景特定信息视为可控指令而非架构修改。

![指令遵循框架](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-2.jpeg)

该框架引入了场景指令（$I_s$），将场景特定上下文（场景 ID、触发商品）编码为自然语言提示。在训练期间，模型学习将不同的指令模式与跨首页信息流、频道探索和结账加购等场景的相应推荐行为关联起来。这种方法使单个模型能够服务于多样化的上下文，同时保持场景特定的性能特征。

## 语义对齐与商品表示

OxygenREC 的一个关键组成部分是其多模态量化商品表示系统，该系统为生成创建了具有语义意义的商品标记。商品使用 Qwen3 编码文本特征，使用 CLIP 编码视觉特征，并将生成的 256 维嵌入通过分层 3 层码本结构离散化为语义 ID（SIDs）。

该系统采用指令引导检索 (IGR) 以确保有效的指令控制。一个适配器机制将指令查询和物品特征投影到共享嵌入空间中，同时一个查询到物品 (Q2I) 损失函数在训练期间将指令嵌入与目标物品表示对齐：

$$
L_{Q2I} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(q, t)/\tau)}{\sum_{i} \exp(\text{sim}(q, i)/\tau)}
$$

其中 $q$ 是查询嵌入，$t$ 是目标物品嵌入，$\tau$ 是一个温度参数。

## 多场景强化学习

为了在不同场景中实现最佳性能，OxygenREC 采用了一种新颖的强化学习算法，称为软自适应分组裁剪策略优化 (SA-GCPO)。该方法通过多项关键创新解决了多场景、多任务优化的挑战。

该系统使用统一的排序模型作为奖励服务，通过格式（错误惩罚）、相对性（相关性）、排序（业务目标）和多样性指标在不同场景中提供一致的排序奖励。SA-GCPO 结合了软自适应重要性采样函数和非对称温度控制，以增强训练稳定性：

$$
w(\rho) = \text{sigmoid}(\alpha \cdot (\rho - \beta))
$$

其中 $\rho$ 是重要性采样比，$\alpha$ 和 $\beta$ 是自适应参数，为稳定性提供平滑的梯度衰减。

![多场景对齐](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-3.jpeg)

## 系统实现与优化

OxygenREC 的实现利用了一个统一的基于 PyTorch 的训练框架，能够处理 TB 级稀疏嵌入和十亿级密集参数。该系统通过分布式稀疏优化和自定义注意力核实现了 40% 的模型浮点运算利用率。

对于推理，xGR 服务系统（基于京东的 xLLM 框架构建）为生成式推荐工作负载提供了专门的优化。这些优化包括用于任务并行化的 xSchedule、用于高效 KV 缓存管理的 xAttention，以及用于优化束搜索和前缀约束解码的 xBeam，以强制执行场景特定的业务规则。

## 实验验证与结果

全面的消融研究在多个维度验证了关键设计选择。使用通义千问3和 CLIP 的多模态物品编码器在命中率@1方面比更重的替代方案相对提升超过 30%，同时在嵌入推理速度上提高了 32 倍。使用专家混合模型将参数从 0.1B 扩展到 3.0B 的实验显示出单调改进，命中率@10从 13.17% 增加到 16.99%。

![扩展定律](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-7.jpeg)

指令遵循能力得到了全面评估，其中“融合指令”（结合场景和触发信息）实现了最佳命中率@1，达到 3.60%。统一模型在六个核心场景中始终优于独立微调的基线，展示了有效的知识迁移和通用用户建模能力。

训练后实验证实了 SA-GCPO 优于现有强化学习方法，与 GRPO 相比，命中率@1提升了 +1.73pp，命中率@10提升了超过 +3pp。合成数据的引入进一步增强了性能，SA-GCPO 在不同数据比例下显示出更一致的增益。

![SA-GCPO 性能](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22386v1/img-8.jpeg)

## 工业影响与部署

OxygenREC 已部署在京东 App 生态系统的三个关键场景中，涵盖了从兴趣触发到转化的完整用户旅程。10% 流量分配的在线 A/B 测试表明，所有业务指标均取得了统计学上的显著改进：

- **主页楼层场景**: GMV增长高达+8.40%
- **频道信息流**: 订单量增长+8.03%，点击质量得到改善
- **结算路径**: GMV增长+11.80%，订单量增长+4.28%

该系统在处理海量流量的同时，严格遵守了延迟要求（50-80毫秒），证明了其在严苛生产环境中的可扩展性和效率。

## 意义和未来方向

OxygenREC 代表着在弥合大型语言模型（LLM）推理能力与工业级推荐系统需求之间差距方面的一项重大进展。通过在不影响延迟的情况下成功整合演绎推理，它将推荐系统从模式匹配推向了智能、上下文感知的辅助。

统一的多场景方法验证了“一次训练，随处部署”的范式，在保持跨多样化场景的高性能的同时，大幅降低了运营开销。在京东如此大规模下的工业影响力展示，为该框架的实用价值和可靠性提供了强有力的经验证据。

未来的研究方向包括探索非自回归生成以进一步优化延迟，以及增强多场景用户轨迹建模以实现更深层次的意图发现。这些发展可以进一步推动该领域，使其迈向更高效、更智能的生成式推荐系统。

abstract: Traditional recommendation systems suffer from inconsistency in multi-stage optimization objectives. Generative Recommendation (GR) mitigates them through an end-to-end framework; however, existing methods still rely on matching mechanisms based on inductive patterns. Although responsive, they lack the ability to uncover complex user intents that require deductive reasoning based on world knowledge. Meanwhile, LLMs show strong deep reasoning capabilities, but their latency and computational costs remain challenging for industrial applications. More critically, there are performance bottlenecks in multi-scenario scalability: as shown in Figure 1, existing solutions require independent training and deployment for each scenario, leading to low resource utilization and high maintenance costs-a challenge unaddressed in GR literature. To address these, we present OxygenREC, an industrial recommendation system that leverages Fast-Slow Thinking to deliver deep reasoning with strict latency and multi-scenario requirements of real-world environments. First, we adopt a Fast-Slow Thinking architecture. Slow thinking uses a near-line LLM pipeline to synthesize Contextual Reasoning Instructions, while fast thinking employs a high-efficiency encoder--decoder backbone for real-time generation. Second, to ensure reasoning instructions effectively enhance recommendation generation, we introduce a semantic alignment mechanism with Instruction-Guided Retrieval (IGR) to filter intent-relevant historical behaviors and use a Query-to-Item (Q2I) loss for instruction-item consistency. Finally, to resolve multi-scenario scalability, we transform scenario information into controllable instructions, using unified reward mapping and Soft Adaptive Group Clip Policy Optimization (SA-GCPO) to align policies with diverse business objectives, realizing a train-once-deploy-everywhere paradigm.

en.title: AutoPP: Towards Automated Product Poster Generation and Optimization
en.abstract: Product posters blend striking visuals with informative text to highlight the product and capture customer attention. However, crafting appealing posters and manually optimizing them based on online performance is laborious and resource-consuming. To address this, we introduce AutoPP, an automated pipeline for product poster generation and optimization that eliminates the need for human intervention. Specifically, the generator, relying solely on basic product information, first uses a unified design module to integrate the three key elements of a poster (background, text, and layout) into a cohesive output. Then, an element rendering module encodes these elements into condition tokens, efficiently and controllably generating the product poster. Based on the generated poster, the optimizer enhances its Click-Through Rate (CTR) by leveraging online feedback. It systematically replaces elements to gather fine-grained CTR comparisons and utilizes Isolated Direct Preference Optimization (IDPO) to attribute CTR gains to isolated elements. Our work is supported by AutoPP1M, the largest dataset specifically designed for product poster generation and optimization, which contains one million high-quality posters and feedback collected from over one million users. Experiments demonstrate that AutoPP achieves state-of-the-art results in both offline and online settings. Our code and dataset are publicly available at: this https URL

summary.summary: JD.COM researchers developed AutoPP, an end-to-end system for automated product poster generation and online optimization using a unified design module and element-isolated preference learning. The system achieves a 4.49% relative Click-Through Rate (CTR) improvement in real-world scenarios while producing visually superior and text-accurate posters compared to previous methods.
originalProblem: Manual product poster creation is laborious, fragmented, and lacks scalability for large e-commerce platforms like JD.COM.
Traditional online optimization for marketing posters is inefficient, relies on manual analysis, and struggles to identify specific design elements driving performance changes.

Prior automated generative models often prioritize offline aesthetics, exhibit design inconsistencies, and struggle with accurate text rendering, while existing CTR optimization methods are limited to background changes.
solution: An Automated Product Poster Generator integrates a Unified Design MLLM (generating background prompts, text, and layout) with an Element Rendering Module (synthesizing the poster using a token-based architecture with decomposed attention and OCR perceptual loss).

An Automated Product Poster Optimizer employs Isolated Direct Preference Optimization (IDPO), which systematically perturbs individual poster elements, collects online CTR feedback from pairwise comparisons, and fine-tunes the generator with element-specific preference weights.

The AutoPP1M dataset, comprising one million high-quality product posters with annotations and 50,000 element-wise paired comparisons with real-world CTR feedback, supports both generation and fine-grained optimization tasks.
keyInsights: A unified design approach, jointly reasoning about background, text, and layout, yields more coherent and higher-quality product posters than fragmented, multi-stage generation pipelines.

Element-isolated optimization (IDPO) effectively attributes online performance gains to specific design components, leading to more targeted, interpretable, and efficient CTR improvements than holistic optimization methods.

Robust and efficient visual text rendering, crucial for marketing content, can be achieved by integrating glyph image token encoding and an OCR perceptual loss within a diffusion model's training objective.
results: AutoPP achieved state-of-the-art performance in poster generation, with superior visual quality (FID 60.71, CLIP-T 29.75), layout rationality (MIoU 0.256), and text rendering accuracy (Sentence Accuracy 65.19%) compared to existing open and closed-source benchmarks.

The system delivered a substantial 4.49% relative CTR improvement over the non-optimized generator, significantly outperforming prior CTR optimization methods which yielded negative or negligible gains.

Ablation studies confirmed the efficiency of the Decomposed Attention mechanism (18-24% GFLOPs reduction) and the effectiveness of IDPO, which outperformed standard DPO with a 3.10% relative CTR compared to IDPO's 4.49%.

en.overview:
## Introduction

AutoPP represents a comprehensive solution for automating the entire lifecycle of product poster creation and optimization in e-commerce. Developed by researchers at JD.COM, one of China's largest e-commerce platforms, this system addresses a critical challenge faced by online retailers: the labor-intensive process of creating visually appealing product posters and optimizing them for maximum user engagement. Traditional approaches require significant manual effort from skilled designers and involve fragmented workflows that often fail to optimize for real-world performance metrics like Click-Through Rate (CTR).

![AutoPP System Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-0.jpeg)

*Figure 1: Comparison of different product poster generation approaches. AutoPP (bottom) provides end-to-end automation with online optimization capabilities, contrasting with existing methods that require manual intervention and lack performance optimization.*

The AutoPP system introduces two key innovations: an automated generator that creates coherent product posters from basic product information, and an optimizer that systematically improves poster performance using real-world user feedback. This represents a paradigm shift from aesthetic-focused generation to performance-driven design optimization, enabling e-commerce platforms to scale their marketing content creation while maximizing business impact.

## Problem Statement and Motivation

Creating effective product posters for e-commerce involves multiple complex challenges. Traditional manual processes require skilled designers to carefully balance visual appeal with informational content, coordinating background imagery, text placement, layout design, and product presentation. This process becomes particularly challenging when dealing with Chinese text rendering, which requires precise character formation and appropriate visual hierarchy.

Beyond creation difficulties, optimizing poster performance presents additional challenges. Conventional optimization relies on manual analysis of performance data and iterative design adjustments based on human intuition. This approach lacks precision in identifying which specific elements - background, text content, or layout - contribute to performance improvements. Existing automated solutions address only fragments of this pipeline, often optimizing single elements like backgrounds while ignoring the holistic impact of all design components.

The motivation behind AutoPP stems from JD.COM's operational needs to process millions of products requiring dynamic, engaging visual content. Manual poster creation and optimization simply cannot scale to meet these demands while maintaining quality and performance standards. The system aims to transform this labor-intensive, fragmented process into a streamlined, data-driven pipeline that maximizes both efficiency and business impact.

## Methodology

AutoPP employs a two-stage pipeline: the **Automated Product Poster Generator** and the **Automated Product Poster Optimizer**, supported by the AutoPP1M dataset.

### Automated Product Poster Generator

The generator consists of two integrated modules that work together to produce high-quality product posters from minimal input.

#### Unified Design Module

The Unified Design Module employs a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) initialized from LLaVA to jointly reason about all poster elements. Given a product image and candidate text options, the MLLM processes structured natural language instructions to generate three coordinated outputs: a background prompt for image generation, optimal text selection from candidates, and layout specifications including bounding box coordinates for product and text placement.

This unified approach contrasts significantly with fragmented pipelines that handle these elements separately. By processing all design decisions simultaneously, the module ensures coherence and consistency across all poster elements. The training objective minimizes cross-entropy loss to maintain design harmony throughout the generation process.

#### Element Rendering Module

The Element Rendering Module synthesizes the final poster using a token-based architecture initialized from FLUX.1. It processes multiple inputs: the background prompt, selected text, layout specifications, and specialized control signals including the product image positioned according to predicted layout masks and glyph images representing text rendered at predicted positions.

A key innovation is the **Decomposed Attention (DA)** mechanism, which modifies standard full attention in MM-DiT blocks to handle long token sequences efficiently. The mechanism operates through:

- **Condition Self-Attention:** Processing glyph and product tokens independently to capture intra-element dependencies
- **Image-Condition Cross-Attention:** Enabling information exchange by constructing queries from prompt and noise tokens while using keys/values from all token types

The training incorporates an **OCR perceptual loss** alongside standard flow matching loss. This additional objective compares intermediate features from a pre-trained PaddleOCRv4 backbone between predicted and target images, explicitly enforcing text legibility and accuracy - crucial for high-quality poster text rendering.

### Automated Product Poster Optimizer

The optimizer refines generated posters to maximize CTR using real-world user feedback through a systematic approach.

#### Systematic Element Replacement

For each generated poster, the system creates variants by systematically perturbing individual elements while keeping others constant:

- **Background Replacement:** GPT-4o generates alternative background prompts that maintain thematic relevance
- **Text Replacement:** Alternative text of similar length is selected from candidate sets  
- **Layout Replacement:** The unified design module regenerates alternative spatial arrangements

This process creates poster pairs differing in only one element, enabling precise attribution of performance changes to specific design components.

#### Isolated Direct Preference Optimization (IDPO)

IDPO represents a novel adaptation of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for fine-grained preference learning. The systematically generated poster pairs undergo randomized online display experiments on JD.COM's platform to collect actual CTR feedback, establishing preference relations where higher-CTR posters are preferred.

Unlike standard DPO that optimizes overall output distributions, IDPO incorporates element-specific weights into the likelihood calculation:

$$
\log \pi_w(y|I, X) = \sum_i w_i \log \pi_\theta(y_i|I, X)
$$

where $w_i = \sum_c \alpha_c \cdot \mathbf{I}(y_i \in c)$ and $\alpha_c$ controls the importance of element $c$. This formulation allows the model to attribute CTR improvements to specific isolated elements, leading to more efficient and interpretable optimization.

The IDPO loss function becomes:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{IDPO} = -\log \sigma\left(\beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta^{(t)}(y^+|I,X)}{\pi_{ref}(y^+|I,X)} - \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta^{(t)}(y^-|I,X)}{\pi_{ref}(y^-|I,X)}\right)
$$

This enables targeted fine-tuning of the unified design module to favor higher-CTR elements while providing interpretable feedback about which design decisions drive performance improvements.

## Dataset and Evaluation

### AutoPP1M Dataset

The researchers introduce AutoPP1M, the largest dataset of product posters to date, containing one million high-quality posters collected from JD.COM. The dataset covers over 60 product categories with consistent 1:1 aspect ratios and minimum 800×800 pixel resolution. All posters underwent rigorous quality filtering including aesthetic evaluation, blur detection, watermark removal, and OCR-based text validation.

Key dataset components include:

- **Generation Annotations:** Detailed visual element annotations including product masks, text content, text bounding boxes, and background prompts generated using state-of-the-art vision models
- **Optimization Subset:** 50,000 pairwise comparisons with real-world CTR feedback collected from over one million users across 10 days of online experiments
- **Element-Level Preferences:** Unique fine-grained preference assessments for background, text, and layout components

### Performance Metrics

The evaluation framework encompasses both offline generation quality and online performance optimization:

**Generation Metrics:**
- Overall quality: FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), CLIP-T (CLIP text-image similarity)
- Layout rationality: Alignment, Overlap, Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU)  
- Text accuracy: Sentence Accuracy, Normalized Edit Distance

**Optimization Metrics:**
- Relative CTR improvement over baseline generators
- Reward accuracy in preference prediction tasks
- Element attribution effectiveness

## Results and Findings

### Generation Performance

AutoPP achieved state-of-the-art results across all evaluation metrics, significantly outperforming existing open-source methods (P&R, PAID) and closed-source baselines (GPT-4o). The system demonstrated superior visual quality with FID of 60.71 and CLIP-T of 29.75, while showing better layout rationality through improved alignment (0.007), reduced overlap (0.011), and higher MIoU (0.256).

![Qualitative comparison showing AutoPP's superior poster generation](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-2.jpeg)

*Figure 2: Qualitative comparison between different generation methods. AutoPP successfully avoids common issues like obstructed products, unclear text, and incorrect text generation that plague other approaches.*

For specialized text rendering evaluation, AutoPP achieved 65.19% sentence accuracy and 12.94 normalized edit distance, outperforming dedicated text generation methods including Glyph-byt5-v2 and AnyText-v2. The system demonstrated particular strength in rendering small Chinese fonts with high legibility.

![Generated poster examples across different product categories](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-3.jpeg)

*Figure 3: Diverse product posters generated by AutoPP across various categories, demonstrating consistent quality and aesthetic appeal while maintaining product visibility and text clarity.*

### Optimization Performance  

The optimization capabilities delivered substantial business impact with a 4.49% relative CTR improvement over non-optimized generators. This performance significantly exceeded existing CTR optimization approaches like CG4CTR and CAIG, which showed negative relative CTRs (-2.15% and -1.29% respectively), highlighting their limitation of optimizing only background elements.

![CTR optimization results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-4.jpeg)

*Figure 4: Relative CTR improvement comparison. AutoPP achieves substantial positive improvement while existing methods show negative performance, demonstrating the importance of holistic optimization.*

The effectiveness of IDPO over standard DPO was validated through ablation studies, with IDPO achieving 4.49% relative CTR compared to DPO's 3.10%. This validates the advantage of element-isolated optimization for more precise and effective learning from user preferences.

### Technical Innovations

The Decomposed Attention mechanism successfully reduced computational overhead by 18% at 800×800 resolution and 24% at 1024×1024 resolution compared to full attention, while maintaining generation quality. The token-based approach for product and text control required no additional parameters, contrasting favorably with ControlNet-based methods that add billions of parameters.

![Cross-lingual generation capabilities](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-8.jpeg)

*Figure 5: AutoPP's emergent cross-lingual capabilities, successfully generating posters in English, Japanese, and Korean despite primary training on Chinese text.*

AutoPP demonstrated versatility through multi-aspect-ratio generation capabilities and emergent cross-lingual generalization, successfully rendering text in English, Japanese, and Korean despite primary training on Chinese characters.

## Significance and Impact

AutoPP represents a significant advancement in automated content creation for commercial applications, with implications extending beyond e-commerce to digital marketing and creative industries more broadly. The system's ability to achieve measurable business impact through a 4.49% CTR improvement demonstrates the practical value of AI-driven marketing optimization.

The technical contributions, particularly the unified design approach and IDPO methodology, advance the state-of-the-art in generative AI and preference learning. The unified design module overcomes the inconsistencies inherent in multi-stage approaches, while IDPO enables fine-grained attribution of performance gains to specific design elements - a capability that extends beyond poster generation to other complex optimization scenarios.

The release of AutoPP1M provides the research community with an unprecedented resource for developing and evaluating next-generation generative models and preference learning algorithms. The dataset's scale, quality, and unique element-level annotations with real-world performance feedback will accelerate innovation in automated visual content creation.

For practitioners, AutoPP democratizes access to high-quality marketing design, enabling small businesses to compete with larger enterprises through AI-powered content creation tools. The system's automation capabilities eliminate the need for specialized design skills while ensuring performance optimization through data-driven insights rather than intuition-based decisions.

The work establishes a new paradigm for AI-generated marketing content, moving beyond aesthetic considerations to direct optimization for business metrics. This approach bridges the gap between generative AI research and commercial applications, providing a template for future developments in performance-driven content creation systems.

It is highly relevant as a foundational concept for controllable generation, a core challenge in creating posters, and is used by competing methods like PosterMaker that are analyzed in the paper.

zh.abstract: 产品海报融合了引人注目的视觉元素和信息丰富的文字，以突出产品并吸引顾客注意力。然而，制作精美的海报并根据在线表现手动优化，既费力又耗费资源。为解决此问题，我们提出了 AutoPP，这是一个无需人工干预的产品海报生成与优化自动化流程。具体而言，生成器仅依赖基础产品信息，首先利用统一设计模块将海报的三个关键元素（背景、文本和布局）整合为一体。接着，元素渲染模块将这些元素编码为条件令牌，从而高效且可控地生成产品海报。基于生成的海报，优化器通过利用在线反馈来提升其点击率（CTR）。它系统地替换元素以收集细粒度的 CTR 比较，并利用隔离直接偏好优化（IDPO）将 CTR 增益归因于隔离的元素。我们的工作得到了 AutoPP1M 的支持，这是专为产品海报生成与优化而设计的最大数据集，其中包含一百万张高质量海报以及从超过一百万用户收集的反馈。实验证明，AutoPP 在离线和在线环境中均取得了最先进（SOTA）的成果。我们的代码和数据集已公开发布于：this https URL

summary.summary: 京东研究人员开发了AutoPP，这是一个端到端系统，通过统一设计模块和元素隔离偏好学习，实现产品海报的自动化生成和在线优化。该系统在实际场景中实现了4.49%的点击率（CTR）相对提升，同时生成了比以往方法视觉效果更佳、文本更准确的海报。
originalProblem: 手动创建产品海报耗时费力、碎片化，且对于京东这类大型电商平台来说缺乏可扩展性。
传统营销海报的在线优化效率低下，依赖人工分析，并且难以识别驱动性能变化的具体设计元素。
先前的自动化生成模型通常优先考虑离线美学，存在设计不一致性，并且难以准确渲染文本，而现有的点击率优化方法仅限于背景更改。
solution: 自动化产品海报生成器整合了统一设计MLLM（生成背景提示、文本和布局）和一个元素渲染模块（使用基于令牌的架构、分解注意力机制和OCR感知损失来合成海报）。
自动化产品海报优化器采用隔离式直接偏好优化（IDPO），该方法系统地扰动单个海报元素，从成对比较中收集在线点击率反馈，并利用元素特定的偏好权重微调生成器。
AutoPP1M数据集包含一百万张高质量产品海报及其注释，以及50,000个带有实际点击率反馈的元素级配对比较，支持生成和细粒度优化任务。
keyInsights: 统一的设计方法，共同推理背景、文本和布局，比碎片化的多阶段生成流程产生更连贯、更高质量的产品海报。
元素隔离优化（IDPO）有效地将在线性能提升归因于特定的设计组件，从而比整体优化方法带来更有针对性、更具可解释性且更高效的点击率提升。
通过在扩散模型的训练目标中整合字形图像令牌编码和OCR感知损失，可以实现对营销内容至关重要的稳健高效的视觉文本渲染。
results: 与现有开源和闭源基准相比，AutoPP在海报生成方面取得了最先进的性能，具有卓越的视觉质量（FID 60.71，CLIP-T 29.75）、布局合理性（MIoU 0.256）和文本渲染准确性（句子准确率 65.19%）。
该系统相对于未优化的生成器实现了4.49%的点击率相对提升，显著优于先前产生负面或微不足道增益的点击率优化方法。
消融研究证实了分解注意力机制的效率（GFLOPs减少18-24%）和IDPO的有效性，IDPO的点击率相对提升为4.49%，而标准DPO为3.10%。

zh.overview:
## 简介

AutoPP 代表着一种全面的解决方案，旨在自动化电子商务中产品海报创建和优化的整个生命周期。该系统由中国最大的电子商务平台之一京东的研究人员开发，旨在解决在线零售商面临的一个关键挑战：创建具有视觉吸引力的产品海报并对其进行优化以实现最大用户参与度的劳动密集型过程。传统方法需要熟练设计师付出大量手动工作，并且涉及碎片化的工作流程，这些工作流程通常无法针对点击率 (CTR) 等实际性能指标进行优化。

![AutoPP 系统概述](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-0.jpeg)

*图 1：不同产品海报生成方法的比较。AutoPP（底部）提供端到端自动化和在线优化功能，与需要手动干预且缺乏性能优化的现有方法形成对比。*

AutoPP 系统引入了两项关键创新：一个自动化生成器，可根据基本产品信息创建连贯的产品海报；以及一个优化器，可利用真实用户反馈系统地提高海报性能。这代表着从以美学为中心的生成到以性能为导向的设计优化的范式转变，使电子商务平台能够扩展其营销内容创作，同时最大化业务影响。

## 问题陈述与动机

为电子商务创建有效的产品海报涉及多个复杂的挑战。传统的手动流程要求熟练设计师仔细平衡视觉吸引力与信息内容，协调背景图像、文本放置、布局设计和产品呈现。当处理中文文本渲染时，这尤其具有挑战性，需要精确的字符形成和适当的视觉层次结构。

除了创作困难之外，优化海报性能也带来了额外的挑战。传统的优化依赖于对性能数据的手动分析以及基于人类直觉的迭代设计调整。这种方法在识别哪些特定元素（背景、文本内容或布局）有助于性能改进方面缺乏精确性。现有的自动化解决方案仅解决了这个管道的碎片，通常只优化单个元素，例如背景，而忽略了所有设计组件的整体影响。

AutoPP 的动机源于京东的运营需求，即需要处理数百万个需要动态、引人入胜的视觉内容的产品。手动海报创建和优化根本无法在满足这些需求的同时保持质量和性能标准。该系统旨在将这种劳动密集型、碎片化的过程转变为一个精简、数据驱动的管道，以最大限度地提高效率和业务影响力。

## 方法论

AutoPP 采用两阶段管道：**自动化产品海报生成器**和**自动化产品海报优化器**，并由 AutoPP1M 数据集提供支持。

### 自动化产品海报生成器

该生成器由两个集成模块组成，它们协同工作，以最少的输入生成高质量的产品海报。

#### 统一设计模块

统一设计模块采用从 LLaVA 初始化而来的多模态大型语言模型 (MLLM)，以共同推理所有海报元素。给定产品图片和候选文本选项，MLLM 处理结构化自然语言指令，以生成三个协调的输出：用于图像生成的背景提示、从候选文本中选择最佳文本，以及包含产品和文本放置的边界框坐标的布局规范。

这种统一的方法与分别处理这些元素的碎片化管道形成了鲜明对比。通过同时处理所有设计决策，该模块确保了所有海报元素的一致性和连贯性。训练目标最小化交叉熵损失，以在整个生成过程中保持设计和谐。

#### 元素渲染模块

元素渲染模块使用从 FLUX.1 初始化的基于令牌的架构合成最终海报。它处理多个输入：背景提示、选定文本、布局规范以及专门的控制信号，包括根据预测布局遮罩定位的产品图像和表示在预测位置渲染的文本的字形图像。

一个关键创新是**分解注意力 (DA)** 机制，它修改了 MM-DiT 块中的标准全注意力，以高效处理长令牌序列。该机制通过以下方式运行：

- **条件自注意力：** 独立处理字形和产品令牌，以捕获元素内部依赖性
- **图像条件交叉注意力：** 通过从提示和噪声令牌构建查询，同时使用所有令牌类型的键/值来启用信息交换

训练中除了标准流匹配损失外，还包含了 **OCR 感知损失**。这一附加目标通过比较预测图像和目标图像之间预训练的 PaddleOCRv4 骨干网络的中间特征，明确强制执行文本可读性和准确性——这对于高质量海报文本渲染至关重要。

### 自动化产品海报优化器

优化器通过系统化方法，利用真实用户反馈来优化生成的海报，以最大化点击率 (CTR)。

#### 系统化元素替换

对于每张生成的海报，系统通过系统地扰动单个元素而保持其他元素不变来创建变体：

- **背景替换：** GPT-4o 生成保持主题相关性的替代背景提示
- **文本替换：** 从候选集中选择长度相似的替代文本
- **布局替换：** 统一设计模块重新生成替代的空间排列

这个过程创建了仅在一个元素上有所不同的海报对，从而能够精确地将性能变化归因于特定的设计组件。

#### 隔离式直接偏好优化 (IDPO)

IDPO 代表了对直接偏好优化 (DPO) 的新颖改编，用于细粒度偏好学习。系统生成的成对海报在京东平台进行随机在线展示实验，以收集实际的 CTR 反馈，从而建立偏好关系，其中 CTR 更高的海报被优先选择。

与优化整体输出分布的标准 DPO 不同，IDPO 将元素特定权重纳入似然计算：

$$
\log \pi_w(y|I, X) = \sum_i w_i \log \pi_\theta(y_i|I, X)
$$

其中 $w_i = \sum_c \alpha_c \cdot \mathbf{I}(y_i \in c)$，$ \alpha_c $ 控制元素 $c$ 的重要性。这个公式允许模型将 CTR 改进归因于特定的隔离元素，从而实现更高效和可解释的优化。

IDPO 损失函数变为：

$$
\mathcal{L}_{IDPO} = -\log \sigma\left(\beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta^{(t)}(y^+|I,X)}{\pi_{ref}(y^+|I,X)} - \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta^{(t)}(y^-|I,X)}{\pi_{ref}(y^-|I,X)}\right)
$$

这使得能够有针对性地微调统一设计模块，以偏好高 CTR 元素，同时提供关于哪些设计决策驱动性能改进的可解释反馈。

## 数据集和评估

### AutoPP1M 数据集

研究人员推出了AutoPP1M，这是迄今为止最大的商品海报数据集，包含从京东（JD.COM）收集的一百万张高质量海报。该数据集涵盖60多个商品类别，具有一致的1:1宽高比和最低800×800像素的分辨率。所有海报都经过严格的质量筛选，包括美学评估、模糊检测、水印去除和基于OCR的文本验证。

关键数据集组件包括：

- **生成标注：** 详细的视觉元素标注，包括商品蒙版、文本内容、文本边界框和使用最先进视觉模型生成的背景提示。
- **优化子集：** 包含50,000对比较，附带从超过一百万用户在10天在线实验中收集的真实世界点击率（CTR）反馈。
- **元素级偏好：** 针对背景、文本和布局组件的独特细粒度偏好评估。

### 性能指标

评估框架包括离线生成质量和在线性能优化：

**生成指标：**
- 整体质量：FID（Fréchet Inception Distance），CLIP-T（CLIP文本-图像相似度）
- 布局合理性：对齐度，重叠度，平均交并比（MIoU）
- 文本准确性：句子准确率，归一化编辑距离

**优化指标：**
- 相较于基线生成器的相对CTR提升
- 偏好预测任务中的奖励准确性
- 元素归因有效性

## 结果与发现

### 生成性能

AutoPP在所有评估指标上均取得了最先进的成果，显著优于现有的开源方法（P&R，PAID）和闭源基线（GPT-4o）。该系统展示了卓越的视觉质量，FID为60.71，CLIP-T为29.75，并通过改进对齐度（0.007）、减少重叠度（0.011）和更高的MIoU（0.256）展现了更好的布局合理性。

![定性比较显示AutoPP卓越的海报生成能力](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-2.jpeg)

*图2：不同生成方法之间的定性比较。AutoPP成功避免了其他方法中常见的商品被遮挡、文本模糊和文本生成错误等问题。*

在专门的文本渲染评估中，AutoPP达到了65.19%的句子准确率和12.94的归一化编辑距离，优于包括Glyph-byt5-v2和AnyText-v2在内的专用文本生成方法。该系统在渲染小尺寸中文字体时表现出特别的优势，具有高可读性。

![不同商品类别下的生成海报示例](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-3.jpeg)

*图3：AutoPP在不同类别下生成的各种商品海报，展示了始终如一的质量和美学吸引力，同时保持了商品的可见性和文本的清晰度。*

### 优化性能

优化能力带来了显著的商业影响，相较于未优化的生成器，相对点击率（CTR）提升了4.49%。这一性能显著超越了现有的CTR优化方法，如CG4CTR和CAIG，它们显示出负的相对CTR（分别为-2.15%和-1.29%），这突出表明它们仅优化背景元素的局限性。

![CTR优化结果](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-4.jpeg)

*图4：相对CTR提升比较。AutoPP实现了显著的正向提升，而现有方法则表现出负面性能，这表明了全面优化的重要性。*

通过消融研究验证了IDPO相对于标准DPO的有效性，IDPO实现了4.49%的相对CTR，而DPO为3.10%。这验证了元素隔离优化在从用户偏好中进行更精确和有效学习方面的优势。

### 技术创新

与全注意力机制相比，分解注意力机制在800×800分辨率下成功将计算开销降低了18%，在1024×1024分辨率下降低了24%，同时保持了生成质量。用于产品和文本控制的基于令牌的方法无需额外参数，与增加数十亿参数的基于ControlNet的方法形成了有利对比。

![跨语言生成能力](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21921v1/img-8.jpeg)

*图5：AutoPP的涌现跨语言能力，尽管主要在中文文本上训练，仍成功生成了英文、日文和韩文海报。*

AutoPP通过多宽高比生成能力和涌现的跨语言泛化能力展示了其多功能性，尽管主要在汉字上训练，仍成功渲染了英文、日文和韩文文本。

## 意义与影响

AutoPP代表着商业应用自动化内容创作领域的重大进步，其影响不仅限于电子商务，还广泛延伸到数字营销和创意产业。该系统通过CTR提升4.49%实现了可衡量的业务影响，证明了AI驱动营销优化的实际价值。

技术贡献，特别是统一设计方法和IDPO方法，提升了生成式AI和偏好学习的最新水平。统一设计模块克服了多阶段方法固有的不一致性，而IDPO则能够将性能提升精细归因于特定的设计元素——这种能力不仅限于海报生成，还可扩展到其他复杂的优化场景。

AutoPP1M的发布为研究社区提供了一个前所未有的资源，用于开发和评估下一代生成模型和偏好学习算法。该数据集的规模、质量以及带有真实世界性能反馈的独特元素级注释将加速自动化视觉内容创作领域的创新。

对于从业者而言，AutoPP使高质量营销设计变得大众化，赋能小企业通过AI驱动的内容创作工具与大型企业竞争。该系统的自动化能力消除了对专业设计技能的需求，同时通过数据驱动的洞察而非基于直觉的决策确保了性能优化。

这项工作为AI生成的营销内容建立了新的范式，超越了美学考量，直接优化业务指标。这种方法弥合了生成式AI研究与商业应用之间的鸿沟，为未来性能驱动内容创作系统的发展提供了模板。

abstract: Product posters blend striking visuals with informative text to highlight the product and capture customer attention. However, crafting appealing posters and manually optimizing them based on online performance is laborious and resource-consuming. To address this, we introduce AutoPP, an automated pipeline for product poster generation and optimization that eliminates the need for human intervention. abstract: Frozen Large Video Language Models (LVLMs) are increasingly employed in micro-video recommendation due to their strong multimodal understanding. However, their integration lacks systematic empirical evaluation: practitioners typically deploy LVLMs as fixed black-box feature extractors without systematically comparing alternative representation strategies. To address this gap, we present the first systematic empirical study along two key design dimensions: (i) integration strategies with ID embeddings, specifically replacement versus fusion, and (ii) feature extraction paradigms, comparing LVLM-generated captions with intermediate decoder hidden states. Extensive experiments on representative LVLMs reveal three key principles: (1) intermediate hidden states consistently outperform caption-based representations, as natural-language summarization inevitably discards fine-grained visual semantics crucial for recommendation; (2) ID embeddings capture irreplaceable collaborative signals, rendering fusion strictly superior to replacement; and (3) the effectiveness of intermediate decoder features varies significantly across layers. Guided by these insights, we propose the Dual Feature Fusion (DFF) Framework, a lightweight and plug-and-play approach that adaptively fuses multi-layer representations from frozen LVLMs with item ID embeddings. DFF achieves state-of-the-art performance on two real-world micro-video recommendation benchmarks, consistently outperforming strong baselines and providing a principled approach to integrating off-the-shelf large vision-language models into micro-video recommender systems.

abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) has recently achieved strong performance across diverse tasks, yet contextual biasing for named entities and hotwords under large vocabularies remains challenging. In this work, we propose a scalable two-stage framework that integrates hotword retrieval with LLM-ASR adaptation. First, we extend the Global-Local Contrastive Language-Audio pre-trained model (GLCLAP) to retrieve a compact top-k set of hotword candidates from a large vocabulary via robustness-aware data augmentation and fuzzy matching. Second, we inject the retrieved candidates as textual prompts into an LLM-ASR model and fine-tune it with Generative Rejection-Based Policy Optimization (GRPO), using a task-driven reward that jointly optimizes hotword recognition and overall transcription accuracy. Experiments on hotword-focused test sets show substantial keyword error rate (KER) reductions while maintaining sentence accuracy on general ASR benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for large-vocabulary contextual biasing.
title: Contextual Biasing for LLM-Based ASR with Hotword Retrieval and Reinforcement Learning
