abstract: In this paper, we present KG20C and KG20C-QA, two curated datasets for advancing question answering (QA) research on scholarly data. KG20C is a high-quality scholarly knowledge graph constructed from the Microsoft Academic Graph through targeted selection of venues, quality-based filtering, and schema definition. Although KG20C has been available online in non-peer-reviewed sources such as GitHub repository, this paper provides the first formal, peer-reviewed description of the dataset, including clear documentation of its construction and specifications. KG20C-QA is built upon KG20C to support QA tasks on scholarly data. We define a set of QA templates that convert graph triples into natural language question--answer pairs, producing a benchmark that can be used both with graph-based models such as knowledge graph embeddings and with text-based models such as large language models. We benchmark standard knowledge graph embedding methods on KG20C-QA, analyze performance across relation types, and provide reproducible evaluation protocols. By officially releasing these datasets with thorough documentation, we aim to contribute a reusable, extensible resource for the research community, enabling future work in QA, reasoning, and knowledge-driven applications in the scholarly domain. The full datasets will be released at https://github.com/tranhungnghiep/KG20C/ upon paper publication.

en.title: A Three-Level Alignment Framework for Large-Scale 3D Retrieval and Controlled 4D Generation
en.abstract: We introduce Uni4D, a unified framework for large scale open vocabulary 3D retrieval and controlled 4D generation based on structured three level alignment across text, 3D models, and image modalities. Built upon the Align3D 130 dataset, Uni4D employs a 3D text multi head attention and search model to optimize text to 3D retrieval through improved semantic alignment. The framework further strengthens cross modal alignment through three components: precise text to 3D retrieval, multi view 3D to image alignment, and image to text alignment for generating temporally consistent 4D assets. Experimental results demonstrate that Uni4D achieves high quality 3D retrieval and controllable 4D generation, advancing dynamic multimodal understanding and practical applications.

summary.summary: Uni4D presents a three-level alignment framework bridging text, 3D models, and images, designed to improve large-scale 3D retrieval and enable controlled 4D generation. The framework achieves an 81.2% top-1 retrieval accuracy on expansive, unclustered 3D datasets and demonstrates superior results in 4D generation, scoring a 92.0 Generated 3D Quality Score and an 0.88 average CLIP similarity, through a novel dataset and a multi-head attention search model.
originalProblem: Traditional text-to-3D retrieval methods struggle with efficiency and accuracy on large, sparse datasets, failing to capture deep semantic relationships.
Generating controlled, high-quality 4D (spatiotemporal) content from natural language commands remains challenging due to the complexity of 4D data and limited cross-modal alignment.
A significant performance gap exists between the maturity of 2D vision tasks and text-to-3D asset alignment and generation.
solution: Develops Uni4D, a framework employing a three-level alignment strategy (text, 3D, image) to bridge semantic gaps for robust cross-modal understanding.
Introduces the 3D-Text Multi-head Attention and Search (ATMS) model, optimized with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based reinforcement learning, to enhance large-scale text-to-3D retrieval.
Creates the Align3D-130 dataset, a large-scale multimodal text-to-3D resource with over 1.3 million GPT-4o generated descriptions, to serve as a robust training foundation.
keyInsights: MCTS-based reinforcement learning significantly optimizes the training of multi-head attention models for large-scale 3D-text retrieval in sparse, high-dimensional spaces.
A holistic three-level alignment framework (text-3D-image) is critical for achieving fine-grained control and temporal consistency in 4D asset generation.
Leveraging advanced large language models like GPT-4o can effectively generate high-quality, semantically rich descriptions to create large-scale 3D datasets, overcoming data annotation challenges.
results: The ATMS model achieved an 81.2% top-1 retrieval accuracy for text-to-3D tasks on large, unclustered datasets, substantially outperforming prior methods like Uni3D and OpenAlign (0.1% each).
Uni4D demonstrated superior 4D generation quality, evidenced by GPT-4o evaluations with a 92.0 Generated 3D Quality Score and an 87.7 Text Alignment Score.
Generated 4D assets showed stronger semantic alignment with text prompts, achieving an average CLIP similarity score of 0.88, surpassing other state-of-the-art 4D generation models.

en.overview:
## Introduction

The field of computer vision has witnessed remarkable advances in 2D image understanding, but the extension to 3D and temporal domains remains challenging. Current 3D retrieval systems struggle with scalability and semantic understanding, while 4D generation - creating dynamic 3D content over time - lacks precise control mechanisms. This paper introduces Uni4D, a comprehensive framework that addresses these limitations through a three-level alignment strategy connecting text, 3D models, and images to enable controlled 4D asset generation.

![Uni4D Framework Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: The Uni4D framework pipeline showing the three-level alignment process from text input through 3D retrieval, multi-view image generation, and final 4D asset creation*

## Dataset Construction and Data Foundation

A critical foundation of Uni4D is the creation of Align3D-130, a large-scale multimodal dataset comprising over 1.3 million text-3D model pairs. The dataset was constructed by integrating content from multiple public repositories including Objaverse-XL, ShapeNet, and 3D-FUTURE. A key innovation was employing GPT-4o to generate semantically rich text descriptions for 3D models that originally lacked annotations.

![Align3D-130 Dataset Composition](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: Composition of the Align3D-130 dataset showing integration from multiple 3D model repositories*

The dataset construction process involved several critical steps:
- **Data cleaning and standardization**: Removing redundancies, unifying coordinate systems, and optimizing model quality
- **GPU-accelerated conversion**: Processing 3D assets into point cloud representations
- **Multi-round generation strategy**: Using GPT-4o with human review to ensure high-quality text descriptions
- **Self-supervised learning framework**: Training without explicit labels using contrastive learning where correct text-3D pairs serve as positive samples

## ATMS Model and Reinforcement Learning Optimization

The core of Uni4D's text-to-3D retrieval capability is the ATMS (3D-Text Multi-head Attention & Search) model. This dual-encoder architecture builds upon existing text encoders like CLIP and 3D encoders like Uni3D, but incorporates multi-head self-attention layers and attention pooling to better handle the sparse, high-dimensional nature of 3D data.

![ATMS Training with MCTS](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: ATMS model training enhanced by Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) reinforcement learning strategy*

A unique aspect of ATMS training is the integration of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based reinforcement learning. The training process is formulated as an environment where:

- **State**: Current learning parameters (learning rate, epoch, temperature) and performance metrics
- **Actions**: Adjusting learning rate, temperature, or maintaining current settings
- **Reward function**: Prioritizes validation accuracy improvements while penalizing overfitting

The MCTS agent uses the Upper Confidence Bound (UCT) formula to balance exploration and exploitation:

$$
UCT(s,a) = Q(s,a) + C \sqrt{\frac{\ln N(s)}{N(s,a)}}
$$

where $Q(s,a)$ is the average reward, $N(s)$ is the visit count for state $s$, $N(s,a)$ is the visit count for action $a$ in state $s$, and $C$ is the exploration constant.

## Three-Level Alignment Framework

The heart of Uni4D's approach is a structured three-level alignment across text, 3D models, and images. This alignment is governed by a total loss function:

$$
S_{total} = \alpha S_{text-3D} + \beta S_{3D-image} + \gamma S_{image-text}
$$

where $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ are weighting parameters for each alignment level.

### Text-to-3D Alignment
The first level uses the ATMS model to retrieve relevant 3D assets. Text inputs are tokenized to extract key terms, and ATMS computes embeddings to find the top-k most similar 3D models using cosine similarity.

### 3D-to-Image Alignment
Retrieved 3D models are rendered from multiple viewpoints using Blender to create a visual bridge between 3D geometry and image modality. This multi-view rendering captures different perspectives of the 3D object.

### Image-to-Text Alignment
The CrOSSMA (Cross-modal Spatial Semantic Multimodal Alignment) model aligns rendered images with the original text input using cross-attention mechanisms. CLIP-encoded text embeddings serve as queries, while CLIP-encoded image embeddings act as keys and values, with the output processed through a Feed-Forward Network.

## Experimental Results and Performance

Uni4D was evaluated on three primary tasks: text-to-3D retrieval, 4D alignment assessment, and 4D asset generation quality.

### Text-to-3D Retrieval Performance

![Retrieval Performance Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-4.jpeg)
*Figure 4: Comparison of retrieval performance between ATMS and existing methods across different top-k values*

The ATMS model achieved significant improvements over existing methods:
- **Top-1 accuracy**: 81.2% on both clustered and randomly shuffled datasets
- **Comparison**: Dramatically outperformed Uni3D (50.1% clustered, 0.1% random) and OpenAlign (48.5% clustered, 0.1% random)
- **Scalability**: Maintained high performance even with unclustered, large-scale data where traditional k-NN methods failed

### 4D Generation Quality Assessment

![4D Generation Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-3.jpeg)
*Figure 5: Visual comparison of 4D generation results for "pink teddy bear dancing" across different methods*

Using GPT-4o as an objective evaluator, Uni4D achieved superior scores across multiple criteria:
- **Text Alignment Score (TA-Score)**: 87.7 vs. DreamGaussian4D (85.5), 4D-fy (80.4), stag4D (70.3)
- **Generated 3D Quality Score (GQ-Score)**: 92.0 vs. 4D-fy (89.1), DreamGaussian4D (86.2), stag4D (84.6)
- **Temporal Logic Movement Score (TM-Score)**: 82.5 vs. 4D-fy (78.9), DreamGaussian4D (75.0), stag4D (65.6)

### CLIP Score Evaluation

For text-to-4D similarity assessment, Uni4D achieved the highest average CLIP similarity score of 0.88 across various dynamic object prompts, compared to DreamGaussian4D (0.83), 4D-fy (0.79), and stag4D (0.78).

![4D Generation Examples](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-5.jpeg)
*Figure 6: Examples of 4D generation results for various objects with dynamic actions*

## Ablation Studies and Component Analysis

Comprehensive ablation studies validated the importance of each framework component:

### Reinforcement Learning Impact
Removing the MCTS-based RL strategy caused ATMS top-1 retrieval accuracy to drop from 81.2% to 34.5%, demonstrating the critical role of adaptive hyperparameter optimization.

### Three-Level Alignment Necessity
Ablation experiments showed that removing any component of the three-level alignment resulted in significant degradation:

![Alignment Component Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-6.jpeg)
*Figure 7: Impact of different alignment misalignments on 4D generation quality*

- **Text-3D misalignment**: Led to semantic inconsistencies between generated models and text descriptions
- **Image-3D misalignment**: Caused uncontrollable 4D generation with chaotic outputs  
- **Text-image misalignment**: Resulted in loss of temporal information in 4D assets

## Significance and Future Directions

Uni4D represents a significant advancement in bridging the gap between 2D and 3D/4D computer vision. The framework's contributions span multiple domains:

**Technical Innovations**: The ATMS model with MCTS optimization provides a scalable solution for large-scale 3D retrieval, while the three-level alignment framework enables unprecedented control over 4D generation.

**Dataset Contribution**: Align3D-130 provides a valuable resource for future research in multimodal 3D understanding, with high-quality text descriptions generated through advanced language models.

**Application Potential**: The framework has immediate applications in robotics, content creation, gaming, and virtual/augmented reality, where controlled generation of dynamic 3D content from natural language descriptions is crucial.

**Research Impact**: By demonstrating robust cross-modal alignment across heterogeneous data types, Uni4D contributes to the broader goal of creating more generalizable multimodal AI systems.

While the authors acknowledge computational efficiency limitations, the framework establishes a strong foundation for future work in dynamic multimodal understanding and generation, potentially leading to more intuitive human-computer interfaces and advanced AI agents capable of sophisticated spatiotemporal reasoning.

zh.title: 一个用于大规模三维检索和受控四维生成的三级对齐框架
zh.abstract: 我们介绍了 Uni4D，这是一个统一框架，用于大规模开放词汇3D检索和受控4D生成。该框架基于文本、3D模型和图像模态之间结构化的三级对齐。Uni4D 以 Align3D 130 数据集为基础，采用3D文本多头注意力与搜索模型，通过改进的语义对齐来优化文本到3D检索。该框架通过三个组件进一步加强了跨模态对齐：精确的文本到3D检索、多视角3D到图像对齐以及图像到文本对齐，以生成时间一致的4D资产。实验结果表明，Uni4D 实现了高质量的3D检索和可控的4D生成，推动了动态多模态理解和实际应用的发展。

summary.summary: Uni4D提出了一个三级对齐框架，连接文本、3D模型和图像，旨在改进大规模3D检索并实现受控的4D生成。该框架在庞大、非聚类的3D数据集上实现了81.2%的top-1检索准确率，并通过新颖的数据集和多头注意力搜索模型，在4D生成方面展示了卓越的成果，获得了92.0的生成3D质量分数和0.88的平均CLIP相似度。
originalProblem: 传统的文本到3D检索方法在大型、稀疏数据集上难以实现效率和准确性，无法捕捉深层语义关系。
由于4D数据的复杂性和有限的跨模态对齐，从自然语言命令生成受控、高质量的4D（时空）内容仍然具有挑战性。
2D视觉任务的成熟度与文本到3D资产的对齐和生成之间存在显著的性能差距。
solution: 开发了Uni4D，一个采用三级对齐策略（文本、3D、图像）的框架，以弥合语义鸿沟，实现稳健的跨模态理解。
引入了3D-文本多头注意力与搜索（ATMS）模型，并用基于蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）的强化学习进行优化，以增强大规模文本到3D检索。
创建了Align3D-130数据集，一个大规模多模态文本到3D资源，包含超过130万条GPT-4o生成的描述，作为稳健的训练基础。
keyInsights: 基于MCTS的强化学习显著优化了多头注意力模型在稀疏、高维空间中进行大规模3D-文本检索的训练。
一个整体的三级对齐框架（文本-3D-图像）对于在4D资产生成中实现精细控制和时间一致性至关重要。
利用GPT-4o等先进的大型语言模型可以有效生成高质量、语义丰富的描述，以创建大规模3D数据集，克服数据标注挑战。
results: ATMS模型在大型、非聚类数据集上的文本到3D任务中实现了81.2%的top-1检索准确率，显著优于Uni3D和OpenAlign等现有方法（均为0.1%）。
Uni4D展示了卓越的4D生成质量，通过GPT-4o评估证明，获得了92.0的生成3D质量分数和87.7的文本对齐分数。
生成的4D资产与文本提示显示出更强的语义对齐，实现了0.88的平均CLIP相似度分数，超越了其他最先进的4D生成模型。

zh.overview:
## 引言

计算机视觉领域在二维图像理解方面取得了显著进展，但扩展到三维和时间域仍然充满挑战。当前的3D检索系统在可扩展性和语义理解方面存在困难，而4D生成——即随着时间创建动态3D内容——则缺乏精确的控制机制。本文介绍了Uni4D，一个全面的框架，通过连接文本、3D模型和图像的三级对齐策略来解决这些局限性，从而实现受控的4D资产生成。

![Uni4D 框架概览](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：Uni4D 框架流程图，展示了从文本输入到3D检索、多视角图像生成和最终4D资产创建的三级对齐过程*

## 数据集构建与数据基础

Uni4D 的一个关键基础是创建了 Align3D-130，这是一个包含超过130万对文本-3D模型的大规模多模态数据集。该数据集通过整合来自多个公共存储库的内容构建而成，包括 Objaverse-XL、ShapeNet 和 3D-FUTURE。一项关键创新是利用 GPT-4o 为最初缺乏注释的3D模型生成语义丰富的文本描述。

![Align3D-130 数据集组成](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：Align3D-130 数据集的组成，显示了来自多个3D模型存储库的整合*

数据集构建过程涉及几个关键步骤：
- **数据清洗和标准化**：去除冗余、统一坐标系并优化模型质量
- **GPU加速转换**：将3D资产处理成点云表示
- **多轮生成策略**：使用 GPT-4o 并进行人工审查，以确保高质量的文本描述
- **自监督学习框架**：使用对比学习在没有明确标签的情况下进行训练，其中正确的文本-3D对作为正样本

## ATMS 模型与强化学习优化

Uni4D 的文本到3D检索能力的核心是 ATMS（3D-Text Multi-head Attention & Search）模型。这种双编码器架构建立在现有文本编码器（如 CLIP）和3D编码器（如 Uni3D）之上，但引入了多头自注意力层和注意力池化，以更好地处理3D数据稀疏、高维的特性。

![ATMS 与 MCTS 训练](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图3：通过蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）强化学习策略增强的ATMS模型训练*

ATMS 训练的一个独特之处是集成了基于蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）的强化学习。训练过程被表述为一个环境，其中：

- **状态**：当前的学习参数（学习率、周期、温度）和性能指标
- **动作**：调整学习率、温度或保持当前设置
- **奖励函数**：优先考虑验证准确性提高，同时惩罚过拟合

MCTS 智能体使用上限置信区间（UCT）公式来平衡探索和利用：

$$
UCT(s,a) = Q(s,a) + C \sqrt{\frac{\ln N(s)}{N(s,a)}}
$$

其中 $Q(s,a)$ 是平均奖励，$N(s)$ 是状态 $s$ 的访问次数，$N(s,a)$ 是在状态 $s$ 下动作 $a$ 的访问次数，$C$ 是探索常数。

## 三级对齐框架

Uni4D 方法的核心是文本、3D模型和图像之间的结构化三级对齐。这种对齐由一个总损失函数控制：

$$
S_{total} = \alpha S_{text-3D} + \beta S_{3D-image} + \gamma S_{image-text}
$$

其中 $\alpha$、$\beta$ 和 $\gamma$ 是每个对齐级别的权重参数。

### 文本到 3D 对齐
第一层使用 ATMS 模型检索相关的 3D 资产。文本输入被标记化以提取关键词，ATMS 计算嵌入，使用余弦相似度找到最相似的 top-k 个 3D 模型。

### 3D 到图像对齐
检索到的 3D 模型使用 Blender 从多个视角渲染，以在 3D 几何和图像模态之间建立视觉桥梁。这种多视角渲染捕捉了 3D 对象的不同视角。

### 图像到文本对齐
CrOSSMA（跨模态空间语义多模态对齐）模型使用交叉注意力机制将渲染图像与原始文本输入对齐。CLIP 编码的文本嵌入作为查询，而 CLIP 编码的图像嵌入作为键和值，输出通过前馈网络处理。

## 实验结果与性能

Uni4D 在三个主要任务上进行了评估：文本到 3D 检索、4D 对齐评估和 4D 资产生成质量。

### 文本到 3D 检索性能

![Retrieval Performance Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-4.jpeg)
*图 4：ATMS 与现有方法在不同 top-k 值下的检索性能比较*

ATMS 模型在现有方法的基础上取得了显著改进：
- **Top-1 准确率**：在聚类和随机打乱的数据集上均达到 81.2%
- **比较**：显著优于 Uni3D（聚类 50.1%，随机 0.1%）和 OpenAlign（聚类 48.5%，随机 0.1%）
- **可扩展性**：即使在传统 k-NN 方法失效的未聚类、大规模数据下，也保持了高性能

### 4D 生成质量评估

![4D Generation Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-3.jpeg)
*图 5：针对“跳舞的粉色泰迪熊”不同方法 4D 生成结果的视觉比较*

使用 GPT-4o 作为客观评估器，Uni4D 在多项标准上取得了优异的分数：
- **文本对齐分数 (TA-Score)**：87.7 对比 DreamGaussian4D (85.5)、4D-fy (80.4)、stag4D (70.3)
- **生成 3D 质量分数 (GQ-Score)**：92.0 对比 4D-fy (89.1)、DreamGaussian4D (86.2)、stag4D (84.6)
- **时间逻辑运动分数 (TM-Score)**：82.5 对比 4D-fy (78.9)、DreamGaussian4D (75.0)、stag4D (65.6)

### CLIP 分数评估

在文本到 4D 相似度评估方面，Uni4D 在各种动态对象提示词上达到了最高的平均 CLIP 相似度分数 0.88，而 DreamGaussian4D 为 0.83，4D-fy 为 0.79，stag4D 为 0.78。

![4D Generation Examples](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-5.jpeg)
*图 6：不同对象动态动作的 4D 生成结果示例*

## 消融研究与组件分析

全面的消融研究验证了每个框架组件的重要性：

### 强化学习影响
移除基于 MCTS 的强化学习策略导致 ATMS 的 top-1 检索准确率从 81.2% 下降到 34.5%，这表明自适应超参数优化的关键作用。

### 三层对齐的必要性
消融实验表明，移除三层对齐中的任何一个组件都会导致显著的性能下降：

![Alignment Component Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.22294v1/img-6.jpeg)
*图 7：不同对齐失误对 4D 生成质量的影响*

- **文本-3D 对齐失误**：导致生成模型与文本描述之间存在语义不一致
- **图像-3D 对齐失误**：导致不可控的 4D 生成，产生混乱的输出
- **文本-图像 对齐失误**：导致 4D 资产中时间信息的丢失

## 意义与未来方向

Uni4D 代表着在弥合 2D 和 3D/4D 计算机视觉之间鸿沟方面的一项重大进展。该框架的贡献涵盖多个领域：

**技术创新**: 采用MCTS优化的ATMS模型为大规模3D检索提供了可扩展的解决方案，而三级对齐框架则实现了对4D生成前所未有的控制。

**数据集贡献**: Align3D-130通过先进语言模型生成的高质量文本描述，为未来多模态3D理解研究提供了宝贵的资源。

**应用潜力**: 该框架在机器人技术、内容创作、游戏以及虚拟/增强现实领域具有即时应用，在这些领域，根据自然语言描述对动态3D内容进行受控生成至关重要。

**研究影响**: 通过展示跨异构数据类型的鲁棒跨模态对齐，Uni4D为创建更具通用性的多模态AI系统的宏伟目标做出了贡献。

尽管作者承认计算效率存在局限性，但该框架为未来动态多模态理解和生成工作奠定了坚实基础，有望带来更直观的人机界面和能够进行复杂时空推理的高级AI代理。

abstract: We introduce Uni4D, a unified framework for large scale open vocabulary 3D retrieval and controlled 4D generation based on structured three level alignment across text, 3D models, and image modalities. Built upon the Align3D 130 dataset, Uni4D employs a 3D text multi head attention and search model to optimize text to 3D retrieval through improved semantic alignment. The framework further strengthens cross modal alignment through three components: precise text to 3D retrieval, multi view 3D to image alignment, and image to text alignment for generating temporally consistent 4D assets. Experimental results demonstrate that Uni4D achieves high quality 3D retrieval and controllable 4D generation, advancing dynamic multimodal understanding and practical applications.
title: A Three-Level Alignment Framework for Large-Scale 3D Retrieval and Controlled 4D Generation

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (RACG) is increasingly adopted to enhance Large Language Models for software development, yet its security implications remain dangerously underexplored. This paper conducts the first systematic exploration of a critical and stealthy threat: backdoor attacks targeting the retriever component, which represents a significant supply-chain vulnerability. It is infeasible to assess this threat realistically, as existing attack methods are either too ineffective to pose a real danger or are easily detected by state-of-the-art defense mechanisms spanning both latent-space analysis and token-level inspection, which achieve consistently high detection rates. To overcome this barrier and enable a realistic analysis, we first developed VenomRACG, a new class of potent and stealthy attack that serves as a vehicle for our investigation. Its design makes poisoned samples statistically indistinguishable from benign code, allowing the attack to consistently maintain low detectability across all evaluated defense mechanisms. Armed with this capability, our exploration reveals a severe vulnerability: by injecting vulnerable code equivalent to only 0.05% of the entire knowledge base size, an attacker can successfully manipulate the backdoored retriever to rank the vulnerable code in its top-5 results in 51.29% of cases. This translates to severe downstream harm, causing models like GPT-4o to generate vulnerable code in over 40% of targeted scenarios, while leaving the system's general performance intact. Our findings establish that retriever backdooring is not a theoretical concern but a practical threat to the software development ecosystem that current defenses are blind to, highlighting the urgent need for robust security measures.

abstract: Item-to-Item (I2I) recommendation models are widely used in real-world systems due to their scalability, real-time capabilities, and high recommendation quality. Research to enhance I2I performance focuses on two directions: 1) model-centric approaches, which adopt deeper architectures but risk increased computational costs and deployment complexity, and 2) data-centric methods, which refine training data without altering models, offering cost-effectiveness but struggling with data sparsity and noise. To address these challenges, we propose LLM-I2I, a data-centric framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to mitigate data quality issues. LLM-I2I includes (1) an LLM-based generator that synthesizes user-item interactions for long-tail items, alleviating data sparsity, and (2) an LLM-based discriminator that filters noisy interactions from real and synthetic data. The refined data is then fused to train I2I models. Evaluated on industry (AEDS) and academic (ARD) datasets, LLM-I2I consistently improves recommendation accuracy, particularly for long-tail items. Deployed on a large-scale cross-border e-commerce platform, it boosts recall number (RN) by 6.02% and gross merchandise value (GMV) by 1.22% over existing I2I models. This work highlights the potential of LLMs in enhancing data-centric recommendation systems without modifying model architectures.
title: LLM-I2I: Boost Your Small Item2Item Recommendation Model with Large Language Model

abstract: Generative recommendation models often struggle with two key challenges: (1) the superficial integration of collaborative signals, and (2) the decoupled fusion of multimodal features. These limitations hinder the creation of a truly holistic item representation. To overcome this, we propose CEMG, a novel Collaborative-Enhaned Multimodal Generative Recommendation framework. Our approach features a Multimodal Fusion Layer that dynamically integrates visual and textual features under the guidance of collaborative signals. Subsequently, a Unified Modality Tokenization stage employs a Residual Quantization VAE (RQ-VAE) to convert this fused representation into discrete semantic codes. Finally, in the End-to-End Generative Recommendation stage, a large language model is fine-tuned to autoregressively generate these item codes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CEMG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

en.title: Selective LLM-Guided Regularization for Enhancing Recommendation Models
en.abstract: Large language models provide rich semantic priors and strong reasoning capabilities, making them promising auxiliary signals for recommendation. However, prevailing approaches either deploy LLMs as standalone recommender or apply global knowledge distillation, both of which suffer from inherent drawbacks. Standalone LLM recommender are costly, biased, and unreliable across large regions of the user item space, while global distillation forces the downstream model to imitate LLM predictions even when such guidance is inaccurate. Meanwhile, recent studies show that LLMs excel particularly in re-ranking and challenging scenarios, rather than uniformly across all this http URL introduce Selective LLM Guided Regularization, a model-agnostic and computation efficient framework that activates LLM based pairwise ranking supervision only when a trainable gating mechanism informing by user history length, item popularity, and model uncertainty predicts the LLM to be reliable. All LLM scoring is performed offline, transferring knowledge without increasing inference cost. Experiments across multiple datasets show that this selective strategy consistently improves overall accuracy and yields substantial gains in cold start and long tail regimes, outperforming global distillation baselines.

summary.summary: The S-LLMR framework integrates Large Language Model (LLM) knowledge into traditional recommender models through a selective, reliability-aware mechanism. This approach utilizes a learnable gating function to apply LLM-guided pairwise ranking regularization, leading to consistent AUC improvements across various backbones and datasets, particularly enhancing performance in cold-start and long-tail scenarios.
originalProblem: Traditional recommender systems exhibit degraded performance in sparse data regimes, such as cold-start users and long-tail items.
Standalone Large Language Models (LLMs) for recommendation are computationally intensive, prone to biases, and can produce unreliable predictions.

Existing global knowledge distillation methods from LLMs transfer knowledge uniformly, often introducing noise or inaccuracies when LLM signals are unreliable, potentially hindering overall performance.
solution: An offline process generates LLM soft rankings for user-item pairs, augmented with synthetic data to address cold-start and long-tail scenarios.
A learnable gating mechanism dynamically determines when LLM supervision should be activated, based on cold-start indicators, long-tail indicators, and the base recommender model's uncertainty.
An LLM-guided pairwise ranking regularizer encourages the base model to align with LLM-implied relative item orderings, applied selectively via the gating mechanism.
keyInsights: LLM guidance is not universally reliable but proves most beneficial when selectively applied in contexts where traditional recommender signals are weak, such as sparse data regimes.

A learnable gating mechanism is critical for effective knowledge transfer, as it allows the model to judiciously leverage LLM strengths while mitigating the risks of injecting noisy or detrimental global LLM supervision.
Pairwise ranking losses are more effective for transferring LLM knowledge than pointwise methods, as they focus on relative item orderings which LLMs excel at.
results: S-LLMR consistently achieved superior AUC scores across six diverse recommendation backbones (e.g., DeepFM, DCNv2) and three Amazon datasets, outperforming both non-LLM baselines and global LLM-assisted methods.
The framework delivered disproportionately greater performance gains in cold-start user and long-tail item scenarios, confirming its targeted effectiveness in addressing data sparsity challenges.
Ablation studies demonstrated that both the selective gating mechanism and the pairwise ranking loss are essential components for achieving consistent and substantial performance improvements.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Recommender systems face persistent challenges in data-sparse environments, particularly with cold-start users and long-tail items where traditional collaborative filtering approaches struggle. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer rich semantic knowledge that could address these limitations, current integration strategies either deploy LLMs directly as recommenders (leading to high computational costs and reliability issues) or apply global knowledge distillation that uniformly transfers LLM predictions without considering their contextual reliability.

![S-LLMR Framework Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21526v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: Overview of the S-LLMR framework showing the offline LLM scoring phase and the training phase with selective gating mechanism.*

The paper "Selective LLM-Guided Regularization for Enhancing Recommendation Models" introduces S-LLMR, a model-agnostic framework that selectively leverages LLM knowledge through a learnable gating mechanism. This approach addresses the fundamental issue that LLM signals are contextually reliable rather than universally trustworthy, providing targeted guidance only when empirically beneficial.

## Core Methodology

S-LLMR operates through three interconnected components that work together to selectively integrate LLM knowledge into traditional recommendation models.

### LLM-Generated Soft Rankings

The framework begins with an offline phase where LLM knowledge is extracted and stored. For each user, the system constructs textual summaries of their recent interaction history (typically the last 10 interactions) and queries an LLM (GPT-4o-mini in the experiments) to generate soft relevance scores for candidate items. These scores $s_{u,i}^{LLM} \in [0,1]$ represent the LLM's assessment of how well each item matches the user's preferences.

To specifically address sparse data scenarios, the system creates synthetic supervision data:
- **Cold-start augmentation**: Users with minimal interaction histories (≤3 interactions) are paired with diverse sampled items
- **Long-tail augmentation**: Items in the lowest 10% of popularity are paired with sampled users

This targeted data generation ensures LLM supervision is available precisely where traditional models are weakest.

### Selective Gating Mechanism

The core innovation lies in the learnable gating mechanism that determines when LLM supervision should be activated. For each user-item pair $(u,i)$, three reliability signals are computed:

1. **Cold-start indicator**: $Cold(u) = 1$ if user $u$ has fewer than $\tau_u$ interactions, 0 otherwise
2. **Long-tail indicator**: $Tail(i) = 1$ if item $i$ falls within the bottom $\tau_i$ popularity percentile, 0 otherwise  
3. **Model uncertainty**: $q_{u,i}$, a continuous score normalized to [0,1] derived from the base recommender's predictive confidence

These signals are combined into a feature vector $z_{u,i} = [Cold(u), Tail(i), q_{u,i}]$ and fed into a single-layer gating network:

$$
\alpha_{u,i} = \sigma(w^T z_{u,i} + b)
$$

The gate produces values between 0 and 1, scaling the contribution of LLM supervision. The gating parameters are learned jointly with the base recommender through backpropagation, enabling automatic identification of contexts where LLM guidance is beneficial.

### LLM-Guided Pairwise Ranking Regularizer

Rather than attempting to match absolute LLM scores, S-LLMR focuses on preserving relative orderings through a pairwise ranking loss. When the LLM indicates $s_{u,i}^{LLM} > s_{u,j}^{LLM}$, the base recommender is encouraged to predict $s_{u,i} > s_{u,j}$ with margin $m$:

$$
L_{LLM} = \sum_{(u,i,j) \in P} \alpha_{u,i,j} \cdot \max(0, m - (s_{u,i} - s_{u,j}))
$$

where $P$ represents user-consistent ordered pairs and $\alpha_{u,i,j} = 0.5 \cdot (\alpha_{u,i} + \alpha_{u,j})$ is the averaged gating weight. The final training objective combines the base recommender loss with the LLM regularization:

$$
L = L_{rec} + \lambda L_{LLM}
$$

## Experimental Results and Key Findings

The experimental evaluation demonstrates S-LLMR's effectiveness across six diverse recommendation backbones (DeepFM, xDeepFM, AutoInt, DCNv1, DCNv2, DIN) and three Amazon datasets (Sports & Outdoors, Beauty, Toys & Games).

### Performance Across Different Scenarios

S-LLMR consistently achieved the highest AUC scores across all tested configurations, with particularly notable improvements in challenging scenarios:

![Performance Gains by Model and Scenario](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21526v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: AUC gains achieved by S-LLMR across different model backbones, showing overall gains and specific improvements for cold-start and long-tail scenarios.*

- **Cold-start users**: Gains of 0.029-0.051 AUC across different models
- **Long-tail items**: Improvements of 0.034-0.056 AUC
- **Overall performance**: Consistent improvements of 0.008-0.019 AUC

The results reveal that S-LLMR delivers disproportionately large benefits in sparse data regimes, directly confirming the hypothesis that selective gating activates LLM guidance where collaborative filtering signals are weakest.

### Ablation Study Insights

Critical ablation experiments validated the necessity of both core components:

1. **Gated vs. Global Regularization**: Applying LLM supervision globally without gating often degraded performance, particularly for long-tail accuracy, providing strong evidence against uniform knowledge distillation approaches.

2. **Pairwise vs. Pointwise Supervision**: Replacing pairwise ranking with pointwise supervision (BCE/MSE) failed to yield meaningful improvements, confirming that preserving relative orderings is more effective than matching absolute scores.

## Significance and Contributions

S-LLMR represents a paradigm shift from unconditional knowledge transfer to reliability-aware integration. The framework's key contributions include:

**Targeted Sparsity Resolution**: By selectively activating LLM guidance in cold-start and long-tail scenarios, S-LLMR directly addresses fundamental weaknesses in traditional collaborative filtering while preserving model performance in dense regions.

**Model-Agnostic Design**: The framework's compatibility with diverse recommendation architectures, combined with offline LLM processing that introduces no inference overhead, makes it highly practical for real-world deployment.

**Empirical Validation of Contextual Reliability**: The comprehensive experiments provide strong evidence that LLM signals are contextually rather than universally reliable, establishing the need for selective integration strategies.

**Novel Regularization Paradigm**: The introduction of learnable, context-dependent LLM regularization opens new directions for incorporating auxiliary knowledge from powerful but imperfect models, moving beyond simple loss matching to sophisticated guidance mechanisms.

The work demonstrates that effective LLM integration in recommendation requires nuanced approaches that respect both the strengths and limitations of these powerful models, providing a foundation for more robust and intelligent recommendation systems.

zh.title: 选择性大语言模型引导正则化以增强推荐模型
zh.abstract:
大型语言模型（LLM）提供了丰富的语义先验和强大的推理能力，使其成为推荐系统中很有前景的辅助信号。然而，目前主流的方法要么将LLM作为独立的推荐器，要么应用全局知识蒸馏，这两种方法都存在固有的缺点。独立的LLM推荐器在用户-物品空间的许多区域中成本高昂、存在偏差且不可靠，而全局蒸馏则强制下游模型模仿LLM的预测，即使这种指导不准确。同时，最新研究表明，LLM在重排序和具有挑战性的场景中表现尤为出色，而非在所有情况下都表现一致。

为此，我们引入了“选择性LLM引导正则化”（Selective LLM Guided Regularization），这是一个模型无关且计算高效的框架。它仅在由用户历史长度、物品流行度和模型不确定性指导的可训练门控机制预测LLM可靠时，才激活基于LLM的成对排序监督。所有LLM评分均离线完成，在不增加推理成本的情况下实现了知识转移。在多个数据集上的实验表明，这种选择性策略持续提高了整体准确性，并在冷启动和长尾场景中获得了显著提升，优于全局蒸馏基线方法。

summary.summary: S-LLMR框架通过一种选择性、可靠性感知的机制，将大型语言模型（LLM）知识整合到传统推荐模型中。该方法利用可学习的门控函数来应用LLM引导的成对排序正则化，从而在各种骨干网络和数据集上持续改进AUC，特别是在冷启动和长尾场景中显著提升了性能。
originalProblem: 传统推荐系统在数据稀疏的情况下（例如冷启动用户和长尾商品）性能下降。
用于推荐的独立大型语言模型（LLM）计算密集、容易产生偏差，并可能生成不可靠的预测。
现有的LLM全局知识蒸馏方法统一传输知识，当LLM信号不可靠时，常常引入噪声或不准确性，可能阻碍整体性能。
solution: 一个离线过程生成用户-商品对的LLM软排序，并辅以合成数据来解决冷启动和长尾场景。
一个可学习的门控机制根据冷启动指标、长尾指标和基础推荐模型的不确定性，动态决定何时激活LLM监督。
一个LLM引导的成对排序正则化器鼓励基础模型与LLM隐含的相对商品排序保持一致，并通过门控机制选择性地应用。
keyInsights: LLM指导并非普遍可靠，但在传统推荐信号较弱的场景（如稀疏数据情境）中选择性应用时，其效益最大。
可学习的门控机制对于有效的知识迁移至关重要，因为它允许模型审慎地利用LLM的优势，同时减轻注入噪声或有害的全局LLM监督的风险。
成对排序损失比逐点方法更有效地传递LLM知识，因为它们专注于LLM擅长的相对商品排序。
results: S-LLMR在六种不同的推荐骨干网络（例如DeepFM、DCNv2）和三个亚马逊数据集上持续获得了更高的AUC分数，优于非LLM基线和全局LLM辅助方法。
该框架在冷启动用户和长尾商品场景中带来了不成比例的更大性能提升，证实了其在解决数据稀疏性挑战方面的目标有效性。
消融研究表明，选择性门控机制和成对排序损失都是实现持续显著性能改进的必要组成部分。

zh.overview:
## 引言

推荐系统在数据稀疏环境中面临着持续的挑战，尤其是在冷启动用户和长尾物品方面，传统协同过滤方法举步维艰。尽管大型语言模型（LLM）提供了丰富的语义知识，可以解决这些局限性，但当前的集成策略要么直接将LLM部署为推荐器（导致高计算成本和可靠性问题），要么应用全局知识蒸馏，统一传输LLM预测，而不考虑其上下文可靠性。

![S-LLMR 框架概览](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21526v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：S-LLMR 框架概览，展示了离线LLM评分阶段和带有选择性门控机制的训练阶段。*

论文《Selective LLM-Guided Regularization for Enhancing Recommendation Models》（S-LLMR：增强推荐模型的选择性LLM引导正则化）介绍了S-LLMR，一个模型无关的框架，它通过可学习的门控机制选择性地利用LLM知识。这种方法解决了LLM信号在上下文中可靠而非普遍可信的根本问题，仅在经验上证明有益时提供有针对性的指导。

## 核心方法论

S-LLMR 通过三个相互关联的组件协同工作，选择性地将LLM知识集成到传统推荐模型中。

### LLM 生成的软排名

该框架首先进行离线阶段，在此阶段提取和存储LLM知识。对于每个用户，系统构建其近期交互历史（通常是最近的10次交互）的文本摘要，并查询LLM（实验中使用GPT-4o-mini）以生成候选物品的软相关性分数。这些分数 $s_{u,i}^{LLM} \in [0,1]$ 代表LLM对每个物品与用户偏好匹配程度的评估。

为了特别解决稀疏数据场景，系统创建合成监督数据：
- **冷启动增强**：交互历史最少（≤3次交互）的用户与各种抽样物品配对。
- **长尾增强**：流行度最低10%的物品与抽样用户配对。

这种有针对性的数据生成确保了LLM监督精确地在传统模型最薄弱的地方可用。

### 选择性门控机制

核心创新在于可学习的门控机制，它决定何时激活LLM监督。对于每个用户-物品对 $(u,i)$，计算三个可靠性信号：

1. **冷启动指标**：如果用户 $u$ 的交互次数少于 $\tau_u$，则 $Cold(u) = 1$，否则为0。
2. **长尾指标**：如果物品 $i$ 属于流行度最低的 $\tau_i$ 百分位数，则 $Tail(i) = 1$，否则为0。
3. **模型不确定性**：$q_{u,i}$，一个归一化到 [0,1] 的连续分数，来源于基础推荐器的预测置信度。

这些信号被组合成特征向量 $z_{u,i} = [Cold(u), Tail(i), q_{u,i}]$ 并输入到单层门控网络中：

$$
\alpha_{u,i} = \sigma(w^T z_{u,i} + b)
$$

该门控产生介于0和1之间的值，用于缩放LLM监督的贡献。门控参数与基础推荐器通过反向传播共同学习，从而能够自动识别LLM指导何时有益的上下文。

### LLM 引导的成对排名正则化器

S-LLMR 不试图匹配绝对的LLM分数，而是通过成对排名损失来保留相对顺序。当LLM指示 $s_{u,i}^{LLM} > s_{u,j}^{LLM}$ 时，鼓励基础推荐器以边距 $m$ 预测 $s_{u,i} > s_{u,j}$：

$$
L_{LLM} = \sum_{(u,i,j) \in P} \alpha_{u,i,j} \cdot \max(0, m - (s_{u,i} - s_{u,j}))
$$

其中 $P$ 表示用户一致的有序对，$\alpha_{u,i,j} = 0.5 \cdot (\alpha_{u,i} + \alpha_{u,j})$ 是平均门控权重。最终的训练目标将基础推荐器损失与LLM正则化相结合：

$$
L = L_{rec} + \lambda L_{LLM}
$$

## 实验结果和主要发现

实验评估表明，S-LLMR 在六种不同的推荐骨干网络（DeepFM、xDeepFM、AutoInt、DCNv1、DCNv2、DIN）和三个亚马逊数据集（运动与户外、美容、玩具与游戏）上均表现出有效性。

### 不同场景下的性能

S-LLMR 在所有测试配置中均持续获得最高的 AUC 分数，在具有挑战性的场景中表现出尤其显著的改进：

![模型和场景的性能增益](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21526v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：S-LLMR 在不同模型骨干上实现的 AUC 增益，显示了整体增益以及在冷启动和长尾场景中的具体改进。*

- **冷启动用户**：在不同模型中 AUC 增益为 0.029-0.051
- **长尾物品**：AUC 改进为 0.034-0.056
- **整体性能**：AUC 持续改进 0.008-0.019

结果表明，S-LLMR 在稀疏数据状态下带来了不成比例的巨大益处，直接证实了选择性门控在协同过滤信号最弱时激活 LLM 指导的假设。

### 消融研究见解

关键的消融实验验证了两个核心组件的必要性：

1.  **门控 vs. 全局正则化**：在没有门控的情况下全局应用 LLM 监督通常会降低性能，特别是对长尾准确性而言，这为反对统一知识蒸馏方法提供了有力证据。

2.  **成对 vs. 逐点监督**：用逐点监督（BCE/MSE）替换成对排序未能产生有意义的改进，证实了保持相对顺序比匹配绝对分数更有效。

## 意义与贡献

S-LLMR 代表了从无条件知识迁移到可靠性感知集成的范式转变。该框架的主要贡献包括：

**目标稀疏性解决**：通过在冷启动和长尾场景中选择性地激活 LLM 指导，S-LLMR 直接解决了传统协同过滤的根本弱点，同时在密集区域保持了模型性能。

**模型无关设计**：该框架与各种推荐架构的兼容性，以及不引入推理开销的离线 LLM 处理，使其在实际部署中具有高度实用性。

**上下文可靠性的经验验证**：全面的实验提供了有力证据，表明 LLM 信号是上下文而非普遍可靠的，从而确立了选择性集成策略的必要性。

**新颖的正则化范式**：可学习、上下文相关的 LLM 正则化的引入，为从强大但不完美的模型中整合辅助知识开辟了新方向，超越了简单的损失匹配，实现了复杂的指导机制。

这项工作表明，在推荐中有效集成 LLM 需要细致入微的方法，既要尊重这些强大模型的优势，也要考虑其局限性，为更健壮、更智能的推荐系统奠定了基础。

abstract: Large language models provide rich semantic priors and strong reasoning capabilities, making them promising auxiliary signals for recommendation. However, prevailing approaches either deploy LLMs as standalone recommender or apply global knowledge distillation, both of which suffer from inherent drawbacks. Standalone LLM recommender are costly, biased, and unreliable across large regions of the user item space, while global distillation forces the downstream model to imitate LLM predictions even when such guidance is inaccurate. Meanwhile, recent studies show that LLMs excel particularly in re-ranking and challenging scenarios, rather than uniformly across all contexts.We introduce Selective LLM Guided Regularization, a model-agnostic and computation efficient framework that activates LLM based pairwise ranking supervision only when a trainable gating mechanism informing by user history length, item popularity, and model uncertainty predicts the LLM to be reliable. All LLM scoring is performed offline, transferring knowledge without increasing inference cost. Experiments across multiple datasets show that this selective strategy consistently improves overall accuracy and yields substantial gains in cold start and long tail regimes, outperforming global distillation baselines.

abstract: In search engine advertising (SEA) market, where competition among retailers is intense and multifaceted, channel coordination between retailers and manufacturers emerges as a critical factor, which significantly influences the effectiveness of advertising strategies. This research attempts to provide managerial guidelines for cooperative advertising in the SEA context by modeling two cooperative advertising decision scenarios. Scenario I defines a simple cooperative channel consisting of one manufacturer and one retailer. In Scenario II, we consider a more general setting where there is an independent retailer who competes with the Manufacturer-Retailer alliance in Scenario I. We propose a novel cooperative advertising optimization model, wherein a manufacturer can advertise product directly through SEA campaigns and indirectly by subsidizing its retailer. To highlight the distinctive features of SEA, our model incorporates dynamic quality scores and focuses on a finite time horizon. In each scenario, we provide a feasible equilibrium solution of optimal policies for all members. Subsequently, we conduct numerical experiments to perform sensitivity analysis for both the quality score and gross margin. Additionally, we explore the impact of the initial market share of the competing retailer in Scenario II. Finally, we investigate how retail competition affects the cooperative alliance's optimal strategy and channel performance. alphaxiv_detail.title: Dynamic Cooperative Strategies in Search Engine Advertising Market: With and Without Retail Competition
alphaxiv_detail.abstract: In search engine advertising (SEA) market, where competition among retailers is intense and multifaceted, channel coordination between retailers and manufacturers emerges as a critical factor, which significantly influences the effectiveness of advertising strategies. This research attempts to provide managerial guidelines for cooperative advertising in the SEA context by modeling two cooperative advertising decision scenarios. Scenario I defines a simple cooperative channel consisting of one manufacturer and one retailer. In Scenario II, we consider a more general setting where there is an independent retailer who competes with the Manufacturer-Retailer alliance in Scenario I. We propose a novel cooperative advertising optimization model, wherein a manufacturer can advertise product directly through SEA campaigns and indirectly by subsidizing its retailer. To highlight the distinctive features of SEA, our model incorporates dynamic quality scores and focuses on a finite time horizon. In each scenario, we provide a feasible equilibrium solution of optimal policies for all members. Subsequently, we conduct numerical experiments to perform sensitivity analysis for both the quality score and gross margin. Additionally, we explore the impact of the initial market share of the competing retailer in Scenario II. Finally, we investigate how retail competition affects the cooperative alliance's optimal strategy and channel performance. Our identified properties derived from the equilibrium and numerical analyses offer crucial insights for participants engaged in cooperative advertising within the SEA market.

en.title: C2LLM Technical Report: A New Frontier in Code Retrieval via Adaptive Cross-Attention Pooling
en.abstract: We present C2LLM - Contrastive Code Large Language Models, a family of code embedding models in both 0.5B and 7B sizes. Building upon Qwen-2.5-Coder backbones, C2LLM adopts a Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) module for generating sequence embedding from token embeddings, effectively 1) utilizing the LLM's causal representations acquired during pretraining, while also 2) being able to aggregate information from all tokens in the sequence, breaking the information bottleneck in EOS-based sequence embeddings, and 3) supporting flexible adaptation of embedding dimension, serving as an alternative to MRL. Trained on three million publicly available data, C2LLM models set new records on MTEB-Code among models of similar sizes, with C2LLM-7B ranking 1st on the overall leaderboard.

summary.summary: C2LLM, a family of code embedding models developed by Ant Group and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, introduces a Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) module that adaptively aggregates token representations from causal LLM backbones for code retrieval. The C2LLM-7B model achieved an average score of 80.75 on the MTEB-Code benchmark, ranking first among all models, while C2LLM-0.5B led the sub-1B parameter category with a score of 75.46.
originalProblem: General-purpose text embedding models perform sub-optimally for code retrieval due to the distinct structural and semantic properties of code.
Existing pooling strategies for causal LLM backbones, such as mean pooling and EOS token representation, introduce limitations like architectural mismatches or information bottlenecks.
Relying solely on an End-of-Sequence (EOS) token for representation results in significant information loss for long code sequences, hindering detailed semantic understanding.
solution: C2LLM integrates a Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) module directly after the LLM, using a single learnable query vector in a cross-attention layer to selectively aggregate token information.
The models are built upon fine-tuned causal LLM backbones, specifically Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, leveraging their pretraining knowledge.
A robust contrastive learning framework is employed for fine-tuning, utilizing a diverse 3 million-sample dataset, LoRA for efficiency, and hard-negative contrastive learning.
keyInsights: The PMA module effectively aggregates salient information from all tokens without altering the causal architecture of the backbone LLM, resolving limitations of prior pooling methods.
PMA decouples the LLM's internal hidden dimension from the final embedding dimension, enabling the generation of compact, flexible embeddings suitable for large-scale vector databases.

A comprehensive training strategy combining diverse public code-related datasets, efficient fine-tuning techniques, and specialized contrastive learning methods is crucial for achieving high-performance code embeddings.
results: C2LLM-7B achieved the #1 rank on the MTEB-Code benchmark with an average score of 80.75, surpassing all open and closed-source competitors.
C2LLM-0.5B attained an average score of 75.46 on MTEB-Code, positioning it as the #1 model among all models with less than 1 billion parameters.
Both C2LLM variants demonstrated strong performance in complex reasoning tasks, such as CodeFeedback, indicating effective capture of nuanced intent in natural language queries for code.

en.overview:
## Introduction

The landscape of code retrieval has become increasingly critical as software development workflows evolve toward greater automation and intelligence. Modern code agents that can plan, search, and edit code autonomously depend heavily on accurate retrieval systems to function effectively. While large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in understanding and generating code, translating these capabilities into effective code embeddings for retrieval tasks has proven challenging.

![MTEB-Code Performance Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21332v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: Performance comparison on the MTEB-Code benchmark showing C2LLM-7B achieving state-of-the-art results with a score of 80.75, and C2LLM-0.5B leading among models under 1B parameters with 75.46.*

The C2LLM Technical Report presents a family of contrastive code embedding models that address fundamental limitations in how existing approaches aggregate sequence information. Developed collaboratively by Ant Group and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, C2LLM introduces an innovative pooling mechanism specifically designed to unlock the full potential of causal language models for code retrieval tasks.

## Core Problem and Motivation

Current code embedding approaches face a fundamental challenge when attempting to leverage modern causal LLMs like Qwen2.5-Coder. Two predominant pooling strategies create significant limitations:

**Mean Pooling** averages token embeddings across the entire sequence but requires bidirectional attention mechanisms that diverge from the causal pretraining paradigm of state-of-the-art code LLMs. This architectural mismatch prevents mean pooling from fully utilizing the rich representations learned during pretraining.

**End-of-Sequence (EOS) Token Representation** uses the final token's embedding as the sequence representation. While computationally simple, this approach creates an severe information bottleneck, particularly problematic for lengthy code files containing thousands of tokens where critical syntactic and semantic information becomes compressed into a single position.

The authors identify this as a critical gap preventing the effective application of powerful code LLMs to embedding tasks, where general-purpose text embedding models continue to dominate benchmarks like MTEB-Code despite being less specialized for code understanding.

## Technical Architecture

### Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) Module

The core innovation of C2LLM lies in its **Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) module**, which serves as a bridge between causal LLM representations and effective sequence embeddings. The PMA module operates as a single cross-attention layer positioned directly after the LLM backbone.

![C2LLM Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21332v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: Architecture diagram of the C2LLM model showing the PMA module's integration with the LLM backbone, featuring cross-attention mechanisms with learnable query vectors.*

Given the LLM's hidden states $H \in \mathbb{R}^{l \times d_{LLM}}$ for $l$ tokens with dimension $d_{LLM}$, the PMA module employs a single learnable query vector $q \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times d_q}$ to attend to all token representations. The process involves:

$$
Q = qW_q, \quad K = HW_k, \quad V = HW_v
$$

where $W_q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_q \times d}$ and $W_k, W_v \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{LLM} \times d}$ are projection matrices. Cross-attention is computed as:

$$
O = \text{softmax}(QK^T)V
$$

The output undergoes residual connections and layer normalization twice, producing the final embedding $E \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times d}$.

### Key Architectural Advantages

**Selective Information Aggregation**: Unlike simple averaging or single-token approaches, the PMA module's attention mechanism dynamically learns to prioritize the most salient tokens for sequence representation, such as function signatures or critical logic components.

**Causal Architecture Preservation**: The module maintains the original causal attention mechanism of the backbone LLM, ensuring full exploitation of pretraining knowledge without requiring architectural modifications that might diminish performance.

**Dimensional Flexibility**: PMA decouples the LLM's internal hidden dimension from the final embedding dimension, enabling generation of compact embeddings suitable for large-scale vector databases without computationally expensive techniques like Multi-Resolution Learning.

## Training Methodology

### Dataset and Contrastive Learning Framework

C2LLM models are trained on 3 million publicly available samples spanning diverse code-related tasks including CodeSearchNet, APPS, CodeFeedback, CodeEditSearch, CosQA, StackOverflowQA, SyntheticText2SQL, and CodeTransOcean. This comprehensive dataset ensures broad code understanding and retrieval capabilities across multiple programming paradigms.

The training employs sophisticated contrastive learning strategies:

**In-batch Contrastive Learning** utilizes global batch synchronization across distributed processes, effectively expanding the negative sample pool within each batch. **Hard-Negative Contrastive Learning** incorporates $K=7$ hard negatives per query, forcing the model to distinguish between semantically similar but incorrect samples.

Temperature scaling with $\tau = 0.05$ is applied to both contrastive loss components, while specialized batching groups data by source and programming language to ensure high-quality contrastive signals relevant to specific code contexts.

### Efficient Training Configuration

The models leverage **LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)** with rank $r=64$ and alpha $\alpha=32$ for efficient fine-tuning of large backbones. **Flash Attention 2** optimization enhances computational throughput while reducing memory requirements.

Training proceeds for 3 epochs with learning rate $1 \times 10^{-4}$ and maximum sequence length 1024 tokens using left-padding. The final models result from weighted merging of four checkpoints captured at different global steps, implementing an ensemble-like technique to improve stability and generalization.

## Experimental Results

### MTEB-Code Benchmark Performance

C2LLM demonstrates exceptional performance across the MTEB-Code benchmark's 12 distinct code retrieval tasks:

**C2LLM-7B** achieves an average score of **80.75**, establishing it as the **top-ranked model** on the entire leaderboard, surpassing previous leaders including Seed1.6-Embedding (80.71) and Qwen3-Embedding-8B (80.69).

**C2LLM-0.5B** achieves **75.46**, claiming the **#1 position among models under 1 billion parameters** and ranking sixth overall. Remarkably, this smaller model outperforms substantially larger competitors like INF-Retriever-7B (69.70), demonstrating exceptional parameter efficiency.

### Task-Specific Excellence

The models show particularly strong performance in complex reasoning tasks. In CodeFeedback evaluations, C2LLM-7B achieves scores of 94.32 for multi-turn conversations and 90.66 for single-turn interactions, indicating effective capture of nuanced natural language intent in code contexts—crucial for real-world developer tools.

The consistency of high performance across both 7B and 0.5B variants validates the robustness and universal effectiveness of the PMA pooling strategy regardless of model scale.

## Significance and Impact

### Advancing Code Retrieval Capabilities

C2LLM's state-of-the-art MTEB-Code performance directly translates to improved developer productivity through faster, more accurate code discovery. The superior performance in complex reasoning tasks enables more sophisticated development workflows and better natural language interfaces to codebases.

### Architectural Innovation

The PMA module represents a significant contribution to LLM-based embedding architectures, effectively resolving the longstanding pooling dilemma for causal models. This innovation extends beyond code applications, potentially inspiring similar approaches across other domains requiring sequence-to-vector transformations with causal LLMs.

### Practical Deployment Benefits

The exceptional efficiency demonstrated by C2LLM-0.5B makes advanced code retrieval accessible to resource-constrained environments and large-scale deployments. The flexible embedding dimensionality support enhances practical applicability for vector databases, reducing storage requirements and accelerating similarity searches.

### Ecosystem Contributions

As part of the CodeFuse Embedding family's commitment to open research, C2LLM strengthens the open-source ecosystem by providing powerful, accessible tools that enable further innovation. The planned expansion into massively multilingual and multi-domain scenarios signals continued contributions to the broader AI community.

The work represents a critical advancement in bridging the gap between powerful code-understanding LLMs and effective embedding generation, with implications spanning from immediate developer productivity improvements to enabling next-generation autonomous code agents.

zh.title: C2LLM 技术报告：基于自适应交叉注意力池化的代码检索新前沿
zh.abstract: 我们提出了 C2LLM（对比代码大语言模型），这是一个包含 0.5B 和 7B 两种规模的代码嵌入模型家族。C2LLM 基于 Qwen-2.5-Coder 主干网络构建，并采用了一种名为多头注意力池化（PMA）的模块，用于从 token 嵌入生成序列嵌入，有效地：1) 利用了预训练期间获得的 LLM 因果表示；2) 能够聚合序列中所有 token 的信息，打破了基于 EOS 的序列嵌入中存在的信息瓶颈；以及 3) 支持嵌入维度的灵活调整，可作为 MRL 的替代方案。C2LLM 模型在三百万公开可用数据上进行训练，在 MTEB-Code 榜单上，与同等规模的模型相比，它们创造了新纪录，其中 C2LLM-7B 在总排行榜上名列第一。

summary.summary: C2LLM 是蚂蚁集团和上海交通大学联合开发的一系列代码嵌入模型，它引入了多头注意力池化 (PMA) 模块，该模块能自适应地聚合来自因果大语言模型骨干网络的 token 表示，用于代码检索。C2LLM-7B 模型在 MTEB-Code 基准测试中取得了 80.75 的平均分数，位列所有模型之首，而 C2LLM-0.5B 以 75.46 的分数领跑参数量小于 10 亿的模型类别。
originalProblem: 由于代码独特的结构和语义特性，通用文本嵌入模型在代码检索方面的表现不佳。
现有针对因果大语言模型骨干网络的池化策略，例如均值池化和 EOS token 表示，存在架构不匹配或信息瓶颈等局限性。
仅依靠序列结束 (EOS) token 进行表示会导致长代码序列的显著信息丢失，从而阻碍详细的语义理解。
solution: C2LLM 在大语言模型之后直接集成了多头注意力池化 (PMA) 模块，在交叉注意力层中使用单个可学习的查询向量来选择性地聚合 token 信息。
这些模型基于经过微调的因果大语言模型骨干网络构建，特别是 Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct 和 Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct，充分利用了它们的预训练知识。
采用了强大的对比学习框架进行微调，该框架利用多样化的 300 万样本数据集、LoRA 以提高效率以及硬负例对比学习。
keyInsights: PMA 模块能有效地从所有 token 中聚合显著信息，同时不改变骨干大语言模型的因果架构，解决了现有池化方法的局限性。
PMA 将大语言模型的内部隐藏维度与最终嵌入维度解耦，从而能够生成紧凑、灵活的嵌入，适用于大规模向量数据库。
结合多样化的公共代码相关数据集、高效微调技术和专业对比学习方法的综合训练策略对于实现高性能代码嵌入至关重要。
results: C2LLM-7B 在 MTEB-Code 基准测试中以 80.75 的平均分数位列第一，超越了所有开源和闭源竞争对手。
C2LLM-0.5B 在 MTEB-Code 上取得了 75.46 的平均分数，使其成为所有参数量小于 10 亿的模型中的第一名。
两种 C2LLM 变体在 CodeFeedback 等复杂推理任务中均表现出色，表明它们能够有效捕捉自然语言代码查询中细微的意图。

zh.overview:
## 引言

随着软件开发工作流程向更高程度的自动化和智能化演进，代码检索的重要性日益突出。能够自主规划、搜索和编辑代码的现代代码智能体，其有效运行在很大程度上依赖于准确的检索系统。尽管大型语言模型（LLMs）在理解和生成代码方面展现出卓越的能力，但将这些能力转化为有效的代码嵌入以用于检索任务已被证明具有挑战性。

![MTEB-Code 性能比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21332v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：MTEB-Code基准测试性能比较显示，C2LLM-7B以80.75分取得了最先进的成果，C2LLM-0.5B以75.46分在参数小于1B的模型中领先。*

C2LLM技术报告介绍了一系列对比代码嵌入模型，这些模型解决了现有方法在聚合序列信息方面的根本局限性。C2LLM由蚂蚁集团和上海交通大学合作开发，引入了一种创新的池化机制，专门旨在释放因果语言模型在代码检索任务中的全部潜力。

## 核心问题与动机

当前的代码嵌入方法在尝试利用Qwen2.5-Coder等现代因果LLM时面临一个根本性挑战。两种主要的池化策略造成了显著的局限性：

**均值池化**对整个序列的标记嵌入进行平均，但这需要双向注意力机制，这与最先进的代码LLM的因果预训练范式相悖。这种架构不匹配阻碍了均值池化充分利用预训练期间学到的丰富表示。

**序列末尾（EOS）标记表示**使用最终标记的嵌入作为序列表示。虽然计算简单，但这种方法造成了严重的信息瓶颈，对于包含数千个标记的长代码文件尤为成问题，因为关键的句法和语义信息被压缩到一个单一位置。

作者认为这是一个关键的空白，阻碍了强大的代码LLM有效应用于嵌入任务，而通用文本嵌入模型尽管对代码理解的专业化程度较低，却仍在MTEB-Code等基准测试中占据主导地位。

## 技术架构

### 基于多头注意力的池化（PMA）模块

C2LLM的核心创新在于其**基于多头注意力的池化（PMA）模块**，它充当了因果LLM表示与有效序列嵌入之间的桥梁。PMA模块作为一个单一的交叉注意力层，直接位于LLM骨干之后。

![C2LLM 架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21332v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：C2LLM模型的架构图，显示了PMA模块与LLM骨干的集成，其特点是带有可学习查询向量的交叉注意力机制。*

给定LLM的隐状态 $H \in \mathbb{R}^{l \times d_{LLM}}$，其中 $l$ 是标记数，$d_{LLM}$ 是维度，PMA模块采用一个可学习的查询向量 $q \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times d_q}$ 来关注所有标记表示。该过程包括：

$$
Q = qW_q, \quad K = HW_k, \quad V = HW_v
$$

其中 $W_q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_q \times d}$ 以及 $W_k, W_v \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{LLM} \times d}$ 是投影矩阵。交叉注意力计算如下：

$$
O = \text{softmax}(QK^T)V
$$

输出经过两次残差连接和层归一化，生成最终的嵌入 $E \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times d}$。

### 关键架构优势

**选择性信息聚合**：与简单的平均或单标记方法不同，PMA模块的注意力机制动态学习优先处理对序列表示最显著的标记，例如函数签名或关键逻辑组件。

**因果架构保留**：该模块保持了骨干LLM原始的因果注意力机制，确保充分利用预训练知识，而无需进行可能降低性能的架构修改。

**维度灵活性**：PMA将LLM的内部隐藏维度与最终嵌入维度解耦，从而能够生成适用于大规模向量数据库的紧凑嵌入，而无需多分辨率学习等计算昂贵的技术。

## 训练方法

### 数据集和对比学习框架

C2LLM模型在300万个公开样本上进行训练，这些样本涵盖了各种代码相关任务，包括CodeSearchNet、APPS、CodeFeedback、CodeEditSearch、CosQA、StackOverflowQA、SyntheticText2SQL和CodeTransOcean。这一综合数据集确保了模型在多种编程范式下具有广泛的代码理解和检索能力。

训练采用了复杂的对比学习策略：

**批内对比学习**利用分布式进程间的全局批同步，有效地扩大了每个批次内的负样本池。**难负例对比学习**为每个查询引入了$K=7$个难负例，迫使模型区分语义相似但不正确的样本。

温度缩放 $\tau = 0.05$ 应用于两个对比损失分量，同时通过源和编程语言对数据进行专门的批处理分组，以确保与特定代码上下文相关的高质量对比信号。

### 高效训练配置

模型利用**LoRA（低秩适应）**，其秩 $r=64$ 和 alpha $\alpha=32$，用于大型骨干模型的高效微调。**Flash Attention 2**优化提高了计算吞吐量，同时减少了内存需求。

训练进行3个 epoch，学习率为 $1 \times 10^{-4}$，最大序列长度为1024个token，采用左侧填充。最终模型是通过加权合并在不同全局步捕获的四个检查点而得到的，这实现了一种类似集成学习的技术，以提高稳定性和泛化能力。

## 实验结果

### MTEB-Code基准性能

C2LLM在MTEB-Code基准的12个不同代码检索任务中表现出色：

**C2LLM-7B**取得了**80.75**的平均分数，使其成为整个排行榜上**排名第一的模型**，超越了之前的领先者，包括Seed1.6-Embedding (80.71) 和 Qwen3-Embedding-8B (80.69)。

**C2LLM-0.5B**取得了**75.46**的分数，在**10亿参数以下模型中排名第一**，并总体排名第六。值得注意的是，这个较小的模型超越了诸如INF-Retriever-7B (69.70) 等规模大得多的竞争对手，展示了卓越的参数效率。

### 特定任务表现

模型在复杂推理任务中表现出特别强大的性能。在CodeFeedback评估中，C2LLM-7B在多轮对话中取得了94.32分，在单轮交互中取得了90.66分，这表明它能有效捕捉代码上下文中细微的自然语言意图——这对于现实世界的开发工具至关重要。

7B和0.5B变体都保持了高性能的一致性，这验证了PMA池化策略的鲁棒性和普遍有效性，无论模型规模如何。

## 意义与影响

### 推进代码检索能力

C2LLM在MTEB-Code上的最先进性能直接转化为通过更快、更准确的代码发现来提高开发人员生产力。在复杂推理任务中的卓越表现使得更复杂的开发工作流程和更好的代码库自然语言接口成为可能。

### 架构创新

PMA 模块对基于 LLM 的嵌入架构做出了重大贡献，有效解决了因果模型的长期存在的池化困境。这项创新超越了代码应用，可能启发其他需要使用因果 LLM 进行序列到向量转换的领域采用类似方法。

### 实际部署优势

C2LLM-0.5B 所展现的卓越效率，使得先进的代码检索在资源受限环境和大规模部署中成为可能。灵活的嵌入维度支持增强了向量数据库的实际适用性，减少了存储需求并加速了相似性搜索。

### 生态系统贡献

作为 CodeFuse Embedding 家族开放研究承诺的一部分，C2LLM 通过提供强大、易用的工具来加强开源生态系统，从而实现进一步创新。计划扩展到大规模多语言和多领域场景，预示着将继续为更广泛的 AI 社区做出贡献。

这项工作代表了弥合强大代码理解 LLM 与有效嵌入生成之间差距的关键进展，其影响范围从即时提高开发者生产力到赋能下一代自主代码代理。

abstract: We present C2LLM - Contrastive Code Large Language Models, a family of code embedding models in both 0.5B and 7B sizes. Building upon Qwen-2.5-Coder backbones, C2LLM adopts a Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) module for generating sequence embedding from token embeddings, effectively 1) utilizing the LLM's causal representations acquired during pretraining, while also 2) being able to aggregate information from all tokens in the sequence, breaking the information bottleneck in EOS-based sequence embeddings, and 3) supporting flexible adaptation of embedding dimension, serving as an alternative to MRL. Trained on three million publicly available data, C2LLM models set new records on MTEB-Code among models of similar sizes, with C2LLM-7B ranking 1st on the overall leaderboard.

en.title: ReaSeq: Unleashing World Knowledge via Reasoning for Sequential Modeling
en.abstract:
Industrial recommender systems face two fundamental limitations under the log-driven paradigm: (1) knowledge poverty in ID-based item representations that causes brittle interest modeling under data sparsity, and (2) systemic blindness to beyond-log user interests that constrains model performance within platform boundaries. These limitations stem from an over-reliance on shallow interaction statistics and close-looped feedback while neglecting the rich world knowledge about product semantics and cross-domain behavioral patterns that Large Language Models have learned from vast corpora.
To address these challenges, we introduce ReaSeq, a reasoning-enhanced framework that leverages world knowledge in Large Language Models to address both limitations through explicit and implicit reasoning. Specifically, ReaSeq employs explicit Chain-of-Thought reasoning via multi-agent collaboration to distill structured product knowledge into semantically enriched item representations, and latent reasoning via Diffusion Large Language Models to infer plausible beyond-log behaviors. Deployed on Taobao's ranking system serving hundreds of millions of users, ReaSeq achieves substantial gains: >6.0% in IPV and CTR, >2.9% in Orders, and >2.5% in GMV, validating the effectiveness of world-knowledge-enhanced reasoning over purely log-driven approaches.

summary.summary: The TaoRank Team at Taobao developed ReaSeq, a framework that integrates explicit and latent reasoning capabilities from Large Language Models into industrial sequential recommender systems. ReaSeq achieves over 6.0% increases in IPV and CTR, and over 2.5% in GMV, by enriching item representations with world knowledge and inferring beyond-log user interests.
originalProblem: Existing log-driven sequential recommenders suffer from "knowledge poverty" due to opaque, ID-based item representations, leading to brittle interest modeling and representation collapse for sparse data and long-tail items.
Traditional systems exhibit "systemic blindness" to user interests that occur beyond platform interaction logs, missing cross-platform activities, offline behaviors, and emerging trends.
Purely statistical pattern matching limits the depth of understanding of user intentions and product attributes, creating an inherent performance bottleneck.
solution: ReaSeq employs a Multi-Agent Knowledge Reasoning (MAKR) framework to distill structured product knowledge into semantically enriched item representations, utilizing hierarchical LLM agents for categorical extraction, dimension refinement, and item-specific knowledge generation.

It integrates these knowledge-enhanced representations into industrial ranking systems via both Retrieval-Based (GSU-ESU) and Compression-Based modeling paradigms, complemented by Semantic Item IDs (SIDs) for high-level pattern capture.

Generative Behavior Reasoning (GBR) leverages Diffusion Large Language Models (DLLM) to infer plausible "beyond-log behaviors" by identifying missing interaction positions in user sequences (based on temporal/cognitive discontinuities) and dynamically generating augmented representations for these inferred actions.
keyInsights: Supervised fine-tuning (Image-to-Text and Intra-User-Interaction contrastive learning) is crucial for adapting LLM embeddings to the recommender domain, significantly boosting recall-oriented metrics.

MAKR enhances semantic richness and generalization for item representations, proving more beneficial for cold-start scenarios, while sometimes degrading instance-level identification due to abstraction.
The placement and context of inferred behaviors, rather than just their quantity, are critical for generative models to learn discriminative semantic representations of beyond-log actions.
results: Online A/B tests on Taobao showed ReaSeq delivered substantial gains, with over +6.0% in IPV and CTR, +2.9% in Orders, and +2.5% in GMV across 'Guess What You Like' and 'Post-Buy' scenarios.

Offline evaluations demonstrated that integrating GME-enhanced representations improved overall GAUC by +0.120%, with a more pronounced +0.150% for Cold-Start Users, highlighting the benefit of rich content understanding.

The full ReaSeq framework combining all enhancements achieved the highest overall GAUC of +0.41% (+0.45% for Cold-Start Users) in offline experiments, confirming the synergistic and additive nature of its components.

en.overview:
## ReaSeq Framework Overview

![ReaSeq Framework](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-0.jpeg)

ReaSeq introduces a reasoning-enhanced framework that transforms sequential modeling in recommender systems by integrating world knowledge from Large Language Models (LLMs). The framework addresses fundamental limitations of traditional ID-based approaches through two complementary components that leverage explicit and latent reasoning capabilities.

Traditional recommender systems rely heavily on interaction logs and ID-based item representations, which suffer from two critical shortcomings: knowledge poverty in item representations and systemic blindness to user interests that exist beyond platform interactions. ReaSeq tackles these challenges by moving from reactive "co-occurrence fitting" to proactive "world-aware reasoning," enabling recommender systems to understand items and user preferences at a deeper semantic level.

## Multi-Agent Knowledge Reasoning (MAKR)

![MAKR System](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-1.jpeg)

The reasoning-enhanced representation component employs a sophisticated Multi-Agent Knowledge Reasoning (MAKR) system to combat knowledge poverty in item representations. This hierarchical framework uses specialized LLM agents to progressively refine semantic knowledge through three layers of reasoning:

The first layer consists of categorical information extraction agents that operate through two parallel streams. The User Demand Orientation Stream analyzes historical user queries to build a user-centric demand taxonomy focused on aspects like "comfort requirements" and "style preferences," independent of merchant-provided schemas. Simultaneously, the Product Attribute Orientation Stream processes merchant attribute specifications to create a normalized product-centric taxonomy covering elements like "material properties" and "design aesthetics."

The second layer employs dimension refinement agents that specialize the categorical taxonomies into finer-grained subcategories using Chain-of-Thought prompting. These agents ensure refined dimensions are orthogonal, comprehensive, and objective, either adapting parent taxonomy dimensions or creating new subcategory-specific ones.

![Knowledge Generation Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-2.jpeg)

The third layer features item-specific knowledge generation agents that instantiate abstract dimensions into concrete, item-specific semantic knowledge. For each dimension, these agents extract factual evidence from item metadata, synthesize characterizations, and distill keywords while providing explicit justification for factual grounding.

The structured knowledge from both user demand and product attribute perspectives is concatenated into unified textual sequences, then mapped into dense semantic vectors using a pre-trained sentence embedding model. These dual-perspective representations are combined via element-wise addition to form knowledge-enhanced item representations.

## Reasoning-Enhanced Sequential Modeling

![Sequential Modeling Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-3.jpeg)

The enriched item representations are integrated into industrial ranking architectures through two complementary paradigms. The retrieval-based modeling approach employs a two-stage pipeline where a General Search Unit (GSU) efficiently retrieves top-N relevant historical interactions using semantic similarity, followed by an Exact Search Unit (ESU) that refines these interactions via target-aware multi-head attention.

The compression-based modeling paradigm uses learnable interest anchors to compress entire ultra-long behavioral sequences via cross-attention, providing dense gradient coverage for all items and enabling end-to-end optimization. The framework also introduces Semantic Item IDs (SIDs) derived from quantizing continuous semantic vectors using a Residual Quantized Variational Autoencoder, serving as discrete, memory-efficient features that capture complementary high-level patterns.

## Generative Behavior Reasoning (GBR)

![GBR Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-4.jpeg)

The Generative Behavior Reasoning component addresses systemic blindness to beyond-log user interests by inferring plausible behaviors that are not captured in platform interactions. The system first identifies positions in user sequences where missing interactions likely occurred based on three key assumptions: temporal continuity (large time gaps suggest external activities), cognitive inertia (abrupt category transitions imply missing intermediate behaviors), and collaborative coherence (low co-occurrence frequency indicates missing interactions).

A hybrid coarse-to-fine pipeline combines rule-based filtering for temporal and category discontinuities with model-based fine-grained filtering using sequential recommenders to identify statistically implausible transitions. The framework then employs Diffusion Large Language Models (DLLM) as the generative backbone to fill identified missing positions.

![Behavior Generation Examples](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-5.jpeg)

The system uses special `[FILL]` tokens to mark missing positions and creates self-supervised training data by masking items critical for collaborative coherence. The DLLM is trained using dynamic random masking with a sampled softmax loss function employing cosine similarity, encouraging bidirectional latent reasoning to synthesize contextually coherent behaviors.

## Experimental Results and Validation

![Representation Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-6.jpeg)

Extensive offline analyses demonstrate the effectiveness of both components. For reasoning-enhanced representations, supervised fine-tuning proves indispensable, with domain adaptation significantly boosting macro recall performance. The MAKR system provides consistent improvements in recall-oriented metrics, indicating richer semantic understanding, though with some trade-offs in instance-level identification due to abstraction effects.

![Knowledge Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-7.jpeg)

Integration into industrial ranking systems shows substantial gains, with compression-based modeling achieving +0.34% GAUC improvement and semantic IDs providing additional complementary value. The framework demonstrates particularly strong performance for cold-start users, with +0.45% GAUC improvement when all enhancements are combined.

For Generative Behavior Reasoning, quantitative validation reveals that category discontinuity-based location yields superior performance compared to temporal discontinuity. The context-aware loss function proves essential for learning discriminative semantic representations, while qualitative analysis shows successful reconstruction of plausible beyond-log items that maintain semantic consistency and contextual relevance.

## Real-World Impact and Deployment

ReaSeq's deployment on Taobao's recommendation system serving hundreds of millions of users demonstrated substantial business impact. Over a two-week A/B test across "Guess What You Like" and "Post-Buy" scenarios, the framework achieved impressive gains: over 6.0% improvement in both IPV (Item Page Views) and CTR (Click-Through Rate), over 2.9% increase in orders, and over 2.5% growth in GMV (Gross Merchandise Value).

The mathematical foundation of ReaSeq can be expressed through its core representation learning objective:

$$
h_t^{enhanced} = \Phi(concat(K_{user\_demand}, K_{product\_attr}))
$$

where $\Phi$ represents the pre-trained sentence embedding model, and $K_{user\_demand}$ and $K_{product\_attr}$ are the structured knowledge outputs from the MAKR system.

For the generative component, the training objective uses a sampled softmax loss with cosine similarity:

$$
L_{cosInfoNCE} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(h_{[FILL]}, h_{target})/\tau)}{\sum_{j} \exp(\text{sim}(h_{[FILL]}, h_j)/\tau)}
$$

where $\text{sim}$ represents cosine similarity, $\tau$ is the temperature parameter, and the denominator includes both positive and negative samples.

ReaSeq represents a significant advancement in industrial recommender systems by successfully integrating LLM reasoning capabilities into core recommendation tasks. The framework provides a practical, deployable solution that enhances both item understanding and user behavior modeling, establishing a new foundation for recommendation systems to proactively model user interests through world-aware reasoning rather than purely statistical pattern matching.

zh.title: ReaSeq：通过推理利用世界知识进行序列建模
zh.abstract:
工业推荐系统在日志驱动范式下，面临两个根本性局限：(1) 基于ID的物品表示存在知识匮乏，导致在数据稀疏性下兴趣建模能力不足；(2) 对日志之外的用户兴趣存在系统性盲区，将模型性能限制在平台边界之内。这些局限源于对浅层交互统计数据和闭环反馈的过度依赖，同时却忽视了由大语言模型从海量语料库中学习到的关于产品语义和跨领域行为模式的丰富世界知识。

为解决这些挑战，我们引入了ReaSeq，一个利用大语言模型中世界知识，通过显式和隐式推理来解决上述两个局限的推理增强框架。具体而言，ReaSeq通过多智能体协作采用显式思维链推理（Chain-of-Thought reasoning），将结构化的产品知识提炼并转化为语义丰富的物品表示；并通过隐式推理，借助扩散大语言模型（Diffusion Large Language Models）推断合理的日志外行为。ReaSeq已部署在服务数亿用户的淘宝排名系统上，取得了显著的提升：IPV和CTR（点击率）均提升超过6.0%，订单量提升超过2.9%，GMV（商品交易总额）提升超过2.5%。这验证了相较于纯日志驱动方法，世界知识增强型推理的有效性。

summary.summary: 淘宝陶淘团队开发了ReaSeq，这是一个将大型语言模型（LLMs）的显性和潜在推理能力集成到工业级序列推荐系统中的框架。ReaSeq通过用世界知识丰富商品表示并推断日志之外的用户兴趣，实现了IPV和CTR超过6.0%的增长，以及GMV超过2.5%的增长。
originalProblem: 现有基于日志驱动的序列推荐器因不透明、基于ID的商品表示而存在“知识贫乏”问题，导致兴趣建模脆弱，对稀疏数据和长尾商品出现表示崩溃。
传统系统对平台互动日志之外的用户兴趣表现出“系统性盲点”，错过了跨平台活动、线下行为和新兴趋势。
纯粹的统计模式匹配限制了对用户意图和产品属性理解的深度，造成固有的性能瓶颈。
solution: ReaSeq采用多智能体知识推理（MAKR）框架，利用分层LLM智能体进行类别提取、维度细化和商品特定知识生成，将结构化产品知识提炼为语义丰富的商品表示。
它通过基于检索（GSU-ESU）和基于压缩的建模范式，将这些知识增强型表示集成到工业排名系统中，并辅以语义商品ID（SIDs）以捕获高层模式。
生成式行为推理（GBR）利用扩散大型语言模型（DLLM），通过识别用户序列中缺失的互动位置（基于时间/认知不连续性），并动态生成这些推断行为的增强表示，从而推断出合理的“日志外行为”。
keyInsights: 监督式微调（图像到文本和用户内互动对比学习）对于使LLM嵌入适应推荐领域至关重要，显著提升了召回导向的指标。
MAKR增强了商品表示的语义丰富性和泛化能力，对冷启动场景更有益，但有时会因抽象而降低实例级识别能力。
推断行为的放置和上下文，而不仅仅是其数量，对于生成模型学习日志外行为的判别性语义表示至关重要。
results: 淘宝在线A/B测试显示，ReaSeq在“猜你喜欢”和“购后”场景中取得了显著收益，IPV和CTR增长超过+6.0%，订单增长+2.9%，GMV增长+2.5%。
离线评估表明，集成GME增强型表示将整体GAUC提高了+0.120%，其中冷启动用户更是提高了+0.150%，凸显了丰富内容理解的益处。
结合所有增强功能的完整ReaSeq框架在离线实验中实现了最高的整体GAUC，达到+0.41%（冷启动用户为+0.45%），证实了其组件的协同和累加性质。

zh.overview:
## ReaSeq 框架概述

![ReaSeq Framework](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-0.jpeg)

ReaSeq 引入了一个推理增强框架，通过整合来自大型语言模型（LLM）的世界知识，转变了推荐系统中的序列建模。该框架通过利用显式和潜在推理能力的两个互补组件，解决了传统基于 ID 方法的根本局限性。

传统推荐系统严重依赖交互日志和基于 ID 的物品表示，这导致了两个关键缺陷：物品表示中的知识贫乏，以及对平台交互之外的用户兴趣的系统性盲点。ReaSeq 通过从反应性的“共现拟合”转向主动的“世界感知推理”来解决这些这些挑战，使推荐系统能够在更深层次的语义层面理解物品和用户偏好。

## 多智能体知识推理 (MAKR)

![MAKR System](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-1.jpeg)

推理增强表示组件采用复杂的多智能体知识推理（MAKR）系统，以解决物品表示中的知识贫乏问题。这个分层框架利用专门的 LLM 智能体，通过三个推理层逐步完善语义知识：

第一层由分类信息提取智能体组成，它们通过两个并行流运作。用户需求导向流分析历史用户查询，构建一个以用户为中心的需求分类体系，重点关注“舒适度要求”和“风格偏好”等方面，独立于商家提供的方案。同时，产品属性导向流处理商家属性规范，创建一个标准化的以产品为中心的分类体系，涵盖“材料特性”和“设计美学”等元素。

第二层采用维度细化智能体，利用思维链提示将分类分类体系细化为更精细的子类别。这些智能体确保细化后的维度是正交、全面和客观的，它们或是调整父分类体系的维度，或是创建新的特定于子类别的维度。

![Knowledge Generation Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-2.jpeg)

第三层是物品特定知识生成智能体，它们将抽象维度实例化为具体的、物品特定的语义知识。对于每个维度，这些智能体从物品元数据中提取事实证据，综合特征描述，提炼关键词，并为事实依据提供明确的理由。

来自用户需求和产品属性双重视角的结构化知识被连接成统一的文本序列，然后使用预训练的句子嵌入模型映射成稠密的语义向量。这些双视角表示通过元素级相加组合，形成知识增强的物品表示。

## 推理增强序列建模

![Sequential Modeling Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-3.jpeg)

丰富的物品表示通过两种互补范式集成到工业排名架构中。基于检索的建模方法采用两阶段管道：通用搜索单元（GSU）通过语义相似性高效检索出前 N 个相关历史交互，然后精确搜索单元（ESU）通过目标感知多头注意力对这些交互进行细化。

基于压缩的建模范式利用可学习的兴趣锚点，通过交叉注意力压缩整个超长行为序列，为所有项目提供密集的梯度覆盖，并实现端到端优化。该框架还引入了语义商品ID（SIDs），这些ID是通过使用残差量化变分自编码器量化连续语义向量而得出的，作为离散的、内存高效的特征，捕捉互补的高级模式。

## 生成式行为推理 (GBR)

![GBR流程](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-4.jpeg)

生成式行为推理组件通过推断未在平台交互中捕获的合理行为，解决了对日志外用户兴趣的系统性盲点。该系统首先根据三个关键假设识别用户序列中可能发生缺失交互的位置：时间连续性（大时间间隔暗示外部活动）、认知惯性（突然的品类转换意味着缺失的中间行为）和协同连贯性（低共同出现频率表明缺失交互）。

一个混合的粗粒度到细粒度管道将基于规则的过滤（用于时间和品类不连续性）与基于模型的细粒度过滤（使用序列推荐器识别统计上不合理的转换）相结合。然后，该框架采用扩散大语言模型（DLLM）作为生成骨干，以填充识别出的缺失位置。

![行为生成示例](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-5.jpeg)

该系统使用特殊的`[FILL]`标记来标记缺失位置，并通过掩盖对协同连贯性至关重要的项目来创建自监督训练数据。DLLM使用动态随机掩码和采用余弦相似度的采样softmax损失函数进行训练，鼓励双向潜在推理以合成上下文连贯的行为。

## 实验结果与验证

![表示分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-6.jpeg)

广泛的离线分析证明了这两个组件的有效性。对于推理增强表示，监督微调证明不可或缺，领域适应显著提升了宏观召回性能。MAKR系统在召回导向指标上提供了持续改进，表明更丰富的语义理解，尽管由于抽象效应，在实例级识别上存在一些权衡。

![知识比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.21257v2/img-7.jpeg)

集成到工业级排序系统显示出显著增益，其中基于压缩的建模实现了+0.34%的GAUC提升，语义ID提供了额外的互补价值。该框架对冷启动用户表现尤为出色，当所有增强功能结合时，GAUC提升了+0.45%。

对于生成式行为推理，定量验证表明，基于品类不连续性的定位相比时间不连续性产生了优越的性能。上下文感知损失函数对于学习判别性语义表示至关重要，而定性分析显示成功重建了合理的日志外项目，这些项目保持了语义一致性和上下文相关性。

## 实际影响与部署

ReaSeq在淘宝推荐系统上部署并服务数亿用户，展现了显著的业务影响。在“猜你喜欢”和“购后”场景下为期两周的A/B测试中，该框架取得了令人印象深刻的收益：IPV（商品详情页浏览量）和CTR（点击率）均提升超过6.0%，订单量增长超过2.9%，GMV（商品交易总额）增长超过2.5%。

ReaSeq的数学基础可以通过其核心表示学习目标来表达：

$$
h_t^{enhanced} = \Phi(concat(K_{user\_demand}, K_{product\_attr}))
$$

其中 $\Phi$ 代表预训练的句子嵌入模型，$K_{user\_demand}$ 和 $K_{product\_attr}$ 是来自 MAKR 系统的结构化知识输出。

对于生成组件，训练目标使用带有余弦相似度的采样 softmax 损失：

$$
L_{cosInfoNCE} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(h_{[FILL]}, h_{target})/\tau)}{\sum_{j} \exp(\text{sim}(h_{[FILL]}, h_j)/\tau)}
$$

其中 $\text{sim}$ 代表余弦相似度，$\tau$ 是温度参数，分母包含正样本和负样本。

ReaSeq 通过成功地将 LLM 推理能力集成到核心推荐任务中，代表了工业推荐系统中的一个显著进步。该框架提供了一个实用、可部署的解决方案，它增强了物品理解和用户行为建模能力，为推荐系统奠定了新的基础，使其能够通过世界感知推理而不是纯粹的统计模式匹配来主动地建模用户兴趣。
