en.title: Hindsight is 20/20: Building Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects
en.abstract: Agent memory has been touted as a dimension of growth for LLM-based applications, enabling agents that can accumulate experience, adapt across sessions, and move beyond single-shot question answering. The current generation of agent memory systems treats memory as an external layer that extracts salient snippets from conversations, stores them in vector or graph-based stores, and retrieves top-k items into the prompt of an otherwise stateless model. While these systems improve personalization and context carry-over, they still blur the line between evidence and inference, struggle to organize information over long horizons, and offer limited support for agents that must explain their reasoning. We present Hindsight, a memory architecture that treats agent memory as a structured, first-class substrate for reasoning by organizing it into four logical networks that distinguish world facts, agent experiences, synthesized entity summaries, and evolving beliefs. This framework supports three core operations -- retain, recall, and reflect -- that govern how information is added, accessed, and updated. Under this abstraction, a temporal, entity aware memory layer incrementally turns conversational streams into a structured, queryable memory bank, while a reflection layer reasons over this bank to produce answers and to update information in a traceable way. On key long-horizon conversational memory benchmarks like LongMemEval and LoCoMo, Hindsight with an open-source 20B model lifts overall accuracy from 39% to 83.6% over a full-context baseline with the same backbone and outperforms full context GPT-4o. Scaling the backbone further pushes Hindsight to 91.4% on LongMemEval and up to 89.61% on LoCoMo (vs. 75.78% for the strongest prior open system), consistently outperforming existing memory architectures on multi-session and open-domain questions.

summary.summary: HINDSIGHT introduces a novel memory architecture for AI agents, integrating structured memory (TEMPR) with preference-conditioned reasoning (CARA) to enhance long-term recall and behavioral consistency. The system achieves state-of-the-art results on challenging benchmarks, reaching 91.4% accuracy on LongMemEval and 89.61% on LoCoMo, significantly outperforming existing memory systems and full-context baselines, even with open-source LLM backbones.
originalProblem: Existing RAG-based agent memory systems struggle to preserve long-term information and often blur the distinction between observed evidence and inferred beliefs.
Current agents exhibit inconsistent reasoning styles and viewpoints across interactions, failing to maintain a stable persona or track knowledge evolution over extended periods.
Memory systems lack robust support for temporal reasoning and entity-aware knowledge organization, hindering multi-hop discovery and precise information access over long conversational histories.
solution: HINDSIGHT employs a four-network memory organization (World, Experience, Opinion, Observation) to epistemically distinguish facts, agent experiences, synthesized entities, and subjective beliefs with confidence scores.

It implements three core operations: Retain (converts conversational streams into structured, linked memories), Recall (retrieves relevant memories using a multi-strategy approach including semantic, keyword, graph, and temporal search), and Reflect (generates responses and updates opinions based on a configurable behavioral profile).
The CARA component integrates a behavioral profile (skepticism, literalism, empathy, bias strength) to modulate system prompts, ensuring preference-conditioned reasoning and consistent agent styles.
keyInsights: Epistemically separating memory into distinct networks for facts, experiences, observations, and evolving opinions provides clarity, traceability, and a robust substrate for advanced reasoning in AI agents.

A multi-strategy retrieval approach, combining vector, keyword, graph-based spreading activation, and temporal search, significantly improves the precision and breadth of memory recall in long-horizon contexts.

Integrating explicit behavioral parameters into an agent's reasoning process enables stable preference consistency and allows for dynamic opinion formation and evolution, moving beyond static persona descriptions.
results: On the LongMemEval benchmark, HINDSIGHT (OSS-20B) achieved 83.6% overall accuracy, a +44.6 percentage point gain over the OSS-20B full-context baseline (39.0%), and outperformed GPT-4o (60.2%) and other memory systems.

HINDSIGHT, when backed by Gemini-3 Pro, achieved the highest overall accuracy of 91.4% on LongMemEval and 89.61% on LoCoMo, demonstrating top-tier performance on multi-session and open-domain question answering.

The system showed substantial improvements in specific long-term categories, increasing multi-session reasoning from 21.1% to 79.7% and temporal reasoning from 31.6% to 79.7% on LongMemEval, confirming its effectiveness against context dilution.

en.overview:
## Overview

Agent memory systems are critical for building AI agents capable of sustained, intelligent interactions over extended periods. Current approaches, primarily based on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, treat memory as external storage that retrieves relevant snippets for otherwise stateless large language models. However, these systems struggle with fundamental limitations: they blur the distinction between observed facts and subjective beliefs, perform poorly at organizing information over long time horizons, offer limited explainability, and fail to maintain consistent agent personalities across interactions.

![HINDSIGHT Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12818v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: Overview of the HINDSIGHT architecture, showing the integration of TEMPR (Temporal Entity Memory Priming Retrieval) and CARA (Coherent Adaptive Reasoning Agents) components with the four-network memory organization.*

HINDSIGHT addresses these challenges through a structured memory architecture that explicitly separates different types of knowledge and implements three core operations: Retain, Recall, and Reflect. This system enables agents to accumulate experiences, maintain epistemic clarity between facts and beliefs, and exhibit consistent behavioral profiles across long-term interactions.

## Memory Architecture and Core Components

HINDSIGHT organizes agent memory into four distinct logical networks, each serving a specific epistemic purpose:

- **World Network (W)**: Stores objective facts about the external world, independent of the agent's perspective
- **Experience Network (B)**: Contains biographical information about the agent itself, written in first person, covering actions and personal history
- **Opinion Network (O)**: Houses subjective judgments formed by the agent, each tagged with confidence scores and timestamps for belief evolution
- **Observation Network (S)**: Maintains preference-neutral entity summaries synthesized from underlying facts

This four-network structure provides epistemic clarity by explicitly distinguishing what the agent has observed (evidence) from what it believes (inference), addressing a key limitation of current memory systems.

The architecture implements two primary components: TEMPR (Temporal Entity Memory Priming Retrieval) handles memory storage and retrieval operations, while CARA (Coherent Adaptive Reasoning Agents) manages preference-conditioned response generation and belief formation.

## The Retain Operation: Structured Memory Formation

The Retain operation, implemented by TEMPR, converts conversational data into structured narrative facts within the memory bank. Unlike fragmented sentence-level extraction common in existing systems, TEMPR employs coarse-grained chunking to extract 2-5 self-contained narrative facts per conversation, preserving cross-turn context and temporal information.

The system performs entity resolution and linking, mapping entity mentions to canonical entities using similarity metrics based on string matching, co-occurrence patterns, and temporal proximity. These canonical entities create entity links in the memory graph, enabling multi-hop reasoning across related information.

Beyond entity connections, the memory graph incorporates multiple link types:

$$
\text{Links} = \{\text{temporal}, \text{semantic}, \text{entity}, \text{causal}\}
$$

- **Temporal links** connect memories close in time with weights decaying by temporal distance
- **Semantic links** connect memories with high cosine similarity between embeddings
- **Causal links** represent cause-effect relationships extracted by the LLM

An observation paradigm generates objective, preference-neutral entity summaries asynchronously, updating when underlying facts change. The system also implements opinion reinforcement, where new facts trigger confidence adjustments in related existing opinions based on whether evidence supports or contradicts them.

## The Recall Operation: Multi-Strategy Memory Retrieval

The Recall operation retrieves relevant memories using a token budget constraint rather than a fixed top-k approach, ensuring retrieved context fits downstream language model limitations. TEMPR implements four parallel retrieval strategies:

1. **Semantic Retrieval**: Vector similarity search using cosine similarity
2. **Keyword Retrieval**: Full-text lexical search via BM25 for precise term matching
3. **Graph Retrieval**: Breadth-first search using spreading activation along entity, temporal, semantic, and causal links
4. **Temporal Graph Retrieval**: Filters memories by occurrence intervals for temporally-constrained queries

These parallel channels undergo Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to combine diverse relevance signals, followed by neural cross-encoder reranking for improved precision. The system then applies token budget filtering, greedily selecting top-ranked memories until the specified token limit is reached.

## The Reflect Operation: Preference-Conditioned Reasoning

![CARA Reflection Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12818v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: The CARA reflection process, showing how agent disposition and background information influence response generation and belief formation.*

CARA implements the Reflect operation, generating responses shaped by configurable behavioral profiles. The system defines agent personality through four parameters:

$$
\Theta = (S, L, E, \beta)
$$

where:
- **S ∈ {1,...,5}**: Skepticism level (trusting to skeptical)
- **L ∈ {1,...,5}**: Literalism level (flexible to literal)  
- **E ∈ {1,...,5}**: Empathy level (detached to empathetic)
- **β ∈ [0,1]**: Bias strength controlling profile influence

These numeric parameters are verbalized into natural language to modulate system prompts, ensuring consistent agent behavior across interactions. When queries require subjective judgment, CARA retrieves relevant facts via TEMPR, incorporates the agent's behavioral profile, and uses an LLM to generate preference-conditioned responses while forming new opinions with confidence scores.

## Empirical Validation and Performance

HINDSIGHT was evaluated on two challenging benchmarks: LongMemEval and LoCoMo, which test conversational memory over extended interactions spanning multiple sessions and requiring recall from hundreds of thousands to millions of tokens.

On LongMemEval, HINDSIGHT with an open-source GPT-OSS-20B backbone achieved 83.6% overall accuracy, representing a dramatic +44.6 percentage point improvement over the full-context OSS-20B baseline (39.0%). The system outperformed frontier models including full-context GPT-4o (60.2%) and leading memory systems like Zep with GPT-4o (71.2%).

The most substantial improvements occurred in categories explicitly testing long-term memory capabilities:
- Multi-session reasoning: improved from 21.1% to 79.7%
- Temporal reasoning: increased from 31.6% to 79.7%  
- Preference questions: rose from 20.0% to 66.7%

When paired with larger backbone models, performance scaled further, reaching 91.4% overall accuracy with Gemini-3 Pro, marking the best result across all evaluated systems.

On LoCoMo, HINDSIGHT consistently outperformed prior open memory systems, achieving 83.18% with GPT-OSS-20B and 89.61% with Gemini-3 Pro, effectively matching the performance of proprietary systems while maintaining a fully open-source memory stack.

## Unique Contributions and Differentiation

HINDSIGHT distinguishes itself from existing approaches through several key innovations. While systems like MemGPT introduce tiered context management and approaches like Zep build temporal knowledge graphs, most focus solely on objective facts without modeling subjective beliefs or behavioral consistency.

HINDSIGHT is among the few systems that simultaneously:
- Separates facts from opinions with epistemic clarity
- Supports temporal reasoning with validity tracking
- Employs entity-aware graph structures for rich memory connections
- Facilitates opinion evolution with confidence-based belief updates
- Integrates behavioral parameters for consistent agent personalities
- Utilizes external-only memory to avoid parametric editability issues
- Leverages multi-strategy retrieval for enhanced recall precision

This comprehensive approach addresses the fundamental limitations of current memory systems while establishing new benchmarks for long-term conversational agents.

## Implications and Future Directions

HINDSIGHT represents a significant advancement toward truly long-lived AI agents capable of accumulating experiences, maintaining consistent personalities, and reasoning over extended time horizons. The explicit separation of different knowledge types provides unprecedented transparency and explainability, crucial for applications requiring trust and accountability.

The demonstrated success with open-source language models democratizes advanced agent capabilities, reducing dependence on expensive proprietary systems. This accessibility, combined with the release of open-source code and benchmarking tools, positions HINDSIGHT to accelerate community innovation in agent memory systems.

Future research directions include jointly optimizing memory components through reinforcement learning, integrating richer tool-use and workflow orchestration, and developing controlled forgetting mechanisms. The architecture also opens possibilities for more sophisticated cognitive features like belief revision, self-reflection, and privacy-aware memory management.

By treating memory as a structured, dynamic substrate for reasoning rather than simple information storage, HINDSIGHT establishes a foundation for a new generation of more capable, transparent, and user-centric AI agents across diverse applications requiring sustained intelligent interaction.

zh.title: 后见之明，洞察秋毫：构建可保留、回忆与反思的智能体记忆
zh.abstract:
智能体记忆被誉为大型语言模型（LLM）应用的一个增长维度，它使智能体能够积累经验、跨会话适应，并超越单次问答的局限。当前一代的智能体记忆系统将记忆视为一个外部层，该层从对话中提取关键片段，将其存储在基于向量或图的存储中，并将检索到的前 K 项放入一个无状态模型的提示中。尽管这些系统改善了个性化和上下文承接，但它们仍然模糊了证据与推理之间的界限，难以在长周期内组织信息，并且对需要解释其推理过程的智能体支持有限。

我们提出了 Hindsight，这是一种记忆架构，它将智能体记忆视为结构化、一流的推理基底，通过将其组织成四个逻辑网络来区分世界事实、智能体经验、合成的实体摘要和不断演变的信念。该框架支持三个核心操作——保留（retain）、回忆（recall）和反思（reflect）——它们管理着信息的添加、访问和更新方式。在这种抽象下，一个具备时序和实体感知能力的记忆层逐步将对话流转化为结构化、可查询的记忆库，而一个反思层则对该记忆库进行推理，以生成答案并以可追溯的方式更新信息。

在 LongMemEval 和 LoCoMo 等关键长周期对话记忆基准测试中，Hindsight 结合一个200亿参数的开源模型，将总体准确率从39%提升至83.6%（相比使用相同骨干模型的全上下文基线），并超越了使用完整上下文的 GPT-4o 的表现。进一步扩展骨干模型将 Hindsight 在 LongMemEval 上的表现推至91.4%，在 LoCoMo 上最高达到89.61%（相比最强的现有开源系统为75.78%），在多会话和开放域问题上持续优于现有记忆架构。

summary.summary: HINDSIGHT为AI智能体引入了一种新颖的记忆架构，它将结构化记忆（TEMPR）与偏好条件推理（CARA）相结合，以增强长期记忆召回和行为一致性。该系统在具有挑战性的基准测试中取得了最先进的结果，在LongMemEval上达到91.4%的准确率，在LoCoMo上达到89.61%，即使使用开源大型语言模型（LLM）骨干网络，也显著优于现有记忆系统和全上下文基线。
originalProblem: 现有基于RAG的智能体记忆系统难以保留长期信息，并且常常模糊观察到的证据与推断信念之间的区别。
当前的智能体在不同交互中表现出不一致的推理风格和视角，未能维持稳定的角色或跟踪长期知识演变。
记忆系统缺乏对时间推理和实体感知知识组织的强大支持，这阻碍了在漫长对话历史中的多跳发现和精确信息访问。
solution: HINDSIGHT采用四网络记忆组织（世界、经验、观点、观察），以认识论的方式区分事实、智能体经验、合成实体和带有置信度分数的客观信念。
它实现三个核心操作：保留（将对话流转换为结构化、链接的记忆）、召回（使用多策略方法检索相关记忆，包括语义、关键词、图和时间搜索）和反思（根据可配置的行为配置文件生成响应并更新观点）。
CARA组件集成了一个行为配置文件（怀疑度、字面性、同理心、偏见强度）来调节系统提示，确保偏好条件推理和一致的智能体风格。
keyInsights: 将记忆认识论地分离为事实、经验、观察和演变观点的不同网络，为AI智能体中的高级推理提供了清晰度、可追溯性和强大的基础。
结合向量、关键词、基于图的传播激活和时间搜索的多策略检索方法，显著提高了长期上下文中记忆召回的精度和广度。
将明确的行为参数整合到智能体的推理过程中，能够实现稳定的偏好一致性，并允许动态的观点形成和演变，超越了静态的角色描述。
results: 在LongMemEval基准测试中，HINDSIGHT (OSS-20B) 取得了83.6%的总体准确率，比OSS-20B全上下文基线（39.0%）提高了44.6个百分点，并且优于GPT-4o（60.2%）和其他记忆系统。
当由Gemini-3 Pro支持时，HINDSIGHT在LongMemEval上取得了91.4%的最高总体准确率，在LoCoMo上取得了89.61%，在多会话和开放域问答方面表现出顶尖水平。
该系统在特定的长期类别中显示出显著改进，LongMemEval上多会话推理从21.1%提高到79.7%，时间推理从31.6%提高到79.7%，证实了其对抗上下文稀释的有效性。

zh.overview:
## 概述

智能体记忆系统对于构建能够长期持续进行智能交互的AI智能体至关重要。当前的方法主要基于检索增强生成（RAG）管道，将记忆视为外部存储，为无状态的大型语言模型检索相关片段。然而，这些系统在基本限制上举步维艰：它们模糊了观察到的事实和主观信念之间的区别，在长时间范围内组织信息表现不佳，可解释性有限，并且未能保持智能体在不同交互中一致的个性。

![HINDSIGHT 架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12818v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：HINDSIGHT架构概述，展示了TEMPR（时间实体记忆预检索）和CARA（连贯自适应推理智能体）组件与四网络记忆组织的集成。*

HINDSIGHT通过结构化的记忆架构解决了这些挑战，该架构明确分离了不同类型的知识，并实现了三个核心操作：保留（Retain）、回忆（Recall）和反思（Reflect）。该系统使智能体能够积累经验，保持事实与信念之间的认知清晰度，并在长期交互中展现一致的行为特征。

## 记忆架构和核心组件

HINDSIGHT将智能体记忆组织成四个不同的逻辑网络，每个网络服务于特定的认知目的：

-   **世界网络（W）**：存储关于外部世界的客观事实，独立于智能体的视角
-   **经验网络（B）**：包含关于智能体自身的传记信息，以第一人称撰写，涵盖行动和个人历史
-   **观点网络（O）**：存储智能体形成的主观判断，每个判断都标记有置信度分数和时间戳，用于信念演变
-   **观察网络（S）**：维护从基础事实合成的偏好中性实体摘要

这种四网络结构通过明确区分智能体观察到的内容（证据）和它相信的内容（推论），提供了认知清晰度，解决了当前记忆系统的一个关键限制。

该架构实现了两个主要组件：TEMPR（时间实体记忆预检索）负责记忆存储和检索操作，而CARA（连贯自适应推理智能体）则管理偏好条件下的响应生成和信念形成。

## 保留操作：结构化记忆形成

保留操作由TEMPR实现，将对话数据转换为记忆库中的结构化叙事事实。与现有系统中常见的零碎句子级提取不同，TEMPR采用粗粒度分块，从每次对话中提取2-5个自包含的叙事事实，保留了跨回合上下文和时间信息。

系统执行实体解析和链接，使用基于字符串匹配、共现模式和时间接近度的相似性度量，将实体提及映射到规范实体。这些规范实体在记忆图中创建实体链接，从而实现跨相关信息的多跳推理。

除了实体连接，记忆图还包含多种链接类型：

$$
\text{链接} = \{\text{时间}, \text{语义}, \text{实体}, \text{因果}\}
$$

-   **时间链接**：连接时间上相近的记忆，权重随时间距离衰减
-   **语义链接**：连接嵌入之间具有高余弦相似度的记忆
-   **因果链接**：表示由LLM提取的因果关系

观察范式异步生成客观、偏好中性的实体摘要，并在底层事实发生变化时更新。系统还实现了观点强化，即新事实会根据证据是否支持或矛盾来触发对相关现有观点的置信度调整。

## 回忆操作：多策略记忆检索

回忆操作使用令牌预算约束而非固定的top-k方法检索相关记忆，确保检索到的上下文符合下游语言模型的限制。TEMPR实现了四种并行检索策略：

1.  **语义检索**：使用余弦相似度进行向量相似性搜索
2.  **关键词检索**：通过BM25进行全文词法搜索，实现精确的术语匹配
3.  **图检索**：使用广度优先搜索，沿实体、时间、语义和因果链接进行传播激活
4.  **时间图检索**：根据发生间隔过滤记忆，用于受时间限制的查询

这些并行通道经过倒数排序融合（RRF）以结合多样的相关性信号，然后通过神经网络交叉编码器进行重新排序以提高精度。系统随后应用令牌预算过滤，贪婪地选择排名靠前的记忆，直到达到指定的令牌限制。

## 反思操作：偏好条件推理

![CARA 反思过程](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12818v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：CARA反思过程，展示了代理倾向和背景信息如何影响响应生成和信念形成。*

CARA实施反思操作，生成由可配置行为档案塑造的响应。系统通过四个参数定义代理的个性：

$$
\Theta = (S, L, E, \beta)
$$

其中：
- **S ∈ {1,...,5}**：怀疑程度（信任到怀疑）
- **L ∈ {1,...,5}**：字面程度（灵活到字面）
- **E ∈ {1,...,5}**：同理心程度（冷漠到有同理心）
- **β ∈ [0,1]**：偏见强度，控制档案影响力

这些数值参数被口头化为自然语言，以调节系统提示，确保代理在不同交互中行为一致。当查询需要主观判断时，CARA通过TEMPR检索相关事实，整合代理的行为档案，并使用大型语言模型（LLM）生成偏好条件响应，同时以置信度分数形成新观点。

## 经验验证与性能

HINDSIGHT在两个具有挑战性的基准测试中进行了评估：LongMemEval和LoCoMo，它们测试跨多个会话的长时间交互中的对话记忆，并要求从数十万到数百万个令牌中进行回忆。

在LongMemEval上，配备开源GPT-OSS-20B主干的HINDSIGHT实现了83.6%的整体准确率，相较于全上下文OSS-20B基线（39.0%）提升了惊人的44.6个百分点。该系统超越了包括全上下文GPT-4o（60.2%）在内的前沿模型，以及Zep与GPT-4o（71.2%）等领先记忆系统。

在明确测试长期记忆能力的类别中，改进最为显著：
- 多会话推理：从21.1%提高到79.7%
- 时间推理：从31.6%提高到79.7%
- 偏好问题：从20.0%上升到66.7%

当与更大的主干模型配对时，性能进一步提升，使用Gemini-3 Pro实现了91.4%的整体准确率，标志着所有评估系统中最好的结果。

在LoCoMo上，HINDSIGHT始终优于先前的开放记忆系统，使用GPT-OSS-20B实现了83.18%，使用Gemini-3 Pro实现了89.61%，有效地与专有系统的性能匹配，同时保持了完全开源的记忆堆栈。

## 独特贡献与差异化

HINDSIGHT通过几项关键创新使其与现有方法区分开来。尽管MemGPT等系统引入了分层上下文管理，Zep等方法构建了时间知识图谱，但大多数只关注客观事实，而没有对主观信念或行为一致性进行建模。

HINDSIGHT 是少数能够同时做到以下几点的系统之一：
- 以认知清晰度将事实与观点分离
- 通过有效性跟踪支持时间推理
- 采用实体感知图结构，实现丰富的记忆连接
- 通过基于置信度的信念更新促进观点演变
- 整合行为参数，保持代理的一致性个性
- 利用纯外部记忆，避免参数可编辑性问题
- 利用多策略检索，提高回忆精度

这种全面的方法解决了当前记忆系统的根本局限性，同时为长期会话代理建立了新的基准。

## 影响与未来方向

HINDSIGHT 代表着向真正长寿的AI代理迈出的重要一步，这些代理能够积累经验、保持一致的个性并进行跨越长时间范围的推理。不同知识类型的明确分离提供了前所未有的透明度和可解释性，这对于需要信任和问责制的应用至关重要。

通过开源语言模型展示的成功使先进的代理能力大众化，减少了对昂贵专有系统的依赖。这种可访问性，结合开源代码和基准测试工具的发布，使HINDSIGHT能够加速社区在代理记忆系统方面的创新。

未来的研究方向包括通过强化学习共同优化记忆组件、整合更丰富的工具使用和工作流编排，以及开发受控遗忘机制。该架构还为更复杂的认知功能开辟了可能性，例如信念修正、自我反思和隐私感知记忆管理。

通过将记忆视为一种结构化的、动态的推理基质，而非简单的信息存储，HINDSIGHT为新一代更强大、更透明、以用户为中心的AI代理奠定了基础，适用于需要持续智能交互的各种应用。

abstract: Agent memory has been touted as a dimension of growth for LLM-based applications, enabling agents that can accumulate experience, adapt across sessions, and move beyond single-shot question answering. The current generation of agent memory systems treats memory as an external layer that extracts salient snippets from conversations, stores them in vector or graph-based stores, and retrieves top-k items into the prompt of an otherwise stateless model. While these systems improve personalization and context carry-over, they still blur the line between evidence and inference, struggle to organize information over long horizons, and offer limited support for agents that must explain their reasoning. We present Hindsight, a memory architecture that treats agent memory as a structured, first-class substrate for reasoning by organizing it into four logical networks that distinguish world facts, agent experiences, synthesized entity summaries, and evolving beliefs. This framework supports three core operations -- retain, recall, and reflect -- that govern how information is added, accessed, and updated. Under this abstraction, a temporal, entity aware memory layer incrementally turns conversational streams into a structured, queryable memory bank, while a reflection layer reasons over this bank to produce answers and to update information in a traceable way. On key long-horizon conversational memory benchmarks like LongMemEval and LoCoMo, Hindsight with an open-source 20B model lifts overall accuracy from 39% to 83.6% over a full-context baseline with the same backbone and outperforms full context GPT-4o. Scaling the backbone further pushes Hindsight to 91.4% on LongMemEval and up to 89.61% on LoCoMo (vs. 75.78% for the strongest prior open system), consistently outperforming existing memory architectures on multi-session and open-domain questions.
title: Hindsight is 20/20: Building Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects

abstract: The rapid acceleration of scientific publishing has created substantial challenges for researchers attempting to discover, contextualize, and interpret relevant literature. Traditional keyword-based search systems provide limited semantic understanding, while existing AI-driven tools typically focus on isolated tasks such as retrieval, clustering, or bibliometric visualization. This paper presents an integrated system for scientific literature exploration that combines large-scale data acquisition, hybrid retrieval, semantic topic modeling, and heterogeneous knowledge graph construction. The system builds a comprehensive corpus by merging full-text data from arXiv with structured metadata from OpenAlex. A hybrid retrieval architecture fuses BM25 lexical search with embedding-based semantic search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Topic modeling is performed on retrieved results using BERTopic or non-negative matrix factorization depending on computational resources. A knowledge graph unifies papers, authors, institutions, countries, and extracted topics into an interpretable structure. The system provides a multi-layered exploration environment that reveals not only relevant publications but also the conceptual and relational landscape surrounding a query. Evaluation across multiple queries demonstrates improvements in retrieval relevance, topic coherence, and interpretability. The proposed framework contributes an extensible foundation for AI-assisted scientific discovery.
title: Intelligent Scientific Literature Explorer using Machine Learning (ISLE)

en.title: FuXi-$γ$: Efficient Sequential Recommendation with Exponential-Power Temporal Encoder and Diagonal-Sparse Positional Mechanism
en.abstract: Sequential recommendation aims to model users' evolving preferences based on their historical interactions. Recent advances leverage Transformer-based architectures to capture global dependencies, but existing methods often suffer from high computational overhead, primarily due to discontinuous memory access in temporal encoding and dense attention over long sequences. To address these limitations, we propose FuXi-$\gamma$, a novel sequential recommendation framework that improves both effectiveness and efficiency through principled architectural design. FuXi-$\gamma$ adopts a decoder-only Transformer structure and introduces two key innovations: (1) An exponential-power temporal encoder that encodes relative temporal intervals using a tunable exponential decay function inspired by the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve. This encoder enables flexible modeling of both short-term and long-term preferences while maintaining high efficiency through continuous memory access and pure matrix operations. (2) A diagonal-sparse positional mechanism that prunes low-contribution attention blocks using a diagonal-sliding strategy guided by the persymmetry of Toeplitz matrix. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that FuXi-$\gamma$ achieves state-of-the-art performance in recommendation quality, while accelerating training by up to 4.74$\times$ and inference by up to 6.18$\times$, making it a practical and scalable solution for long-sequence recommendation. Our code is available at this https URL.

summary.summary: FuXi-𝛾 introduces an efficient sequential recommendation model that integrates an exponential-power temporal encoder, inspired by cognitive forgetting curves, and a diagonal-sparse positional mechanism. This architecture achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while accelerating training by up to 4.74x and inference by up to 6.18x for long sequences, making advanced recommender systems more scalable for industrial applications.
originalProblem: Computational overhead significantly hinders the practical deployment of state-of-the-art generative Transformer-based sequential recommendation models, especially for long user sequences.
Existing temporal encoders, such as T5-style bucket-based methods, suffer from inefficient, non-contiguous memory access patterns that impede parallel execution.
Relative positional encoding in Transformer architectures often introduces redundant O(n²) complexity, which can be partially unnecessary given other available positional signals.
solution: Developed FuXi-𝛾, a decoder-only Transformer with a dual-channel self-attention mechanism to explicitly separate and combine temporal and positional information.

Implemented an Exponential-Power Temporal Encoder, inspired by the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, to model user interest decay continuously and efficiently with learnable parameters for diverse behavioral patterns.
Introduced a Diagonal-Sparse Positional Mechanism that leverages Toeplitz matrix properties for structured pruning of redundant positional attention blocks, primarily optimizing inference efficiency.
keyInsights: Modeling temporal decay with a cognitively-inspired exponential-power function provides both high accuracy and superior computational efficiency due to continuous memory access and flexible parameterization.

Redundancy in relative positional encoding can be effectively mitigated through a diagonal-sparse pruning mechanism, intelligently leveraging attention matrix properties without significant accuracy loss.

A minimalistic single-head attention and hardware-friendly architecture, coupled with explicit data type pre-conversion, are crucial for achieving substantial efficiency gains in large-scale sequential recommendation.
results: Achieved state-of-the-art recommendation quality, outperforming baselines by up to 13.70% in MRR on an industrial music dataset and 4.46% in NDCG@10 on public datasets.
Demonstrated significant efficiency improvements with up to 4.74x faster training and 6.18x faster inference for long sequences (length 1000) compared to leading generative models.

The exponential-power temporal encoder alone improved HR@10, NDCG@10, and MRR by averages of 8.82%, 11.16%, and 11.15% respectively, while offering up to 11.00x speedup over bucket-based methods. The diagonal-sparse positional mechanism reduced positional attention FLOPs by up to 74.56% with minimal accuracy impact.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Sequential recommendation systems aim to predict user preferences based on their historical interaction patterns, forming a cornerstone of modern recommendation infrastructure across e-commerce, streaming, and social media platforms. While recent advances in Transformer-based generative models have achieved impressive accuracy gains, they often come with prohibitive computational costs that limit their practical deployment. FuXi-γ addresses this critical efficiency-effectiveness trade-off by introducing two key architectural innovations: an Exponential-Power Temporal Encoder inspired by cognitive science principles and a Diagonal-Sparse Positional Mechanism that intelligently prunes redundant attention computations.

![FuXi-γ Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: Overall architecture of FuXi-γ, showing the dual-channel attention mechanism with specialized temporal and positional encoders within each FuXi-γ block.*

## Problem Statement and Motivation

Modern sequential recommendation faces a fundamental scalability challenge: while state-of-the-art generative models like HSTU and FuXi-α demonstrate superior predictive performance, they introduce substantial computational overhead that makes them impractical for large-scale production environments. The authors identify two primary bottlenecks in existing approaches:

First, temporal encoding mechanisms in current models suffer from inefficient memory access patterns. T5-style bucket-based encoders used in HSTU and FuXi-α create irregular, fragmented memory operations due to log-transformation and discretization of temporal intervals, resulting in O(n²) non-contiguous memory access that severely hampers parallel execution on modern hardware.

Second, relative positional encoding introduces redundant O(n²) complexity as a separate attention channel, despite the presence of absolute positional embeddings and implicit temporal ordering signals. This redundancy becomes particularly problematic for long user interaction sequences, where the quadratic scaling of attention mechanisms creates significant computational bottlenecks.

FuXi-γ is motivated by the need to preserve the accuracy benefits of advanced generative recommendation models while achieving the computational efficiency required for real-world deployment, particularly in scenarios involving extensive user interaction histories.

## Exponential-Power Temporal Encoder

The core innovation of FuXi-γ lies in its cognitively-inspired temporal encoding mechanism. Drawing from the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, which describes exponential memory decay in human cognition, the temporal encoder models time-aware user interest decay through a mathematically elegant formulation:

$$
A_{ts} = \alpha \cdot \gamma^{(T^{\beta})}
$$

where $T$ represents the relative temporal matrix with $T_{i,j} = |t_i - t_j|$, $\alpha$ is a learnable base interest intensity, $\beta$ controls the nonlinearity of the scaling transformation, and $\gamma \in (0, 1)$ is a learnable decay parameter.

This approach offers several advantages over existing methods. Unlike bucket-based encoders that suffer from discontinuous "sawtooth" patterns and information loss through discretization, the exponential-power formulation provides smooth, continuous decay curves. The learnable parameters $\gamma$ and $\beta$ enable adaptation to diverse behavioral patterns, capturing both short-term preferences (smaller $\gamma$) and long-term interests (larger $\gamma$).

Critically, the encoder employs explicit data type pre-conversion, casting the temporal matrix $T$ from `int64` to `float32` during preprocessing. This seemingly minor optimization eliminates costly implicit runtime type casting during power and exponential operations, contributing significantly to the overall computational efficiency.

## Diagonal-Sparse Positional Mechanism

The second key innovation addresses positional encoding redundancy through a structured sparse attention approach. The mechanism operates on the principle that many positional attention patterns contain redundant information that can be pruned without significant accuracy loss.

![Diagonal-Sparse Mechanism](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: The four-step process of the diagonal-sparse positional mechanism: block division, leftmost scoring, diagonal-sliding selection, and final sparse attention generation.*

The approach consists of four steps:

1. **Block Division**: The n×n positional attention map is partitioned into s×s blocks, with the upper triangular region masked for decoder-only architecture compatibility.

2. **Leftmost Scoring**: Leveraging the Toeplitz matrix property where $W_{i,j} = W_{i+m,j+m}$, importance scores are computed only for blocks in the leftmost column, efficiently covering all diagonal slices.

3. **Diagonal-Sliding Selection**: Based on importance scores, the k most unimportant blocks are identified according to a pruning ratio τ.

4. **Block Sparse Attention**: The identified blocks are "slid" diagonally across the attention map to generate a sparse mask, zeroing out redundant attention weights while preserving meaningful patterns.

This semi-structured pruning offers an optimal balance between accuracy retention and computational efficiency, with the structured nature ensuring hardware-friendly execution.

## Experimental Results

Comprehensive experiments across four datasets (ML-1M, ML-20M, KuaiRand, and Industrial music) demonstrate FuXi-γ's superior performance in both accuracy and efficiency metrics.

### Recommendation Performance

FuXi-γ consistently achieves state-of-the-art recommendation quality, with particularly impressive results on the large-scale industrial dataset. Compared to other autoregressive baselines, FuXi-γ shows average improvements of 3.79% in HR@10, 2.37% in HR@50, 4.46% in NDCG@10, 3.49% in NDCG@50, and 4.24% in MRR on public datasets. On the industrial music dataset, the gains are even more pronounced, achieving 25.06% higher HR@10 and 42.86% higher NDCG@10 on average.

### Computational Efficiency

![Efficiency Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: Training (left) and inference (right) efficiency comparison showing FuXi-γ's superior performance, especially for long sequences.*

FuXi-γ demonstrates exceptional computational efficiency across varying sequence lengths. At a sequence length of 1000, it achieves training speedups of up to 4.74× compared to LLaMa and 4.48× compared to HSTU, while maintaining 1.86× speedup over its predecessor FuXi-β. Similar improvements are observed for inference, with speedups reaching 6.18× and 6.07× respectively.

### Temporal Encoder Analysis

![Temporal Encoder Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-4.jpeg)
*Figure 4: Efficiency comparison of different temporal encoders across sequence lengths (left) and batch sizes (right).*

The exponential-power temporal encoder consistently demonstrates the lowest latency across varying configurations, achieving up to 11.00× speedup over bucket-based methods and 2.52× speedup over inverse-proportional functions at sequence length 1000.

![Temporal Weight Visualization](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-6.jpeg)
*Figure 5: Visualization of temporal attention weights showing smooth decay curves produced by FuXi-γ compared to discontinuous patterns from other methods.*

The visualization reveals that FuXi-γ produces smooth, continuous decay curves that effectively differentiate between short-term and long-term intervals, contrasting with the discontinuous "sawtooth" patterns of bucket-based encoders.

### Sparse Positional Mechanism Evaluation

![Sparsity Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-10.jpeg)
*Figure 6: Impact of pruning ratio τ on ML-20M dataset, showing NDCG@10 performance (left) and corresponding FLOP reduction (right).*

The diagonal-sparse positional mechanism effectively reduces computational overhead with minimal accuracy loss. On ML-20M, a 60% pruning ratio reduces positional attention FLOPs by 74.56% while retaining 98.92% of original accuracy. Similar results are observed across other datasets, with some cases showing slight accuracy improvements due to regularization effects.

## Technical Contributions and Significance

FuXi-γ makes several important technical contributions to the field of sequential recommendation:

**Cognitively-Inspired Design**: The exponential-power temporal encoder represents a principled approach to modeling temporal dynamics, grounding the mathematical formulation in established cognitive science principles rather than ad-hoc engineering choices.

**Hardware-Optimized Architecture**: The emphasis on continuous memory access patterns, pure matrix operations, and explicit data type optimization demonstrates how algorithmic design can be co-optimized with hardware characteristics for substantial performance gains.

**Structured Sparse Attention**: The diagonal-sparse mechanism offers a practical approach to attention pruning that maintains accuracy while providing significant efficiency improvements, particularly valuable for long-sequence scenarios.

**Scalability for Long Sequences**: The demonstrated ability to maintain both accuracy and efficiency as sequence length increases addresses a critical limitation in current sequential recommendation systems.

## Limitations and Future Directions

While FuXi-γ represents a significant advance, several limitations warrant consideration. The cognitive inspiration, while theoretically grounded, may not generalize across all user behavior patterns or domains. The sparse attention mechanism, though effective, requires careful tuning of hyperparameters like pruning ratio and block size for optimal performance.

Future work could explore adaptive sparsity patterns that adjust based on sequence characteristics, integration of additional cognitive principles beyond the forgetting curve, and extension to multi-modal recommendation scenarios. The hardware optimization strategies could also be further refined for emerging computing architectures.

The work establishes a strong foundation for efficient, scalable sequential recommendation systems that maintain state-of-the-art accuracy while meeting the computational constraints of real-world deployment scenarios. By successfully bridging the gap between theoretical advances and practical applicability, FuXi-γ represents an important step toward more widespread adoption of sophisticated recommendation algorithms in production environments.

zh.title: FuXi-$γ$: 基于指数幂时间编码器和对角稀疏位置机制的高效序列推荐
zh.abstract: 序列推荐旨在基于用户的历史交互建模其演进的偏好。最新进展利用Transformer架构捕获全局依赖，但现有方法常面临高计算开销，这主要归因于时序编码中的非连续内存访问以及长序列上的密集注意力。为克服这些局限，我们提出了 FuXi-$\gamma$，一种通过精心设计的架构同时提升有效性与效率的新颖序列推荐框架。FuXi-$\gamma$ 采用仅解码器Transformer结构，并引入了两项关键创新：(1) 一种指数幂时序编码器，它使用受艾宾浩斯遗忘曲线启发的、可调的指数衰减函数来编码相对时间间隔。该编码器通过连续内存访问和纯矩阵操作保持高效率，同时能够灵活建模短期和长期偏好。(2) 一种对角稀疏位置机制，它借鉴托普利茨矩阵的共对称性，采用对角滑动策略剪枝低贡献注意力块。在四个真实世界数据集上的大量实验表明，FuXi-$\gamma$ 在推荐质量上达到了最先进的性能，同时将训练速度提高了高达4.74倍，推理速度提高了高达6.18倍，使其成为长序列推荐的一个实用且可扩展的解决方案。我们的代码可在 [this https URL](this https URL) 获取。

summary.summary: FuXi-𝛾 引入了一种高效的序列推荐模型，该模型集成了受认知遗忘曲线启发的指数幂时间编码器和对角稀疏位置机制。这种架构在实现最先进准确性的同时，将长序列的训练速度提高了4.74倍，推理速度提高了6.18倍，使先进的推荐系统在工业应用中更具可扩展性。

引入了对角稀疏位置机制，利用Toeplitz矩阵特性对冗余位置注意力块进行结构化剪枝，主要优化推理效率。
keyInsights: 利用受认知启发的指数幂函数建模时间衰减，通过连续内存访问和灵活的参数化，提供了高精度和卓越的计算效率。
通过对角稀疏剪枝机制，可以有效缓解相对位置编码中的冗余，智能地利用注意力矩阵特性而不会显著损失准确性。
简约的单头注意力机制和硬件友好的架构， coupled with explicit data type pre-conversion, 对于在大规模序列推荐中实现显著效率提升至关重要。
results: 实现了最先进的推荐质量，在工业音乐数据集上MRR比基线高出13.70%，在公共数据集上NDCG@10高出4.46%。
与领先的生成模型相比，对于长序列（长度1000），训练速度提高了4.74倍，推理速度提高了6.18倍，显示出显著的效率提升。
仅指数幂时间编码器就将HR@10、NDCG@10和MRR平均分别提高了8.82%、11.16%和11.15%，同时比基于桶的方法提速高达11.00倍。对角稀疏位置机制将位置注意力FLOPs减少了高达74.56%，而对准确性影响最小。

zh.overview:
## 引言

序列推荐系统旨在根据用户的历史交互模式预测用户偏好，构成了电子商务、流媒体和社交媒体平台现代推荐基础设施的基石。尽管基于Transformer的生成模型最近取得了令人印象深刻的精度提升，但它们通常伴随着高昂的计算成本，这限制了其实际部署。FuXi-γ通过引入两项关键的架构创新来解决这一关键的效率与效果权衡：受认知科学原理启发的指数幂时间编码器，以及智能裁剪冗余注意力计算的对角稀疏位置机制。

![FuXi-γ 架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：FuXi-γ 的整体架构，展示了每个FuXi-γ块内具有专门的时间和位置编码器的双通道注意力机制。*

## 问题陈述与动机

现代序列推荐面临着根本性的可扩展性挑战：尽管像HSTU和FuXi-α这样的最先进生成模型表现出卓越的预测性能，但它们引入了大量的计算开销，使其在大规模生产环境中不切实际。作者指出了现有方法中的两个主要瓶颈：

首先，当前模型中的时间编码机制存在低效的内存访问模式。HSTU和FuXi-α中使用的T5风格的基于桶的编码器，由于对时间间隔进行对数变换和离散化，产生了不规则、碎片化的内存操作，导致O(n²)的非连续内存访问，严重阻碍了现代硬件上的并行执行。

其次，尽管存在绝对位置嵌入和隐式时间排序信号，相对位置编码作为独立的注意力通道引入了冗余的O(n²)复杂度。对于长用户交互序列，这种冗余变得尤为突出，注意力机制的二次缩放产生了显著的计算瓶颈。

FuXi-γ的动机在于需要保留先进生成推荐模型的精度优势，同时实现实际部署所需的计算效率，特别是在涉及大量用户交互历史的场景中。

## 指数幂时间编码器

FuXi-γ的核心创新在于其受认知启发的时间编码机制。借鉴艾宾浩斯遗忘曲线（描述人类认知中记忆的指数衰减），时间编码器通过一个数学上优雅的公式来建模时间感知的用户兴趣衰减：

$$
A_{ts} = \alpha \cdot \gamma^{(T^{\beta})}
$$

其中，$T$表示相对时间矩阵，$T_{i,j} = |t_i - t_j|$，$\alpha$是可学习的基础兴趣强度，$\beta$控制缩放变换的非线性，$\gamma \in (0, 1)$是可学习的衰减参数。

这种方法比现有方法具有多项优势。与通过离散化导致不连续的“锯齿状”模式和信息丢失的基于桶的编码器不同，指数幂公式提供了平滑、连续的衰减曲线。可学习参数$\gamma$和$\beta$能够适应不同的行为模式，捕捉短期偏好（较小的$\gamma$）和长期兴趣（较大的$\gamma$）。

关键的是，该编码器采用显式数据类型预转换，在预处理期间将时间矩阵$T$从`int64`转换为`float32`。这种看似微小的优化消除了幂运算和指数运算过程中代价高昂的隐式运行时类型转换，显著提高了整体计算效率。

## 对角稀疏位置机制

第二项关键创新通过结构化稀疏注意力方法解决了位置编码冗余问题。该机制基于一个原则：许多位置注意力模式包含冗余信息，这些信息可以在不显著损失准确性的情况下进行修剪。

![对角稀疏机制](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：对角稀疏位置机制的四步过程：块划分、最左侧评分、对角滑动选择和最终稀疏注意力生成。*

该方法包括四个步骤：

1.  **块划分**：n×n的位置注意力图被划分为s×s的块，其中上三角区域被遮蔽以兼容仅解码器架构。

2.  **最左侧评分**：利用Toeplitz矩阵的性质，$W_{i,j} = W_{i+m,j+m}$，仅计算最左侧列中块的重要性分数，从而高效覆盖所有对角切片。

3.  **对角滑动选择**：根据重要性分数，按照剪枝率τ识别出k个最不重要的块。

4.  **块稀疏注意力**：将识别出的块在注意力图上进行对角“滑动”，生成稀疏掩码，将冗余的注意力权重归零，同时保留有意义的模式。

这种半结构化剪枝在保持准确性和计算效率之间提供了最佳平衡，其结构化特性确保了硬件友好的执行。

## 实验结果

在四个数据集（ML-1M、ML-20M、KuaiRand和工业音乐）上进行的综合实验表明，FuXi-γ在准确性和效率指标上均表现出色。

### 推荐性能

FuXi-γ始终达到最先进的推荐质量，在大型工业数据集上表现尤为出色。与其他自回归基线相比，FuXi-γ在公共数据集上平均提高了HR@10 3.79%、HR@50 2.37%、NDCG@10 4.46%、NDCG@50 3.49%和MRR 4.24%。在工业音乐数据集上，增益更为显著，平均HR@10高出25.06%，NDCG@10高出42.86%。

### 计算效率

![效率比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图3：训练（左）和推理（右）效率比较，显示了FuXi-γ的卓越性能，尤其是在长序列上。*

FuXi-γ在不同序列长度下均表现出卓越的计算效率。在序列长度为1000时，与LLaMa相比，训练速度提升高达4.74倍；与HSTU相比，提升4.48倍；同时，相对于其前身FuXi-β，仍保持1.86倍的加速。推理方面也观察到类似的改进，速度分别达到6.18倍和6.07倍。

### 时间编码器分析

![时间编码器比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-4.jpeg)
*图4：不同时间编码器在不同序列长度（左）和批次大小（右）下的效率比较。*

指数幂时间编码器在各种配置下始终表现出最低延迟，在序列长度为1000时，比基于桶的方法提速高达11.00倍，比反比例函数提速2.52倍。

![时间权重可视化](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-6.jpeg)
*图5：时间注意力权重可视化，展示了FuXi-γ产生的平滑衰减曲线，与其它方法产生的不连续模式形成对比。*

可视化结果表明，FuXi-γ产生了平滑、连续的衰减曲线，有效区分了短期和长期间隔，这与基于桶的编码器产生的不连续“锯齿状”模式形成了对比。

### 稀疏位置机制评估

![Sparsity Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12740v1/img-10.jpeg)
*图6：剪枝率τ对ML-20M数据集的影响，展示了NDCG@10性能（左）以及相应的FLOPs减少（右）。*

对角稀疏位置机制有效地减少了计算开销，同时保持了最小的精度损失。在ML-20M上，60%的剪枝率将位置注意力FLOPs减少了74.56%，同时保留了98.92%的原始精度。在其他数据集上也观察到了类似的结果，在某些情况下，由于正则化效应，甚至略微提高了精度。

## 技术贡献与意义

FuXi-γ在序列推荐领域做出了几项重要的技术贡献：

**认知启发式设计**：指数幂时间编码器代表了一种建模时间动态的原则性方法，将数学公式建立在既定的认知科学原理之上，而非临时的工程选择。

**硬件优化架构**：强调连续内存访问模式、纯矩阵操作和显式数据类型优化，展示了算法设计如何与硬件特性协同优化以实现显著的性能提升。

**结构化稀疏注意力**：对角稀疏机制提供了一种实用的注意力剪枝方法，既能保持精度又能显著提高效率，对于长序列场景尤其有价值。

**长序列的可扩展性**：所展示的随着序列长度增加仍能保持精度和效率的能力，解决了当前序列推荐系统中的一个关键限制。

## 局限性与未来方向

尽管FuXi-γ代表了显著的进步，但仍有一些局限性值得考虑。认知启发，虽然有理论基础，但可能无法泛化到所有用户行为模式或领域。稀疏注意力机制，尽管有效，需要仔细调整剪枝率和块大小等超参数以获得最佳性能。

未来的工作可以探索基于序列特征进行调整的自适应稀疏模式，整合超越遗忘曲线的其他认知原理，并扩展到多模态推荐场景。硬件优化策略也可以针对新兴计算架构进行进一步完善。

这项工作为高效、可扩展的序列推荐系统奠定了坚实的基础，这些系统在保持最先进精度的同时，满足了实际部署场景的计算限制。通过成功弥合理论进展与实际应用之间的差距，FuXi-γ代表了在生产环境中更广泛采用复杂推荐算法的重要一步。

abstract: Sequential recommendation aims to model users' evolving preferences based on their historical interactions. Recent advances leverage Transformer-based architectures to capture global dependencies, but existing methods often suffer from high computational overhead, primarily due to discontinuous memory access in temporal encoding and dense attention over long sequences. To address these limitations, we propose FuXi-$γ$, a novel sequential recommendation framework that improves both effectiveness and efficiency through principled architectural design. FuXi-$γ$ adopts a decoder-only Transformer structure and introduces two key innovations: (1) An exponential-power temporal encoder that encodes relative temporal intervals using a tunable exponential decay function inspired by the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve. This encoder enables flexible modeling of both short-term and long-term preferences while maintaining high efficiency through continuous memory access and pure matrix operations. (2) A diagonal-sparse positional mechanism that prunes low-contribution attention blocks using a diagonal-sliding strategy guided by the persymmetry of Toeplitz matrix. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that FuXi-$γ$ achieves state-of-the-art performance in recommendation quality, while accelerating training by up to 4.74$\times$ and inference by up to 6.18$\times$, making it a practical and scalable solution for long-sequence recommendation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Yeedzhi/FuXi-gamma.

abstract: Large-scale digitization initiatives have unlocked massive collections of historical newspapers, yet effective computational access remains hindered by OCR corruption, multilingual orthographic variation, and temporal language drift. We develop and evaluate a multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline specifically designed for question answering on noisy historical documents. Our approach integrates: (i) semantic query expansion and multi-query fusion using Reciprocal Rank Fusion to improve retrieval robustness against vocabulary mismatch; (ii) a carefully engineered generation prompt that enforces strict grounding in retrieved evidence and explicit abstention when evidence is insufficient; and (iii) a modular architecture enabling systematic component evaluation. We conduct comprehensive ablation studies on Named Entity Recognition and embedding model selection, demonstrating the importance of syntactic coherence in entity extraction and balanced performance-efficiency trade-offs in dense retrieval. Our end-to-end evaluation framework shows that the pipeline generates faithful answers for well-supported queries while correctly abstaining from unanswerable questions. The hybrid retrieval strategy improves recall stability, particularly benefiting from RRF's ability to smooth performance variance across query formulations. We release our code and configurations at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/RAGs-C5AE/, providing a reproducible foundation for robust historical document question answering.

en.title: Patch-wise Retrieval: A Bag of Practical Techniques for Instance-level Matching
en.abstract: Instance-level image retrieval aims to find images containing the same object as a given query, despite variations in size, position, or appearance. To address this challenging task, we propose Patchify, a simple yet effective patch-wise retrieval framework that offers high performance, scalability, and interpretability without requiring fine-tuning. Patchify divides each database image into a small number of structured patches and performs retrieval by comparing these local features with a global query descriptor, enabling accurate and spatially grounded matching. To assess not just retrieval accuracy but also spatial correctness, we introduce LocScore, a localization-aware metric that quantifies whether the retrieved region aligns with the target object. This makes LocScore a valuable diagnostic tool for understanding and improving retrieval behavior. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks, backbones, and region selection strategies, showing that Patchify outperforms global methods and complements state-of-the-art reranking pipelines. Furthermore, we apply Product Quantization for efficient large-scale retrieval and highlight the importance of using informative features during compression, which significantly boosts performance. Project website: this https URL

summary.summary: This research presents Patchify, a single-stage framework for instance-level image retrieval that uses structured multi-scale patches encoded by frozen pre-trained visual models. The system achieves high performance, scalability through product quantization, and inherent interpretability, outperforming global descriptors and offering a memory-efficient alternative to complex reranking pipelines.
originalProblem: Global descriptor-based retrieval methods struggle with small, occluded, or off-center object instances and lack fine-grained spatial detail.
State-of-the-art two-stage reranking pipelines, while accurate, demand substantial memory and computational resources, limiting scalability to large image databases.
Existing retrieval techniques often lack interpretability, failing to explicitly indicate which specific image regions contribute to a successful match.
Deploying high-performance instance retrieval systems in practical, large-scale scenarios is often hindered by the need for extensive fine-tuning or complex multi-stage setups.
solution: Introduces 'Patchify,' a single-stage pipeline that decomposes database images into a small, fixed number of structured multi-scale grid patches.
Utilizes frozen, pre-trained general-purpose visual encoders (e.g., DINOv2, CLIP, SigLIP) to encode each patch, avoiding domain-specific fine-tuning.
Employs max-similarity retrieval for ranking and integrates Product Quantization (IVFPQ) to enable memory-efficient and scalable approximate nearest neighbor search.
Proposes LocScore, a novel localization-aware metric, to evaluate retrieval quality based on both accuracy and the spatial alignment of matched regions.
keyInsights: Structured, sparse multi-scale patch representations consistently and substantially outperform global descriptors for instance-level matching, especially with challenging object instances.
The effectiveness of visual encoders for retrieval is highly dependent on the scale of their pre-training data, with larger datasets yielding better generalization regardless of architecture.
Product Quantization effectively compresses patch descriptors for scalable retrieval with minimal performance drop, but the quality of features used for PQ training is critical.
The LocScore metric provides valuable diagnostic insights, showing that high retrieval accuracy (mAP) can occur even when matched regions are spatially imprecise.
results: Patchify consistently achieves superior retrieval performance (mAP) compared to global baselines across multiple datasets (INSTRE, ILIAS) and backbones, particularly with transformer-based models and larger pre-training datasets.
The framework demonstrates remarkable memory efficiency, requiring significantly less storage (e.g., 5.75x less on mini-ILIAS) than state-of-the-art reranking methods.
When integrated into a two-stage pipeline, Patchify functions as an effective first-stage representation, boosting overall performance and often matching or surpassing prior reranking baselines.

Experiments confirm LocScore's diagnostic utility by revealing instances where high mAP coexists with low spatial alignment, highlighting the importance of evaluating both aspects of retrieval quality.

en.overview:
## Problem Motivation and Approach

Instance-level image retrieval is a fundamental computer vision task that seeks to find images containing the exact same object instance as a query, despite variations in scale, viewpoint, lighting, or background clutter. While global image descriptors offer efficiency and have benefited from large-scale pre-training, they often struggle with objects that are small, occluded, or positioned off-center. Conversely, dense local feature methods provide better accuracy but incur significant computational and memory overhead that limits their scalability.

![Interpretability comparison between previous methods and Patchify approach](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-0.jpeg)

This paper introduces "Patchify," a patch-wise retrieval framework that bridges the gap between efficient global methods and accurate local approaches. The key innovation lies in decomposing images into a small, fixed number of structured multi-scale grid patches rather than dense local descriptors, while maintaining the interpretability that allows users to understand which specific region triggered a match.

## Core Methodology: Patchify Framework

The Patchify pipeline operates through several interconnected components designed for both performance and scalability. The framework decomposes each database image into structured, non-overlapping grid patches at multiple scales. For example, the L2 configuration combines patches from 1×1 (global), 2×2, and 3×3 grids, creating a hierarchical representation with only 14 total patches per image.

![Patchify pipeline overview showing multi-scale patch decomposition and similarity search](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-1.jpeg)

Each extracted patch is independently encoded using frozen, pre-trained visual encoders such as DINOv2, CLIP, or SigLIP. This zero-shot approach eliminates the need for domain-specific fine-tuning while leveraging the representation power of large-scale pre-trained models. During retrieval, the global descriptor of the query image is compared against all patch-level descriptors from database images, with the maximum similarity score determining the final ranking.

To enable large-scale deployment, the framework incorporates Product Quantization (PQ) for descriptor compression. This significantly reduces memory footprint while maintaining fast approximate nearest neighbor search capabilities, making patch-wise retrieval practical for massive databases.

## LocScore: Spatial Evaluation Metric

A significant contribution of this work is the introduction of LocScore, a localization-aware evaluation metric that goes beyond traditional retrieval accuracy measures. LocScore combines retrieval precision with spatial alignment quality by incorporating the Intersection over Union (IoU) between predicted patch locations and ground-truth object bounding boxes.

The metric is formulated as:

$$
\text{LocScore} = \frac{1}{|Q|} \sum_{q \in Q} \sum_{r \in R_q^+} \frac{\text{IoU}(r, q) \cdot \text{precision}(r)}{\text{rank}(r)}
$$

where $Q$ represents queries, $R_q^+$ denotes positive retrievals for query $q$, and the precision and ranking terms weight the spatial accuracy by retrieval quality.

![Examples of LocScore evaluation showing spatial alignment between predicted patches and ground truth](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-3.jpeg)

## Experimental Results and Key Findings

The evaluation demonstrates several important findings across multiple benchmarks (INSTRE, ILIAS) and visual encoders. Most significantly, patch-wise representations consistently outperform global descriptors across all tested configurations, with particularly strong improvements for challenging scenarios involving small or occluded objects.

![Qualitative comparison showing global vs. Patchify retrieval results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-2.jpeg)

The scale of pre-training emerges as a critical factor, with models trained on larger datasets (such as ConvNeXt on LAION-2B or SigLIP on WebLI) demonstrating superior performance regardless of architecture. Transformer-based encoders generally outperform CNN-based counterparts, though the pre-training scale often matters more than architectural choice.

Memory efficiency represents another key advantage, with Patchify using 5.75× less storage than state-of-the-art reranking methods while achieving competitive or superior performance. The integration with Product Quantization further reduces memory usage with minimal performance degradation.

![Memory comparison showing Patchify's efficiency advantage](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-6.jpeg)

## Multi-Scale Analysis and Feature Behavior

The framework's multi-scale approach reveals interesting patterns in how different patch levels contribute to retrieval performance. Analysis across various object characteristics shows that local features particularly excel with smaller objects and those positioned away from image centers, where global descriptors struggle.

![Performance analysis across different object sizes and positions](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-7.jpeg)

The LocScore metric proves valuable as a diagnostic tool, revealing cases where high retrieval accuracy (mAP) masks poor spatial localization. This insight helps identify when matches are based on background similarities rather than the target object, providing crucial feedback for system improvement.

## Impact and Practical Significance

Patchify addresses several critical limitations in current instance retrieval systems. By eliminating fine-tuning requirements while maintaining strong performance, it significantly reduces the barrier to deployment across diverse domains. The built-in interpretability through explicit patch attribution represents a meaningful step toward more transparent AI systems, allowing users to understand why specific images were retrieved.

The framework's scalability advantages make it particularly suitable for real-world applications requiring large-scale image databases, while the comprehensive evaluation methodology, including the LocScore metric, provides a more complete assessment of retrieval system performance that considers both accuracy and spatial precision.

This work establishes a practical middle ground between global and dense local approaches, offering a compelling combination of performance, efficiency, and interpretability that should prove valuable for both research and industrial applications in visual search and recognition systems.

zh.title: 分块检索：面向实例级匹配的实用技术集
zh.abstract:
实例级图像检索旨在查找包含与给定查询相同对象的图像，即便这些对象在尺寸、位置或外观上存在差异。为应对这一挑战性任务，我们提出了 Patchify，一个简单而有效的基于图像块的检索框架。它无需微调，即可提供高性能、可扩展性和可解释性。Patchify 将每个数据库图像划分为少量结构化图像块，并通过将这些局部特征与全局查询描述符进行比较来执行检索，从而实现准确且具有空间定位（spatially grounded）的匹配。

为了不仅评估检索准确性，还评估其空间正确性，我们引入了 LocScore，这是一种定位感知指标，用于量化检索到的区域是否与目标对象对齐。LocScore 因此成为理解和改进检索行为的宝贵诊断工具。我们在多个基准、骨干网络和区域选择策略上进行了大量实验，结果表明 Patchify 优于全局方法，并能有效补充最先进的重排序（reranking）流程。此外，我们应用乘积量化（Product Quantization）以实现高效的大规模检索，并强调在压缩过程中使用信息丰富特征的重要性，这显著提升了性能。

项目网站：this https URL

summary.summary: 本研究提出了Patchify，一个用于实例级图像检索的单阶段框架，该框架利用由冻结的预训练视觉模型编码的结构化多尺度图像块。该系统实现了高性能，通过乘积量化实现了可扩展性，并具有固有的可解释性，其性能优于全局描述符，并为复杂的重排序流水线提供了一种内存高效的替代方案。
originalProblem: 基于全局描述符的检索方法在处理小型、被遮挡或偏离中心的物体实例时表现不佳，并且缺乏细粒度的空间细节。
最先进的两阶段重排序流水线虽然准确，但需要大量的内存和计算资源，限制了其在大规模图像数据库中的可扩展性。
现有的检索技术通常缺乏可解释性，未能明确指出哪些特定的图像区域促成了成功的匹配。
在实际的大规模场景中部署高性能实例检索系统常常因需要大量的微调或复杂的多阶段设置而受阻。
solution: 引入“Patchify”，一个单阶段流水线，将数据库图像分解为少量、固定数量的结构化多尺度网格图像块。
利用冻结的、预训练的通用视觉编码器（例如DINOv2、CLIP、SigLIP）来编码每个图像块，避免了领域特定的微调。
采用最大相似度检索进行排名，并集成乘积量化（IVFPQ）以实现内存高效和可扩展的近似最近邻搜索。
提出了一种新颖的局部化感知度量LocScore，用于根据准确性和匹配区域的空间对齐来评估检索质量。
keyInsights: 结构化、稀疏的多尺度图像块表示在实例级匹配中始终显著优于全局描述符，尤其是在处理具有挑战性的物体实例时。
视觉编码器用于检索的有效性高度依赖于其预训练数据规模，更大的数据集无论架构如何都能产生更好的泛化能力。
乘积量化有效压缩图像块描述符以实现可扩展检索，同时性能下降最小，但用于PQ训练的特征质量至关重要。
LocScore度量提供了有价值的诊断洞察，表明即使匹配区域在空间上不精确，也可能出现高检索准确性（mAP）。
results: Patchify在多个数据集（INSTRE、ILIAS）和骨干网络上，特别是对于基于Transformer的模型和更大的预训练数据集，始终比全局基线实现更优的检索性能（mAP）。
该框架展现出卓越的内存效率，比最先进的重排序方法所需的存储空间显著减少（例如，在mini-ILIAS上减少5.75倍）。
当集成到两阶段流水线中时，Patchify作为有效的第一个阶段表示，提高了整体性能，并且通常匹配或超越了先前的重排序基线。
实验证实了LocScore的诊断效用，揭示了高mAP与低空间对齐并存的情况，强调了评估检索质量这两个方面的重要性。

zh.overview:
## 问题动机与方法

实例级图像检索是一项基础的计算机视觉任务，旨在寻找包含与查询图像完全相同对象实例的图像，尽管存在尺度、视角、光照或背景杂波的差异。虽然全局图像描述符效率高，并受益于大规模预训练，但它们在处理小型、被遮挡或偏离中心的对象时常常表现不佳。相反，密集局部特征方法提供了更高的准确性，但会产生显著的计算和内存开销，从而限制了其可扩展性。

![先前方法与Patchify方法的解释性比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-0.jpeg)

本文介绍了“Patchify”，一个基于补丁的检索框架，它弥合了高效全局方法和准确局部方法之间的差距。关键创新在于将图像分解成少量固定数量的结构化多尺度网格补丁，而不是密集局部描述符，同时保持了可解释性，允许用户理解是哪个特定区域触发了匹配。

## 核心方法论：Patchify 框架

Patchify 管道通过几个相互关联的组件运行，这些组件旨在兼顾性能和可扩展性。该框架将每个数据库图像分解成多个尺度的结构化、非重叠网格补丁。例如，L2 配置结合了来自 1×1（全局）、2×2 和 3×3 网格的补丁，为每张图像创建了一个仅包含 14 个补丁的分层表示。

![Patchify 管道概述，显示多尺度补丁分解和相似性搜索](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-1.jpeg)

每个提取的补丁都使用冻结的、预训练的视觉编码器（如 DINOv2、CLIP 或 SigLIP）独立编码。这种零样本方法消除了对领域特定微调的需求，同时利用了大规模预训练模型的表示能力。在检索过程中，查询图像的全局描述符与数据库图像的所有补丁级描述符进行比较，通过最大相似度得分确定最终排名。

为了实现大规模部署，该框架引入了乘积量化（PQ）进行描述符压缩。这显著减少了内存占用，同时保持了快速的近似最近邻搜索能力，使得基于补丁的检索在大规模数据库中变得实用。

## LocScore：空间评估指标

这项工作的一个重要贡献是引入了 LocScore，这是一个超越传统检索准确度衡量标准的、感知定位的评估指标。LocScore 通过将预测补丁位置与真实对象边界框之间的交并比（IoU）结合起来，将检索精度与空间对齐质量相结合。

该指标的公式为：

$$
\text{LocScore} = \frac{1}{|Q|} \sum_{q \in Q} \sum_{r \in R_q^+} \frac{\text{IoU}(r, q) \cdot \text{precision}(r)}{\text{rank}(r)}
$$

其中 $Q$ 表示查询，$R_q^+$ 表示查询 $q$ 的正向检索结果，精度和排名项根据检索质量对空间精度进行加权。

![LocScore 评估示例，显示预测补丁与真实标签之间的空间对齐](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-3.jpeg)

## 实验结果和主要发现

评估结果显示了在多个基准（INSTRE、ILIAS）和视觉编码器上的几个重要发现。最重要的是，基于补丁的表示在所有测试配置中始终优于全局描述符，尤其是在涉及小型或被遮挡对象的挑战性场景中，改进效果显著。

![全局与Patchify检索结果的定性比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-2.jpeg)

预训练的规模是一个关键因素，在更大数据集（如在LAION-2B上训练的ConvNeXt或在WebLI上训练的SigLIP）上训练的模型表现出卓越的性能，无论架构如何。基于Transformer的编码器通常优于基于CNN的对应物，尽管预训练规模的重要性往往超过架构选择。

内存效率是另一个关键优势，Patchify使用的存储空间比最先进的重排序方法少5.75倍，同时实现了有竞争力或更优的性能。与乘积量化的集成进一步减少了内存使用，同时性能下降微乎其微。

![内存比较显示Patchify的效率优势](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-6.jpeg)

## 多尺度分析与特征行为

该框架的多尺度方法揭示了不同补丁级别如何影响检索性能的有趣模式。对各种对象特征的分析表明，局部特征在处理较小对象和远离图像中心的对象时表现出色，而全局描述符在这种情况下则表现不力。

![不同对象大小和位置的性能分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12610v1/img-7.jpeg)

LocScore指标被证明是一个有价值的诊断工具，它揭示了高检索精度（mAP）可能掩盖了糟糕的空间定位的情况。这一见解有助于识别匹配是基于背景相似性而非目标对象的情况，为系统改进提供了关键反馈。

## 影响与实际意义

Patchify解决了当前实例检索系统中的几个关键限制。通过消除微调要求同时保持强大性能，它显著降低了在不同领域部署的门槛。通过明确的补丁归因实现内置可解释性，是迈向更透明AI系统的重要一步，允许用户理解为什么检索到特定图像。

该框架的可扩展性优势使其特别适用于需要大规模图像数据库的实际应用，而包括LocScore指标在内的全面评估方法，提供了对检索系统性能更完整的评估，同时考虑了准确性和空间精度。

这项工作在全球和密集局部方法之间建立了一个实用的中间地带，提供了性能、效率和可解释性的引人注目的结合，这对于视觉搜索和识别系统中的研究和工业应用都将证明是宝贵的。

abstract: Instance-level image retrieval aims to find images containing the same object as a given query, despite variations in size, position, or appearance. To address this challenging task, we propose Patchify, a simple yet effective patch-wise retrieval framework that offers high performance, scalability, and interpretability without requiring fine-tuning. Patchify divides each database image into a small number of structured patches and performs retrieval by comparing these local features with a global query descriptor, enabling accurate and spatially grounded matching. To assess not just retrieval accuracy but also spatial correctness, we introduce LocScore, a localization-aware metric that quantifies whether the retrieved region aligns with the target object. This makes LocScore a valuable diagnostic tool for understanding and improving retrieval behavior. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks, backbones, and region selection strategies, showing that Patchify outperforms global methods and complements state-of-the-art reranking pipelines. Furthermore, we apply Product Quantization for efficient large-scale retrieval and highlight the importance of using informative features during compression, which significantly boosts performance. Project website: https://wons20k.github.io/PatchwiseRetrieval/
title: Patch-wise Retrieval: A Bag of Practical Techniques for Instance-level Matching

abstract: Modern vector databases enable efficient retrieval over high-dimensional neural embeddings, powering applications from web search to retrieval-augmented generation. However, classical theory predicts such tasks should suffer from the curse of dimensionality, where distances between points become nearly indistinguishable, thereby crippling efficient nearest-neighbor search. We revisit this paradox through the lens of stability, the property that small perturbations to a query do not radically alter its nearest neighbors. Building on foundational results, we extend stability theory to three key retrieval settings widely used in practice: (i) multi-vector search, where we prove that the popular Chamfer distance metric preserves single-vector stability, while average pooling aggregation may destroy it; (ii) filtered vector search, where we show that sufficiently large penalties for mismatched filters can induce stability even when the underlying search is unstable; and (iii) sparse vector search, where we formalize and prove novel sufficient stability conditions. Across synthetic and real datasets, our experimental results match our theoretical predictions, offering concrete guidance for model and system design to avoid the curse of dimensionality.
title: Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality: On the Stability of Modern Vector Retrieval

zh.title: WeDetect: 快速开放词汇目标检测即检索
zh.abstract:
开放词汇目标检测旨在通过文本提示检测任意类别。不含跨模态融合层的方法（非融合方法）通过将识别视为一个检索问题，即在共享嵌入空间中匹配区域与文本查询，从而提供更快的推理速度。在这项工作中，我们全面探索了这种检索理念，并通过一个名为 WeDetect 的模型家族，展示了其在效率和多功能性方面的独特优势，具体包括：

(1) **最先进的性能**。WeDetect 是一个采用双塔架构的实时检测器。我们表明，凭借精心策划的数据和充分的训练，非融合的 WeDetect 能够超越其他融合模型，并奠定强大的开放词汇基础。
(2) **历史数据的快速回溯**。WeDetect-Uni 是一个基于 WeDetect 的通用候选框生成器。我们冻结了整个检测器，仅微调一个目标性提示，以检索跨类别的通用目标候选框。重要的是，这些候选框嵌入是类别特定的，并催生了一项新应用——目标检索，支持在历史数据中检索目标。
(3) **与大型多模态模型（LMM）集成以实现指代表达理解（REC）**。我们进一步提出了 WeDetect-Ref，一个基于 LMM 的目标分类器，用于处理复杂的指代表达。它从 WeDetect-Uni 提取的候选框列表中检索目标对象，摒弃了下一词元预测，并在单次前向传播中完成目标分类。

综上所述，WeDetect 家族在一个连贯的检索框架下，统一了检测、候选框生成、目标检索和指代表达理解（REC），在 15 个基准测试中均实现了最先进的性能，并具有高推理效率。

summary.summary: WeDetect引入了一个基于检索的框架，用于开放词汇目标检测、通用候选区域生成和指代表达式理解，在保持实时推理速度的同时，实现了最先进的准确性。该框架并行处理目标，在效率上显著优于基于融合和顺序解码的方法。
originalProblem: 现有的使用深度跨模态融合层的开放词汇目标检测（OVD）方法存在显著的计算开销和缓慢的推理速度问题。
用于指代表达式理解（REC）的大型视觉-语言模型（LVLMs）由于顺序的下一词元预测，在精确边界框回归和缓慢推理方面表现不佳。
之前的非融合（双塔）OVD方法虽然高效，但通常缺乏基于融合方法所能实现的细粒度视觉-语言对齐和准确性。
solution: WeDetect框架采用双塔、非融合架构，将开放词汇识别视为共享嵌入空间中的快速检索问题。
通过使用自动目标性检测器和用于分层标签生成的微调MLLM，构建了一个包含3.3亿个边界框标注的大规模高质量基础数据集。
WeDetect-Ref将REC重新定义为LLM内的检索任务，通过一个二元分类头并行处理多个目标候选区域，从而绕过顺序解码并提高定位准确性。
keyInsights: 精心设计的非融合双塔架构，结合细致的数据整理和分阶段训练，可以在实时推理速度下实现最先进的OVD性能，挑战了深度跨模态融合的必要性。
将指代表达式理解重新定义为基于LLM的检索问题，与传统顺序解码相比可实现13倍的速度提升，同时提高准确性。
通过冻结一个强大的检测器并训练一个单一的可学习目标性提示，可以有效地实现通用目标候选区域生成和细粒度目标检索，从而支持诸如局部目标搜索等新应用。
results: WeDetect-Tiny在LVIS数据集上以62.5帧/秒的速度达到31.4 AP，超过YOLO-World-L 2.0-4.6 AP，同时更快更小，展示了在不牺牲准确性的前提下卓越的效率。
WeDetect-Large在LVIS数据集上达到49.4 AP，比LLMDet高出7.4 AP，比T-Rex2高出3.6 AP，并且比Grounding-DINO快3-6倍。
WeDetect-Ref 4B在RefCOCO/+/g上取得93.2的平均分数，比Qwen3-VL 4B提速13倍，并且是第一个在COCO数据集上AP超过50（50.0 AP）的LMM。

zh.overview:
## 引言

目标检测已从传统的封闭集分类发展到更灵活的开放词汇方法，后者可以通过文本描述检测任意指定的对象类别。“WeDetect：作为检索的快速开放词汇目标检测”研究论文介绍了一个全面的框架，将视觉识别视为一个检索问题，从而在多个视觉-语言任务中实现了高准确性和实时性能。

WeDetect家族包含三个专用模型：用于开放词汇目标检测的WeDetect，用于通用提议生成和对象检索的WeDetect-Uni，以及使用大型语言模型进行指代表达理解的WeDetect-Ref。这种统一的方法表明，基于检索的方法可以实现最先进的结果，同时保持现有基于融合的方法难以匹敌的计算效率。

![WeDetect 架构概览](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：核心WeDetect架构采用双塔设计，分别设有文本编码器和视觉编码器，通过对比学习执行对象分类，无需计算成本高昂的跨模态融合层。*

## 基于检索的方法论

WeDetect 的根本创新在于它致力于将对象识别视为一个检索问题，而不是依赖于深度跨模态融合。传统的开放词汇检测方法，如 Grounding-DINO，通过密集的融合层（融合视觉和文本特征）实现了高准确性，但这种方法带来了显著的计算成本，通常每张图像需要数秒的推理时间。

WeDetect 采用双塔架构，其中视觉和文本表示被单独处理，并在共享的嵌入空间中进行匹配。视觉编码器使用带有 CSPRepBiFPAN 颈部的 ConvNeXt 主干，而文本编码器使用 XLM-RoBERTa。分类通过区域特征和文本嵌入之间的简单点积操作进行，无需针对查询的特征计算。

这种架构选择实现了关键的效率提升。视觉特征可以一次计算并跨多个文本查询重复使用，使得该系统特别适合需要对大型类别词汇进行评估的应用。例如，在 LVIS 上对 1,203 个类别进行评估时，传统的融合方法必须为每个类别执行单独的前向传播，而 WeDetect 则一次性计算视觉特征并执行快速相似度匹配。

## 数据整理与训练策略

WeDetect 成功的关键组成部分是其庞大且精心策划的训练数据集。研究人员从 SAM-1B、LAION、CC12M 和各种目标检测数据集等不同来源收集了 1500 万张图像。其关键创新在于他们的自动标注流程，该流程为每个检测到的对象生成高质量、多粒度的标签。

标注过程使用对象性检测器识别潜在对象，然后由一个微调的多模态大型语言模型（Qwen2.5-VL 7B）生成分层标签。例如，一个对象可能收到多个粒度的标签：“动物”、“狗”和“一只黄狗”。这种多粒度方法提供了丰富的监督，帮助模型学习细粒度的视觉-语言对齐，而无需依赖融合层。

训练遵循三阶段方法：

$$
\text{阶段 1: CLIP 风格预训练} \rightarrow \text{阶段 2: 头部和颈部训练} \rightarrow \text{阶段 3: 端到端微调}
$$

在训练过程中，标签会从每个对象的候选列表中随机采样，从而创建多样化的负样本并丰富文本多样性。事实证明，这种策略对于实现强大的开放词汇性能至关重要。

## WeDetect-Uni：通用目标提议

在WeDetect基础之上，WeDetect-Uni解决了对类别无关目标提议的需求，并引入了一项名为“目标检索”的新任务。该模型通过冻结整个WeDetect检测器并仅训练一个可学习的目标性提示符来创建，从而有效地将分类头部重新用于通用目标检测。

![WeDetect-Uni 架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：WeDetect-Uni通过引入一个可学习的目标性提示符来扩展基础架构，同时冻结预训练的WeDetect参数，从而实现通用目标提议生成。*

目标检索能力相对于CLIP等传统图像级检索系统是一个重大进步。虽然CLIP可以找到包含特定概念的图像，但WeDetect-Uni可以根据细粒度的局部目标来识别和检索图像。该系统预先提取目标提议及其嵌入，通过查询嵌入与缓存目标特征之间的简单点积操作实现快速检索。

![目标检索示例](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-4.jpeg)
*图3：WeDetect-Uni的目标检索能力允许用户在图像中搜索特定目标，展示了超越传统图像级检索的细粒度局部感知能力。*

## WeDetect-Ref：基于LLM的指代表达理解

WeDetect-Ref通过将指代表达理解（REC）重新表述为大型语言模型框架内的检索问题来解决。传统的LLM由于边界框回归能力差和顺序解码速度慢而难以处理REC。WeDetect-Ref通过将REC视为目标分类而非坐标预测来克服这些限制。

![WeDetect-Ref 架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图4：WeDetect-Ref通过一个二元分类头部并行处理目标提议，避免了LLM中常见的顺序令牌生成所带来的计算开销。*

该过程始于WeDetect-Uni生成目标提议。多尺度RoI特征被提取并通过线性投影器压缩成单个“目标令牌”。LLM（基于Qwen3-VL）同时处理完整的图像、用户查询和所有目标令牌。一个二元分类头部确定哪些目标与指代表达匹配，从而实现并行处理而不是顺序生成。

训练涉及三个阶段：使用标注数据进行区域投影器训练，使用指令数据进行区域感知微调，以及使用检测数据集进行区域分类训练。这种方法实现了显著的效率提升——WeDetect-Ref的运行速度比基础Qwen3-VL模型快13倍，同时达到了更高的准确性。

## 性能结果与分析

WeDetect在多个基准测试中展现出卓越的性能，同时保持了优越的推理速度。基础WeDetect模型在LVIS、COCO和ODinW数据集上取得了最先进的结果。值得注意的是，WeDetect-Large在LVIS上达到了49.4 AP，以显著优势超越了以往的方法，并且比同类融合模型快3倍。

![检测结果](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-5.jpeg)
*图5：WeDetect通过细粒度类别识别和精确本地化，在多样化场景中实现全面的目标检测。*

WeDetect-Uni在通用提议生成和目标检索任务中表现出色。该模型在标准基准测试中实现了高召回率，并在所提出的目标检索任务中表现出卓越性能，相比图像级CLIP基线，F1分数提高了37.2点。

WeDetect-Ref 在指代表达理解方面树立了新标杆，在 RefCOCO/+/g 数据集上取得了 93.2 的平均分数，运行速度达到 5.3 帧/秒，而传统 LLM 方法的速度为 0.4 帧/秒。该模型也成为首个在 COCO 检测上 AP 超过 50（50.0 AP）的 LMM，展示了其在不同视觉理解任务中的多功能性。

![通用提案](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-6.jpeg)
*图 6：WeDetect-Uni 在各种场景中生成全面的物体提案，为包括物体检索和指代表达理解在内的各种下游应用提供了基础。*

## 独特贡献与创新

WeDetect 的主要贡献在于证明了基于检索的方法可以达到或超越计算密集型融合方法的性能，同时保持实时推理速度。这挑战了深度跨模态融合对于高精度开放词汇检测是必要的主流假设。

引入物体检索作为一项新任务，解决了细粒度视觉搜索能力方面的一个显著空白。与图像级检索系统不同，WeDetect-Uni 使用户能够在图像中搜索特定物体，为详细的视觉探索和验证开辟了新的可能性。

将指代表达理解重构为 LLM 内的检索问题，代表了一种范式转变，克服了传统语言模型方法在视觉定位方面的根本局限性。通过避免边界框回归和序列解码，WeDetect-Ref 实现了更高的准确性和显著提高的效率。

## 技术创新与实施细节

自动标注管道代表了一项重大的技术成就，它将物体检测与微调的多模态语言模型相结合，以大规模生成高质量、分层标签。多粒度标注策略对于训练没有融合层的有效双塔模型至关重要。

三阶段训练方法在保留预训练知识与任务特定适应之间实现了精细的平衡。分阶段方法防止了对有价值的 CLIP 式表示的破坏，同时实现了有效的区域级学习。

对于 WeDetect-Ref，通过二元分类头实现的并行物体处理机制，代表了与序列 LLM 生成的根本区别，从而在保持大型模型语言理解能力的同时显著提高了速度。

![REC 结果](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.12309v1/img-9.jpeg)
*图 7：WeDetect-Ref 展示了精确的指代表达理解能力，能够根据复杂的自然语言描述准确识别物体。*

## 更广泛的影响与意义

WeDetect 的基于检索的方法不仅对物体检测有影响，还可能影响未来视觉语言模型的设计。效率和准确性并非互斥的证明挑战了现有的架构假设，并可能启发多模态学习的新方法。

实时性能使先进的开放词汇检测适用于以前受计算限制的应用，包括自主系统、增强现实和实时内容分析。涵盖检测、提案生成和指代表达理解的统一框架为各种视觉理解应用提供了全面的基础。

引入物体检索作为一项新能力，解决了视觉搜索和内容分析中的实际需求，实现了比以前基于图像的方法更细粒度、更精确的视觉查询系统。
