en.title: VLM2GeoVec: Toward Universal Multimodal Embeddings for Remote Sensing
en.abstract: Satellite imagery differs fundamentally from natural images: its aerial viewpoint, very high resolution, diverse scale variations, and abundance of small objects demand both region-level spatial reasoning and holistic scene understanding. Current remote-sensing approaches remain fragmented between dual-encoder retrieval models, which excel at large-scale cross-modal search but cannot interleave modalities, and generative assistants, which support region-level interpretation but lack scalable retrieval capabilities. We propose $\textbf{VLM2GeoVec}$, an instruction-following, single-encoder vision-language model trained contrastively to embed interleaved inputs (images, text, bounding boxes, and geographic coordinates) in a unified vector space. Our single encoder interleaves all inputs into one joint embedding trained with a contrastive loss, eliminating multi-stage pipelines and task-specific modules. To evaluate its versatility, we introduce $\textbf{RSMEB}$, a novel benchmark covering key remote-sensing embedding applications: scene classification; cross-modal search; compositional retrieval; visual-question answering; visual grounding and region-level reasoning; and semantic geospatial retrieval. On RSMEB, it achieves $\textbf{26.6%}$ P@1 on region-caption retrieval (+25 pp vs. dual-encoder baselines), $\textbf{32.5%}$ P@1 on referring-expression retrieval (+19 pp), and $\textbf{17.8%}$ P@1 on semantic geo-localization retrieval (over $3\times$ prior best), while matching or exceeding specialized baselines on conventional tasks such as scene classification and cross-modal retrieval. VLM2GeoVec unifies scalable retrieval with region-level spatial reasoning, enabling cohesive multimodal analysis in remote sensing. We will publicly release the code, checkpoints, and data upon acceptance.

summary.summary: VLM2GeoVec is introduced as an instruction-following single-encoder vision-language model that generates universal multimodal embeddings for remote sensing, seamlessly integrating images, text, bounding boxes, and geographic coordinates into a unified vector space. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on the new RSMEB benchmark, showing a +25.31 percentage point gain in region-caption retrieval and over a 3x improvement in semantic geo-localization retrieval compared to previous baselines.
originalProblem: Existing vision-language models for remote sensing are fragmented, with dual-encoders lacking fine-grained spatial integration and generative models lacking scalable retrieval.
General-purpose VLMs suffer from a 'domain shift' when applied to remote sensing imagery, leading to weaker cross-modal performance and failure in metadata-aware tasks.

Evaluation benchmarks for remote sensing are typically task-specific, hindering a holistic assessment of a model's multimodal retrieval and reasoning capabilities, especially concerning spatial metadata.
solution: Developed VLM2GeoVec, a single-encoder, instruction-following VLM that interleaves visual tokens, descriptive text, bounding boxes, and latitude-longitude coordinates into a unified token stream.

Employed instruction-conditioned contrastive learning with InfoNCE loss and a large effective batch size, using LoRA adapters for efficient fine-tuning of a Qwen2-VL backbone initialized from VLM2Vec checkpoints.
Introduced RSMEB, a comprehensive, unified ranking-based benchmark consolidating 21 tasks across 6 meta-tasks to holistically evaluate multimodal remote sensing embedding models.
keyInsights: A single-encoder architecture with deep multimodal interleaving provides more coherent contextual understanding and reasoning across images, text, and spatial metadata than fragmented approaches.
Instruction-conditioned contrastive pretraining, combined with domain adaptation, effectively overcomes the 'domain shift' challenge for general-purpose VLMs in remote sensing.
Unified evaluation across diverse tasks through a benchmark like RSMEB is crucial for driving holistic progress in multimodal remote sensing AI, moving beyond task-specific optimizations.
results: VLM2GeoVec achieved the lowest overall Friedman score (1.93) on the RSMEB benchmark, outperforming all general-purpose and specialized remote sensing baselines across 21 tasks.

Demonstrated substantial improvements in novel multimodal tasks, including a +25.31 percentage point gain in Region-Caption Retrieval P@1 and over a 3x improvement in Semantic Geo-localization Retrieval P@1 compared to prior best baselines.

Achieved competitive or superior performance in conventional tasks like zero-shot scene classification (e.g., 77.25% on AID, 79.76% on PatternNet) and cross-modal retrieval, validating its effective domain adaptation.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Remote sensing applications have experienced tremendous growth with the proliferation of high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery. However, the unique characteristics of remote sensing data - including overhead perspectives, extreme scale variations, and the prevalence of small objects - present distinct challenges that differentiate this domain from conventional computer vision tasks. Current vision-language models (VLMs) designed for remote sensing face a fundamental trade-off: dual-encoder models excel at large-scale cross-modal retrieval but cannot handle fine-grained spatial metadata, while generative models provide detailed spatial reasoning but lack efficient retrieval capabilities.

![Performance comparison across 21 tasks in RSMEB showing VLM2GeoVec (green) outperforming existing models](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-0.jpeg)

VLM2GeoVec addresses this limitation by introducing a unified single-encoder architecture that seamlessly integrates images, text, bounding boxes, and geographic coordinates into universal multimodal embeddings. This work represents a significant step toward creating truly versatile remote sensing AI systems capable of both scalable retrieval and precise spatial reasoning within a single framework.

## Problem Statement and Motivation

The remote sensing domain faces several critical challenges that existing multimodal models fail to address comprehensively. Traditional dual-encoder VLMs like CLIP and its remote sensing variants (RemoteCLIP, SkyCLIP) process images holistically and cannot incorporate spatial metadata such as bounding boxes or geographic coordinates into unified queries. This architectural limitation severely restricts their applicability for tasks requiring precise spatial understanding.

Conversely, generative VLM assistants designed for remote sensing (GeoChat, TEOChat) excel at region-level interpretation and visual question answering but lack the efficient embedding-based retrieval mechanisms necessary for searching large-scale image archives. This fragmentation forces practitioners to use different model architectures for different aspects of the same workflow.

Furthermore, existing evaluation frameworks are task-specific and fail to provide comprehensive assessment of multimodal capabilities. The absence of unified benchmarks that incorporate spatial and geospatial metadata integration has hindered progress toward developing truly universal remote sensing embeddings.

## Methodology

### VLM2GeoVec Architecture

VLM2GeoVec employs a single-encoder architecture built upon the Qwen2-VL backbone, initialized from pre-trained VLM2Vec checkpoints. The core innovation lies in its ability to process interleaved multimodal token streams containing up to four distinct modalities:

**Visual Processing**: Images are processed at 336×336 resolution using a ViT-L-14 backbone, generating 14×14 patch-based visual tokens that capture both macro-level scene context and micro-level spatial details.

**Textual Integration**: Descriptive text, captions, and task instructions are tokenized and integrated directly into the token stream, enabling instruction-following behavior.

**Spatial Metadata**: Axis-aligned bounding boxes are normalized to [0, 100] range and incorporated as textual tokens, allowing precise region specification within images.

**Geospatial Coordinates**: Latitude-longitude coordinates are encoded as textual tuples (e.g., "(34.052275, 118.243739)"), enabling geographic context integration.

![VLM2GeoVec architecture showing multimodal input processing and unified embedding generation](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-1.jpeg)

The model utilizes Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) layers injected into self-attention and MLP components, enabling efficient fine-tuning while preserving the pre-trained backbone's capabilities. The interleaved token stream is processed by the single encoder, with embeddings derived from the final token of each sequence.

### Training Strategy

The training approach centers on instruction-conditioned contrastive learning using the InfoNCE loss:

$$
\mathcal{L} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(h_q, h_t^+) / \tau)}{\sum_{i=1}^{N} \exp(\text{sim}(h_q, h_t^i) / \tau)}
$$

where $h_q$ and $h_t^+$ represent query and positive target embeddings, respectively, and $\tau$ is the temperature parameter.

To achieve effective contrastive learning, GradCache is employed to accumulate gradients across multiple sub-batches, enabling a large effective batch size of 1,024. This approach is crucial for learning discriminative embeddings across the diverse range of remote sensing tasks.

Linguistic robustness is enhanced through template diversity, with approximately ten instruction templates per task used during training. This randomization teaches the model to generalize across different phrasings of the same semantic intent.

### RSMEB Benchmark

A significant contribution is the introduction of RSMEB (Remote Sensing Multimodal Embedding Benchmark), which consolidates 21 tasks from various public datasets into 6 meta-tasks:

1. **Classification**: Image-to-label mapping
2. **Multimodal Retrieval**: Cross-modal and region-based composed image retrieval
3. **Visual Question Answering**: Image + question to answer mapping
4. **Visual Grounding**: Text-to-region localization
5. **Spatial Localization**: Region-caption and grounded text-to-image retrieval
6. **Semantic Geo-localization**: Geographic coordinate-aware image retrieval

Performance is evaluated using task-appropriate metrics (accuracy, R@k, P@1), with overall model comparison conducted using Friedman scores for consistent ranking across diverse tasks.

## Results and Analysis

### Overall Performance

VLM2GeoVec achieves superior performance across RSMEB, obtaining the lowest Friedman score (1.93) among all evaluated models. This ranking significantly outperforms general-purpose VLMs (CLIP, VLM2Vec), specialized remote sensing dual-encoders (RemoteCLIP, SkyCLIP, GeoRSCLIP), and generative assistants (GeoChat).

![Detailed performance radar chart showing VLM2GeoVec's consistent excellence across all task categories](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-3.jpeg)

### Task-Specific Achievements

**Spatial and Geospatial Tasks**: VLM2GeoVec demonstrates exceptional performance in tasks requiring spatial metadata integration:

- **Region-Caption Retrieval**: 26.56% P@1 (+25.31pp over VLM2Vec baseline)
- **Semantic Geo-localization**: 17.8% P@1 (3× improvement over SkyCLIP's 5.1%)
- **Region-based Composed Image Retrieval**: 22.99% P@1 (5× better than SkyCLIP's 3.96%)

**Traditional Tasks**: The model maintains competitive performance in conventional remote sensing tasks:

- **Scene Classification**: Ranks first in zero-shot classification, achieving 77.25% on AID and 79.76% on PatternNet
- **Cross-Modal Retrieval**: Ranks second overall, closely trailing RemoteCLIP while demonstrating superior generalization

### Qualitative Analysis

![Qualitative comparison showing VLM2GeoVec's superior spatial understanding compared to VLM2Vec](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-4.jpeg)

The qualitative results demonstrate VLM2GeoVec's enhanced spatial understanding. In grounded text-to-image retrieval tasks, VLM2GeoVec consistently identifies images that precisely match spatial constraints specified in queries, while baseline models often retrieve semantically similar but spatially incorrect results.

### Ablation Studies

Key findings from ablation experiments include:

**Initialization Strategy**: Bootstrapping from VLM2Vec weights provides substantial improvements (Friedman score improvement from 2.45 to 1.36 for the 7B model), confirming the value of transferable multimodal priors.

**Model Scaling**: Performance consistently improves with increased model capacity from 2B to 7B parameters, highlighting the benefits of larger VLM architectures for complex multimodal reasoning.

**Domain Adaptation Impact**: A 2B VLM2GeoVec model trained from scratch matches the performance of a 7B general-purpose VLM2Vec, demonstrating the significant value of domain-specific adaptation.

## Significance and Impact

VLM2GeoVec represents a paradigm shift in remote sensing AI by successfully unifying scalable retrieval capabilities with fine-grained spatial and geospatial reasoning. This unification addresses a critical fragmentation in the field, where different model architectures were previously required for different aspects of multimodal understanding.

### Technical Contributions

The work makes several important technical contributions. The multimodal interleaving architecture provides a principled approach to integrating diverse metadata types within a single embedding space. The instruction-conditioned contrastive learning framework enables flexible task adaptation while maintaining retrieval efficiency. Most importantly, RSMEB establishes a comprehensive evaluation standard that will drive future research toward more holistic model development.

### Practical Applications

The enhanced capabilities enable sophisticated real-world applications:

**Urban Planning**: Planners can perform complex spatial queries combining visual, textual, and geographic constraints, such as identifying specific building types within defined areas.

**Environmental Monitoring**: The model enables precise identification and quantification of environmental phenomena through combined visual recognition and spatial grounding.

**Disaster Response**: Emergency responders can quickly locate specific damage types or critical infrastructure within geographic boundaries, improving response efficiency.

### Future Directions

While VLM2GeoVec represents significant progress, the authors acknowledge limitations that point toward future research opportunities. Current constraints include single-view RGB imagery and textual coordinate encoding. Future work may explore richer spatial representations through learned geodesic embeddings and extend the framework to incorporate additional remote sensing modalities such as SAR, multispectral, and LiDAR data.

The introduction of temporal sequences for change detection applications represents another promising direction, potentially enabling dynamic analysis of evolving geographic phenomena over time.

## Conclusion

VLM2GeoVec successfully demonstrates that unified multimodal embeddings can achieve both scalable retrieval and precise spatial reasoning in remote sensing applications. Through its instruction-conditioned architecture, comprehensive training strategy, and rigorous evaluation on the newly introduced RSMEB benchmark, this work establishes a new standard for multimodal understanding in the remote sensing domain. The model's superior performance across diverse tasks, from traditional classification to sophisticated geo-localized retrieval, validates the approach and provides a solid foundation for future developments in remote sensing AI systems.

zh.title: VLM2GeoVec: 迈向遥感通用多模态嵌入
zh.abstract:
卫星图像与自然图像有着根本性的不同：其独特的空中视角、超高分辨率、多样的尺度变化以及大量小目标，要求同时具备区域级空间推理能力和整体场景理解能力。当前遥感领域的研究方法仍显碎片化，主要分为两类：一类是双编码器检索模型，它们擅长大规模跨模态搜索，但无法交织处理多模态信息；另一类是生成式辅助模型，它们支持区域级解释，但缺乏可扩展的检索能力。

我们提出了 $\textbf{VLM2GeoVec}$，这是一个遵循指令的单编码器视觉语言模型，它采用对比学习方式训练，能够将交织的输入（图像、文本、边界框和地理坐标）嵌入到统一的向量空间中。我们的单编码器将所有输入交织成一个联合嵌入，并通过对比损失进行训练，从而消除了多阶段流水线和针对特定任务的模块。为了评估其多功能性，我们引入了一个新颖的基准 $\textbf{RSMEB}$，涵盖了关键的遥感嵌入应用，包括：场景分类、跨模态搜索、组合检索、视觉问答、视觉定位和区域级推理，以及语义地理空间检索。

在 RSMEB 上，$\textbf{VLM2GeoVec}$ 在区域-标题检索中实现了 $\textbf{26.6%}$ 的 P@1 (相较于双编码器基线提高了 25 个百分点)，在指代表达检索中实现了 $\textbf{32.5%}$ 的 P@1 (提高了 19 个百分点)，并在语义地理定位检索中实现了 $\textbf{17.8%}$ 的 P@1 (超过了此前最佳性能的 3 倍以上)，同时在场景分类和跨模态检索等传统任务上与专门的基线模型持平或超越。VLM2GeoVec 将可扩展检索与区域级空间推理相统一，从而在遥感领域实现了连贯的多模态分析。论文接收后，我们将公开发布代码、预训练模型和数据。

summary.summary: VLM2GeoVec 被引入作为一种遵循指令的单编码器视觉-语言模型，它生成用于遥感的通用多模态嵌入，将图像、文本、边界框和地理坐标无缝集成到统一的向量空间中。它在新的 RSMEB 基准测试中取得了最先进的性能，在区域-标题检索方面实现了 +25.31 个百分点的增益，在语义地理定位检索方面比以前的基线提高了三倍以上。
originalProblem: 现有用于遥感的视觉-语言模型支离破碎，双编码器缺乏细粒度的空间集成，而生成模型缺乏可扩展的检索。
通用VLM在应用于遥感图像时面临“领域迁移”问题，导致跨模态性能较弱，并在元数据感知任务中失效。
遥感的评估基准通常是任务特定的，这阻碍了对模型多模态检索和推理能力的整体评估，尤其是在涉及空间元数据方面。
solution: 开发了 VLM2GeoVec，一个单编码器、遵循指令的VLM，它将视觉标记、描述性文本、边界框和经纬度坐标交织成一个统一的标记流。
采用指令条件对比学习，结合InfoNCE损失和大的有效批处理大小，使用LoRA适配器对从VLM2Vec检查点初始化的Qwen2-VL骨干进行高效微调。
引入了 RSMEB，一个全面的、统一的基于排名的基准测试，整合了6个元任务下的21个任务，以整体评估多模态遥感嵌入模型。
keyInsights: 与分散的方法相比，具有深度多模态交织的单编码器架构在图像、文本和空间元数据之间提供了更连贯的上下文理解和推理。
指令条件对比预训练与领域适应相结合，有效克服了通用VLM在遥感中的“领域迁移”挑战。
通过 RSMEB 等基准测试在不同任务中进行统一评估，对于推动多模态遥感人工智能的整体进步至关重要，超越了任务特定的优化。
results: VLM2GeoVec 在 RSMEB 基准测试中获得了最低的总体 Friedman 分数 (1.93)，在21个任务中超越了所有通用和专用遥感基线。
在新型多模态任务中表现出显著改进，包括区域-标题检索P@1方面实现了+25.31个百分点的增益，以及与之前最佳基线相比，语义地理定位检索P@1方面提高了三倍以上。
在零样本场景分类（例如，AID上77.25%，PatternNet上79.76%）和跨模态检索等传统任务中取得了有竞争力或优异的性能，验证了其有效的领域适应能力。

zh.overview:
## 引言

随着高分辨率卫星和航空图像的普及，遥感应用经历了巨大的增长。然而，遥感数据独特的特性——包括俯视视角、极端的尺度变化以及小目标的普遍存在——带来了独特的挑战，使该领域与传统的计算机视觉任务区分开来。当前为遥感设计的视觉-语言模型（VLMs）面临一个根本性的权衡：双编码器模型擅长大规模跨模态检索，但无法处理细粒度的空间元数据；而生成模型提供详细的空间推理，但缺乏高效的检索能力。

![VLM2GeoVec（绿色）在RSMEB的21项任务中表现优于现有模型的性能比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-0.jpeg)

VLM2GeoVec 通过引入一种统一的单编码器架构来解决这一限制，该架构无缝地将图像、文本、边界框和地理坐标集成到通用的多模态嵌入中。这项工作代表着向创建真正多功能遥感人工智能系统迈出了重要一步，该系统能够在单一框架内实现可扩展检索和精确空间推理。

## 问题陈述与动机

遥感领域面临着若干关键挑战，现有多模态模型未能全面解决这些挑战。传统的双编码器 VLM，如 CLIP 及其遥感变体（RemoteCLIP、SkyCLIP），整体处理图像，无法将边界框或地理坐标等空间元数据整合到统一的查询中。这种架构限制严重限制了它们在需要精确空间理解的任务中的适用性。

相反，为遥感设计的生成式 VLM 助手（GeoChat、TEOChat）擅长区域级解释和视觉问答，但缺乏搜索大规模图像档案所需的基于嵌入的高效检索机制。这种碎片化迫使从业者对同一工作流的不同方面使用不同的模型架构。

此外，现有评估框架是任务特定的，未能提供对多模态能力的全面评估。缺乏整合空间和地理空间元数据的统一基准，阻碍了开发真正通用的遥感嵌入的进展。

## 方法论

### VLM2GeoVec 架构

VLM2GeoVec 采用基于 Qwen2-VL 主干的单编码器架构，该架构从预训练的 VLM2Vec 检查点初始化。其核心创新在于能够处理交错的多模态令牌流，这些令牌流包含多达四种不同的模态：

**视觉处理**：图像以 336×336 的分辨率使用 ViT-L-14 主干进行处理，生成 14×14 基于补丁的视觉令牌，这些令牌捕获宏观场景上下文和微观空间细节。

**文本集成**：描述性文本、标题和任务指令被标记化并直接集成到令牌流中，实现指令遵循行为。

**空间元数据**：轴对齐的边界框被归一化到 [0, 100] 范围，并作为文本令牌整合，允许图像内的精确区域指定。

**地理空间坐标**：经纬度坐标被编码为文本元组（例如，“(34.052275, 118.243739)”），从而实现地理上下文集成。

![VLM2GeoVec 架构展示了多模态输入处理和统一嵌入生成](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-1.jpeg)

该模型利用注入到自注意力层和多层感知器（MLP）组件中的低秩适应（LoRA）层，在保持预训练主干网络能力的同时，实现了高效的微调。交错的 token 流由单个编码器处理，嵌入向量则从每个序列的最后一个 token 派生。

### 训练策略

训练方法以指令条件对比学习为核心，采用 InfoNCE 损失函数：

$$
\mathcal{L} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(h_q, h_t^+) / \tau)}{\sum_{i=1}^{N} \exp(\text{sim}(h_q, h_t^i) / \tau)}
$$

其中，$h_q$ 和 $h_t^+$ 分别代表查询和正样本目标嵌入向量，$\tau$ 是温度参数。

为了实现有效的对比学习，采用了 GradCache 来跨多个子批次累积梯度，从而实现 1,024 的大有效批次大小。这种方法对于学习各种遥感任务中的判别性嵌入向量至关重要。

通过模板多样性增强了语言的鲁棒性，训练期间每个任务使用了大约十个指令模板。这种随机化教会模型泛化同一语义意图的不同措辞。

### RSMEB 基准

一个重要的贡献是引入了 RSMEB（遥感多模态嵌入基准），它将来自各种公共数据集的 21 个任务整合为 6 个元任务：

1.  **分类**：图像到标签的映射
2.  **多模态检索**：跨模态和基于区域的组合图像检索
3.  **视觉问答**：图像 + 问题到答案的映射
4.  **视觉定位**：文本到区域的定位
5.  **空间定位**：区域-描述和基于文本的图像检索
6.  **语义地理定位**：地理坐标感知的图像检索

性能使用适合任务的指标（准确率、R@k、P@1）进行评估，并通过 Friedman 分数进行整体模型比较，以确保在不同任务中排名的 S一致性。

## 结果与分析

### 整体性能

VLM2GeoVec 在 RSMEB 上取得了卓越的性能，在所有评估模型中获得了最低的 Friedman 分数（1.93）。这一排名显著优于通用 VLM（CLIP、VLM2Vec）、专业遥感双编码器（RemoteCLIP、SkyCLIP、GeoRSCLIP）和生成式助手（GeoChat）。

![详细性能雷达图显示 VLM2GeoVec 在所有任务类别中持续表现出色](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-3.jpeg)

### 特定任务成就

**空间和地理空间任务**：VLM2GeoVec 在需要空间元数据集成任务中表现出卓越的性能：

-   **区域-描述检索**：26.56% P@1（比 VLM2Vec 基线提高 25.31 个百分点）
-   **语义地理定位**：17.8% P@1（比 SkyCLIP 的 5.1% 提高 3 倍）
-   **基于区域的组合图像检索**：22.99% P@1（比 SkyCLIP 的 3.96% 提高 5 倍）

**传统任务**：模型在传统遥感任务中保持了有竞争力的性能：

-   **场景分类**：在零样本分类中排名第一，在 AID 上达到 77.25%，在 PatternNet 上达到 79.76%
-   **跨模态检索**：整体排名第二，紧随 RemoteCLIP 之后，同时展现出卓越的泛化能力

### 定性分析

![定性比较显示 VLM2GeoVec 相较于 VLM2Vec 具有更优越的空间理解能力](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11490v1/img-4.jpeg)

定性结果表明 VLM2GeoVec 增强了空间理解能力。在基于文本的图像检索任务中，VLM2GeoVec 始终能识别出精确匹配查询中指定空间约束的图像，而基线模型通常检索到语义相似但空间不正确的结果。

### 消融研究

消融实验的主要发现包括：

**初始化策略**：从 VLM2Vec 权重进行引导，带来了显著的改进（7B 模型 Friedman 分数从 2.45 提高到 1.36），证实了可迁移多模态先验的价值。

**模型扩展**：性能随着模型容量从 2B 增加到 7B 参数而持续提升，突显了大型 VLM 架构在复杂多模态推理方面的优势。

**领域适应影响**：从零开始训练的 2B VLM2GeoVec 模型达到了 7B 通用 VLM2Vec 模型的性能，表明领域特定适应的巨大价值。

## 意义与影响

VLM2GeoVec 通过成功地将可扩展的检索能力与精细的空间和地理空间推理相结合，代表了遥感人工智能的范式转变。这种统一解决了该领域的一个关键碎片化问题，此前，对于多模态理解的不同方面，需要不同的模型架构。

### 技术贡献

这项工作做出了几项重要的技术贡献。多模态交织架构提供了一种将不同元数据类型整合到单一嵌入空间中的原则性方法。指令条件对比学习框架实现了灵活的任务适应，同时保持了检索效率。最重要的是，RSMEB 建立了一个全面的评估标准，将推动未来的研究走向更整体的模型开发。

### 实际应用

增强的功能支持复杂的实际应用：

**城市规划**：规划者可以执行结合视觉、文本和地理约束的复杂空间查询，例如在指定区域内识别特定建筑类型。

**环境监测**：该模型通过结合视觉识别和空间定位，能够精确识别和量化环境现象。

**灾害响应**：应急响应人员可以快速定位地理边界内的特定损害类型或关键基础设施，提高响应效率。

### 未来方向

虽然 VLM2GeoVec 代表了重大进展，但作者承认存在局限性，并指出了未来的研究机会。当前的限制包括单视图 RGB 图像和文本坐标编码。未来的工作可以探索通过学习的测地线嵌入来获取更丰富的空间表示，并将框架扩展到包含额外的遥感模态，如 SAR、多光谱和 LiDAR 数据。

引入时间序列用于变化检测应用代表了另一个有前景的方向，可能能够实现对随时间演变的地理现象的动态分析。

## 结论

VLM2GeoVec 成功证明了统一的多模态嵌入可以在遥感应用中实现可扩展的检索和精确的空间推理。通过其指令条件架构、全面的训练策略以及在新引入的 RSMEB 基准上的严格评估，这项工作为遥感领域的多模态理解建立了新标准。该模型在从传统分类到复杂的地理定位检索等各种任务中表现出的卓越性能，验证了该方法的有效性，并为未来遥感人工智能系统的发展奠定了坚实基础。

abstract: Satellite imagery differs fundamentally from natural images: its aerial viewpoint, very high resolution, diverse scale variations, and abundance of small objects demand both region-level spatial reasoning and holistic scene understanding. Current remote-sensing approaches remain fragmented between dual-encoder retrieval models, which excel at large-scale cross-modal search but cannot interleave modalities, and generative assistants, which support region-level interpretation but lack scalable retrieval capabilities. We propose $\textbf{VLM2GeoVec}$, an instruction-following, single-encoder vision-language model trained contrastively to embed interleaved inputs (images, text, bounding boxes, and geographic coordinates) in a unified vector space. Our single encoder interleaves all inputs into one joint embedding trained with a contrastive loss, eliminating multi-stage pipelines and task-specific modules. To evaluate its versatility, we introduce $\textbf{RSMEB}$, a novel benchmark covering key remote-sensing embedding applications: scene classification; cross-modal search; compositional retrieval; visual-question answering; visual grounding and region-level reasoning; and semantic geospatial retrieval. On RSMEB, it achieves $\textbf{26.6%}$ P@1 on region-caption retrieval (+25 pp vs. dual-encoder baselines), $\textbf{32.5%}$ P@1 on referring-expression retrieval (+19 pp), and $\textbf{17.8%}$ P@1 on semantic geo-localization retrieval (over $3\times$ prior best), while matching or exceeding specialized baselines on conventional tasks such as scene classification and cross-modal retrieval. VLM2GeoVec unifies scalable retrieval with region-level spatial reasoning, enabling cohesive multimodal analysis in remote sensing. We will publicly release the code, checkpoints, and data upon acceptance.

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) offers potential for democratizing scientific knowledge and converting this to clear, actionable information, yet its application in agri-food science remains unexplored. Here, we verify the scientific knowledge on agroecological crop protection that is generated by either web-grounded or non-grounded large language models (LLMs), i.e., DeepSeek versus the free-tier version of ChatGPT. For nine globally limiting pests, weeds, and plant diseases, we assessed the factual accuracy, data consistency, and breadth of knowledge or data completeness of each LLM. Overall, DeepSeek consistently screened a 4.8-49.7-fold larger literature corpus and reported 1.6-2.4-fold more biological control agents or management solutions than ChatGPT. As a result, DeepSeek reported 21.6% higher efficacy estimates, exhibited greater laboratory-to-field data consistency, and showed more realistic effects of pest identity and management tactics. However, both models hallucinated, i.e., fabricated fictitious agents or references, reported on implausible ecological interactions or outcomes, confused old and new scientific nomenclatures, and omitted data on key agents or solutions. Despite these shortcomings, both LLMs correctly reported low-resolution efficacy trends. Overall, when paired with rigorous human oversight, LLMs may pose a powerful tool to support farm-level decision-making and unleash scientific creativity.

abstract: Loop transformations are semantics-preserving optimization techniques, widely used to maximize objectives such as parallelism. Despite decades of research, applying the optimal composition of loop transformations remains challenging due to inherent complexities, including cost modeling for optimization objectives. Recent studies have explored the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) for code optimization. However, our key observation is that LLMs often struggle with effective loop transformation optimization, frequently leading to errors or suboptimal optimization, thereby missing opportunities for performance improvements. To bridge this gap, we propose LOOPRAG, a novel retrieval-augmented generation framework designed to guide LLMs in performing effective loop optimization on Static Control Part. We introduce a parameter-driven method to harness loop properties, which trigger various loop transformations, and generate diverse yet legal example codes serving as a demonstration source. To effectively obtain the most informative demonstrations, we propose a loop-aware algorithm based on loop features, which balances similarity and diversity for code retrieval. To enhance correct and efficient code generation, we introduce a feedback-based iterative mechanism that incorporates compilation, testing and performance results as feedback to guide LLMs. Each optimized code undergoes mutation, coverage and differential testing for equivalence checking. We evaluate LOOPRAG on PolyBench, TSVC and LORE benchmark suites, and compare it against compilers (GCC-Graphite, Clang-Polly, Perspective and ICX) and representative LLMs (DeepSeek and GPT-4). The results demonstrate average speedups over base compilers of up to 11.20$\times$, 14.34$\times$, and 9.29$\times$ for PolyBench, TSVC, and LORE, respectively, and speedups over base LLMs of up to 11.97$\times$, 5.61$\times$, and 11.59$\times$.

en.title: FAIR: Focused Attention Is All You Need for Generative Recommendation
en.abstract: Recently, transformer-based generative recommendation has garnered significant attention for user behavior modeling. However, it often requires discretizing items into multi-code representations (e.g., typically four code tokens or more), which sharply increases the length of the original item sequence. This expansion poses challenges to transformer-based models for modeling user behavior sequences with inherent noises, since they tend to overallocate attention to irrelevant or noisy context. To mitigate this issue, we propose FAIR, the first generative recommendation framework with focused attention, which enhances attention scores to relevant context while suppressing those to irrelevant ones. Specifically, we propose (1) a focused attention mechanism integrated into the standard Transformer, which learns two separate sets of Q and K attention weights and computes their difference as the final attention scores to eliminate attention noise while focusing on relevant contexts; (2) a noise-robustness objective, which encourages the model to maintain stable attention patterns under stochastic perturbations, preventing undesirable shifts toward irrelevant context due to noise; and (3) a mutual information maximization objective, which guides the model to identify contexts that are most informative for next-item prediction. We validate the effectiveness of FAIR on four public benchmarks, demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing methods.

summary.summary: FAIR introduces a non-autoregressive generative recommendation framework designed to mitigate attention noise in Transformer models caused by lengthy multi-code item sequences. The system consistently achieved top performance across multiple datasets, demonstrating improvements such as 13.18% in Recall@5 and 10.99% in NDCG@5 over the strongest generative baseline (RPG) on the Toys benchmark.
originalProblem: Transformer-based generative recommendation models, by discretizing items into multiple code tokens, generate excessively long user historical sequences.
These long, often noisy, sequences cause Transformer attention mechanisms to over-allocate focus to irrelevant contexts, leading to 'attention noise'.
This misdirected attention diminishes the model's ability to identify and leverage truly relevant historical interactions, thereby degrading recommendation accuracy.
solution: A Focused Attention Mechanism (FAM) is introduced, which uses dual query and key projections to compute and subtract two attention distributions, thereby suppressing noise and amplifying discriminative signals.

A Noise-Robustness Task (NRT) employs a triplet loss to enforce consistency between representations of original and synthetically perturbed input sequences, enhancing model resilience to stochastic noise.

A Mutual Information Maximization (MIM) task, implemented with an InfoNCE objective, guides the model to maximize the mutual information between input sequences and their target item representations, encouraging focus on predictive contexts.
keyInsights: Explicitly designing attention mechanisms to filter out 'attention noise' is crucial for improving Transformer-based generative recommender performance when dealing with expanded, multi-code item representations.
A differential attention approach, by subtracting attention distributions, can effectively isolate and amplify genuinely informative signals from noisy or redundant sequence elements.

Combining both input-level noise robustness and target-prediction-oriented mutual information maximization provides a comprehensive strategy to guide Transformer attention towards relevant user history.
results: FAIR consistently outperformed a wide range of state-of-the-art traditional and generative baselines, ranking first in 15 out of 16 evaluation metrics across four Amazon product review datasets.
The framework achieved substantial gains, including a 13.18% improvement in Recall@5 and 10.99% in NDCG@5 compared to the strongest generative baseline RPG on the Toys benchmark.

Ablation studies confirmed that all three core components (FAM, NRT, MIM) are indispensable, with their removal leading to significant performance degradation, validating their individual contributions to the overall effectiveness.

en.overview:
## Problem Definition and Motivation

![Figure 1: Attention visualization showing how FAIR improves focus on relevant items](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11254v2/img-0.jpeg)

Generative recommendation systems represent a paradigm shift from traditional approaches by treating recommendation as a sequence generation task. These systems tokenize items into discrete codes and use Transformer-based language models to predict the next item a user will interact with. While this approach leverages the power of modern language models and can capture richer semantic information, it introduces a critical challenge: attention noise.

The core problem arises when items are discretized into multiple code tokens (typically 4 or more) to enhance representational capacity. This multi-code representation significantly expands the length of user historical sequences. For example, a sequence of 100 items, each represented by 32 codes, becomes a 3,200-token sequence. Transformer models, despite their sophistication, tend to overallocate attention to irrelevant or noisy contexts in these expanded sequences, hindering their ability to focus on truly predictive user interactions.

FAIR (Focused Attention Is All You Need) addresses this fundamental limitation by introducing the first generative recommendation framework explicitly designed to mitigate attention noise. The framework amplifies attention to relevant contexts while suppressing noise, thereby improving the model's ability to make accurate next-item predictions.

## Architecture and Methodology

![Figure 2: Overview of FAIR architecture showing the three main components](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11254v2/img-1.jpeg)

FAIR employs a non-autoregressive (NAR) generative approach built on a 2-layer Transformer decoder architecture. Unlike autoregressive models that generate codes sequentially, FAIR predicts all L codes of the next item simultaneously using a multi-token prediction (MTP) objective. This design choice addresses computational efficiency while handling the long code sequences that FAIR is specifically designed to manage.

The framework incorporates three key technical innovations:

### Focused Attention Mechanism (FAM)

The core architectural innovation draws inspiration from differential amplifiers in signal processing. Instead of learning a single set of Query (Q) and Key (K) projection matrices like standard Transformers, FAM learns two distinct sets: $(Q_1, K_1)$ and $(Q_2, K_2)$, along with a single Value (V) matrix.

The mechanism computes two separate scaled dot-product attention score matrices and derives the final focused attention through subtraction:

$$
A = \text{Norm}(\lambda_1 A_1 - \lambda_2 A_2)
$$

This differential approach suppresses common or noisy correlations present in both distributions while highlighting discriminative differences that emphasize informative contexts.

### Noise-Robustness Task (NRT)

To enhance model resilience against input perturbations, FAIR incorporates a noise-robustness objective that creates synthetic noisy versions of input sequences through random masking and substitution. The framework then applies a triplet loss to enforce consistency between clean and noisy representations while pushing apart representations from different items:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{NR} = \max(0, d(\mathbf{h}, \tilde{\mathbf{h}}) - d(\mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}^-) + m)
$$

where $\mathbf{h}$ represents the clean sequence representation, $\tilde{\mathbf{h}}$ is the noisy version, and $\mathbf{h}^-$ represents negative samples.

### Mutual Information Maximization (MIM)

The third component guides the model to focus on contexts most predictive of the target item by maximizing mutual information between input sequences and their corresponding targets. Since direct mutual information maximization is intractable, FAIR employs the InfoNCE objective as a contrastive surrogate:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{MIM} = -\log\frac{\exp(f(\mathbf{x}_t)^T f(\mathbf{h}_t)/\tau)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N} \exp(f(\mathbf{x}_t)^T f(\mathbf{h}_j)/\tau)}
$$

This encourages the model to make target representations highly predictable from their true contexts while reducing attention to irrelevant tokens.

## Experimental Results and Analysis

FAIR was evaluated on four Amazon product review benchmarks (Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games, CDs and Vinyl) using Recall@k and NDCG@k metrics. The results demonstrate consistent superiority across nearly all evaluation scenarios.

### Performance Comparison

FAIR achieved top performance in 15 out of 16 evaluation metrics, with particularly notable improvements on the Toys benchmark: 13.18% improvement in Recall@5 and 10.99% improvement in NDCG@5 compared to the strongest baseline, RPG. The results confirm that generative methods generally outperform traditional sequential recommendation approaches, with FAIR representing the current state-of-the-art in this paradigm.

### Ablation Studies

Comprehensive ablation studies validated the necessity of each component. Removing any single component (FAM, NRT, or MIM) led to performance degradation, with the removal of all three resulting in the worst performance. This confirms that each proposed module contributes meaningfully to FAIR's effectiveness.

### Hyperparameter Analysis

![Figure 3-6: Performance analysis across different code lengths and embedding dimensions](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11254v2/img-2.jpeg)

The analysis revealed several important insights:

**Code Length Impact**: Increasing code length L from 4 to 32 continuously improved performance, highlighting the benefit of richer semantic expressiveness. However, further increases to L=64 showed diminishing returns, suggesting an optimal balance at L=32.

**Embedding Dimension**: Performance improved as embedding dimension increased from 128 to 512, with d=512 representing the optimal trade-off before redundancy and overfitting began to appear.

**Regularization**: Surprisingly, FAIR achieved best performance with zero dropout, suggesting that its explicit noise robustness modeling effectively replaces conventional stochastic regularization techniques.

## Technical Contributions and Significance

FAIR makes several important contributions to the field of generative recommendation:

1. **First Framework for Attention Noise**: FAIR pioneered the explicit identification and mitigation of attention noise in Transformer-based generative recommendation, addressing a previously unrecognized bottleneck.

2. **Innovative Attention Design**: The Focused Attention Mechanism provides a direct and elegant solution for filtering noise through differential attention computation, inspired by signal processing principles.

3. **Comprehensive Noise Handling**: The integration of both explicit noise robustness training and mutual information maximization provides a multi-pronged approach to enhance model resilience and focus.

4. **Practical Validation**: The consistent performance improvements across diverse datasets demonstrate the real-world applicability of the approach, particularly important given the industrial research context from Huawei Noah's Ark Lab.

The research has significant implications for industrial recommendation systems, where large item catalogs and noisy user behavior data are common challenges. By making generative models more robust and focused, FAIR enhances the viability of this paradigm as a successor to traditional similarity-based methods. The work also provides valuable insights for Transformer design in other domains dealing with long, potentially noisy sequences, opening new avenues for research in advanced attention mechanisms and explicit noise modeling approaches.

zh.title: FAIR：聚焦注意力足矣，用于生成式推荐
zh.abstract:
近来，基于Transformer的生成式推荐在用户行为建模方面受到了广泛关注。然而，它通常需要将物品离散化为多码表示（例如，通常需要四个或更多编码token），这导致原始物品序列的长度急剧增加。这种扩展对基于Transformer的模型在建模带有固有噪声的用户行为序列时带来了挑战，因为它们倾向于将注意力过度分配给不相关或带有噪声的上下文。

为了缓解这一问题，我们提出了FAIR，这是首个具有聚焦注意力的生成式推荐框架，它增强了对相关上下文的注意力分数，同时抑制了对不相关上下文的注意力分数。具体而言，我们提出了：
(1) 一种集成到标准Transformer中的聚焦注意力机制，它学习两组独立的Q和K注意力权重，并计算它们的差值作为最终注意力分数，以消除注意力噪声，同时聚焦于相关上下文；
(2) 一个噪声鲁棒性目标，它鼓励模型在随机扰动下保持稳定的注意力模式，防止由于噪声导致的不必要的注意力向不相关上下文转移；
(3) 一个互信息最大化目标，它指导模型识别对下一项预测最具信息量的上下文。

我们在四个公共基准数据集上验证了FAIR的有效性，证明了其相比现有方法的卓越性能。

summary.summary: FAIR引入了一个非自回归的生成式推荐框架，旨在缓解Transformer模型中由冗长的多码项序列引起的注意力噪声。该系统在多个数据集上持续取得最佳性能，在Toys基准测试中，相较于最强的生成式基线（RPG），Recall@5提升了13.18%，NDCG@5提升了10.99%。
originalProblem: 基于Transformer的生成式推荐模型通过将物品离散化为多个代码标记，生成了过长的用户历史序列。
这些冗长、通常带有噪声的序列导致Transformer注意力机制过度关注不相关的上下文，从而产生'注意力噪声'。
这种误导的注意力削弱了模型识别和利用真正相关的历史交互的能力，从而降低了推荐准确性。
solution: 引入了聚焦注意力机制（FAM），它使用双重查询和键投影来计算并减去两个注意力分布，从而抑制噪声并放大判别性信号。
噪声鲁棒性任务（NRT）采用三重损失来强制原始输入序列和合成扰动输入序列表示之间的一致性，增强模型对随机噪声的弹性。
互信息最大化（MIM）任务，通过InfoNCE目标实现，引导模型最大化输入序列及其目标物品表示之间的互信息，鼓励模型关注预测性上下文。
keyInsights: 在处理扩展的多码物品表示时，明确设计注意力机制以过滤'注意力噪声'对于提高基于Transformer的生成式推荐器性能至关重要。
通过减去注意力分布的差分注意力方法，可以有效地从噪声或冗余序列元素中分离并放大真正有信息量的信号。
结合输入级别的噪声鲁棒性和面向目标预测的互信息最大化，提供了一种全面的策略来引导Transformer注意力关注相关的用户历史。
results: FAIR持续超越了广泛的最新传统和生成式基线模型，在四个Amazon产品评论数据集的16项评估指标中，有15项排名第一。
该框架取得了显著的提升，包括在Toys基准测试中，相较于最强的生成式基线RPG，Recall@5提升了13.18%，NDCG@5提升了10.99%。
消融研究证实，所有三个核心组件（FAM、NRT、MIM）都不可或缺，它们的移除会导致显著的性能下降，验证了它们各自对整体有效性的贡献。

zh.overview:
## 问题定义和动机

![图 1：注意力可视化，展示 FAIR 如何提高对相关项目的关注](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11254v2/img-0.jpeg)

生成式推荐系统通过将推荐视为序列生成任务，代表了传统方法的范式转变。这些系统将项目标记为离散代码，并使用基于 Transformer 的语言模型来预测用户将与之交互的下一个项目。虽然这种方法利用了现代语言模型的强大功能并可以捕获更丰富的语义信息，但它引入了一个关键挑战：注意力噪声。

核心问题在于，当项目被离散化为多个代码标记（通常是 4 个或更多）以增强表示能力时。这种多代码表示显著扩展了用户历史序列的长度。例如，一个包含 100 个项目，每个项目由 32 个代码表示的序列，将变成一个 3200 个标记的序列。Transformer 模型尽管复杂，但在这些扩展序列中往往会过度分配注意力给不相关或嘈杂的上下文，从而阻碍它们专注于真正具有预测性的用户交互。

FAIR（Focused Attention Is All You Need）通过引入第一个明确设计用于减轻注意力噪声的生成式推荐框架，解决了这一根本性限制。该框架增强了对相关上下文的注意力，同时抑制了噪声，从而提高了模型进行准确的下一个项目预测的能力。

## 架构和方法论

![图 2：FAIR 架构概述，显示了三个主要组件](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11254v2/img-1.jpeg)

FAIR 采用基于 2 层 Transformer 解码器架构的非自回归（NAR）生成方法。与顺序生成代码的自回归模型不同，FAIR 使用多标记预测（MTP）目标同时预测下一个项目的所有 L 个代码。这种设计选择在处理 FAIR 专门设计用于管理的长时间代码序列的同时，解决了计算效率问题。

该框架包含三个关键技术创新：

### 聚焦注意力机制（FAM）

核心架构创新灵感来源于信号处理中的差分放大器。与标准 Transformer 学习一组 Query (Q) 和 Key (K) 投影矩阵不同，FAM 学习两组不同的投影矩阵：$(Q_1, K_1)$ 和 $(Q_2, K_2)$，以及一个 Value (V) 矩阵。

该机制计算两个独立的缩放点积注意力分数矩阵，并通过减法推导出最终的聚焦注意力：

$$
A = \text{Norm}(\lambda_1 A_1 - \lambda_2 A_2)
$$

这种差分方法抑制了两种分布中存在的共同或噪声相关性，同时突出了强调信息上下文的区分性差异。

### 噪声鲁棒性任务（NRT）

为了增强模型对输入扰动的弹性，FAIR 引入了一个噪声鲁棒性目标，通过随机掩码和替换创建输入序列的合成噪声版本。然后，该框架应用三重损失来强制保持干净和噪声表示之间的一致性，同时将来自不同项目的表示推开：

$$
\mathcal{L}_{NR} = \max(0, d(\mathbf{h}, \tilde{\mathbf{h}}) - d(\mathbf{h}, \mathbf{h}^-) + m)
$$

其中 $\mathbf{h}$ 表示干净序列表示，$\tilde{\mathbf{h}}$ 是噪声版本，$\mathbf{h}^-$ 表示负样本。

### 互信息最大化（MIM）

第三个组件通过最大化输入序列及其对应目标之间的互信息，引导模型关注最能预测目标项目的上下文。由于直接最大化互信息是难以处理的，FAIR 采用 InfoNCE 目标作为对比替代：

$$
\mathcal{L}_{MIM} = -\log\frac{\exp(f(\mathbf{x}_t)^T f(\mathbf{h}_t)/\tau)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N} \exp(f(\mathbf{x}_t)^T f(\mathbf{h}_j)/\tau)}
$$

这鼓励模型使其目标表示可以从其真实上下文中高度预测，同时减少对不相关token的关注。

## 实验结果与分析

FAIR在四个亚马逊商品评论基准（美妆、运动与户外、玩具和游戏、CD与黑胶唱片）上使用Recall@k和NDCG@k指标进行了评估。结果表明，FAIR在几乎所有评估场景中都展现出持续的优越性。

### 性能比较

FAIR在16个评估指标中的15个中取得了最佳性能，尤其在玩具基准上表现突出：与最强的基线RPG相比，Recall@5提升了13.18%，NDCG@5提升了10.99%。结果证实，生成式方法通常优于传统的序列推荐方法，而FAIR代表了该范式中的当前最先进水平。

### 消融研究

全面的消融研究验证了每个组件的必要性。移除任何单个组件（FAM、NRT或MIM）都会导致性能下降，而移除所有三个组件则会导致最差的性能。这证实了每个提出的模块都对FAIR的有效性做出了有意义的贡献。

### 超参数分析

![图3-6：不同码长和嵌入维度下的性能分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.11254v2/img-2.jpeg)

分析揭示了几个重要的见解：

**码长影响**：将码长L从4增加到32持续提高了性能，突出了更丰富的语义表达能力带来的好处。然而，进一步增加到L=64则显示出收益递减，表明L=32是一个最佳平衡点。

**嵌入维度**：随着嵌入维度从128增加到512，性能有所提高，其中d=512在冗余和过拟合开始出现之前代表了最佳权衡。

**正则化**：令人惊讶的是，FAIR在零dropout的情况下实现了最佳性能，这表明其显式的噪声鲁棒性建模有效替代了传统的随机正则化技术。

## 技术贡献和意义

FAIR对生成式推荐领域做出了几项重要贡献：

1.  **首个注意力噪声框架**：FAIR率先在基于Transformer的生成式推荐中明确识别并缓解注意力噪声，解决了之前未被识别的瓶颈。

2.  **创新注意力设计**：聚焦注意力机制（Focused Attention Mechanism）受信号处理原理启发，通过差分注意力计算提供了一种直接而优雅的噪声过滤解决方案。

3.  **全面噪声处理**：将显式噪声鲁棒性训练和互信息最大化相结合，提供了一种多管齐下的方法，以增强模型的弹性和聚焦能力。

4.  **实际验证**：在不同数据集上持续的性能改进证明了该方法的实际应用价值，鉴于华为诺亚方舟实验室的工业研究背景，这一点尤为重要。

这项研究对工业推荐系统具有重要意义，在这些系统中，大型商品目录和嘈杂的用户行为数据是常见的挑战。通过使生成模型更加鲁棒和聚焦，FAIR增强了这种范式作为传统基于相似性方法继任者的可行性。这项工作还为处理长序列、可能嘈杂序列的其他领域中的Transformer设计提供了宝贵见解，为高级注意力机制和显式噪声建模方法的研究开辟了新途径。

abstract: Recently, transformer-based generative recommendation has garnered significant attention for user behavior modeling. However, it often requires discretizing items into multi-code representations (e.g., typically four code tokens or more), which sharply increases the length of the original item sequence. This expansion poses challenges to transformer-based models for modeling user behavior sequences with inherent noises, since they tend to overallocate attention to irrelevant or noisy context. To mitigate this issue, we propose FAIR, the first generative recommendation framework with focused attention, which enhances attention scores to relevant context while suppressing those to irrelevant ones. Specifically, we propose (1) a focused attention mechanism integrated into the standard Transformer, which learns two separate sets of Q and K attention weights and computes their difference as the final attention scores to eliminate attention noise while focusing on relevant contexts; (2) a noise-robustness objective, which encourages the model to maintain stable attention patterns under stochastic perturbations, preventing undesirable shifts toward irrelevant context due to noise; and (3) a mutual information maximization objective, which guides the model to identify contexts that are most informative for next-item prediction. We validate the effectiveness of FAIR on four public benchmarks, demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing methods.

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often fail on multi-hop queries when the initial retrieval misses a bridge fact. Prior corrective approaches, such as Self-RAG, CRAG, and Adaptive-$k$, typically address this by \textit{adding} more context or pruning existing lists. However, simply expanding the context window often leads to \textbf{context dilution}, where distractors crowd out relevant information. We propose \textbf{SEAL-RAG}, a training-free controller that adopts a \textbf{``replace, don't expand''} strategy to fight context dilution under a fixed retrieval depth $k$. SEAL executes a (\textbf{S}earch $\rightarrow$ \textbf{E}xtract $\rightarrow$ \textbf{A}ssess $\rightarrow$ \textbf{L}oop) cycle: it performs on-the-fly, entity-anchored extraction to build a live \textit{gap specification} (missing entities/relations), triggers targeted micro-queries, and uses \textit{entity-first ranking} to actively swap out distractors for gap-closing evidence. We evaluate SEAL-RAG against faithful re-implementations of Basic RAG, CRAG, Self-RAG, and Adaptive-$k$ in a shared environment on \textbf{HotpotQA} and \textbf{2WikiMultiHopQA}. On HotpotQA ($k=3$), SEAL improves answer correctness by \textbf{+3--13 pp} and evidence precision by \textbf{+12--18 pp} over Self-RAG. abstract: The dominant paradigm for Audio-Text Retrieval (ATR) relies on mini-batch-based contrastive learning. This process, however, is inherently limited by what we formalize as the Gradient Locality Bottleneck (GLB), which structurally prevents models from leveraging out-of-batch knowledge and thus impairs fine-grained and long-tail learning. While external knowledge-enhanced methods can alleviate the GLB, we identify a critical, unaddressed side effect: the Representation-Drift Mismatch (RDM), where a static knowledge base becomes progressively misaligned with the evolving model, turning guidance into noise. To address this dual challenge, we propose the Adaptive Self-improving Knowledge (ASK) framework, a model-agnostic, plug-and-play solution. ASK breaks the GLB via multi-grained knowledge injection, systematically mitigates RDM through dynamic knowledge refinement, and introduces a novel adaptive reliability weighting scheme to ensure consistent knowledge contributes to optimization. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets with superior, state-of-the-art performance justify the efficacy of our proposed ASK framework.

abstract:
Background: While intravascular imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography (OCT), improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, its interpretation is operator-dependent. General-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise but lacks domain-specific reliability. We evaluated the performance of CA-GPT, a novel large model deployed on an AI-OCT system, against that of the general-purpose ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians for OCT-guided PCI planning and assessment.
  Methods: In this single-center analysis of 96 patients who underwent OCT-guided PCI, the procedural decisions generated by the CA-GPT, ChatGPT-5, and junior physicians were compared with an expert-derived procedural record. Agreement was assessed using ten pre-specified metrics across pre-PCI and post-PCI phases.
  Results: For pre-PCI planning, CA-GPT demonstrated significantly higher median agreement scores (5[IQR 3.75-5]) compared to both ChatGPT-5 (3[2-4], P<0.001) and junior physicians (4[3-4], P<0.001). CA-GPT significantly outperformed ChatGPT-5 across all individual pre-PCI metrics and showed superior performance to junior physicians in stent diameter (90.3% vs. 72.2%, P<0.05) and length selection (80.6% vs. 52.8%, P<0.01). In post-PCI assessment, CA-GPT maintained excellent overall agreement (5[4.75-5]), significantly higher than both ChatGPT-5 (4[4-5], P<0.001) and junior physicians (5[4-5], P<0.05). Subgroup analysis confirmed CA-GPT's robust performance advantage in complex scenarios.
  Conclusion: The CA-GPT-based AI-OCT system achieved superior decision-making agreement versus a general-purpose large language model and junior physicians across both PCI planning and assessment phases. This approach provides a standardized and reliable method for intravascular imaging interpretation, demonstrating significant potential to augment operator expertise and optimize OCT-guided PCI.

abstract: Popularity bias fundamentally undermines the personalization capabilities of collaborative filtering (CF) models, causing them to disproportionately recommend popular items while neglecting users' genuine preferences for niche content. While existing approaches treat this as an external confounding factor, we reveal that popularity bias is an intrinsic geometric artifact of Bayesian Pairwise Ranking (BPR) optimization in CF models. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, we prove that BPR systematically organizes item embeddings along a dominant "popularity direction" where embedding magnitudes directly correlate with interaction frequency. This geometric distortion forces user embeddings to simultaneously handle two conflicting tasks-expressing genuine preference and calibrating against global popularity-trapping them in suboptimal configurations that favor popular items regardless of individual tastes. We propose Directional Decomposition and Correction (DDC), a universally applicable framework that surgically corrects this embedding geometry through asymmetric directional updates. DDC guides positive interactions along personalized preference directions while steering negative interactions away from the global popularity direction, disentangling preference from popularity at the geometric source. Extensive experiments across multiple BPR-based architectures demonstrate that DDC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art debiasing methods, reducing training loss to less than 5% of heavily-tuned baselines while achieving superior recommendation quality and fairness. Code is available in https://github.com/LingFeng-Liu-AI/DDC.

full_text: Rethinking Popularity Bias in Collaborative Filtering via Analytical Vector Decomposition Popularity bias fundamentally undermines the personalization capabilities of collaborative filtering (CF) models, causing them to disproportionately recommend popular items while neglecting users' genuine preferences for niche content. While existing approaches treat this as an external confounding factor, we reveal that popularity bias is an intrinsic geometric artifact of Bayesian Pairwise Ranking (BPR) optimization in CF models. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, we prove that BPR systematically organizes item embeddings along a dominant "popularity direction" where embedding magnitudes directly correlate with interaction frequency. This geometric distortion forces user embeddings to simultaneously handle two conflicting tasks-expressing genuine preference and calibrating against global popularity-trapping them in suboptimal configurations that favor popular items regardless of individual tastes. We propose Directional Decomposition and Correction (DDC), a universally applicable framework that surgically corrects this embedding geometry through asymmetric directional updates. DDC guides positive interactions along personalized preference directions while steering negative interactions away from the global popularity direction, disentangling preference from popularity at the geometric source. Extensive experiments across multiple BPR-based architectures demonstrate that DDC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art debiasing methods, reducing training loss to less than 5% of heavily-tuned baselines while achieving superior recommendation quality and fairness. Code is available in https://github.com/LingFeng-Liu-AI/DDC.

en.title: Beyond Pixels: A Training-Free, Text-to-Text Framework for Remote Sensing Image Retrieval
en.abstract: Semantic retrieval of remote sensing (RS) images is a critical task fundamentally challenged by the \textquote{semantic gap}, the discrepancy between a model's low-level visual features and high-level human concepts. While large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer a promising path to bridge this gap, existing methods often rely on costly, domain-specific training, and there is a lack of benchmarks to evaluate the practical utility of VLM-generated text in a zero-shot retrieval context. To address this research gap, we introduce the Remote Sensing Rich Text (RSRT) dataset, a new benchmark featuring multiple structured captions per image. Based on this dataset, we propose a fully training-free, text-only retrieval reference called TRSLLaVA. Our methodology reformulates cross-modal retrieval as a text-to-text (T2T) matching problem, leveraging rich text descriptions as queries against a database of VLM-generated captions within a unified textual embedding space. This approach completely bypasses model training or fine-tuning. Experiments on the RSITMD and RSICD benchmarks show our training-free method is highly competitive with state-of-the-art supervised models. For instance, on RSITMD, our method achieves a mean Recall of 42.62\%, nearly doubling the 23.86\% of the standard zero-shot CLIP baseline and surpassing several top supervised models. This validates that high-quality semantic representation through structured text provides a powerful and cost-effective paradigm for remote sensing image retrieval.

summary.summary: A training-free framework for remote sensing image retrieval reformulates the task as text-to-text matching, converting images into rich, structured textual descriptions using large Vision-Language Models, and demonstrates performance competitive with or superior to fine-tuned supervised methods.
originalProblem: Traditional Remote Sensing Image Retrieval (RSIR) methods suffer from a "semantic gap" between low-level pixel data and high-level human concepts.
Existing VLM-based RSIR approaches lack true zero-shot generalization, relying on extensive supervised training, and often provide only coarse-grained image representations.
These methods utilize implicit and entangled feature spaces, hindering fine-grained and compositional querying of specific objects, attributes, or spatial relationships.
solution: The framework reformulates cross-modal retrieval as a training-free, text-to-text (T2T) matching problem, leveraging rich textual descriptions as the primary semantic representation.

A dedicated Remote Sensing Rich Text (RSRT) corpus is constructed offline, where GPT-4.1 generates five distinct, structured textual descriptions for each remote sensing image using specific instruction prompts.

During online retrieval, LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B textualizes image queries, and a frozen text encoder (`text-embedding-3-small`) maps all textual data into a unified embedding space for cosine similarity-based matching.
keyInsights: High-quality, VLM-generated structured text can effectively bridge the semantic gap and serve as a robust, explicit semantic representation for complex remote sensing images.
It is possible to achieve strong retrieval performance in remote sensing without any domain-specific training or fine-tuning, by entirely operating within a text-to-text paradigm.
Decomposing image content into explicit textual elements enables fine-grained and compositional querying, addressing limitations of single, coarse global feature vectors.
results: The introduced RSRT dataset comprises 17,764 images with 88,820 rich caption sets, featuring an average of 10.16 relations and 4.58 entities per image.
The framework achieves an overall mean Recall (mR) of 42.62% on RSITMD, nearly doubling the standard zero-shot CLIP-Baseline (23.86%) and outperforming several top supervised models.
On the RSICD dataset, it delivers an mR of 31.33%, more than double the CLIP-Baseline (15.64%), with particular strength in Image-to-Text (I2T) retrieval (R@5 of 38.39%, R@10 of 52.68%).

en.overview:
## Overview

Remote Sensing Image Retrieval (RSIR) has traditionally relied on content-based methods that struggle with the "semantic gap" - the disconnect between low-level pixel features and high-level human concepts. While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP have shown promise by learning shared representations between images and text, existing approaches in remote sensing typically require extensive domain-specific training and produce coarse-grained representations that compress complex satellite imagery into single feature vectors.

![Framework Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.10596v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: The TRSLLaVA framework pipeline, showing the offline construction of the RSRT dataset using GPT-4.1 to generate structured text descriptions from remote sensing images*

This paper presents TRSLLaVA, a training-free framework that fundamentally reformulates cross-modal retrieval in remote sensing as a pure text-to-text matching problem. By leveraging large language models to convert images into rich, structured textual descriptions, the approach bypasses the need for costly domain-specific training while enabling fine-grained queries about specific objects, attributes, and spatial relationships within satellite imagery.

## Methodology

The framework operates through a two-stage process: offline corpus construction and online retrieval. During the offline phase, the authors create the Remote Sensing Rich Text (RSRT) dataset by using GPT-4.1 to generate five distinct structured caption variants for each image from established benchmarks (RSICD and RSITMD). These captions include:

- A concise one-sentence summary
- A list of directional and relational features 
- A detailed descriptive paragraph

The generation process uses carefully designed prompts ($P_{structured}$) that instruct GPT-4.1 to focus on spatial relationships, object attributes, and compositional details. Quality control involves both automated checks (file validity, deduplication) and human auditing of a stratified sample to verify factual accuracy.

For online retrieval, all operations occur purely in text space using frozen models. Text-to-image retrieval embeds the query using OpenAI's `text-embedding-3-small` model and finds the maximum cosine similarity with any of the five description variants for each candidate image. Image-to-text retrieval first converts the query image to text using LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B, then proceeds with the same text-matching process.

The relevance score between query $T_q$ and candidate image $I_c$ is defined as:

$$
\text{Relevance}(T_q, I_c) = \max_{v \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}} \cos(v_q, v_{c,v})
$$

where $v_q$ is the embedded query vector and $v_{c,v}$ represents the embedded description variants for the candidate image.

## Key Contributions

The paper makes several significant contributions to remote sensing image retrieval:

**Training-Free Architecture**: Unlike existing methods that require extensive fine-tuning on remote sensing datasets, TRSLLaVA operates entirely with frozen, pre-trained models. This eliminates computational overhead while maintaining competitive performance.

**Rich Semantic Representation**: By converting images to structured text descriptions averaging 43 words across 3 sentences, the method captures fine-grained details including spatial relationships (average 10.16 relations per image) and object attributes that single feature vectors cannot represent.

**RSRT Benchmark Dataset**: The authors release a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating fine-grained, text-based retrieval in remote sensing, comprising 88,820 caption sets across 17,764 images.

![Quality Control Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.10596v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: The quality control pipeline showing automated checks and human verification processes, along with an example of the three types of structured captions generated for each image*

**Compositional Query Capability**: The framework enables complex queries like "a sports field with a red running track" rather than just generic category matches, addressing a key limitation of existing coarse-grained approaches.

## Experimental Results

The authors evaluate TRSLLaVA on two established benchmarks: RSITMD and RSICD. The results demonstrate substantial improvements over zero-shot baselines and competitive performance with supervised methods.

On RSITMD, TRSLLaVA achieves a mean Recall (mR) of 42.62%, nearly doubling the standard CLIP baseline (23.86%). The method shows particular strength in Recall@5 and Recall@10 metrics, with image-to-text retrieval reaching R@5 of 44.91% and R@10 of 61.28%. This indicates the framework's robustness in placing correct matches within the top candidates, which is crucial for practical applications.

On the more challenging RSICD dataset, the pattern holds with an mR of 31.33%, more than double the CLIP baseline (15.64%). The consistent superior performance in higher recall metrics (R@5, R@10) across both datasets validates the hypothesis that rich textual descriptions provide diverse semantic cues that improve retrieval robustness.

## Implications and Impact

This work represents a paradigm shift toward training-free, text-centric approaches in remote sensing image retrieval. By demonstrating that frozen VLMs can generate sufficiently rich semantic representations to outperform trained models, it opens new possibilities for resource-constrained applications and rapid deployment scenarios.

The framework's ability to handle fine-grained, compositional queries addresses critical needs in applications like urban planning, environmental monitoring, and disaster response, where users need to find specific object combinations or spatial arrangements. The superior performance in Recall@5 and Recall@10 metrics suggests practical utility for scenarios where users prefer multiple relevant results rather than a single perfect match.

The introduction of the RSRT benchmark provides the research community with a valuable resource for developing and evaluating future text-based retrieval methods. While the current approach relies on proprietary models (GPT-4.1) for corpus generation, the authors point toward future work exploring open-source alternatives, potentially leading to entirely reproducible and accessible RSIR pipelines.

The demonstrated effectiveness of general-purpose VLMs as "semantic knowledge bases" for specialized domains suggests broader applications beyond remote sensing, potentially influencing how other scientific and technical fields approach cross-modal retrieval problems.

zh.title: 超越像素：一个免训练的文本到文本遥感图像检索框架
zh.abstract:
遥感（RS）图像的语义检索是一项关键任务，但其根本挑战在于“语义鸿沟”，即模型低级视觉特征与高级人类概念之间的差异。尽管大型视觉-语言模型（VLMs）为弥合这一鸿沟提供了一条有前景的路径，但现有方法通常依赖于昂贵的、领域特定的训练，并且缺乏在零样本检索背景下评估VLM生成文本实用性的基准。

为解决这一研究空白，我们引入了遥感富文本（RSRT）数据集，这是一个每张图像包含多个结构化描述的新基准。基于此数据集，我们提出了一种名为TRSLLaVA的完全无需训练的纯文本检索参考方法。我们的方法将跨模态检索重新定义为文本到文本（T2T）匹配问题，在一个统一的文本嵌入空间内，利用富文本描述作为查询来匹配VLM生成的描述数据库。这种方法完全绕过了模型训练或微调。

在RSITMD和RSICD基准上的实验表明，我们的无需训练方法与最先进的监督模型相比具有高度竞争力。例如，在RSITMD上，我们的方法达到了42.62%的平均召回率，这几乎是标准零样本CLIP基线23.86%的两倍，并超越了多个顶级的监督模型。这验证了通过结构化文本实现高质量语义表示，为遥感图像检索提供了一种强大且经济高效的范式。

summary.summary: 一个用于遥感图像检索的免训练框架将任务重新定义为文本到文本的匹配，利用大型视觉-语言模型将图像转换为丰富、结构化的文本描述，并展示了与经过微调的监督方法相比具有竞争力甚至更优的性能。
originalProblem: 传统的遥感图像检索（RSIR）方法存在低级像素数据与高级人类概念之间的“语义鸿沟”问题。
现有的基于VLM的RSIR方法缺乏真正的零样本泛化能力，依赖于大量的监督训练，并且通常只提供粗粒度的图像表示。
这些方法使用隐式且纠缠的特征空间，阻碍了对特定对象、属性或空间关系的细粒度和组合式查询。
solution: 该框架将跨模态检索重新定义为一个免训练的文本到文本（T2T）匹配问题，利用丰富的文本描述作为主要的语义表示。
离线构建了一个专用的遥感富文本（RSRT）语料库，其中GPT-4.1使用特定的指令提示为每张遥感图像生成五种不同的结构化文本描述。
在在线检索过程中，LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B对图像查询进行文本化，然后一个冻结的文本编码器（`text-embedding-3-small`）将所有文本数据映射到一个统一的嵌入空间，用于基于余弦相似度的匹配。
keyInsights: 高质量、VLM生成的结构化文本可以有效地弥合语义鸿沟，并作为复杂遥感图像的鲁棒、显式语义表示。
通过完全在文本到文本范式内操作，可以在遥感领域实现强大的检索性能，而无需任何特定领域的训练或微调。
将图像内容分解为显式文本元素，可以实现细粒度和组合式查询，解决了单一、粗粒度全局特征向量的局限性。
results: 引入的RSRT数据集包含17,764张图像，共88,820个丰富的图像描述集，每张图像平均包含10.16个关系和4.58个实体。
该框架在RSITMD数据集上取得了42.62%的总体平均召回率（mR），几乎是标准零样本CLIP-Baseline（23.86%）的两倍，并且优于几个顶级的监督模型。
在RSICD数据集上，它实现了31.33%的mR，是CLIP-Baseline（15.64%）的两倍多，尤其在图像到文本（I2T）检索方面表现出色（R@5为38.39%，R@10为52.68%）。

zh.overview:
## 概述

遥感图像检索 (RSIR) 传统上依赖于基于内容的方法，这些方法难以解决“语义鸿沟”问题——即低级像素特征与高级人类概念之间的脱节。尽管像 CLIP 这样的视觉-语言模型 (VLM) 通过学习图像和文本之间的共享表示展现了前景，但遥感领域现有的方法通常需要大量的领域特定训练，并生成粗粒度表示，将复杂的卫星图像压缩成单一特征向量。

![Framework Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.10596v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图 1: TRSLLaVA 框架流程图，展示了使用 GPT-4.1 从遥感图像生成结构化文本描述的 RSRT 数据集的离线构建过程*

本文提出了 TRSLLaVA，一个无需训练的框架，它从根本上将遥感领域的跨模态检索重新定义为纯粹的文本到文本匹配问题。通过利用大型语言模型将图像转换为丰富、结构化的文本描述，该方法避免了昂贵的领域特定训练需求，同时能够对卫星图像中的特定对象、属性和空间关系进行细粒度查询。

## 方法论

该框架通过两阶段过程运行：离线语料库构建和在线检索。在离线阶段，作者使用 GPT-4.1 为来自既定基准数据集（RSICD 和 RSITMD）的每张图像生成五种不同的结构化描述变体，从而创建了遥感富文本 (RSRT) 数据集。这些描述包括：

-   简洁的一句话摘要
-   方向和关系特征列表
-   详细的描述性段落

生成过程使用精心设计的提示 ($P_{structured}$)，指导 GPT-4.1 关注空间关系、对象属性和构成细节。质量控制包括自动化检查（文件有效性、去重）和对分层样本进行人工审核以验证事实准确性。

对于在线检索，所有操作纯粹在文本空间中使用冻结模型进行。文本到图像检索使用 OpenAI 的 `text-embedding-3-small` 模型嵌入查询，并为每个候选图像找到与五种描述变体中任何一种的最大余弦相似度。图像到文本检索首先使用 LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B 将查询图像转换为文本，然后进行相同的文本匹配过程。

查询 $T_q$ 和候选图像 $I_c$ 之间的相关性得分定义为：

$$
\text{Relevance}(T_q, I_c) = \max_{v \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}} \cos(v_q, v_{c,v})
$$

其中 $v_q$ 是嵌入的查询向量，$v_{c,v}$ 表示候选图像的嵌入描述变体。

## 主要贡献

本文对遥感图像检索做出了几项重要贡献：

**免训练架构**：与现有方法需要对遥感数据集进行大量微调不同，TRSLLaVA 完全使用冻结的预训练模型进行操作。这消除了计算开销，同时保持了有竞争力的性能。

**丰富的语义表示**：通过将图像转换为平均每 3 句话 43 个单词的结构化文本描述，该方法捕获了细粒度细节，包括空间关系（平均每张图像 10.16 个关系）和单一特征向量无法表示的对象属性。

**RSRT 基准数据集**：作者发布了一个新基准，专门用于评估遥感领域的细粒度、基于文本的检索，该基准包含 17,764 张图像的 88,820 个描述集。

![Quality Control Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.10596v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图 2: 质量控制流程图，展示了自动化检查和人工验证过程，以及为每张图像生成的三种结构化描述的示例*

**组合查询能力**：该框架能够实现“带红色跑道的运动场”之类的复杂查询，而不仅仅是通用类别匹配，解决了现有粗粒度方法的关键局限性。

## 实验结果

作者在两个既有基准：RSITMD 和 RSICD 上评估了 TRSLLaVA。结果表明，与零样本基线相比，性能有显著提升，与监督方法相比，性能也具有竞争力。

在 RSITMD 上，TRSLLaVA 实现了 42.62% 的平均召回率 (mR)，几乎是标准 CLIP 基线 (23.86%) 的两倍。该方法在 Recall@5 和 Recall@10 指标上表现出特别的优势，图像到文本检索的 R@5 达到 44.91%，R@10 达到 61.28%。这表明该框架在将正确匹配项置于靠前候选位置方面的鲁棒性，这对于实际应用至关重要。

在更具挑战性的 RSICD 数据集上，该模式依然成立，mR 为 31.33%，是 CLIP 基线 (15.64%) 的两倍多。在两个数据集上，在更高召回率指标 (R@5, R@10) 上持续优越的性能验证了以下假设：丰富的文本描述提供了多样化的语义线索，从而提高了检索的鲁棒性。

## 影响与意义

这项工作代表了遥感图像检索领域向免训练、以文本为中心的方法的范式转变。通过证明冻结的 VLM 可以生成足够丰富的语义表示以超越训练模型，它为资源受限的应用和快速部署场景开辟了新的可能性。

该框架处理细粒度、组合查询的能力解决了城市规划、环境监测和灾害响应等应用中的关键需求，在这些应用中，用户需要查找特定的对象组合或空间排列。在 Recall@5 和 Recall@10 指标上的卓越性能表明，对于用户更喜欢多个相关结果而不是单个完美匹配的场景，它具有实际实用性。

RSRT 基准的引入为研究社区提供了一个宝贵的资源，用于开发和评估未来的基于文本的检索方法。尽管当前的方法依赖于专有模型 (GPT-4.1) 来生成语料库，但作者指出未来的工作将探索开源替代方案，这可能导致完全可复现和可访问的 RSIR 管道。

通用 VLM 作为专业领域“语义知识库”所展示的有效性表明了遥感之外的更广泛应用，可能会影响其他科学和技术领域处理跨模态检索问题的方式。

abstract: Semantic retrieval of remote sensing (RS) images is a critical task fundamentally challenged by the \textquote{semantic gap}, the discrepancy between a model's low-level visual features and high-level human concepts. While large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer a promising path to bridge this gap, existing methods often rely on costly, domain-specific training, and there is a lack of benchmarks to evaluate the practical utility of VLM-generated text in a zero-shot retrieval context. To address this research gap, we introduce the Remote Sensing Rich Text (RSRT) dataset, a new benchmark featuring multiple structured captions per image. Based on this dataset, we propose a fully training-free, text-only retrieval reference called TRSLLaVA. Our methodology reformulates cross-modal retrieval as a text-to-text (T2T) matching problem, leveraging rich text descriptions as queries against a database of VLM-generated captions within a unified textual embedding space. This approach completely bypasses model training or fine-tuning. Experiments on the RSITMD and RSICD benchmarks show our training-free method is highly competitive with state-of-the-art supervised models. For instance, on RSITMD, our method achieves a mean Recall of 42.62\%, nearly doubling the 23.86\% of the standard zero-shot CLIP baseline and surpassing several top supervised models. This validates that high-quality semantic representation through structured text provides a powerful and cost-effective paradigm for remote sensing image retrieval.

abstract: Effective code retrieval is indispensable and it has become an important paradigm to search code in hybrid mode using both natural language and code snippets. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether existing approaches can effectively leverage such hybrid queries, particularly in cross-language contexts. We conduct a comprehensive empirical study of representative code models and reveal three challenges: (1) insufficient semantic understanding; (2) inefficient fusion in hybrid code retrieval; and (3) weak generalization in cross-language scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose UniCoR, a novel self-supervised framework that learns Unified Code Representations framework designed to learn unified and robust code representations. Firstly, we design a multi-perspective supervised contrastive learning module to enhance semantic understanding and modality fusion. It aligns representations from multiple perspectives, including code-to-code, natural language-to-code, and natural language-to-natural language, enforcing the model to capture a semantic essence among modalities. Secondly, we introduce a representation distribution consistency learning module to improve cross-language generalization, which explicitly aligns the feature distributions of different programming languages, enabling language-agnostic representation learning. Extensive experiments on both empirical benchmark and large-scale benchmark show that UniCoR outperforms all baseline models, achieving an average improvement of 8.64% in MRR and 11.54% in MAP over the best-performing baseline. Furthermore, UniCoR exhibits stability in hybrid code retrieval and generalization capability in cross-language scenarios.
