citations.justification: This paper establishes the core technique of using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to discover interpretable, monosemantic features within LLMs. The main paper's central methodological contribution is leveraging this SAE-based interpretability to detect hallucinations in RAG.

citations.title: Redeep: Detecting hallucination in retrieval-augmented generation via mechanistic interpretability
citations.fullCitation: Zhongxiang Sun, Xiaoxue Zang, Kai Zheng, Jun Xu, Xiao Zhang, Weijie Yu, Yang Song, and Han Li. citations.justification: This paper represents a direct state-of-the-art approach for RAG hallucination detection using internal model representations, the same specific problem RAGLens addresses. The main paper explicitly compares its performance against this method to demonstrate its superior effectiveness.

zh.title: 迈向基于稀疏自编码器的忠实检索增强生成
zh.abstract: 检索增强生成（RAG）通过将输出基于检索到的证据，提升了大型语言模型（LLM）的事实性，但忠实性失效（即生成内容与提供的信息相矛盾或超出其范围）仍然是一个严峻的挑战。现有的RAG幻觉检测方法通常依赖于大规模检测器训练（这需要大量的标注数据），或依赖于查询外部LLM判官（这导致高昂的推理成本）。尽管有些方法试图利用LLM的内部表示进行幻觉检测，但其准确性仍然有限。受机制可解释性最新进展的启发，我们采用了稀疏自编码器（SAE）来解耦内部激活，成功识别出在RAG幻觉发生时被特异性激活的特征。基于信息熵特征选择和加性特征建模的系统流程，我们引入了RAGLens，一种轻量级幻觉检测器，它能利用LLM的内部表示准确标记不忠实的RAG输出。RAGLens不仅在检测性能上优于现有方法，而且为其决策提供了可解释的理由，从而实现了对不忠实RAG的有效事后缓解。最后，我们论证了我们的设计选择，并揭示了关于LLM内部幻觉相关信号分布的新见解。代码可在 [https://this.url](https://this.url) 获取。

summary.summary: RAGLens是一个轻量级框架，通过利用大型语言模型(LLM)内部状态上的稀疏自编码器(Sparse Autoencoders, SAEs)，准确识别并解释检索增强生成(RAG)输出中的忠实性问题。该方法在RAG基准测试中实现了超过80%的AUC，并提供了可解释的、令牌级的反馈，以有效缓解幻觉。
originalProblem: 尽管提供了外部证据，检索增强生成(RAG)系统仍然存在幻觉问题，产生事实不准确或无根据的信息。
现有的RAG幻觉检测方法受限于高数据需求、巨大的计算开销，或在探测LLM内部表示时准确性和可解释性不足。
LLM内部表示固有的不透明性和多义性阻碍了提取清晰、可靠的幻觉相关特征，从而影响了有效检测。
solution: RAGLens利用预训练的稀疏自编码器(SAEs)从冻结的LLM隐藏状态的特定层中提取解耦的、语义有意义的特征，隐式捕获上下文-答案交互。
它采用通道最大池化(channel-wise max pooling)将令牌级SAE激活汇总为实例级表示，然后通过基于互信息(Mutual Information)的特征选择来识别最具区分性的特征。
使用广义加性模型(Generalized Additive Model, GAM)作为透明预测器，根据选定的SAE特征对幻觉进行分类，同时为每个特征的贡献提供可解释的形状函数。
keyInsights: LLM在其内部表示中拥有潜在的忠实性信号，这些信号并非总是通过明确推理表达出来，SAEs可以有效地揭示这些信号，这表明LLM通常“知道的比它们说的多”。
SAE特征可以解耦为语义一致的概念（例如，“不支持的数字/时间细节”），为RAG幻觉检测提供细粒度的可解释性。
RAGLens通过GAM和特征归因提供的可解释性，能够进行局部（令牌级）和全局（特征级）解释，从而促进可操作的事后缓解策略。
results: RAGLens在RAGTruth和Dolly基准测试中持续实现了卓越的幻觉检测性能，AUC分数超过80%，显著优于各种LLM骨干的基线模型。
该框架展示了强大的跨模型和跨领域泛化能力，在未见过的数据集上优于LLM CoT风格的自我判断，并表明泛化能力与训练数据多样性相关。
利用RAGLens的可解释反馈进行缓解，实例级和令牌级警告都有效降低了LLM修订中的幻觉率，其中令牌级反馈带来了更大的改进。

zh.overview:
## 引言

大型语言模型（LLMs）在文本生成方面取得了卓越的能力，但它们仍然容易出现“幻觉”，即生成事实上不正确或缺乏依据的信息。检索增强生成（RAG）作为一种有前景的解决方案应运而生，它将LLM的输出建立在外部证据来源之上。然而，即使是RAG系统也无法完全避免忠实性失败，即生成内容与提供的上下文相矛盾或超出其范围。本文介绍了RAGLens，这是一种利用稀疏自编码器（SAEs）通过探测LLM的内部表示来检测RAG幻觉的新方法。

![RAGLens 框架概述](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08892v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：RAGLens 框架由三个主要组件组成：使用SAE特征进行幻觉检测、通过特征分析提供可解释的解释以及通过反馈循环进行缓解。该系统从LLM隐藏状态中提取令牌级特征，应用最大池化和特征选择，然后使用广义加性模型进行透明预测。*

## 问题背景与现有方法的局限性

现有检测RAG幻觉的方法可分为几类，每类都有其显著局限性。微调专业检测器需要大量的标注训练数据，这既昂贵又耗时。将LLM作为判官的方法会增加计算开销，并且可能难以检测由同一模型产生的幻觉。此前探测LLM内部表示的尝试受到神经元多义性和隐藏状态不透明性的限制。

可解释机器学习领域借助稀疏自编码器（SAEs）取得了显著进展，SAEs能够从高维LLM表示中解耦出具有语义意义的特征。这些特征通常对应于人类可解释的概念，为理解和控制LLM行为提供了途径。然而，它们在RAG特定幻觉检测中的应用仍未得到充分探索。

## 方法论：RAGLens 框架

RAGLens 通过一个系统的三阶段管道解决了RAG幻觉检测的挑战，该管道将内部LLM表示转换为可解释的幻觉预测。

### 问题公式化

任务被公式化为二元分类：给定用户查询 (q)、检索到的段落 (C) 和 LLM 生成的答案 (y)，确定 y 是否包含相对于 C 的幻觉。该方法假设可以访问冻结的 LLM (Φ) 和一个在特定层 (L) 的隐藏状态上操作的预训练 SAE (E)。令牌级隐藏状态被转换为稀疏特征：

$$
z_t = E(h_t) \text{ 其中 } h_t = \Phi_L(y_{1:t}, q, C)
$$

至关重要的是，虽然 SAE 在一般语料库上进行训练，但 RAGLens 中 y 的编码是以 C 和 q 为条件的，这使得 SAE 特征能够隐式捕获上下文-答案交互。

### 实例级特征聚合

由于幻觉标签是在实例级别分配的，因此必须将令牌级 SAE 激活汇总为单个表示。RAGLens 采用通道级最大池化：

$$
\bar{z}_k = \max_{1 \le t \le T} z_{t,k}
$$

作者通过定理1为这一选择提供了理论依据，证明在稀疏激活机制下，最大池化能够放大相关信号，同时抑制噪声。该定理表明，关于标签的互信息与序列长度 T 呈线性关系，与幻觉和非幻觉情况下激活概率的差异呈二次关系。

### 基于信息的特征选择

为了关注最具判别性的特征，RAGLens 使用互信息（MI）量化每个池化特征的相关性：

$$
I(\bar{z}_k; \ell)
$$

特征按MI分数排序，并选择前K'个维度，从而得到一个简化的特征向量，该向量在保持计算效率的同时，保留了用于幻觉检测的最具信息量的信号。

### 基于广义加性模型的透明预测

将所选特征输入广义加性模型（GAM）进行二元分类：

$$
g(E[\ell | \tilde{\bar{z}}]) = \beta_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{K'} f_j(\tilde{\bar{z}}_j)
$$

选择GAMs是专门为了其可解释性——每个特征的贡献都可以独立建模并可视化为形状函数。这种设计避免了黑箱复杂性，同时捕获了特征与幻觉预测之间的非线性关系。

## 实验结果与性能分析

### 卓越的检测性能

RAGLens在多个基准测试中始终优于现有基线。在RAGTruth和Dolly数据集上，使用Llama2-7B和Llama2-13B作为骨干模型，RAGLens实现了超过80%的AUC分数，显著超越了基于提示、基于不确定性和其他内部表示方法。

![跨模型性能比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08892v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：RAGLens（基于SAE，红色条）与思维链自评估（CoT，蓝色条）在不同模型和数据集上的性能比较。RAGLens持续优于CoT方法，表明模型拥有关于幻觉的内部知识，但这种知识并非总是通过显式推理表达出来。*

### 跨模型泛化：“知其然，不言其所以然”

跨模型评估中出现了一个关键发现：基于SAE的检测器在各种模型（Llama2、Llama3、Qwen）和数据集上，始终优于LLM自身的思维链（CoT）自判断。这表明LLM在其内部表示中拥有潜在的忠实度信号，这些信号并非总是通过显式推理表达出来，而SAE能够有效地揭示这些“隐藏”信号。

### 领域和任务泛化

RAGLens在多样化数据集上训练时表现出强大的泛化能力。该框架在不同RAG任务（摘要、问答、数据到文本）之间展现出有效的迁移，其中经过摘要训练的检测器表现出最强的整体泛化能力。

![逐层性能分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08892v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图3：RAGTruth三个子任务在不同LLM层上的性能热图。分析表明，中间层（归一化深度约为0.5）包含摘要和问答任务中幻觉检测最具信息量的信号，而Data2txt则显示出更分散的模式。*

## 设计选择分析和消融研究

### 最佳层选择

研究表明，摘要和问答任务的性能在中间层附近达到峰值，这表明这些层捕获了RAG幻觉检测中最具信息量的信号。数据到文本任务在各层中的性能表现较为平坦，表明其表示动态不同。

### 特征选择效率

![特征选择影响](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08892v1/img-3.jpeg)
*图4：随着所选特征数量的减少，性能下降。基于互信息（MI）的选择（蓝色）显著优于随机选择（橙色），即使在特征集大幅减少的情况下也能保持强大的性能。*

基于互信息的特征选择显著优于随机选择，证明了其在识别最具信息量特征方面的有效性。即使在特征集大幅减少的情况下，性能依然保持稳健，凸显了该方法的效率。

### 预测器架构比较

![预测器架构比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08892v1/img-4.jpeg)
*图5：雷达图比较了不同预测器架构（LR、GAM、MLP、XGBoost）在多个模型-数据集组合下的表现。GAM（粉色线）始终保持高性能，同时相比更复杂的模型具有可解释性优势。*

GAM在不同数据集和模型上始终优于逻辑回归、MLP和XGBoost。这验证了以下假设：尽管单个特征效应可能是非线性的，但它们对幻觉信号的集体贡献可以通过加性方式很好地捕获。

### SAE特征与原始隐藏状态

![SAE与隐藏状态性能](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08892v1/img-5.jpeg)
*图6：比较SAE特征（蓝色）与原始隐藏状态（橙色）随着特征数量减少时的表现。SAE特征在性能保持上明显优于隐藏状态，尤其是在特征数量减少时，这表明它们在压缩幻觉相关信号方面具有卓越能力。*

当特征数量减少时，SAE特征在性能保持上显著优于原始隐藏状态，尤其是在单任务数据集上。这突出了SAE将幻觉相关信号解耦并压缩为更具可解释性和效率的表示的能力。

## 可解释性与可操作的解释

RAGLens为其预测提供局部和全局解释。局部解释通过稀疏特征归因识别特定的问题文本段，而全局解释则利用SAE特征的语义一致性提供人类可理解的概念（例如，“不支持的数字/时间细节”）。研究表明，较小的LLM倾向于表现出更通用的幻觉特征，而较大的模型则发展出更具体和细致的模式。

## 实际缓解能力

RAGLens提供的可解释反馈能够实现有效的后验缓解。当Llama2-7B在RAGLens反馈的提示下修改输出时，实例级和令牌级反馈都降低了幻觉率。RAGLens的可解释性实现的令牌级反馈始终带来更大的改进，这证明了透明解释的实用价值。

## 意义与未来方向

RAGLens代表了可信AI的重大进步，它为RAG系统提供了准确、可解释和可操作的幻觉检测。该框架弥合了机制可解释性与实际NLP应用之间的鸿沟，验证了SAE可以有效地为复杂的应用问题解耦有意义的特征。

这项研究开辟了几个有前途的方向：开发生成过程中的先发控制机制、创建领域特定的特征工程方法，以及将RAGLens直接集成到RAG管道中进行持续监控。该方法的轻量级特性，利用选定的SAE特征和GAM分类器，使其在实际部署中具有计算效率。

这项工作从根本上推进了我们对LLM如何内部表示忠实度的理解，并证明了复杂的解释工具可以为构建更值得信赖的AI系统带来实际好处。

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the factuality of large language models (LLMs) by grounding outputs in retrieved evidence, but faithfulness failures, where generations contradict or extend beyond the provided sources, remain a critical challenge. Existing hallucination detection methods for RAG often rely either on large-scale detector training, which requires substantial annotated data, or on querying external LLM judges, which leads to high inference costs. Although some approaches attempt to leverage internal representations of LLMs for hallucination detection, their accuracy remains limited. Motivated by recent advances in mechanistic interpretability, we employ sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to disentangle internal activations, successfully identifying features that are specifically triggered during RAG hallucinations. Building on a systematic pipeline of information-based feature selection and additive feature modeling, we introduce RAGLens, a lightweight hallucination detector that accurately flags unfaithful RAG outputs using LLM internal representations. RAGLens not only achieves superior detection performance compared to existing methods, but also provides interpretable rationales for its decisions, enabling effective post-hoc mitigation of unfaithful RAG. Finally, we justify our design choices and reveal new insights into the distribution of hallucination-related signals within LLMs. The code is available at https://github.com/Teddy-XiongGZ/RAGLens.

full_text: Toward Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Sparse Autoencoders Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the factuality of large language models (LLMs) by grounding outputs in retrieved evidence, but faithfulness failures, where generations contradict or extend beyond the provided sources, remain a critical challenge. Existing hallucination detection methods for RAG often rely either on large-scale detector training, which requires substantial annotated data, or on querying external LLM judges, which leads to high inference costs. Although some approaches attempt to leverage internal representations of LLMs for hallucination detection, their accuracy remains limited. Motivated by recent advances in mechanistic interpretability, we employ sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to disentangle internal activations, successfully identifying features that are specifically triggered during RAG hallucinations. Building on a systematic pipeline of information-based feature selection and additive feature modeling, we introduce RAGLens, a lightweight hallucination detector that accurately flags unfaithful RAG outputs using LLM internal representations. RAGLens not only achieves superior detection performance compared to existing methods, but also provides interpretable rationales for its decisions, enabling effective post-hoc mitigation of unfaithful RAG. Finally, we justify our design choices and reveal new insights into the distribution of hallucination-related signals within LLMs. The code is available at https://github.com/Teddy-XiongGZ/RAGLens.

abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative components, such as LoRAs, has created a vast but unstructured ecosystem. Existing discovery methods depend on unreliable user descriptions or biased popularity metrics, hindering usability. We present CARLoS, a large-scale framework for characterizing LoRAs without requiring additional metadata. Analyzing over 650 LoRAs, we employ them in image generation over a variety of prompts and seeds, as a credible way to assess their behavior. Using CLIP embeddings and their difference to a base-model generation, we concisely define a three-part representation: Directions, defining semantic shift; Strength, quantifying the significance of the effect; and Consistency, quantifying how stable the effect is. Using these representations, we develop an efficient retrieval framework that semantically matches textual queries to relevant LoRAs while filtering overly strong or unstable ones, outperforming textual baselines in automated and human evaluations. While retrieval is our primary focus, the same representation also supports analyses linking Strength and Consistency to legal notions of substantiality and volition, key considerations in copyright, positioning CARLoS as a practical system with broader relevance for LoRA analysis.
title: CARLoS: Retrieval via Concise Assessment Representation of LoRAs at Scale

abstract: Phase retrieval using a frame for a finite-dimensional Hilbert space is known to always be Lipschitz stable. However, phase retrieval using a frame or a continuous frame for an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is always unstable. In order to bridge the gap between the finite and infinite dimensional phenomena, Cahill-Casazza-Daubechies (Trans.Amer.Math.Soc. 2016) gave a construction of a family of nonlinear subsets of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space where phase retrieval could be performed with a Hölder stability estimate. They then posed the question of whether these subsets satisfied Lipschitz stable phase retrieval. We solve this problem both by giving examples which fail Lipschitz stability and by giving examples which satisfy Lipschitz stability.
title: The Cahill-Casazza-Daubechies problem on Hölder stable phase retrieval

en.title: VI-MMRec: Similarity-Aware Training Cost-free Virtual User-Item Interactions for Multimodal Recommendation
en.abstract: Although existing multimodal recommendation models have shown promising performance, their effectiveness continues to be limited by the pervasive data sparsity problem. This problem arises because users typically interact with only a small subset of available items, leading existing models to arbitrarily treat unobserved items as negative samples. To this end, we propose VI-MMRec, a model-agnostic and training cost-free framework that enriches sparse user-item interactions via similarity-aware virtual user-item interactions. These virtual interactions are constructed based on modality-specific feature similarities of user-interacted items. Specifically, VI-MMRec introduces two different strategies: (1) Overlay, which independently aggregates modality-specific similarities to preserve modality-specific user preferences, and (2) Synergistic, which holistically fuses cross-modal similarities to capture complementary user preferences. To ensure high-quality augmentation, we design a statistically informed weight allocation mechanism that adaptively assigns weights to virtual user-item interactions based on dataset-specific modality relevance. As a plug-and-play framework, VI-MMRec seamlessly integrates with existing models to enhance their performance without modifying their core architecture. Its flexibility allows it to be easily incorporated into various existing models, maximizing performance with minimal implementation effort. Moreover, VI-MMRec introduces no additional overhead during training, making it significantly advantageous for practical deployment. Comprehensive experiments conducted on six real-world datasets using seven state-of-the-art multimodal recommendation models validate the effectiveness of our VI-MMRec.

summary.summary: VI-MMRec introduces a model-agnostic, training cost-free framework that generates similarity-aware virtual user-item interactions from multimodal item features. This method consistently enhances the performance of state-of-the-art multimodal recommendation models by up to 22.25% in Recall@10, effectively addressing data sparsity and improving cold-start recommendations.
originalProblem: Pervasive data sparsity in multimodal recommendation systems, where users interact with only a tiny fraction of available items.
Conventional approaches arbitrarily treat unobserved user-item pairs as negative samples, leading to a loss of genuine latent user preferences.
Existing models primarily focus on architectural improvements rather than enriching the fundamental sparse interaction data.
solution: VI-MMRec constructs 'similarity-aware virtual user-item interactions' by leveraging item modality-specific features (e.g., visual, textual) to find items highly similar to those a user has already interacted with.
It offers two strategies for virtual interaction generation: Overlay (modality-specific aggregation) and Synergistic (holistic cross-modal summation).

A statistically informed weight allocation mechanism adaptively assigns weights to virtual interactions based on their relevance to real user preferences, ensuring high-quality data augmentation without additional training cost for the downstream model.
keyInsights: Modality similarity strongly correlates with user preferences, and multiple modal similarities can synergistically infer latent preferences for unobserved items.

The Overlay strategy, independently aggregating modality-specific similarities, generally outperforms the holistic Synergistic approach, indicating the importance of preserving distinct modal preference signals.
Adaptive weighting of virtual interactions based on dataset characteristics and overlap rates with real interactions is crucial for effective and robust data augmentation.
results: Consistently improved Recall@10 and NDCG@10 for all seven baseline multimodal recommendation models across six real-world datasets, with improvements up to 22.25% in Recall@10 for MMGCN on the TikTok dataset.
Demonstrated significant enhancements in mitigating data sparsity across varying user interaction counts and substantially boosted performance in cold-start scenarios.
Maintained stable performance gains and improved model robustness even when item features were subjected to different levels of representation noise or information errors.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Multimodal recommender systems represent a significant advancement over traditional collaborative filtering approaches, incorporating rich content information like visual features, textual descriptions, and audio data to enhance recommendation quality. However, these systems still face a fundamental challenge: the data sparsity problem. Users typically interact with only a tiny fraction of available items, forcing models to treat most unobserved user-item pairs as negative examples during training. This approach potentially discards valuable latent user preferences, limiting the effectiveness of even the most sophisticated multimodal architectures.

VI-MMRec addresses this challenge through a fundamentally different approach - rather than developing yet another complex model architecture, it focuses on enriching the underlying interaction data itself. The framework leverages multimodal item similarities to construct "virtual user-item interactions" that capture latent user preferences, providing a richer foundation for any downstream multimodal recommender system.

![VI-MMRec Framework](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-0.jpeg)

*Figure 1: Overview of the VI-MMRec framework showing both Overlay and Synergistic strategies for constructing virtual user-item interactions using multimodal similarities.*

## Core Methodology

The VI-MMRec framework operates on a simple yet powerful intuition: users who interact with an item are likely to be interested in other items that share similar visual, textual, or audio characteristics. The framework implements this through two complementary strategies for generating virtual interactions.

### Similarity-Based Virtual Interaction Construction

The foundation of VI-MMRec lies in computing item-item similarities using pre-trained, frozen multimodal encoders. For each modality $m$ (visual, textual, audio), the framework calculates cosine similarity between item embeddings:

$$
S_{i,j}^m = \frac{e_i^m \cdot e_j^m}{||e_i^m|| \cdot ||e_j^m||}
$$

where $e_i^m$ represents the embedding of item $i$ in modality $m$.

**Overlay Strategy**: This approach maintains separate similarity matrices for each modality. For every observed user-item interaction $(u, i)$, the framework identifies the top-$k$ most similar items to $i$ within each modality $m$, forming modality-specific item sets $I_{u,i}^m$. Virtual interaction matrices $R^m$ are then constructed for each modality, where $R_{u,j}^m = 1$ if item $j$ appears in any $I_{u,i}^m$ for user $u$.

**Synergistic Strategy**: Instead of treating modalities separately, this approach combines similarities across all modalities:

$$
S_{i,j}^s = \sum_{m} S_{i,j}^m
$$

This creates a single holistic similarity matrix that captures cross-modal complementarity, from which virtual interactions are generated using the same top-$k$ selection process.

### Statistically Informed Weight Allocation

A critical innovation in VI-MMRec is its adaptive weighting mechanism that ensures high-quality virtual interactions. Rather than arbitrarily assigning weights, the framework employs a statistically grounded approach:

$$
w^m = \frac{O_{real}^m}{O_{avg}}
$$

where $O_{real}^m$ represents the overlap rate between virtual interactions generated for modality $m$ and actual user interactions, while $O_{avg}$ serves as a baseline computed from randomly generated virtual interactions. This ratio ensures that modalities more predictive of actual user preferences receive higher weights.

The final augmented interaction matrix is constructed as:

$$
\bar{R} = \text{Confine}(R + \lambda \sum_m w^m R^m)
$$

for the Overlay strategy, where the $\text{Confine}()$ function ensures interaction weights remain within the realistic range [0,1], and $\lambda$ controls the overall influence of virtual interactions.

## Experimental Validation and Results

The framework was extensively evaluated across six real-world datasets (Baby, Sports, Clothing, Pet, Office, TikTok) and seven state-of-the-art multimodal recommendation models (MMGCN, DualGNN, SLMRec, FREEDOM, DRAGON, LGMRec, DiffMM).

### Performance Improvements

VI-MMRec demonstrated consistent and significant improvements across all tested combinations. The Overlay strategy (VI-MMRec-O) generally outperformed the Synergistic strategy (VI-MMRec-S), with improvements in Recall@10 ranging from 8.26% on the Clothing dataset to 22.25% on the TikTok dataset when applied to MMGCN. The TikTok dataset, which incorporates audio modality alongside visual and textual features, showed the highest performance gains, suggesting that richer multimodal contexts enable more accurate virtual interaction inference.

![Ablation Study Results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-1.jpeg)

*Figure 2: Ablation study results showing the importance of both refinement ("w/o Refine") and confinement ("w/o Confine") components across all datasets and models.*

### Data Sparsity Analysis

The framework's effectiveness was particularly pronounced in sparse data scenarios. Analysis across different user interaction count groups (0-5, 5-10, 10-15, 15-20, 20-25 interactions) revealed consistent improvements, with the most significant gains observed for users with fewer historical interactions.

![Data Sparsity Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-2.jpeg)

*Figure 3: Performance analysis across different user interaction count groups, demonstrating VI-MMRec's effectiveness in various sparsity scenarios.*

### Hyperparameter Sensitivity

The framework showed reasonable robustness to hyperparameter choices. The optimal number of similar items ($k$) was typically 10 for most datasets, though the TikTok dataset benefited from $k=20$, suggesting that richer multimodal information can effectively utilize a broader range of similar items. The virtual interaction weight ($\lambda$) generally performed best at $1 \times 10^{-2}$, with slight variations across datasets.

![Hyperparameter Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-3.jpeg)

*Figure 4: Sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters $k$ (number of similar items) and $\lambda$ (virtual interaction weight) across different datasets.*

## Technical Advantages and Practical Impact

VI-MMRec's design offers several key advantages that distinguish it from existing approaches:

**Training Cost-Free Operation**: The framework operates as a preprocessing step, constructing virtual interactions once using frozen pre-trained encoders. This ensures no additional computational overhead during the training phase of downstream recommendation models.

**Model Agnostic Integration**: The plug-and-play design allows seamless integration with any existing multimodal recommendation architecture without requiring modifications to the base model structure or training procedures.

**Robustness to Noise**: Experiments with injected Gaussian noise and information errors demonstrated that VI-MMRec maintains its performance benefits even under noisy conditions, attributed to its use of similarity ranges rather than strict thresholds.

**Cold Start Enhancement**: The framework showed particular effectiveness for cold-start scenarios, where users have minimal interaction history. By providing additional signals based on multimodal similarities, VI-MMRec helps models better align multimodal information with user behavior patterns.

## Limitations and Future Directions

While VI-MMRec demonstrates strong empirical performance, several areas warrant future investigation. The framework relies on pre-trained modality encoders whose quality directly impacts virtual interaction quality. Additionally, the current approach focuses on similarity-based augmentation, potentially overlooking other forms of latent user preferences.

Future research directions could explore dynamic virtual interaction generation that adapts during training, investigation of more sophisticated similarity measures beyond cosine similarity, and extension to other recommendation scenarios such as sequential or session-based recommendation.

The framework's success in improving diverse multimodal recommender systems suggests broader applicability to other domains where data sparsity challenges exist, potentially extending beyond recommendation systems to other collaborative learning scenarios.

zh.title: VI-MMRec: 面向多模态推荐的相似感知免训练成本虚拟用户-物品交互
zh.abstract: 尽管现有多模态推荐模型已展现出可观的性能，但其有效性仍受普遍存在的数据稀疏性问题所限。这个问题产生的原因是用户通常只与一小部分可用物品进行交互，从而导致现有模型任意地将未观察到的物品视为负样本。为此，我们提出了VI-MMRec，这是一个与模型无关且训练零成本的框架，旨在通过相似性感知的虚拟用户-物品交互来丰富稀疏的用户-物品交互。这些虚拟交互是基于用户已交互物品的模态特征相似性构建的。具体而言，VI-MMRec引入了两种不同的策略：(1) “叠加”策略，它独立聚合模态特征相似性以保留模态特定的用户偏好；以及 (2) “协同”策略，它整体地融合跨模态相似性以捕获互补的用户偏好。为确保高质量的增强，我们设计了一种基于统计信息的权重分配机制，该机制能够根据数据集特定的模态相关性自适应地为虚拟用户-物品交互分配权重。作为一个即插即用框架，VI-MMRec能够无缝地与现有模型集成，以增强其性能而无需修改其核心架构。其灵活性使其易于集成到各种现有模型中，以最小的实现代价最大化性能。此外，VI-MMRec在训练过程中不引入额外开销，这使其在实际部署中具有显著优势。在六个真实世界数据集上，使用七个最先进的多模态推荐模型进行的全面实验，验证了我们VI-MMRec的有效性。

summary.summary: VI-MMRec引入了一个与模型无关、无需训练成本的框架，它能从多模态物品特征中生成相似度感知的虚拟用户-物品交互。该方法持续提升了最先进的多模态推荐模型的性能，在Recall@10上最高提升22.25%，有效解决了数据稀疏性问题并改善了冷启动推荐。
originalProblem: 多模态推荐系统中普遍存在的数据稀疏性问题，用户只与极少一部分可用物品进行交互。
传统方法武断地将未观察到的用户-物品对视为负样本，导致真实的潜在用户偏好丢失。
现有模型主要关注架构改进，而不是丰富基础的稀疏交互数据。
solution: VI-MMRec通过利用物品模态特定特征（例如视觉、文本）来寻找与用户已交互物品高度相似的物品，从而构建“相似度感知的虚拟用户-物品交互”。
它提供了两种虚拟交互生成策略：叠加（模态特定聚合）和协同（整体跨模态求和）。
一种基于统计的权重分配机制根据虚拟交互与真实用户偏好的相关性自适应地分配权重，确保高质量的数据增强，同时不为下游模型增加额外训练成本。
keyInsights: 模态相似性与用户偏好密切相关，并且多种模态相似性可以协同推断未观测物品的潜在偏好。
叠加策略（独立聚合模态特定相似性）通常优于整体协同方法，这表明保留不同的模态偏好信号的重要性。
根据数据集特征和与真实交互的重叠率对虚拟交互进行自适应加权对于有效和鲁棒的数据增强至关重要。
results: 在六个真实世界数据集中，持续提升了所有七个基线多模态推荐模型在Recall@10和NDCG@10上的表现，其中在TikTok数据集上，MMGCN的Recall@10最高提升了22.25%。
在不同用户交互次数下，显著增强了缓解数据稀疏性的能力，并大幅提升了冷启动场景下的性能。
即使物品特征受到不同程度的表示噪声或信息错误影响，也能保持稳定的性能提升并提高了模型的鲁棒性。

## 引言

多模态推荐系统在传统协同过滤方法的基础上取得了显著进步，它整合了视觉特征、文本描述和音频数据等丰富的内容信息，以提升推荐质量。然而，这些系统仍然面临一个根本性挑战：数据稀疏性问题。用户通常只与可用物品的极小部分进行交互，这迫使模型在训练过程中将大多数未观察到的用户-物品对视为负样本。这种方法可能会丢弃有价值的潜在用户偏好，从而限制了即使是最复杂的多模态架构的有效性。

VI-MMRec 通过一种根本不同的方法来解决这一挑战——它不是开发另一种复杂的模型架构，而是专注于丰富底层的交互数据本身。该框架利用多模态物品相似性来构建“虚拟用户-物品交互”，从而捕捉潜在的用户偏好，为任何下游多模态推荐系统提供更丰富的基础。

![VI-MMRec 框架](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-0.jpeg)

*图 1：VI-MMRec 框架概述，展示了使用多模态相似性构建虚拟用户-物品交互的覆盖策略和协同策略。*

## 核心方法论

VI-MMRec 框架基于一个简单而强大的直觉：与某个物品交互的用户，很可能对其他具有相似视觉、文本或音频特征的物品感兴趣。该框架通过两种互补的策略来实现虚拟交互的生成。

### 基于相似性的虚拟交互构建

VI-MMRec 的基础在于使用预训练的、冻结的多模态编码器计算物品间的相似性。对于每种模态 $m$（视觉、文本、音频），框架计算物品嵌入之间的余弦相似性：

$$
S_{i,j}^m = \frac{e_i^m \cdot e_j^m}{||e_i^m|| \cdot ||e_j^m||}
$$

其中 $e_i^m$ 表示物品 $i$ 在模态 $m$ 中的嵌入。

**覆盖策略（Overlay Strategy）**：这种方法为每种模态维护单独的相似性矩阵。对于每个观察到的用户-物品交互 $(u, i)$，框架在每种模态 $m$ 中识别与 $i$ 最相似的 Top-$k$ 个物品，形成模态特定的物品集 $I_{u,i}^m$。然后为每种模态构建虚拟交互矩阵 $R^m$，其中如果物品 $j$ 出现在用户 $u$ 的任何 $I_{u,i}^m$ 中，则 $R_{u,j}^m = 1$。

**协同策略（Synergistic Strategy）**：这种方法不是单独处理模态，而是结合所有模态的相似性：

$$
S_{i,j}^s = \sum_{m} S_{i,j}^m
$$

这创建了一个捕获跨模态互补性的单一整体相似性矩阵，然后使用相同的 Top-$k$ 选择过程从该矩阵生成虚拟交互。

### 统计学知情权重分配

VI-MMRec 的一个关键创新是其自适应加权机制，该机制确保了高质量的虚拟交互。该框架采用一种统计学基础的方法，而不是任意分配权重：

$$
w^m = \frac{O_{real}^m}{O_{avg}}
$$

其中 $O_{real}^m$ 表示针对模态 $m$ 生成的虚拟交互与实际用户交互之间的重叠率，而 $O_{avg}$ 是从随机生成的虚拟交互计算的基线。这个比率确保了更能预测实际用户偏好的模态获得更高的权重。

最终的增强交互矩阵构建如下：

$$
\bar{R} = \text{Confine}(R + \lambda \sum_m w^m R^m)
$$

对于覆盖策略，其中 $\text{Confine}()$ 函数确保交互权重保持在现实范围 [0,1] 内，而 $\lambda$ 控制虚拟交互的整体影响。

## 实验验证与结果

该框架在六个真实世界数据集（Baby、Sports、Clothing、Pet、Office、TikTok）和七个最先进的多模态推荐模型（MMGCN、DualGNN、SLMRec、FREEDOM、DRAGON、LGMRec、DiffMM）上进行了广泛评估。

### 性能改进

VI-MMRec 在所有测试组合中都表现出一致且显著的改进。叠加策略（VI-MMRec-O）通常优于协同策略（VI-MMRec-S），当应用于 MMGCN 时，Recall@10 的改进范围从 Clothing 数据集上的 8.26% 到 TikTok 数据集上的 22.25%。TikTok 数据集结合了音频模态以及视觉和文本特征，显示出最高的性能增益，这表明更丰富的多模态上下文能够实现更准确的虚拟交互推断。

![Ablation Study Results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-1.jpeg)

*图2：消融研究结果显示了细化（"w/o Refine"）和限制（"w/o Confine"）组件在所有数据集和模型中的重要性。*

### 数据稀疏性分析

该框架的有效性在稀疏数据场景中尤为突出。对不同用户交互次数分组（0-5、5-10、10-15、15-20、20-25次交互）的分析揭示了持续的改进，其中历史交互较少的用户获得了最显著的收益。

![Data Sparsity Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-2.jpeg)

*图3：对不同用户交互次数分组的性能分析，展示了 VI-MMRec 在各种稀疏场景中的有效性。*

### 超参数敏感性

该框架对超参数选择表现出合理的鲁棒性。对于大多数数据集，相似物品的最佳数量 ($k$) 通常为 10，尽管 TikTok 数据集从 $k=20$ 中受益，这表明更丰富的多模态信息可以有效地利用更广泛的相似物品。虚拟交互权重 ($\lambda$) 通常在 $1 \times 10^{-2}$ 时表现最佳，在不同数据集之间略有差异。

![Hyperparameter Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08702v1/img-3.jpeg)

*图4：关键超参数 $k$（相似物品数量）和 $\lambda$（虚拟交互权重）在不同数据集上的敏感性分析。*

## 技术优势和实际影响

VI-MMRec 的设计提供了几个关键优势，使其与现有方法区别开来：

**训练成本免费操作**：该框架作为预处理步骤运行，使用冻结的预训练编码器一次性构建虚拟交互。这确保了在下游推荐模型的训练阶段没有额外的计算开销。

**模型无关集成**：即插即用设计允许与任何现有的多模态推荐架构无缝集成，而无需修改基础模型结构或训练过程。

**对噪声的鲁棒性**：注入高斯噪声和信息错误的实验表明，VI-MMRec 即使在噪声条件下也能保持其性能优势，这归因于它使用相似性范围而不是严格的阈值。

**冷启动增强**：该框架在用户交互历史最少的冷启动场景中表现出特别的有效性。通过提供基于多模态相似性的额外信号，VI-MMRec 帮助模型更好地将多模态信息与用户行为模式对齐。

## 局限性和未来方向

尽管 VI-MMRec 表现出强大的经验性能，但有几个领域值得未来研究。该框架依赖于预训练的模态编码器，其质量直接影响虚拟交互质量。此外，当前方法侧重于基于相似性的增强，可能忽略了其他形式的潜在用户偏好。

未来的研究方向可以探索在训练期间适应的动态虚拟交互生成，研究超越余弦相似度的更复杂相似性度量，以及扩展到其他推荐场景，例如序列推荐或基于会话的推荐。

该框架在改进多样化多模态推荐系统方面的成功表明，其对存在数据稀疏性挑战的其他领域具有更广泛的适用性，并可能超越推荐系统，扩展到其他协作学习场景。

abstract: Although existing multimodal recommendation models have shown promising performance, their effectiveness continues to be limited by the pervasive data sparsity problem. This problem arises because users typically interact with only a small subset of available items, leading existing models to arbitrarily treat unobserved items as negative samples. To this end, we propose VI-MMRec, a model-agnostic and training cost-free framework that enriches sparse user-item interactions via similarity-aware virtual user-item interactions. These virtual interactions are constructed based on modality-specific feature similarities of user-interacted items. Specifically, VI-MMRec introduces two different strategies: (1) Overlay, which independently aggregates modality-specific similarities to preserve modality-specific user preferences, and (2) Synergistic, which holistically fuses cross-modal similarities to capture complementary user preferences. To ensure high-quality augmentation, we design a statistically informed weight allocation mechanism that adaptively assigns weights to virtual user-item interactions based on dataset-specific modality relevance. As a plug-and-play framework, VI-MMRec seamlessly integrates with existing models to enhance their performance without modifying their core architecture. Its flexibility allows it to be easily incorporated into various existing models, maximizing performance with minimal implementation effort. Moreover, VI-MMRec introduces no additional overhead during training, making it significantly advantageous for practical deployment. Comprehensive experiments conducted on six real-world datasets using seven state-of-the-art multimodal recommendation models validate the effectiveness of our VI-MMRec.
title: VI-MMRec: Similarity-Aware Training Cost-free Virtual User-Item Interactions for Multimodal Recommendation

abstract: Due to excessive memory overhead, most Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can only process videos of limited frames. In this paper, we propose an effective and efficient paradigm to remedy this shortcoming, termed One-shot video-Clip based Retrieval AuGmentation (OneClip-RAG). Compared with existing video RAG methods, OneClip-RAG makes full use of the merits of video clips for augmented video understanding in terms of both knowledge integrity and semantic coherence. Besides, it is also equipped with a novel query-guided video chunking algorithm that can unify clip chunking and cross-modal retrieval in one processing step, avoiding redundant computations. To improve instruction following, we further propose a new dataset called SynLongVideo and design a progressive training regime for OneClip-RAG. OneClip-RAG is plugged into five recent MLLMs and validated on a set of long-video benchmarks. Experimental results not only show the obvious performance gains by OneClip-RAG over MLLMs, e.g., boosting InternLV2 8B and Qwen2-VL 7B to the level of GPT-4o on MLVU, but also show its superior efficiency in handling long videos. e.g., enabling LLaVA-Video understand up to an hour of videos in less than 2.2 minutes on a single 4090 GPU.

score_detail.reasoning: 该论文提出了一种新颖的长视频理解方法OneClip-RAG，通过视频片段检索来增强多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的处理能力，创新性强（85）。方法上设计了query-guided视频分块算法，结合检索增强生成（RAG）技术，整体研究过程科学合理（80）。实验结果表明方法在多个长视频基准上显著提升了性能并提高了效率，结论与研究目标一致，结果具有说服力（88）。论文未提及任何伦理问题，引用和写作规范，符合学术伦理（95）。技术实现方面，作者提到模型被插入选定的MLLMs中并进行了实验验证，但未详细说明代码或算法的细节，因此技术质量较高但不够全面（82）。方法在提升模型处理长视频效率方面具有重要应用价值，对信息检索与多模态学习领域贡献明显，潜在社会影响较大（90）。总体来看，这是一篇具有较高质量的论文。

abstract: Ontology-based knowledge graph (KG) construction is a core technology that enables multidimensional understanding and advanced reasoning over domain knowledge. Industrial standards, in particular, contain extensive technical information and complex rules presented in highly structured formats that combine tables, scopes of application, constraints, exceptions, and numerical calculations, making KG construction especially challenging. In this study, we propose a method that organizes such documents into a hierarchical semantic structure, decomposes sentences and tables into atomic propositions derived from conditional and numerical rules, and integrates them into an ontology-knowledge graph through LLM-based triple extraction. Our approach captures both the hierarchical and logical structures of documents, effectively representing domain-specific semantics that conventional methods fail to reflect. To verify its effectiveness, we constructed rule, table, and multi-hop QA datasets, as well as a toxic clause detection dataset, from industrial standards, and implemented an ontology-aware KG-RAG framework for comparative evaluation. Experimental results show that our method achieves significant performance improvements across all QA types compared to existing KG-RAG approaches. This study demonstrates that reliable and scalable knowledge representation is feasible even for industrial documents with intertwined conditions, constraints, and scopes, contributing to future domain-specific RAG development and intelligent document management.
title: Ontology-Based Knowledge Graph Framework for Industrial Standard Documents via Hierarchical and Propositional Structuring

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance LLMs with external knowledge but introduce a critical attack surface: corpus poisoning. While recent studies have demonstrated the potential of such attacks, they typically rely on impractical assumptions, such as white-box access or known user queries, thereby underestimating the difficulty of real-world exploitation. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proposing MIRAGE, a novel multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed for strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. Operating on surrogate model feedback, MIRAGE functions as an automated optimization framework that integrates three key mechanisms: it utilizes persona-driven query synthesis to approximate latent user search distributions, employs semantic anchoring to imperceptibly embed these intents for high retrieval visibility, and leverages an adversarial variant of Test-Time Preference Optimization (TPO) to maximize persuasion. To rigorously evaluate this threat, we construct a new benchmark derived from three long-form, domain-specific datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.
title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks

en.title: ClinicalTrialsHub: Bridging Registries and Literature for Comprehensive Clinical Trial Access
en.abstract: We present ClinicalTrialsHub, an interactive search-focused platform that consolidates all data from this http URL and augments it by automatically extracting and structuring trial-relevant information from PubMed research articles. Our system effectively increases access to structured clinical trial data by 83.8% compared to relying on this http URL alone, with potential to make access easier for patients, clinicians, researchers, and policymakers, advancing evidence-based medicine. ClinicalTrialsHub uses large language models such as GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro to enhance accessibility. The platform automatically parses full-text research articles to extract structured trial information, translates user queries into structured database searches, and provides an attributed question-answering system that generates evidence-grounded answers linked to specific source sentences. We demonstrate its utility through a user study involving clinicians, clinical researchers, and PhD students of pharmaceutical sciences and nursing, and a systematic automatic evaluation of its information extraction and question answering capabilities.

summary.summary: CLINICALTRIALSHUB unifies clinical trial data from structured registries and unstructured scientific literature, expanding access to structured trial information by 83.8% and providing evidence-grounded, interactive question answering. This platform, developed at The Ohio State University, leverages advanced Large Language Models to streamline information discovery and synthesis for medical professionals and researchers.
originalProblem: Clinical trial data is fragmented across structured registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov) and unstructured scientific literature (e.g., PubMed), leading to incomplete and inconsistent information.
Extracting and systematically analyzing trial details from vast amounts of free-text articles is a time-consuming and challenging task for researchers.
The lack of a unified platform that seamlessly integrates and makes searchable data from both registries and published literature impedes evidence-based decision-making.
solution: CLINICALTRIALSHUB was developed as a user-centered platform to integrate and present clinical trial information from both ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed.
Large Language Models (LLMs) are used to translate natural language user queries into structured search parameters and to extract 211 distinct structured data fields from free-text PubMed articles.
An interactive LLM-powered chat interface provides evidence-grounded answers to specific questions about individual trials, with direct attribution to source sentences.
keyInsights: A substantial amount of clinical trial information exists solely in unstructured scientific literature, revealing a large untapped data source for systematic analysis.
Advanced Large Language Models can effectively bridge the gap between structured registry data and unstructured text by accurately extracting and structuring complex medical information.
Providing attributed, evidence-grounded responses from LLMs is critical for fostering trust and ensuring the practical utility of AI-powered tools in high-stakes clinical and research contexts.
results: The platform increased access to structured clinical trial data by 83.8%, incorporating 899,846 previously unregistered trials extracted from PubMed.
GPT-5.1 achieved strong performance in information extraction, with a Key-level F1 of 0.980 and Value-level F1 of 0.890 for structuring data from free-text articles.
Gemini-3-Pro demonstrated superior grounding scores (0.897) for interactive question answering, with medical professionals rating chatbot answer quality at 4.86/5.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Clinical trial information is fundamental to evidence-based medicine, yet accessing comprehensive trial data remains a significant challenge for patients, clinicians, and researchers. While ClinicalTrials.gov (CTG) provides structured registry data for many studies, it suffers from incomplete coverage, particularly for international trials and delayed result reporting. Conversely, PubMed contains a vast repository of published clinical trials in unstructured text format, making systematic search and analysis difficult. This fragmentation creates substantial barriers to efficient evidence synthesis and clinical decision-making.

![CLINICALTRIALSHUB Search Interface](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08193v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: The unified search interface of CLINICALTRIALSHUB, showing integrated results from both PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov with filtering capabilities and eligibility assessment features.*

CLINICALTRIALSHUB addresses this critical gap by creating the first unified platform that seamlessly integrates clinical trial data from both CTG registries and PubMed literature. The system leverages advanced Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically extract structured information from unstructured research articles and provides an interactive question-answering interface with evidence attribution. This approach represents a significant advancement in biomedical informatics, making previously inaccessible trial data readily discoverable and interpretable.

## System Architecture and Design

CLINICALTRIALSHUB employs a sophisticated three-component architecture designed to unify disparate clinical trial data sources. The platform features two primary user interfaces: a main search page supporting natural language queries and an individual trial detail page with comprehensive information display.

![System Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08193v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 2: The system architecture showing the integration of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov APIs through query generation, scoring, and normalization processes.*

The search functionality operates through a multi-stage pipeline. First, an LLM (GPT-5.1) translates natural language user queries into structured search parameters including condition, intervention, and keywords using specialized prompt templates. The system then executes queries asynchronously across both PubMed's E-utilities API and ClinicalTrials.gov's REST API. Search results undergo BM25 scoring, normalization, and intelligent merging through a bidirectional deduplication algorithm that identifies and combines related entries from both sources.

A key innovation lies in the information extraction component, which structures data from free-text PubMed articles. The system extracts 211 distinct fields across multiple modules covering protocol sections, results sections, and derived information. Each extraction maintains strict schema conformance through comprehensive validation pipelines that check structural integrity, data types, enumerated values, clinical terminology via NCBI MeSH API integration, and statistical consistency.

## Information Extraction Methodology

The information extraction system represents a significant technical achievement in automated clinical trial data structuring. Rather than attempting to extract all fields simultaneously, the system employs a modular approach that processes different sections in parallel while maintaining coherence across related fields.

The extraction process begins with GPT-5.1 analyzing full-text articles and extracting information according to predefined field definitions that mirror the CTG data schema. The system handles missing information deliberately by omission rather than placeholder generation, preserving data integrity. A sophisticated validation pipeline operates asynchronously during extraction, enforcing multiple layers of quality control:

$$
\text{Validation}(field) = \begin{cases}
\text{Schema}(field) \land \text{Enum}(field) \land \text{MeSH}(field) \land \text{Stats}(field) & \text{if extraction successful} \\
\emptyset & \text{if information unavailable}
\end{cases}
$$

Where Schema validates structural integrity, Enum ensures categorical field compliance, MeSH verifies medical terminology, and Stats checks quantitative consistency.

## Interactive Question Answering

The platform incorporates an evidence-grounded question-answering system powered by Gemini-3-Pro, selected for its superior grounding capabilities. This interactive feature allows users to ask specific questions about individual trials while ensuring all responses are factually supported by the provided context.

![Trial Detail Interface](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08193v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 3: The trial detail page showing structured information extraction results, interactive chatbot, and MeSH term glossary integration.*

The QA system operates on both structured CTG data and full-text PMC articles, providing clickable citations that automatically scroll and highlight supporting evidence in the source text. This evidence attribution mechanism ensures trustworthiness and enables verification, which is paramount in clinical contexts where accuracy directly impacts patient care decisions.

## Performance Evaluation and Results

The system underwent comprehensive evaluation across three dimensions: quantitative benchmarking for information extraction, grounded question-answering performance assessment, and qualitative user studies with medical professionals.

For information extraction, three frontier LLMs were evaluated on a curated dataset of 100 PMC-CTG trial pairs. GPT-5.1 achieved the highest performance with a key-level F1 score of 0.980 and value-level F1 score of 0.890, significantly outperforming alternatives. The evaluation revealed that apparent discrepancies often resulted from CTG's incompleteness rather than model hallucination, as evidenced by high "Extra-Valid" rates in descriptive fields.

The question-answering evaluation utilized 236 medical-domain samples from the FACTS Grounding benchmark. Gemini-3-Pro achieved a superior grounding score of 0.897, demonstrating its ability to generate factually supported responses while producing the most concise final answers (698 characters average).

A user study with seven medical professionals validated the system's practical utility. Participants rated search relevance highly, with 6 out of 7 finding 6 or more relevant studies using CLINICALTRIALSHUB compared to 5 out of 7 for PubMed alone. Information extraction accuracy received consistently high ratings across all categories, with Study Overview and Study Plan receiving perfect scores (5.0/5). The interactive chatbot functionality earned exceptional ratings for answer quality (4.86/5) and overall efficiency (4.86/5).

## Data Coverage and Impact

CLINICALTRIALSHUB significantly expands access to structured clinical trial data by bridging the gap between registry and literature sources. The system provides access to 899,846 previously unregistered clinical trials, representing an 83.8% increase in structured trial data availability compared to relying solely on ClinicalTrials.gov.

This expansion addresses a critical limitation in current clinical research infrastructure. Many trials, particularly those conducted outside the United States or published before mandatory registration requirements, exist only in published literature. By automatically structuring this information, CLINICALTRIALSHUB makes a vast repository of clinical evidence searchable and analyzable for the first time.

The unified search capability eliminates the need for researchers to manually navigate multiple platforms and reconcile overlapping information. The system's intelligent deduplication algorithm ensures that trials appearing in both CTG and PubMed are properly merged, providing comprehensive information while avoiding duplication bias in search results.

## Unique Contributions and Differentiators

CLINICALTRIALSHUB distinguishes itself from existing approaches through several key innovations. Unlike previous systems that focus on single data sources (LinkedCT for CTG, Trialstreamer for PubMed) or specific downstream tasks (RobotReviewer for systematic reviews), this platform creates a truly unified ecosystem that spans both structured registries and unstructured literature.

The system's LLM-powered information extraction represents a significant advancement over traditional natural language processing approaches. By leveraging frontier models like GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro, the platform achieves unprecedented accuracy in structuring complex clinical trial information while maintaining schema consistency and clinical terminology compliance.

The evidence-grounded question-answering feature sets a new standard for interactive clinical information systems. Unlike generic chatbots, this system ensures all responses are factually supported by source documents, providing direct citations and highlighting mechanisms that enable immediate verification.

## Future Implications and Applications

CLINICALTRIALSHUB represents a paradigm shift in how clinical trial information is accessed and utilized. For systematic reviewers, the platform can reduce the time required for literature screening from weeks to days by automatically structuring relevant information and enabling sophisticated filtering. Clinicians can quickly access comprehensive trial data to inform treatment decisions, while patients can better understand available treatments through more accessible trial information.

The platform's comprehensive data integration enables new research possibilities, including large-scale meta-analyses across previously fragmented data sources, identification of research gaps through automated trial landscape analysis, and development of AI-powered clinical decision support systems.

Future developments planned for the platform include domain-adapted LLM fine-tuning to further improve extraction accuracy, integration of patient-centric features for eligibility matching and personalized summaries, and expansion to include additional clinical research databases and international registries.

The successful demonstration of LLM capabilities in this high-stakes domain provides a template for similar applications across biomedical informatics, potentially revolutionizing how medical professionals access and synthesize complex scientific information. CLINICALTRIALSHUB stands as evidence of the transformative potential when cutting-edge AI technologies are thoughtfully applied to address real-world challenges in healthcare and medical research.

我们推出 ClinicalTrialsHub，这是一个以交互式搜索为中心的平台，它整合了来自 ClinicalTrials.gov 的所有数据，并通过自动从 PubMed 研究文章中提取和结构化与试验相关的信息来增强这些数据。与仅依赖 ClinicalTrials.gov 相比，我们的系统将结构化临床试验数据的获取量有效提高了 83.8%，这有可能使患者、临床医生、研究人员和政策制定者更容易获取数据，从而推动循证医学的发展。ClinicalTrialsHub 使用 GPT-5.1 和 Gemini-3-Pro 等大型语言模型来增强可访问性。该平台自动解析全文研究文章以提取结构化的试验信息，将用户查询转化为结构化的数据库搜索，并提供一个归因问答系统，该系统能够生成基于证据并链接到特定来源句子的答案。我们通过一项用户研究（涉及临床医生、临床研究人员以及药学和护理学的博士生）以及对其信息提取和问答能力进行的系统性自动化评估，证明了其实用性。

originalProblem: 临床试验数据分散在结构化注册表（例如 ClinicalTrials.gov）和非结构化科学文献（例如 PubMed）中，导致信息不完整和不一致。
从大量的自由文本文章中提取和系统分析试验细节对研究人员来说是一项耗时且具有挑战性的任务。
缺乏一个能够无缝整合并使注册表和已发表文献数据可搜索的统一平台，阻碍了循证决策。
solution: CLINICALTRIALSHUB 被开发为一个以用户为中心的平台，旨在整合并呈现来自 ClinicalTrials.gov 和 PubMed 的临床试验信息。
大型语言模型（LLM）用于将自然语言用户查询转换为结构化搜索参数，并从 PubMed 的自由文本文章中提取 211 个不同的结构化数据字段。
一个由 LLM 驱动的交互式聊天界面为关于特定试验的个性化问题提供基于证据的答案，并直接归因于原文句子。

先进的大型语言模型通过准确提取和结构化复杂的医学信息，可以有效地弥合结构化注册数据和非结构化文本之间的鸿沟。
提供由 LLM 生成的、带有归因且基于证据的回答，对于在高风险临床和研究环境中培养信任并确保人工智能工具的实用性至关重要。

GPT-5.1 在信息提取方面表现出色，从自由文本文章中结构化数据时，Key 级别 F1 值为 0.980，Value 级别 F1 值为 0.890。
Gemini-3-Pro 在交互式问答方面表现出卓越的依据分数（0.897），医学专业人士对聊天机器人答案质量的评分为 4.86/5。

## 引言

临床试验信息是循证医学的基础，然而，获取全面的试验数据对患者、临床医生和研究人员来说仍然是一个重大挑战。尽管ClinicalTrials.gov (CTG) 为许多研究提供了结构化的注册数据，但其覆盖范围不完整，特别是对于国际试验和延迟的结果报告。反之，PubMed 包含了大量的已发表临床试验，以非结构化文本格式呈现，这使得系统搜索和分析变得困难。这种碎片化为高效的证据综合和临床决策带来了实质性障碍。

![CLINICALTRIALSHUB 搜索界面](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08193v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：CLINICALTRIALSHUB 的统一搜索界面，显示了来自 PubMed 和 ClinicalTrials.gov 的整合结果，并具有筛选功能和资格评估功能。*

CLINICALTRIALSHUB 通过创建第一个统一平台来解决这一关键空白，该平台无缝整合了来自 CTG 注册库和 PubMed 文献的临床试验数据。该系统利用先进的大型语言模型（LLMs）自动从非结构化研究文章中提取结构化信息，并提供一个带有证据归属的交互式问答界面。这种方法代表了生物医学信息学领域的重大进步，使得以前难以获取的试验数据变得易于发现和解读。

## 系统架构与设计

CLINICALTRIALSHUB 采用复杂的三组件架构，旨在统一不同的临床试验数据源。该平台具有两个主要用户界面：支持自然语言查询的主搜索页面和显示全面信息的单个试验详情页面。

![系统架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08193v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图2：系统架构图，展示了通过查询生成、评分和标准化过程整合 PubMed 和 ClinicalTrials.gov API。*

搜索功能通过多阶段管道运行。首先，一个大型语言模型 (LLM) (GPT-5.1) 使用专门的提示模板将自然语言用户查询转换为结构化搜索参数，包括疾病、干预措施和关键词。然后，系统异步地在 PubMed 的 E-utilities API 和 ClinicalTrials.gov 的 REST API 上执行查询。搜索结果经过 BM25 评分、标准化，并通过双向去重算法进行智能合并，该算法识别并组合来自两个来源的相关条目。

一个关键创新在于信息提取组件，它从自由文本的 PubMed 文章中构建数据。系统从多个模块中提取211个不同的字段，涵盖方案部分、结果部分和派生信息。每次提取都通过全面的验证管道保持严格的模式一致性，这些管道检查结构完整性、数据类型、枚举值、通过 NCBI MeSH API 集成的临床术语以及统计一致性。

## 信息提取方法

信息提取系统是自动化临床试验数据结构化方面的一项重大技术成就。该系统并非试图同时提取所有字段，而是采用模块化方法，并行处理不同部分，同时保持相关字段之间的一致性。

提取过程始于 GPT-5.1 分析全文文章并根据预定义的字段定义提取信息，这些定义与 CTG 数据模式相符。系统通过省略而非生成占位符来刻意处理缺失信息，从而保持数据完整性。一个复杂的验证管道在提取过程中异步运行，执行多层质量控制：

$$
\text{Validation}(field) = \begin{cases}
\text{Schema}(field) \land \text{Enum}(field) \land \text{MeSH}(field) \land \text{Stats}(field) & \text{if extraction successful} \\
\emptyset & \text{if information unavailable}
\end{cases}
$$

其中 Schema 验证结构完整性，Enum 确保分类字段符合性，MeSH 验证医学术语，Stats 检查定量一致性。

## 交互式问答

该平台整合了一个由 Gemini-3-Pro 驱动的、以证据为基础的问答系统，选择 Gemini-3-Pro 是因为它卓越的依据能力。这一交互功能允许用户就个体试验提出具体问题，同时确保所有回答都由所提供的上下文事实支持。

![试验详情界面](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.08193v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图 3：试验详情页面，显示结构化信息提取结果、交互式聊天机器人和 MeSH 术语表集成。*

该问答系统同时作用于结构化的 CTG 数据和 PMC 全文文章，提供可点击的引文，这些引文会自动滚动并高亮显示源文本中的支持证据。这种证据归因机制确保了可信度并实现了验证，这在临床环境中至关重要，因为准确性直接影响患者护理决策。

## 性能评估与结果

该系统在三个维度上进行了全面评估：信息提取的定量基准测试、基于证据的问答性能评估，以及针对医学专业人员的定性用户研究。

在信息提取方面，我们对 100 对 PMC-CTG 试验的精选数据集上的三个前沿 LLM 进行了评估。GPT-5.1 取得了最高性能，其键级 F1 分数为 0.980，值级 F1 分数为 0.890，显著优于其他替代方案。评估显示，明显的差异通常是由于 CTG 的不完整性而非模型幻觉造成的，描述性字段中高“额外有效”率证实了这一点。

问答评估使用了 FACTS Grounding 基准测试中的 236 个医学领域样本。Gemini-3-Pro 取得了 0.897 的卓越依据分数，这表明它有能力生成事实支持的回答，同时生成最简洁的最终答案（平均 698 个字符）。

一项针对七名医学专业人员的用户研究验证了该系统的实用性。参与者对搜索相关性评价很高，与仅使用 PubMed 相比（7 人中有 5 人），使用 CLINICALTRIALSHUB 时，7 人中有 6 人找到了 6 个或更多相关研究。信息提取准确性在所有类别中均获得持续高评价，其中“研究概览”和“研究计划”获得满分（5.0/5）。交互式聊天机器人功能在答案质量（4.86/5）和整体效率（4.86/5）方面均获得了卓越的评价。

## 数据覆盖与影响

CLINICALTRIALSHUB 通过弥合注册表与文献来源之间的鸿沟，显著扩展了对结构化临床试验数据的访问。该系统提供了对 899,846 项此前未注册的临床试验的访问，与仅依赖 ClinicalTrials.gov 相比，结构化试验数据的可用性增加了 83.8%。

这一扩展解决了当前临床研究基础设施中的一个关键限制。许多试验，特别是那些在美国境外进行或在强制注册要求之前发表的试验，仅存在于已发表的文献中。通过自动构建这些信息，CLINICALTRIALSHUB 首次使庞大的临床证据库变得可搜索和可分析。

统一的搜索功能消除了研究人员手动浏览多个平台并协调重叠信息的需要。系统的智能去重算法确保了同时出现在CTG和PubMed中的试验得到正确合并，在提供全面信息的同时，避免了搜索结果中的重复偏差。

## 独特的贡献和差异化因素

CLINICALTRIALSHUB通过几项关键创新，使其有别于现有方法。与以往专注于单一数据源（CTG的LinkedCT，PubMed的Trialstreamer）或特定下游任务（系统综述的RobotReviewer）的系统不同，该平台创建了一个真正统一的生态系统，涵盖了结构化注册表和非结构化文献。

该系统基于大型语言模型（LLM）的信息提取，代表了对传统自然语言处理方法的重大进步。通过利用GPT-5.1和Gemini-3-Pro等前沿模型，该平台在构建复杂的临床试验信息方面实现了前所未有的准确性，同时保持了模式一致性和临床术语合规性。

证据支持的问答功能为交互式临床信息系统树立了新标准。与通用聊天机器人不同，该系统确保所有回复都有源文档的事实支持，提供直接引用并突出显示可立即验证的机制。

## 未来的影响和应用

CLINICALTRIALSHUB代表了临床试验信息获取和利用方式的范式转变。对于系统评价员，该平台可以通过自动构建相关信息并实现复杂的筛选，将文献筛选所需的时间从数周缩短至数天。临床医生可以快速访问全面的试验数据，为治疗决策提供信息，而患者则可以通过更易获取的试验信息更好地了解现有治疗方案。

该平台的综合数据整合开启了新的研究可能性，包括对以前分散的数据源进行大规模荟萃分析，通过自动化试验概况分析识别研究空白，以及开发人工智能驱动的临床决策支持系统。

平台未来计划的开发包括领域适应性LLM微调以进一步提高提取准确性，集成以患者为中心的功能以进行资格匹配和个性化摘要，以及扩展以包含更多的临床研究数据库和国际注册表。

在这个高风险领域成功展示LLM能力，为生物医学信息学领域的类似应用提供了模板，可能彻底改变医疗专业人员获取和综合复杂科学信息的方式。CLINICALTRIALSHUB证明了当尖端人工智能技术被深思熟虑地应用于解决医疗保健和医学研究中的现实挑战时所具有的变革潜力。

abstract: We present ClinicalTrialsHub, an interactive search-focused platform that consolidates all data from ClinicalTrials.gov and augments it by automatically extracting and structuring trial-relevant information from PubMed research articles. Our system effectively increases access to structured clinical trial data by 83.8% compared to relying on ClinicalTrials.gov alone, with potential to make access easier for patients, clinicians, researchers, and policymakers, advancing evidence-based medicine. ClinicalTrialsHub uses large language models such as GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro to enhance accessibility. The platform automatically parses full-text research articles to extract structured trial information, translates user queries into structured database searches, and provides an attributed question-answering system that generates evidence-grounded answers linked to specific source sentences. We demonstrate its utility through a user study involving clinicians, clinical researchers, and PhD students of pharmaceutical sciences and nursing, and a systematic automatic evaluation of its information extraction and question answering capabilities.

score_detail.reasoning: 论文提出了一个创新性的信息检索平台ClinicalTrialsHub，整合了ClinicalTrials.gov和PubMed的数据，并利用大语言模型（如GPT-5.1和Gemini-3-Pro）提升信息提取与查询能力，新颖性较强。研究方法包括信息提取、用户研究和自动评估，设计较为科学但未提供足够的细节评估其严谨性。结论合理，平台有效解决了临床试验信息获取的难题，且与目标一致。学术规范方面未提及具体问题，引用和伦理风险控制表现良好。技术实现方面虽有提及使用先进的模型，但未说明具体实现细节和代码的可复现性。应用价值显著，尤其在促进循证医学、改善患者和研究者信息获取方面具有广泛社会影响。

abstract: The purpose of this article is to address an open problem posed by Freeman-Oikhberg-Pineau-T.~(\textit{Math.~Ann.}~2024) regarding the existence of large subspaces of $C(K)$ that perform stable phase retrieval (SPR). We begin by proving that for both the real and complex fields, the space $C(K)$ admits an infinite-dimensional SPR subspace if and only if the second Cantor-Bendixson derivative $K{''}$ is nonempty. We then show how to construct ``large" SPR subspaces of $C(K)$, where the size of the subspace depends quantitatively on the number of non-trivial Cantor-Bendixson derivatives that the compact Hausdorff space $K$ possesses.
title: On the existence of large subspaces of $C(K)$ that perform stable phase retrieval

score_detail.reasoning: 论文标题和摘要表明其研究内容集中在信息检索相关的一个重要问题——稳定相位恢复(stable phase retrieval)，特别是在连续函数空间C(K)中构造大子空间以实现该目标。研究问题具有一定的新颖性，尤其是在结合Cantor-Bendixson导集这一拓扑结构来分析SPR子空间的存在性和大小方面。研究方法合理，构建子空间的思路清晰，且依赖于对K的非平凡导集的数量进行量化分析，显示出较强的数学严谨性。结论明确地解决了提出的问题，并与研究目标一致，具有说服力。学术伦理方面没有明显问题。技术质量较高，数学推导规范，但因未提及实验或代码，实验可重现性评分略低。影响力方面，虽然在理论上有重要贡献，但对实际应用的直接价值尚不明确。

category_detail.category_description: Core information retrieval algorithms, ranking models, query processing, and theoretical foundations
category_detail.reasoning: The paper discusses a theoretical problem in the context of stable phase retrieval, which is a foundational topic in signal processing and functional analysis. Although it is not directly about traditional IR tasks like document retrieval or ranking, it relates to the theoretical underpinnings of how signals can be reconstructed from their magnitude, a concept that has implications in retrieval models and information processing. Hence, it is most closely related to the 'Search & Ranking' category, particularly the subcategories 'IR Theory & Foundations' and 'Retrieval Models'.

abstract: Motivated by a question posed by Freeman, Oikhberg, Pineau and Taylor, we prove that if $K$ is a compact Hausdorff space with $K^{(α)}\neq\varnothing$, where $2<α<ω$, then $C[1,ω^α]$ isometrically embeds into $C(K)$ doing stable phase retrieval (SPR). We also show that the latter cannot be extended to the case $α=2$.
title: Isometric embeddings into $C(K)$-spaces doing stable phase retrieval

abstract: In legal matters, text classification models are most often used to filter through large datasets in search of documents that meet certain pre-selected criteria like relevance to a certain subject matter, such as legally privileged communications and attorney-directed documents. In this context, large language models have demonstrated strong performance. This paper presents an empirical study investigating the role of randomness in LLM-based classification for attorney-client privileged document detection, focusing on four key dimensions: (1) the effectiveness of LLMs in identifying legally privileged documents, (2) the influence of randomness control parameters on classification outputs, (3) their impact on overall classification performance, and (4) a methodology for leveraging randomness to enhance accuracy. Experimental results showed that LLMs can identify privileged documents effectively, randomness control parameters have minimal impact on classification performance, and importantly, our developed methodology for leveraging randomness can have a significant impact on improving accuracy. Notably, this methodology that leverages randomness could also enhance a corporation's confidence in an LLM's output when incorporated into its sanctions-compliance processes. As organizations increasingly rely on LLMs to augment compliance workflows, reducing output variability helps build internal and regulatory confidence in LLM-derived sanctions-screening decisions.
title: Exploiting the Randomness of Large Language Models (LLM) in Text Classification Tasks: Locating Privileged Documents in Legal Matters

abstract: The rapid increase in digital image creation and retention presents substantial challenges during legal discovery, digital archive, and content management. Corporations and legal teams must organize, analyze, and extract meaningful insights from large image collections under strict time pressures, making manual review impractical and costly. These demands have intensified interest in automated methods that can efficiently organize and describe large-scale image datasets. This paper presents a systematic investigation of automated cluster description generation through the integration of image clustering, image captioning, and large language models (LLMs). We apply K-means clustering to group images into 20 visually coherent clusters and generate base captions using the Azure AI Vision API. We then evaluate three critical dimensions of the cluster description process: (1) image sampling strategies, comparing random, centroid-based, stratified, hybrid, and density-based sampling against using all cluster images; (2) prompting techniques, contrasting standard prompting with chain-of-thought prompting; and (3) description generation methods, comparing LLM-based generation with traditional TF-IDF and template-based approaches. We assess description quality using semantic similarity and coverage metrics. Results show that strategic sampling with 20 images per cluster performs comparably to exhaustive inclusion while significantly reducing computational cost, with only stratified sampling showing modest degradation. LLM-based methods consistently outperform TF-IDF baselines, and standard prompts outperform chain-of-thought prompts for this task. These findings provide practical guidance for deploying scalable, accurate cluster description systems that support high-volume workflows in legal discovery and other domains requiring automated organization of large image collections.
title: Leveraging Machine Learning and Large Language Models for Automated Image Clustering and Description in Legal Discovery

en.title: A Comparative Study of Retrieval Methods in Azure AI Search
en.abstract: Increasingly, attorneys are interested in moving beyond keyword and semantic search to improve the efficiency of how they find key information during a document review task. Large language models (LLMs) are now seen as tools that attorneys can use to ask natural language questions of their data during document review to receive accurate and concise answers. This study evaluates retrieval strategies within Microsoft Azure's Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to identify effective approaches for Early Case Assessment (ECA) in eDiscovery. During ECA, legal teams analyze data at the outset of a matter to gain a general understanding of the data and attempt to determine key facts and risks before beginning full-scale review. In this paper, we compare the performance of Azure AI Search's keyword, semantic, vector, hybrid, and hybrid-semantic retrieval methods. We then present the accuracy, relevance, and consistency of each method's AI-generated responses. Legal practitioners can use the results of this study to enhance how they select RAG configurations in the future.

summary.summary: Researchers at Ankura Consulting Group's Legal Technology & Data Analytics team empirically compared five retrieval methods in Azure AI Search for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems used in legal eDiscovery, finding that retrieval quality significantly impacts LLM accuracy and that optimal performance depends on query type rather than a universally superior method. The study demonstrated method-specific strengths and weaknesses and the role of prompt engineering in mitigating attribution errors.
originalProblem: Attorneys seek to leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) for natural language queries on legal data, but the effectiveness of these RAG systems is highly dependent on the underlying retrieval mechanism.
There is a lack of empirical understanding regarding the real-world performance of modern retrieval methods (vector, semantic, hybrid, reranked) in eDiscovery-like conditions.
Failures in retrieving correct documents can lead to LLM-generated inaccuracies or 'hallucinations,' compromising the defensibility and reliability of crucial legal tasks.
solution: A comparative experimental approach was conducted using the public Jeb Bush email dataset (over 290,000 documents, chunked into 491,482 segments) to simulate eDiscovery conditions.

Five Azure AI Search retrieval methods (keyword, semantic, vector, hybrid, hybrid-semantic) were evaluated within an Azure RAG architecture, utilizing 'text-embedding-ada-002' for embeddings and 'gpt-4.1-mini' with temperature zero for deterministic LLM responses.

Nine distinct queries, designed to test various retrieval challenges and attribution, were manually assessed for relevance, factual accuracy, and consistency of both retrieved chunks and LLM-generated answers.
keyInsights: Many errors often attributed to 'LLM hallucination' are fundamentally rooted in deficiencies and misconfigurations of the underlying retrieval method, rather than solely the LLM itself.
No single retrieval method universally outperforms others; the optimal choice is contingent on the specific nature of the query and the distribution of information within the dataset.
Prompt engineering, especially incorporating explicit negative constraints, strongly impacts retrieval behavior and can effectively refine the LLM's output to mitigate misattribution errors.
results: Keyword retrieval excelled for structured, non-semantic data but lacked conceptual relevance, while vector retrieval captured semantic similarity effectively but struggled with domain-specific or infrequent keywords.

Semantic reranking (Keyword-Semantic and Hybrid-Semantic) often improved recall but could elevate misleading or tangential information, leading to misattributions from the LLM if initial relevant material was scarce.

Hybrid and Hybrid-Semantic retrieval generally provided the most consistently relevant results across a broader range of queries, with Hybrid-Semantic incurring the highest computational cost among the methods tested.

en.overview:
## Core Technology and Problem Statement

This research addresses a critical challenge in legal technology: how to effectively implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for legal document review. RAG systems combine information retrieval with large language models (LLMs) to provide accurate, contextually grounded responses to natural language queries. While LLMs can generate fluent text, they often "hallucinate" - producing plausible but factually incorrect information. RAG addresses this by first retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base, then using those documents as context for the LLM to generate responses.

The study focuses specifically on Microsoft Azure's RAG ecosystem, using Azure AI Search as the retrieval component and Azure OpenAI as the generation component. In legal contexts, particularly during Early Case Assessment (ECA) and eDiscovery processes, the stakes are exceptionally high. Attorneys need to identify privileged documents, analyze case issues, and conduct factual investigations where errors can have severe legal and financial consequences. The challenge lies in understanding which retrieval methods provide the most accurate and defensible results for different types of legal queries.

The authors, from Ankura Consulting Group's Legal Technology & Data Analytics division, bring practical industry experience to this evaluation. Their work addresses the growing demand from legal professionals to move beyond traditional keyword searches toward more sophisticated AI-powered document analysis capabilities.

## Methodology and Experimental Design

The researchers conducted a comprehensive comparative study using the Jeb Bush email dataset, which contains over 290,000 text documents comparable to modern eDiscovery collections. The dataset was preprocessed into chunks of 2,000 tokens with 500-token overlaps, resulting in 491,482 distinct chunks optimized for retrieval and LLM processing.

The experimental setup utilized OpenAI's 'text-embedding-ada-002' model for vector embeddings (1536 dimensions) and 'gpt-4.1-mini' as the language model with temperature set to zero for deterministic outputs. This configuration ensures that any variations in responses can be attributed solely to differences in retrieved content rather than stochastic LLM behavior.

Five distinct retrieval methods were evaluated:

1. **Keyword search**: Traditional lexical matching based on term frequency
2. **Keyword-Semantic search**: Keyword retrieval with semantic reranking
3. **Vector search**: Embedding-based similarity matching
4. **Hybrid search**: Combined keyword and vector approaches
5. **Hybrid-Semantic search**: Hybrid retrieval with semantic reranking

For each query, the system retrieved the top 50 relevant chunks, then selected the top 5 for LLM context. Nine carefully designed prompts (P1-P9) tested different retrieval scenarios, from specific alphanumeric strings to complex conceptual queries requiring nuanced understanding.

The evaluation employed qualitative manual review focusing on relevance, factual accuracy, and response diversity. While resource-intensive, this approach is appropriate for legal applications where subtle inaccuracies can have significant consequences.

## Key Findings and Performance Characteristics

The study revealed that no single retrieval method consistently outperformed others across all scenarios. Instead, optimal performance depended heavily on query characteristics and data distribution patterns.

**Keyword retrieval** proved essential for structured, non-semantic data such as case numbers and specific alphanumeric strings. It delivered fast results but missed semantically relevant material where exact term matches were absent. For example, when searching for specific case numbers (P1), keyword search was highly effective, but it failed to capture conceptually related documents.

**Vector retrieval** excelled at semantic similarity, successfully identifying conceptually related content like orange production forecasts (P2). However, it struggled with domain-specific keywords and infrequent terms, failing on queries requiring exact lexical matches.

**Semantic reranking** methods (Keyword-Semantic and Hybrid-Semantic) often improved recall and relevance by reordering initial results. These methods successfully uncovered connections like "South Florida" to "West Palm Beach" (P3) and identified nicknames like "T-Squared" (P4). However, a critical weakness emerged: semantic reranking could elevate misleading or tangential text when initial results lacked relevant material, leading to attribution errors where the LLM confidently presented incorrect information.

**Hybrid and Hybrid-Semantic retrieval** generally produced the most consistently relevant results across diverse query types. For instance, these methods effectively found nuanced differences between brothers' climate positions (P6). While Hybrid-Semantic offered high relevance, it incurred higher computational costs and remained susceptible to attribution errors if underlying retrieved chunks were problematic.

A crucial finding was that many errors attributed to "LLM hallucination" actually stemmed from retrieval method deficiencies. The quality of retrieved content proved to be the primary determinant of downstream model performance.

## Prompt Engineering and Attribution Challenges

The research demonstrated that prompt phrasing significantly impacts retrieval behavior and output quality. The evolution from prompt P7 to P9 illustrated this clearly:

- **P7**: "What are Jeb Bush's views on climate change?"
- **P9**: "What are Jeb Bush's views on climate change? Please focus specifically on his personal views, not those of other individuals or political figures, including President Bush."

The refined prompt (P9) with explicit negative constraints successfully prevented misattribution errors that occurred in P7, where President George Bush's views were mistakenly attributed to Jeb Bush due to problematic semantic reranking. This highlights the importance of precise user interaction in addition to system configuration.

The attribution challenge represents a significant concern for legal applications. When semantic reranking elevates chunks containing information about similar entities (e.g., family members with shared surnames), the LLM may confidently present information as belonging to the queried entity even when it doesn't. This type of error can be particularly problematic in legal contexts where accurate attribution is critical.

## Cost-Performance Trade-offs

The study explicitly addressed computational costs associated with different retrieval methods:

$$
\text{Cost Hierarchy: Keyword < Vector < Semantic < Hybrid < Hybrid-Semantic}
$$

Keyword and Vector searches represent relatively low-cost options, while Semantic and Hybrid methods incur medium costs, and Hybrid-Semantic is the most expensive. These cost considerations provide practical guidance for resource allocation in real-world deployments, especially important for large-scale eDiscovery projects where processing costs can be substantial.

The cost analysis reveals a classic trade-off between performance and resources. While Hybrid-Semantic methods often provided the most comprehensive and relevant results, organizations must weigh these benefits against increased computational expenses, particularly for high-volume document processing scenarios.

## Implications for Legal Technology

This research has significant implications for the legal technology landscape. The findings provide empirical guidance for selecting optimal RAG configurations within the Azure ecosystem for Early Case Assessment and broader eDiscovery tasks. Legal practitioners can now make informed decisions understanding the trade-offs between speed, accuracy, cost, and query-specific performance.

The study's emphasis on defensibility addresses a critical concern in legal applications. By demonstrating how retrieval errors can lead to confident but incorrect LLM responses, the research underscores the importance of transparency in RAG systems. Legal professionals need clear understanding of RAG method selection implications, visibility into retrieval scores, and access to source content used for generating responses.

The research also highlights the need for adaptive retrieval systems that can dynamically select appropriate strategies based on query characteristics. Future developments should focus on multi-method approaches that combine the strengths of different retrieval strategies while mitigating their individual weaknesses.

## Future Research Directions

The authors outline several important areas for future investigation. Visualizing retrieval behavior is crucial for building user trust and understanding, enabling users to comprehend why specific documents surfaced for their queries. Developing feedback loops and agentic systems could enable dynamic retrieval strategy selection, moving toward more intelligent and autonomous RAG implementations.

Benchmarking across diverse legal datasets will be essential for validating performance generalizability. Additionally, developing systems to verify LLM-generated results could add another layer of quality control, reducing reliance on manual verification processes.

The research represents a foundational empirical study bridging theoretical RAG advancements with practical legal requirements. It serves as a vital guide for ensuring that AI-powered legal document review achieves not just improved efficiency, but also the accuracy, relevance, and defensibility that legal matters demand. This work establishes a framework for evidence-based decision-making in legal technology adoption, moving beyond anecdotal observations to systematic empirical evaluation.

zh.title: Azure AI Search 中检索方法的比较研究
zh.abstract: 越来越多的律师希望超越关键词和语义搜索，以提高他们在文件审查任务中寻找关键信息的效率。大型语言模型（LLM）现已被视为律师在文件审查过程中，对其数据提出自然语言问题并获得准确、简洁答案的有效工具。本研究评估了微软Azure的检索增强生成（RAG）框架内的检索策略，旨在识别电子发现（eDiscovery）中早期案件评估（ECA）的有效方法。在早期案件评估阶段，法律团队会在案件初期分析数据，以全面了解数据并尝试在启动全面审查之前确定关键事实和潜在风险。在本文中，我们比较了Azure AI搜索的关键词、语义、向量、混合和混合语义检索方法的性能。随后，我们展示了每种方法AI生成响应的准确性、相关性和一致性。法律从业者可以利用本研究的结果，在未来改进他们选择RAG配置的方式。

summary.summary: Ankura Consulting Group 法务技术与数据分析团队的研究人员实证比较了 Azure AI Search 中用于法律电子取证中检索增强生成 (RAG) 系统的五种检索方法，发现检索质量显著影响大型语言模型 (LLM) 的准确性，并且最佳性能取决于查询类型而非存在普遍优越的方法。该研究展示了特定方法的优缺点以及提示工程在减少归因错误方面的作用。
originalProblem: 律师希望利用大型语言模型 (LLM) 对法律数据进行自然语言查询，但这些 RAG 系统的有效性高度依赖于底层的检索机制。
对于电子取证类似条件下现代检索方法（向量、语义、混合、重排）的实际性能缺乏实证理解。
检索到错误文档可能导致大型语言模型生成不准确信息或“幻觉”，从而损害关键法律任务的可辩护性和可靠性。
solution: 采用比较实验方法，利用公开的 Jeb Bush 电子邮件数据集（超过 290,000 份文档，被分块为 491,482 个片段）来模拟电子取证条件。
在 Azure RAG 架构中评估了五种 Azure AI Search 检索方法（关键词、语义、向量、混合、混合-语义），使用“text-embedding-ada-002”进行嵌入，并使用温度为零的“gpt-4.1-mini”来获得确定性的大型语言模型响应。
人工评估了九个旨在测试各种检索挑战和归因的独特查询，以判断检索到的块和大型语言模型生成答案的相关性、事实准确性和一致性。
keyInsights: 许多通常归因于“大型语言模型幻觉”的错误，其根本原因在于底层检索方法的缺陷和错误配置，而非仅仅是大型语言模型本身的问题。
没有一种检索方法能够普遍优于其他方法；最佳选择取决于查询的具体性质和数据集中信息的分布。
提示工程，特别是纳入明确的负面约束，强烈影响检索行为，并能有效地优化大型语言模型输出以减轻归因错误。
results: 关键词检索在结构化、非语义数据方面表现出色，但缺乏概念相关性；而向量检索能有效捕捉语义相似性，但对领域特定或不常见的关键词表现不佳。
语义重排（关键词-语义和混合-语义）通常能提高召回率，但可能会提升误导性或边缘信息，如果初始相关材料稀缺，这可能导致大型语言模型出现归因错误。
混合检索和混合-语义检索通常在更广泛的查询范围内提供最一致的相关结果，其中混合-语义在测试方法中计算成本最高。
