en.title: Spatial Retrieval Augmented Autonomous Driving
en.abstract:
Existing autonomous driving systems rely on onboard sensors (cameras, LiDAR, IMU, etc) for environmental perception. However, this paradigm is limited by the drive-time perception horizon and often fails under limited view scope, occlusion or extreme conditions such as darkness and rain. In contrast, human drivers are able to recall road structure even under poor visibility. To endow models with this ``recall" ability, we propose the spatial retrieval paradigm, introducing offline retrieved geographic images as an additional input. These images are easy to obtain from offline caches (e.g, Google Maps or stored autonomous driving datasets) without requiring additional sensors, making it a plug-and-play extension for existing AD tasks.
For experiments, we first extend the nuScenes dataset with geographic images retrieved via Google Maps APIs and align the new data with ego-vehicle trajectories. We establish baselines across five core autonomous driving tasks: object detection, online mapping, occupancy prediction, end-to-end planning, and generative world modeling. Extensive experiments show that the extended modality could enhance the performance of certain tasks. We will open-source dataset curation code, data, and benchmarks for further study of this new autonomous driving paradigm.

summary.summary: Researchers from Fudan University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University established a spatial retrieval augmented autonomous driving paradigm, integrating offline geographic images to enhance autonomous vehicle robustness. This approach boosted online mapping performance by up to 11.9% mAP and reduced collision rates in planning, particularly under challenging conditions.
originalProblem: Autonomous driving systems heavily rely on onboard sensors, which suffer from limited view scope and performance degradation under challenging conditions like occlusion, poor lighting, or adverse weather.
Current AD systems lack the spatial memory and prior knowledge that human drivers use to navigate confidently even when real-time visibility is compromised.
Vulnerabilities in sensor perception lead to compromised safety and reliability in downstream AD tasks such as online mapping, occupancy prediction, and planning.
solution: A "spatial retrieval paradigm" was developed, augmenting traditional AD data streams with stable, globally accessible offline geographic images (e.g., street view, satellite maps) as a consistent background prior.
The `nuScenes-Geography` dataset was curated, extending nuScenes with location-aligned equirectangular panoramic geographic images from Google Maps APIs and providing retrieval APIs.

A plug-and-play "Spatial Retrieval Adapter" was designed for seamless integration into existing BEV-based AD architectures, using geo-cross-attention and 3D positional encoding, along with a "Reliability Estimation Gate" for adaptive fusion of geographic features.
keyInsights: Offline geographic data acts as a robust "city memory," effectively complementing real-time onboard sensors by providing stable contextual understanding unaffected by environmental disturbances.

Integrating geographic priors substantially improves perception tasks focused on static environmental elements like road structures and occupancy, and enhances planning safety by providing consistent layout information.
Geographic priors provide a crucial structural scaffold for generative world models, significantly reducing scene drift and hallucination during long-horizon video generation.
An adaptive fusion mechanism is essential for practical deployment, ensuring robustness against real-world imperfections in retrieved geographic data such as misalignment or outdatedness.
results: Online mapping performance saw substantial mAP increases for MapTR (+10.9%) and MapTRv2 (+11.9%), demonstrating improved reconstruction of occluded road structures, especially under low exposure or bad weather.
End-to-end planning with the VAD model showed comparable trajectory accuracy but a significant reduction in collision rates (e.g., from 0.55% to 0.48% in challenging nighttime scenarios).

Generative world models (UniMLVG, MagicDriveDit) conditioned on geographic images achieved lower FVD and FID scores (e.g., UVG+Geo showed FVD -6.04, FID -0.22), indicating improved geometric and temporal consistency.

The Reliability Estimation Gate (REG) maintained robust performance, showing graceful degradation even with 50% inaccurate priors and confirming its crucial role in handling real-world data imperfections.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Autonomous driving systems traditionally rely on onboard sensors like cameras and LiDAR for real-time perception and navigation. While these technologies have advanced significantly, they face critical limitations in challenging conditions such as poor lighting, adverse weather, occlusion, and limited view scope. This paper introduces "Spatial Retrieval Augmented Autonomous Driving," a paradigm that addresses these vulnerabilities by incorporating offline geographic information as a complementary input modality, similar to how human drivers leverage spatial memory and prior knowledge of road structures.

![Spatial Retrieval Paradigm Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06865v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: Overview of the spatial retrieval paradigm showing how geographic priors help autonomous driving systems overcome sensor limitations across various tasks including online mapping, occupancy prediction, planning, detection, and generative world modeling.*

## Core Methodology

The spatial retrieval paradigm augments traditional autonomous driving data streams by retrieving relevant geographic information from offline databases. The core approach involves extending the standard AD input `{S_t, P_t}` (onboard sensors and ego-vehicle pose) with retrieved geographic data `R(I_t, I_geo, P_t, P_geo)` from an offline geographic database.

The methodology centers around three key components:

**Spatial Retrieval Adapter**: A plug-and-play module that integrates retrieved geographic images into existing Bird's Eye View (BEV) architectures through cross-attention mechanisms:

$$
F'_{BEV} = F_{BEV} + w \cdot \text{CrossAttn}(F_{BEV}, F_{geo} + F_{pos\_geo}, F_{geo})
$$

where `F_BEV` serves as the query, and `F_geo + F_pos_geo` provides spatially-encoded geographic features as keys and values. The reliability weight `w` is determined by the adaptive fusion mechanism.

**Reliability Estimation Gate (REG)**: An adaptive fusion component that dynamically weights geographic contributions based on data quality:

$$
w = \sigma(\text{MLP}([\text{ZNCC}(F_{onboard}, F_{geo}), d_{GPS}]))
$$

The gate uses Zero-Normalized Cross-Correlation (ZNCC) to measure appearance similarity between onboard and geographic features, and GPS distance `d_GPS` to assess spatial relevance.

![Architecture Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06865v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: System architecture showing integration of geographic images into both on-vehicle tasks (detection, mapping, occupancy, planning) and offline generative world models through cross-attention mechanisms.*

## Dataset Construction and Geographic Data Integration

The researchers created **nuScenes-Geography**, an extended version of the nuScenes dataset incorporating geographic information from Google Maps APIs. The dataset construction process addresses several practical challenges:

**Efficient Storage Strategy**: Geographic images are stored as equirectangular panoramas, reducing storage requirements by over 70% since multiple nuScenes frames often correspond to the same Street View location.

**Virtual Camera Alignment**: For each nuScenes frame, a virtual camera is instantiated at the matched Street View location with identical intrinsic parameters, enabling geometric alignment through reprojection from the equirectangular panorama.

![Data Construction Pipeline](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06865v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: nuScenes-Geography construction pipeline showing how GPS coordinates are used to retrieve Street View panoramas, which are then reprojected to create camera-aligned geographic images.*

The resulting dataset demonstrates high coverage, with approximately 92-94% of frames having reliable geographic data, while ~6-7% are classified as misaligned due to temporal changes, GPS errors, or vertical misalignment issues.

## Experimental Results Across Core Tasks

The evaluation demonstrates consistent improvements across five fundamental autonomous driving tasks:

**Online Mapping**: Geographic priors significantly enhanced road structure prediction, with MapTR showing +10.9% mAP improvement (50.3 → 61.2) and MapTRv2 achieving +11.9% mAP gain (61.5 → 73.4). These improvements are particularly pronounced in scenarios with occlusion or poor lighting conditions.

**Occupancy Prediction**: Models like FB-OCC and FlashOCC showed consistent mIoU gains, especially for static categories. FBOcc+Geo achieved +0.63% overall mIoU increase with notable +2.57% improvement for terrain categories, demonstrating the value of stable geographic anchors for background geometry.

**End-to-End Planning**: While maintaining comparable trajectory accuracy, VAD+Geo significantly reduced collision rates from 0.55% to 0.48% in nighttime scenarios, indicating improved safety through better environmental understanding.

**3D Object Detection**: The impact on dynamic object detection was marginal, which is expected since geographic images primarily provide static background information rather than information about moving vehicles or pedestrians.

**Generative World Models**: Geographic conditioning led to improved consistency metrics, with UniMLVG+Geo showing FVD reduction of -6.04 and FID improvement of -0.22, indicating reduced hallucination and better temporal consistency.

![Qualitative Results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06865v1/img-8.jpeg)
*Figure 4: Qualitative improvements showing how geographic priors help recover missing road elements in challenging conditions like low exposure, bad weather, and occlusion.*

## Robustness and Adaptive Fusion

The Reliability Estimation Gate proves crucial for real-world deployment. Experiments with deliberately corrupted geographic data show that the system degrades gracefully, maintaining significant performance gains even with 50% inaccurate priors. The REG effectively identifies and down-weights unreliable geographic information based on appearance similarity and spatial distance metrics.

![Robustness Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06865v1/img-9.jpeg)
*Figure 5: Robustness analysis showing performance degradation with increasing percentages of incorrect geographic priors, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Reliability Estimation Gate (REG).*

## Technical Contributions and Innovations

This work makes several key technical contributions:

**Paradigm Introduction**: Establishes spatial retrieval as a new complementary modality for autonomous driving, moving beyond purely reactive sensing toward systems with persistent spatial memory.

**Practical Integration Framework**: Develops a general, plug-and-play architecture that can be integrated into existing BEV-based models without extensive modification.

**Adaptive Fusion Mechanism**: Introduces the REG to handle real-world data imperfections, making the system robust to missing or misaligned geographic information.

**Comprehensive Evaluation**: Provides systematic evaluation across multiple core AD tasks, establishing baselines and demonstrating consistent benefits.

**Open Science Contribution**: Creates and releases nuScenes-Geography dataset with associated tools and benchmarks to enable further research.

## Significance and Impact

The spatial retrieval paradigm addresses fundamental limitations of current autonomous driving systems by providing a stable, comprehensive spatial context that complements real-time sensing. This approach offers several significant advantages:

**Enhanced Safety**: The system maintains better situational awareness in challenging conditions, as evidenced by reduced collision rates in nighttime scenarios.

**Cost-Effective Enhancement**: Leverages readily available geographic data without requiring additional expensive onboard sensors, making it a practical upgrade path for existing systems.

**Improved Simulation and Development**: The enhanced consistency of generative world models contributes to better simulation environments for AD development and testing.

**Research Direction**: Establishes a new research paradigm that bridges the gap between reactive sensing and cognitive spatial understanding in autonomous systems.

The work demonstrates that integrating "city memory" into autonomous vehicles can significantly improve their robustness and reliability, particularly in scenarios where traditional sensors struggle. This represents an important step toward more human-like spatial reasoning in autonomous driving systems.

abstract:
Existing autonomous driving systems rely on onboard sensors (cameras, LiDAR, IMU, etc) for environmental perception. However, this paradigm is limited by the drive-time perception horizon and often fails under limited view scope, occlusion or extreme conditions such as darkness and rain. In contrast, human drivers are able to recall road structure even under poor visibility. To endow models with this ``recall" ability, we propose the spatial retrieval paradigm, introducing offline retrieved geographic images as an additional input. These images are easy to obtain from offline caches (e.g, Google Maps or stored autonomous driving datasets) without requiring additional sensors, making it a plug-and-play extension for existing AD tasks.
  For experiments, we first extend the nuScenes dataset with geographic images retrieved via Google Maps APIs and align the new data with ego-vehicle trajectories. We establish baselines across five core autonomous driving tasks: object detection, online mapping, occupancy prediction, end-to-end planning, and generative world modeling. Extensive experiments show that the extended modality could enhance the performance of certain tasks. We will open-source dataset curation code, data, and benchmarks for further study of this new autonomous driving paradigm.

en.title: Foresight Prediction Enhanced Live-Streaming Recommendation
en.abstract: Live-streaming, as an emerging media enabling real-time interaction between authors and users, has attracted significant attention. Unlike the stable playback time of traditional TV live or the fixed content of short video, live-streaming, due to the dynamics of content and time, poses higher requirements for the recommendation algorithm of the platform - understanding the ever-changing content in real time and push it to users at the appropriate moment. Through analysis, we find that users have a better experience and express more positive behaviors during highlight moments of the live-streaming. Furthermore, since the model lacks access to future content during recommendation, yet user engagement depends on how well subsequent content aligns with their interests, an intuitive solution is to predict future live-streaming content. Therefore, we perform semantic quantization on live-streaming segments to obtain Semantic ids (Sid), encode the historical Sid sequence to capture the author's characteristics, and model Sid evolution trend to enable foresight prediction of future content. This foresight enhances the ranking model through refined features. Extensive offline and online experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

summary.summary: Researchers at Kuaishou Technology developed a system that predicts future live-streaming content segments using multi-modal semantic understanding and a Transformer-based model to enhance recommendations. This approach improved core platform metrics in A/B tests, including a +0.457% increase in Exposure and a +2.480% increase in Gift Count.
originalProblem: Live-streaming content is highly dynamic and temporally unstable, posing challenges for real-time recommendation algorithms.
Existing recommendation models lack foresight into future live-stream content, often missing crucial "highlight moments" that drive user engagement.
User experience and positive behaviors, such as retention and gifting, are strongly linked to these dynamic highlight moments within a live-stream.
solution: Implemented Semantic Quantization by fine-tuning a Large Language Model (LLM) to process multi-modal live-stream segments into high-dimensional embeddings, then quantizing them into discrete "Semantic IDs" (Sids) via K-Means clustering.
Developed a Transformer-based Semantic Prediction model to predict future Sids based on historical compressed Sid sequences, enabling foresight into upcoming live-stream content.

Integrated these historical context (encoder output) and foresight prediction (decoder output) features into a multi-task ranking model for enhanced live-streaming recommendation, trained and deployed within a streaming architecture.
keyInsights: Explicitly predicting future live-streaming content segments (foresight) significantly enhances recommendation performance compared to relying solely on historical or current content understanding.
Discretizing complex multi-modal live-stream content into "Semantic IDs" (Sids) effectively captures fine-grained semantic meaning and facilitates sequential modeling for content prediction.
Highlight moments within a live-stream, accurately represented by specific Sids, are strongly correlated with increased user interaction, watch time, and monetization behaviors like gift-sending.
results: Offline evaluations showed foresight prediction (decoder output) yielded significant AUC/GAUC improvements across CTR (+0.05%/+0.24%), WTR (+0.06%/+0.65%), LVTR (+0.03%/+0.32%), and GTR (+0.03%/+0.36%).
Online A/B tests demonstrated substantial business impact on the Kuaishou platform, with overall Exposure increasing by +0.457%, Watch Time by +0.370%, and Gift Count by +2.480%.

The model's Sid prediction achieved an accuracy of 21.35%, significantly outperforming rule-based baselines like "Last Sid" (8.32%), confirming the predictive power of the Transformer-based component.

en.overview:
## Overview

Live-streaming platforms have fundamentally changed how users consume dynamic content, but recommending live-streams presents unique challenges compared to traditional static media. Unlike videos or images with fixed attributes, live-streams evolve continuously in real-time, making it difficult for recommendation systems to capture their essence and predict user engagement effectively. Researchers at Kuaishou Technology have developed a system that addresses this challenge by introducing explicit foresight prediction into live-streaming recommendations, moving beyond reactive content understanding to anticipate future highlight moments.

![Figure 1: Case of highlight moment indication across different live-streaming categories](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-0.jpeg)

*Figure 1: Examples of highlight moments in different live-streaming categories. The audience number charts show clear spikes during engaging content like performances in talent shows (a), gameplay moments (b), and product showcases (c).*

## Problem Statement and Motivation

Traditional recommendation systems excel with static content where features remain constant over time. However, live-streaming presents a fundamentally different paradigm where content quality and user appeal fluctuate moment by moment. The authors identify several critical limitations in current approaches:

**Dynamic Content Challenge**: Live-streams exhibit temporal instability with constantly changing content and interactive quality. Current models struggle to understand this "ever-changing content in real time" and determine the optimal moment to recommend streams to users.

**Highlight Moment Dependency**: Through empirical analysis, the researchers observed that user engagement is significantly higher during specific "highlight moments" - performances in talent shows, key gameplay sequences, or product launches in shopping streams. These moments correspond to dramatic increases in audience size, gifts, and comments.

**Future Content Blindness**: Existing recommendation models make decisions based solely on historical and current content, yet user retention depends heavily on upcoming content quality. This creates a fundamental mismatch between recommendation timing and content value.

The core insight driving this research is that effective live-streaming recommendation requires predicting future content evolution to recommend streams when they are most likely to engage users, rather than reacting to content after it has already occurred.

## Methodology

The proposed "Foresight Prediction Enhanced Live-Streaming Recommendation" system consists of three integrated components that work together within a streaming training framework.

![Figure 2: System architecture showing the integration of semantic understanding and foresight prediction](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-1.jpeg)

*Figure 2: Overall architecture of the proposed system, showing how multi-modal live-stream content is processed through semantic quantization, prediction, and feature refinement components.*

### Semantic Quantization

The first component transforms continuous, high-dimensional multi-modal content into structured discrete representations:

**Multi-modal Understanding**: A fine-tuned Large Language Model processes 30-second live-stream segments, incorporating multiple modalities including author information, video frames, speech transcripts, and user comments. This generates rich semantic embeddings that capture the comprehensive context of each segment.

**Vector Quantization**: The high-dimensional LLM embeddings are quantized using K-Means clustering into discrete "Semantic IDs" (Sids). With N=20,000 clusters, each segment embedding is mapped to its nearest centroid in the codebook C, creating an intuitive categorical representation that reduces storage costs and facilitates downstream processing.

**Sequence Compression**: To handle redundancy where identical Sids may persist across multiple segments, the system compresses the Sid sequence into two parallel streams: a distinct sequence containing only unique Sids in chronological order, and a frequency sequence recording consecutive occurrences of each Sid.

### Semantic Prediction

The core innovation lies in predicting future content using a Transformer-based architecture:

**Encoder Architecture**: The encoder processes the last l=100 segments of compressed Sid sequences and their frequencies as historical context. After mapping Sids to embeddings via lookup tables, multiple self-attention and feed-forward layers capture long-term content patterns and author characteristics, producing an encoded representation Î.

**Decoder for Prediction**: The decoder utilizes cross-attention mechanisms across multiple layers to predict the next segment's Sid. A learnable beginning-of-sequence token serves as the initial query, while the encoder output provides keys and values for attention computation.

**Prediction Optimization**: The decoder output D̂ calculates similarity with the codebook via dot product, followed by softmax to generate probability distributions over all possible Sids. The model optimizes using cross-entropy loss:

$$
L_{pred} = -\sum_{i} y_i \log(p_i)
$$

where $y_i$ represents the true next Sid and $p_i$ the predicted probability.

### Feature Refinement and Integration

The insights from content understanding and prediction are integrated into the recommendation ranking model:

**Enhanced Features**: Both the semantic encoder output Î (representing historical content fusion) and decoder output D̂ (representing future content prediction) serve as refined features alongside traditional user and author features.

**Multi-task Ranking**: These enhanced features feed into a multi-gate mixture-of-experts model that predicts various user interaction probabilities including Click-Through Rate (CTR), Watch-Through Rate (WTR), Long View Through Rate (LVTR), and Gift-Sending Rate (GTR).

**Gradient Isolation**: A stop-gradient operation ensures that while the ranking model leverages prediction features, it doesn't interfere with prediction model training, maintaining clear separation between components.

## Experimental Results

The researchers conducted comprehensive evaluations using both offline metrics and online A/B testing on Kuaishou's live-streaming platform, serving hundreds of millions of users daily.

### Offline Performance

The offline evaluation measured standard recommendation metrics across multiple prediction tasks:

**Historical Content Impact**: Adding encoded historical content (Î) showed modest improvements, with WTR GAUC increasing by +0.48%. This suggests that while valuable, some historical understanding may already be captured by existing model features.

**Foresight Prediction Impact**: The introduction of future content prediction (D̂) yielded substantial improvements across all metrics:
- CTR: +0.05% AUC, +0.24% GAUC
- WTR: +0.06% AUC, +0.65% GAUC  
- LVTR: +0.03% AUC, +0.32% GAUC
- GTR: +0.03% AUC, +0.36% GAUC

The consistently higher GAUC improvements compared to AUC gains indicate enhanced personalization capabilities, as GAUC measures average performance across individual users rather than the overall population.

### Online A/B Testing

Real-world deployment demonstrated significant business impact:

**Core Engagement Metrics**: The system achieved meaningful improvements in fundamental platform metrics including +0.457% overall exposure, +0.243% watch count, and +0.370% watch time. These gains directly translate to increased user engagement and platform retention.

**Interaction and Monetization**: User interaction metrics showed even stronger improvements, with like count increasing by +1.754%, follow count by +0.922%, gift count by +2.480%, and gift users by +1.011%. The substantial gift-related improvements highlight the system's ability to identify revenue-generating highlight moments.

### Sid Analysis and Validation

![Figure 3: Analysis of Semantic ID changes and their correlation with user behavior](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-2.jpeg)

*Figure 3: Living Sid changes during a live-streaming session, showing how different content types (dancing, singing, interaction) correspond to distinct Sids and correlate with user engagement patterns in gifts, comments, and follows.*

**Prediction Accuracy**: The model-based Sid prediction achieved 21.35% accuracy, significantly outperforming rule-based baselines including "Last Sid" (8.32%), "Max Frequency" (8.94%), and "Max Weight" (9.03%).

**Content-Behavior Correlation**: Case study analysis revealed strong correlations between specific Sids and user behaviors. For example, gift-sending predominantly occurred during dancing and singing segments, while comments and follows were more common during interaction segments.

**Semantic Quality**: Author-to-author retrieval experiments demonstrated that the multi-modal Sid representation captures fine-grained semantic relationships, retrieving more precisely related authors compared to basic visual similarity models.

![Figure 4: Author-to-author retrieval comparison showing improved semantic understanding](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-3.jpeg)

*Figure 4: Comparison of author retrieval results between a basic two-tower model (top row) and the proposed Sid-enhanced model (bottom row), demonstrating improved fine-grained semantic understanding.*

## Significance and Impact

This research represents a significant advancement in dynamic content recommendation with implications spanning both academic research and industrial application.

**Academic Contributions**: The work introduces explicit foresight prediction as a new paradigm for dynamic recommendation systems, moving beyond reactive approaches to proactive content understanding. The novel application of semantic quantization using multi-modal LLM embeddings provides a practical framework for representing complex, temporal content in structured formats suitable for machine learning.

**Industrial Impact**: For large-scale platforms, the ability to predict and recommend content during optimal moments significantly enhances user experience and retention. The substantial improvements in monetization metrics, particularly gift-related behaviors, demonstrate direct commercial value through better identification of revenue-generating highlight moments.

**Scalability and Deployment**: The methodology addresses real-world constraints through its streaming architecture design, demonstrating that advanced AI techniques can be effectively deployed in high-throughput, real-time environments. The stop-gradient mechanism ensures stable training across multiple model components, crucial for production deployment.

**Broader Applications**: While demonstrated in live-streaming, the core concept of foresight prediction could extend to other dynamic content domains including real-time gaming, live events, and interactive media, opening new research directions in temporal recommendation systems.

The research successfully bridges the gap between advanced AI capabilities and practical industrial needs, providing a scalable solution that delivers measurable improvements in user engagement and commercial outcomes for large-scale live-streaming platforms.

zh.title: 前瞻性预测增强的直播推荐
zh.abstract: 直播作为一种新兴媒体，实现了主播与用户之间的实时互动，因此受到了广泛关注。与传统电视直播稳定的播放时长或短视频固定的内容不同，直播由于其内容和时间的动态性，对平台推荐算法提出了更高的要求——即实时理解不断变化的内容，并在恰当的时机将其推送给用户。通过分析，我们发现用户在直播的精彩瞬间体验更佳，并表现出更积极的行为。此外，由于模型在推荐时无法获取未来的内容，而用户参与度又取决于后续内容与他们兴趣的契合程度，因此一个直观的解决方案是预测未来的直播内容。为此，我们对直播片段进行语义量化以获得语义ID（Sid），编码历史Sid序列以捕捉主播特征，并建模Sid演变趋势以实现对未来内容的前瞻性预测。这种前瞻性通过精炼的特征增强了排序模型。大量的离线和在线实验证明了我们方法的有效性。

summary.summary: 快手科技的研究人员开发了一个系统，该系统利用多模态语义理解和基于Transformer的模型来预测未来的直播内容片段，以增强推荐。这种方法在A/B测试中改进了核心平台指标，包括曝光量增加0.457%，礼物数增加2.480%。
originalProblem: 直播内容具有高度动态性和时间上的不稳定性，对实时推荐算法构成了挑战。
现有推荐模型缺乏对未来直播内容的预见性，常常错过驱动用户参与的关键“精彩瞬间”。
用户体验和积极行为，例如留存和送礼，与直播中这些动态的精彩瞬间密切相关。
solution: 通过微调大型语言模型（LLM）实现语义量化，将多模态直播片段处理成高维嵌入，然后通过K-Means聚类将其量化为离散的“语义ID”（Sids）。
开发了一个基于Transformer的语义预测模型，根据历史压缩的Sid序列预测未来的Sids，从而实现对即将到来的直播内容的预见。
将这些历史上下文（编码器输出）和预见性预测（解码器输出）特征集成到多任务排序模型中，以增强直播推荐，并在流式架构中进行训练和部署。
keyInsights: 与仅依赖历史或当前内容理解相比，明确预测未来的直播内容片段（预见性）显著提高了推荐性能。
将复杂的多模态直播内容离散化为“语义ID”（Sids），有效捕获了细粒度的语义含义，并促进了内容预测的序列建模。
直播中的精彩瞬间（由特定的Sids准确表示）与用户互动、观看时长以及送礼等变现行为的增加密切相关。
results: 离线评估显示，预见性预测（解码器输出）在CTR（+0.05%/+0.24%）、WTR（+0.06%/+0.65%）、LVTR（+0.03%/+0.32%）和GTR（+0.03%/+0.36%）方面都带来了显著的AUC/GAUC提升。
在线A/B测试表明对快手平台产生了巨大的业务影响，整体曝光量增加了+0.457%，观看时长增加了+0.370%，礼物数增加了+2.480%。
模型的Sid预测准确率达到21.35%，显著优于“Last Sid”（8.32%）等基于规则的基线，证实了基于Transformer组件的预测能力。

zh.overview:
## 概述

直播平台从根本上改变了用户消费动态内容的方式，但与传统的静态媒体相比，推荐直播流面临独特的挑战。与具有固定属性的视频或图像不同，直播流实时持续演变，这使得推荐系统难以捕捉其精髓并有效预测用户参与度。快手科技的研究人员开发了一个系统来解决这一挑战，该系统通过在直播推荐中引入明确的预见性预测，超越了被动的内容理解，以预测未来的高光时刻。

![Figure 1: Case of highlight moment indication across different live-streaming categories](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-0.jpeg)

*图1：不同直播类别中高光时刻的示例。观众人数图表显示，在才艺表演（a）、游戏玩法（b）和产品展示（c）等引人入胜的内容期间，观众人数有明显飙升。*

## 问题陈述与动机

传统的推荐系统擅长处理特征随时间保持不变的静态内容。然而，直播呈现了一种根本不同的范式，内容质量和用户吸引力每时每刻都在波动。作者指出了当前方法中的几个关键局限性：

**动态内容挑战**：直播流表现出时间上的不稳定性，内容和互动质量不断变化。当前模型难以理解这种“实时不断变化的内容”，并确定向用户推荐直播流的最佳时机。

**高光时刻依赖性**：通过实证分析，研究人员观察到，在特定的“高光时刻”——才艺表演中的表演、关键的游戏序列或购物直播中的产品发布——用户参与度显著更高。这些时刻对应着观众人数、礼物和评论的急剧增加。

**未来内容盲点**：现有推荐模型仅基于历史和当前内容做出决策，但用户留存严重依赖于即将到来的内容质量。这在推荐时机和内容价值之间造成了根本性的不匹配。

这项研究的核心见解是，有效的直播推荐需要预测未来的内容演变，以便在直播流最有可能吸引用户时进行推荐，而不是在内容已经发生之后才做出反应。

## 方法论

所提出的“预见性预测增强型直播推荐”系统由三个集成组件组成，这些组件在流式训练框架内协同工作。

![Figure 2: System architecture showing the integration of semantic understanding and foresight prediction](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-1.jpeg)

*图2：所提出系统的整体架构，展示了多模态直播内容如何通过语义量化、预测和特征提炼组件进行处理。*

### 语义量化

第一个组件将连续的、高维度的多模态内容转换为结构化的离散表示：

**多模态理解**：一个经过微调的大型语言模型处理30秒的直播片段，结合了作者信息、视频帧、语音转录和用户评论等多种模态。这生成了丰富的语义嵌入，捕捉了每个片段的全面上下文。

**向量量化**：高维LLM嵌入使用K-Means聚类量化为离散的“语义ID”（Sids）。通过N=20,000个簇，每个片段嵌入被映射到其在码本C中最接近的质心，从而创建了直观的分类表示，降低了存储成本并促进了下游处理。

**序列压缩**：为了处理冗余，即相同的 Sid 可能会在多个片段中持续存在的情况，系统将 Sid 序列压缩成两个并行的流：一个按时间顺序只包含唯一 Sid 的去重序列，以及一个记录每个 Sid 连续出现次数的频率序列。

### 语义预测

核心创新在于使用基于 Transformer 的架构来预测未来的内容：

**编码器架构**：编码器将最后 l=100 个压缩 Sid 序列及其频率作为历史上下文进行处理。通过查表将 Sid 映射到嵌入后，多个自注意力层和前馈层捕获长期的内容模式和作者特征，生成编码表示 Î。

**解码器用于预测**：解码器在多个层中利用交叉注意力机制来预测下一个片段的 Sid。一个可学习的序列起始 token 作为初始查询，而编码器输出提供用于注意力计算的键和值。

**预测优化**：解码器输出 D̂ 通过点积计算与码本的相似性，然后进行 softmax 以生成所有可能 Sid 的概率分布。模型使用交叉熵损失进行优化：

$$
L_{pred} = -\sum_{i} y_i \log(p_i)
$$

其中 $y_i$ 代表真实的下一个 Sid，$p_i$ 代表预测的概率。

### 特征精炼与整合

内容理解和预测的洞察被整合到推荐排名模型中：

**增强特征**：语义编码器输出 Î（代表历史内容融合）和解码器输出 D̂（代表未来内容预测）都作为精炼特征，与传统用户和作者特征一同使用。

**多任务排名**：这些增强特征输入到一个多门控专家混合模型中，该模型预测各种用户交互概率，包括点击率 (CTR)、完播率 (WTR)、长视频观看完成率 (LVTR) 和送礼率 (GTR)。

**梯度隔离**：梯度停止操作确保排名模型在利用预测特征的同时，不会干扰预测模型的训练，从而保持组件之间的清晰分离。

## 实验结果

研究人员在快手直播平台（每日服务数亿用户）上，通过离线指标和在线 A/B 测试进行了全面的评估。

### 离线表现

离线评估衡量了多个预测任务的标准推荐指标：

**历史内容影响**：添加编码后的历史内容 (Î) 显示出适度改进，WTR GAUC 增加了 +0.48%。这表明尽管有价值，但某些历史理解可能已经被现有模型特征捕获。

**前瞻预测影响**：引入未来内容预测 (D̂) 在所有指标上都带来了显著改进：
- CTR：+0.05% AUC，+0.24% GAUC
- WTR：+0.06% AUC，+0.65% GAUC
- LVTR：+0.03% AUC，+0.32% GAUC
- GTR：+0.03% AUC，+0.36% GAUC

与 AUC 增益相比，GAUC 持续更高的改进表明增强的个性化能力，因为 GAUC 衡量的是个体用户的平均表现，而非整体人群。

### 在线 A/B 测试

实际部署显示了显著的业务影响：

**核心参与度指标**：系统在平台核心指标上实现了有意义的改进，包括整体曝光量 +0.457%、观看次数 +0.243% 和观看时长 +0.370%。这些增长直接转化为用户参与度和平台留存率的提高。

**互动与变现**：用户互动指标显示出更强的改善，点赞数增加+1.754%，关注数增加+0.922%，礼物数增加+2.480%，送礼用户数增加+1.011%。大幅提升的礼物相关指标凸显了系统识别创收高光时刻的能力。

### Sid分析与验证

![图3：语义ID变化及其与用户行为的相关性分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-2.jpeg)

*图3：直播会话期间Living Sid的变化，展示了不同内容类型（舞蹈、唱歌、互动）如何对应不同的Sid，并与礼物、评论和关注中的用户参与模式相关联。*

**预测准确性**：基于模型的Sid预测准确率达到21.35%，显著优于基于规则的基线，包括“上一个Sid”（8.32%）、“最大频率”（8.94%）和“最大权重”（9.03%）。

**内容-行为关联**：案例研究分析揭示了特定Sid与用户行为之间存在强烈的关联。例如，送礼行为主要发生在舞蹈和唱歌环节，而评论和关注在互动环节更为常见。

**语义质量**：作者对作者检索实验表明，多模态Sid表示捕获了细粒度的语义关系，与基本视觉相似性模型相比，检索到了更精确相关的作者。

![图4：作者对作者检索比较显示语义理解的提升](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06700v1/img-3.jpeg)

*图4：基本双塔模型（顶行）与提出的Sid增强模型（底行）的作者检索结果比较，展示了细粒度语义理解的提升。*

## 意义与影响

这项研究代表了动态内容推荐领域的重大进展，对学术研究和工业应用都具有重要意义。

**学术贡献**：该工作引入了显式预见预测作为动态推荐系统的新范式，超越了反应式方法，实现了主动式内容理解。多模态LLM嵌入语义量化的新颖应用为以结构化格式表示复杂时间内容提供了实用的框架，适用于机器学习。

**工业影响**：对于大型平台而言，在最佳时刻预测和推荐内容显著提升了用户体验和留存率。变现指标（特别是礼物相关行为）的大幅改善，通过更好地识别创收高光时刻，证明了直接的商业价值。

**可扩展性与部署**：该方法通过其流式架构设计解决了现实世界的限制，表明先进的AI技术可以有效地部署在高吞吐量、实时环境中。停止梯度机制确保了多个模型组件之间的稳定训练，这对于生产部署至关重要。

**更广泛的应用**：虽然在直播中得到了验证，但预见预测的核心概念可以扩展到其他动态内容领域，包括实时游戏、直播活动和交互式媒体，为时间推荐系统开辟了新的研究方向。

这项研究成功地弥合了先进人工智能能力与实际工业需求之间的鸿沟，提供了一个可扩展的解决方案，为大型直播平台带来了用户参与度和商业成果方面的显著提升。

abstract: Live-streaming, as an emerging media enabling real-time interaction between authors and users, has attracted significant attention. Unlike the stable playback time of traditional TV live or the fixed content of short video, live-streaming, due to the dynamics of content and time, poses higher requirements for the recommendation algorithm of the platform - understanding the ever-changing content in real time and push it to users at the appropriate moment. Through analysis, we find that users have a better experience and express more positive behaviors during highlight moments of the live-streaming. Furthermore, since the model lacks access to future content during recommendation, yet user engagement depends on how well subsequent content aligns with their interests, an intuitive solution is to predict future live-streaming content. Therefore, we perform semantic quantization on live-streaming segments to obtain Semantic ids (Sid), encode the historical Sid sequence to capture the author's characteristics, and model Sid evolution trend to enable foresight prediction of future content. This foresight enhances the ranking model through refined features. Extensive offline and online experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.
title: Foresight Prediction Enhanced Live-Streaming Recommendation

full_text: Foresight Prediction Enhanced Live-Streaming Recommendation Live-streaming, as an emerging media enabling real-time interaction between authors and users, has attracted significant attention. Unlike the stable playback time of traditional TV live or the fixed content of short video, live-streaming, due to the dynamics of content and time, poses higher requirements for the recommendation algorithm of the platform - understanding the ever-changing content in real time and push it to users at the appropriate moment. Through analysis, we find that users have a better experience and express more positive behaviors during highlight moments of the live-streaming. Furthermore, since the model lacks access to future content during recommendation, yet user engagement depends on how well subsequent content aligns with their interests, an intuitive solution is to predict future live-streaming content. Therefore, we perform semantic quantization on live-streaming segments to obtain Semantic ids (Sid), encode the historical Sid sequence to capture the author's characteristics, and model Sid evolution trend to enable foresight prediction of future content. This foresight enhances the ranking model through refined features. Extensive offline and online experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

en.title: An Index-based Approach for Efficient and Effective Web Content Extraction
en.abstract: As web agents (e.g., Deep Research) routinely consume massive volumes of web pages to gather and analyze information, LLM context management -- under large token budgets and low signal density -- emerges as a foundational, high-importance, and technically challenging problem for agentic and RAG pipelines. Existing solutions for extracting relevant content are inadequate: generative extraction models suffer from high latency, rule-based heuristics lack adaptability, and chunk-and-rerank methods are blind to webpage structure. To overcome these issues, we introduce Index-based Web Content Extraction to reframe the extraction process from slow, token-by-token generation into a highly efficient, discriminative task of index prediction, achieving both effectiveness and efficiency. We partition HTML into structure-aware, addressable segments, and extract only the positional indices of content relevant to a given query. This method decouples extraction latency from content length, enabling rapid, query-relevant extraction. We first evaluate our method as a post-retrieval processing component within an RAG QA system and find that it improves QA accuracy. Then we directly measure its match rate with the target content in two scenarios: main content extraction (ME) and query-relevant extraction (QE). Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing works in both accuracy and speed, effectively bridging the gap between LLMs and the vast webpages.

summary.summary: Researchers from the University of Science and Technology of China and Metastone Technology introduced an index-based localization paradigm, reframing web content extraction as an index prediction task for Large Language Models. This approach achieved an average F1 score of 55.41 in RAG QA systems and extracted content up to 10 times faster than generative methods, drastically improving efficiency and accuracy in web content processing.
originalProblem: Large Language Models (LLMs) face severe context window limitations when processing extensive, noisy web pages, often leading to "lost in the middle" issues.

Existing web content extraction methods are either too slow (generative token-by-token models) or ineffective (rule-based lack adaptability, chunk-and-rerank ignores webpage structure and query relevance).
There is a need for precise, structure-aware, and query-relevant content extraction that can efficiently provide clean input to LLMs for tasks like deep research and RAG.
solution: A novel "Index-based Localization" paradigm was developed, which transforms raw HTML into a sequence of numerically indexed content blocks via cleaning and structured segmentation.
An IndexLM model (fine-tuned Qwen3) performs discriminative index prediction, identifying start and end indices of relevant content intervals from the indexed blocks, webpage title, and user query.
A post-processing stage reassembles split blocks, restores structural elements, and converts the final extracted content into Markdown for optimal LLM consumption.
keyInsights: Reframing web content extraction from slow, token-by-token generation to a discriminative index prediction task drastically improves both processing efficiency and extraction effectiveness.
Structured, indexed content blocks coupled with a specialized prediction model allow for high precision in isolating main content and query-relevant information from noisy web pages.

Joint training on both main content extraction and query-relevant extraction tasks is crucial for a single model to achieve versatile and robust performance across different web content processing needs.
results: The IndexLM series achieved the best average F1 scores in RAG QA systems (55.41 with Qwen3-4B as answer model) across five datasets, using significantly fewer tokens (~1900-2000) than baselines.

IndexLM demonstrated exceptional speed, with the 0.6B model performing main content extraction in 0.35 seconds and query-relevant extraction in 1.39 seconds, up to 10 times faster than generative models.
It achieved high accuracy for main content extraction (87.40 F1, 92.46 Recall) and competitive performance for query-relevant extraction (31.69 F1), outperforming existing specialized methods.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Web content extraction has become a critical bottleneck in the deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) for autonomous web agents and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Modern web pages frequently exceed typical LLM context windows, with median HTML sources containing approximately 223K tokens that must be reduced to manageable sizes while preserving relevant information. Current approaches suffer from fundamental trade-offs: generative models provide high-quality extraction but with latency that scales linearly with output length, while rule-based methods offer speed but lack adaptability to diverse web structures.

![Efficiency vs. Effectiveness Trade-off](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Performance comparison showing IndexLM models achieving superior efficiency-effectiveness balance compared to existing approaches*

This paper introduces a paradigm shift from generative token-by-token extraction to discriminative index prediction, addressing both efficiency and effectiveness challenges simultaneously. The proposed Index-based Web Content Extraction method reframes the extraction task as predicting relevant content intervals within structured, indexed webpage blocks rather than generating extracted text directly.

## The Index-based Extraction Framework

The core innovation lies in transforming web content extraction from a generation problem into a discrimination problem through three distinct stages: Index Construction, Indices Extraction, and Post-processing.

![Method Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Complete pipeline of the Index-based Web Content Extraction framework*

### Index Construction

The framework begins by parsing raw HTML using BeautifulSoup, removing non-content elements like CSS and JavaScript while preserving potentially useful textual information embedded within scripts. The cleaned HTML undergoes systematic segmentation through Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal of the DOM tree.

Block-level elements form the primary segmentation units, with inline elements processed according to specific rules: images are preserved only with captions and reformatted as standardized strings, formatting tags are retained, hyperlink tags are stripped while preserving anchor text, and other inline tags are removed. To handle content length constraints, blocks exceeding a maximum threshold ($L_{max,block}$) are recursively split by sentences, then words, maintaining text structure integrity.

Each processed segment receives a unique sequential index, creating an indexed sequence $B = \{b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n\}$ formatted as `[i] <tag>contents</tag>`. This transformation converts unstructured web content into an addressable, structured format suitable for discriminative processing.

### IndexLM: The Discriminative Extraction Model

The IndexLM model represents the core discriminative component, learning a mapping function $f(B, Q)$ that outputs index intervals $I^* \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ representing relevant content segments. Unlike generative approaches that produce text token-by-token, IndexLM predicts start and end indices of relevant content intervals (e.g., `[[1,2], [3,5]]`).

The model architecture builds upon Qwen3 models (0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B parameters), chosen for their balance of capability and efficiency. Training involves supervised fine-tuning using datasets combining query-relevant samples from HotpotQA, Natural Questions, and MultiHopRAG, alongside main content extraction data from Common Crawl.

For pages exceeding context windows, the framework partitions indexed blocks into manageable chunks, processes each separately, and merges resulting index intervals. This approach maintains computational efficiency while handling arbitrarily large web pages.

The training objective follows standard supervised fine-tuning:

$$
L_{SFT}(\theta) = -E_{(P,I) \sim D} [\log E_{\theta}(I | P)]
$$

where $P$ represents the input prompt containing URL, title, and indexed blocks, and $I$ represents the target index intervals formatted as Python lists.

### Post-processing and Reconstruction

The final stage reconstructs extracted content from predicted indices. Split blocks are reassembled using their metadata attributes, and HTML structure is restored through heuristic methods that recover common parent-child relationships disrupted during segmentation. The reconstructed content forms a new HTML document combined with the original webpage title, then converts to Markdown format for simplified LLM consumption.

![Method Example](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-3.jpeg)
*Detailed example showing the complete extraction process from raw HTML to final Markdown output*

## Experimental Results and Performance Analysis

The evaluation encompasses both downstream RAG QA performance and direct extraction quality metrics across multiple datasets and baselines.

### RAG QA System Performance

When integrated into RAG systems, IndexLM consistently achieved superior question-answering performance across five datasets. With Qwen3-4B as the answer model, IndexLM-4B achieved an average F1 score of 55.41, outperforming Firecrawl Extract (52.72) and significantly surpassing traditional Chunk-Rerank methods (49.44). Similar performance advantages were observed with Gemma3-27B-it as the answer model (F1: 57.94).

![Context Length Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-4.jpeg)
*Performance across different context token limits showing IndexLM's consistent superiority*

Notably, IndexLM achieved these results while using significantly fewer tokens (approximately 1900-2000) compared to methods utilizing full context limits, demonstrating effective information distillation without sacrificing relevance.

![Extended Context Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-5.jpeg)
*Extended analysis up to 30K tokens showing IndexLM's robustness across context lengths*

### Direct Extraction Performance

For main content extraction, IndexLM-4B achieved an F1 score of 87.40 with 92.46 recall, substantially outperforming specialized models like ReaderLM-v2 (F1: 68.89) and HtmlRAG (F1: 48.65). In query-relevant extraction, IndexLM-4B scored 31.69 F1, surpassing most baselines including generative approaches.

The efficiency gains proved remarkable: IndexLM-0.6B demonstrated 0.35-second average latency for main content extraction, while IndexLM-4B (0.81 seconds) remained approximately 49× faster than Qwen3-4B with prompting (17.35 seconds) and 33× faster than ReaderLM-v2 (11.76 seconds).

![Query Example](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-6.jpeg)
*Example demonstrating query-relevant extraction capability with sports-related content*

### Ablation Studies

Joint training on both query-relevant and main content data proved essential for model versatility. Training exclusively on query-relevant data maintained QE performance but degraded ME capability, while main-content-only training nearly failed on QE tasks. Additionally, the framework's inherent effectiveness was demonstrated by reasonable performance even when replacing trained IndexLM with untrained Qwen3-4B models.

## Significance and Implications

This research addresses a fundamental bottleneck in LLM-powered web applications by decoupling extraction latency from content length while maintaining high accuracy. The discriminative approach enables processing of vast web corpora at unprecedented speeds, crucial for real-time web agents and large-scale RAG deployments.

![Token Distribution](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-7.jpeg)
*Token distribution comparison showing the scale of web content processing challenges*

The paradigm shift from generation to discrimination offers broader implications beyond web extraction, potentially applicable to document processing, database querying, and structured information retrieval tasks. The demonstrated effectiveness of smaller models (0.6B-4B parameters) makes the approach accessible for resource-constrained deployments while maintaining competitive performance.

## Technical Contributions and Future Directions

The paper's primary contributions include: (1) reframing web extraction as index prediction rather than text generation, (2) developing a comprehensive framework for HTML structure preservation during segmentation and reconstruction, (3) demonstrating significant efficiency gains without sacrificing extraction quality, and (4) providing extensive empirical validation across multiple tasks and datasets.

The framework's modular design and the authors' discussion of extending beyond web content suggest promising research directions in structured information extraction across diverse domains. The combination of speed, accuracy, and structural awareness positions this approach as a foundational technology for next-generation LLM applications requiring efficient web-scale information processing.

zh.title: 基于索引的高效有效网页内容提取方法
zh.abstract:
当网络智能体（例如Deep Research）例行性地处理海量网页以收集和分析信息时，LLM上下文管理——在庞大的token预算和低信息密度下——成为智能体和RAG（检索增强生成）管道中一个基础性、高重要性且具有技术挑战性的问题。现有提取相关内容的解决方案均不尽人意：生成式提取模型存在高延迟问题，基于规则的启发式方法缺乏适应性，而分块-重排方法则无法感知网页结构。

为了克服这些问题，我们引入了**基于索引的网页内容抽取（Index-based Web Content Extraction）**方法，将抽取过程从缓慢的逐token生成重构为高效的判别式索引预测任务，从而同时实现了有效性和效率。我们将HTML划分为感知结构的可寻址片段，并仅抽取与给定查询相关内容的**位置索引**。这种方法将抽取延迟与内容长度解耦，实现了快速、与查询相关的抽取。

我们首先在一个RAG问答系统中将其作为检索后处理组件进行评估，发现它能提高问答准确性。然后，我们在两种场景下直接衡量了它与目标内容的匹配率：主内容抽取（ME）和查询相关抽取（QE）。实验结果表明，我们的方法在准确性和速度上均优于现有工作，有效弥合了LLMs与海量网页之间的鸿沟。

summary.summary: 中国科学技术大学和Metastone Technology的研究人员引入了一种基于索引的定位范式，将网络内容提取重新定义为大型语言模型的索引预测任务。该方法在RAG问答系统中取得了55.41的平均F1分数，并且内容提取速度比生成式方法快10倍，极大地提高了网络内容处理的效率和准确性。
originalProblem: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在处理大量嘈杂的网页时面临严重的上下文窗口限制，经常导致“中间迷失”问题。
现有的网络内容提取方法要么太慢（逐词生成的模型），要么效果不佳（基于规则的方法缺乏适应性，分块重排忽略了网页结构和查询相关性）。
需要一种精确、结构感知且与查询相关的内容提取方法，能够高效地为LLMs提供干净的输入，用于深度研究和RAG等任务。
solution: 开发了一种新颖的“基于索引的定位”范式，通过清理和结构化分段将原始HTML转换为一系列数字索引的内容块。
IndexLM模型（微调后的Qwen3）执行判别性索引预测，从索引块、网页标题和用户查询中识别相关内容区间的起始和结束索引。
后处理阶段重新组合已分割的块，恢复结构元素，并将最终提取的内容转换为Markdown格式，以便LLMs的最佳使用。
keyInsights: 将网络内容提取从缓慢的逐词生成重新定义为判别性索引预测任务，极大地提高了处理效率和提取效果。
结构化、索引化的内容块与专门的预测模型相结合，能够高精度地从嘈杂的网页中分离出主要内容和与查询相关的信息。
对主要内容提取和查询相关提取任务进行联合训练，对于单个模型在不同的网络内容处理需求中实现多功能和鲁棒性能至关重要。
results: IndexLM系列在五个数据集的RAG问答系统中取得了最佳平均F1分数（使用Qwen3-4B作为答案模型时为55.41），并且使用的tokens数量（约1900-2000）显著少于基线。
IndexLM展示了卓越的速度，其中0.6B模型在0.35秒内完成主要内容提取，在1.39秒内完成查询相关提取，比生成式模型快达10倍。
它在主要内容提取方面取得了高准确性（87.40 F1，92.46 Recall），并在查询相关提取方面表现出竞争力（31.69 F1），优于现有专门方法。

zh.overview:
## 引言

网页内容提取已成为部署大型语言模型（LLMs）用于自主网络代理和检索增强生成（RAG）系统的关键瓶颈。现代网页经常超出LLM典型的上下文窗口，其中HTML源文件的中位数包含约223K个tokens，必须将其缩减到可管理的大小，同时保留相关信息。当前方法面临根本性的权衡：生成模型提供高质量的提取，但其延迟与输出长度线性相关；而基于规则的方法速度快，但缺乏对多样化网页结构的适应性。

![效率与效果的权衡](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-0.jpeg)
*性能比较显示，与现有方法相比，IndexLM模型在效率-效果平衡方面表现更优*

本文提出了一种从生成式逐令牌提取到判别式索引预测的范式转变，同时解决了效率和效果的挑战。所提出的基于索引的网页内容提取方法将提取任务重新定义为预测结构化、索引化的网页块中的相关内容区间，而不是直接生成提取文本。

## 基于索引的提取框架

核心创新在于通过三个不同的阶段将网页内容提取从生成问题转换为判别问题：索引构建、索引提取和后处理。

![方法概述](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-2.jpeg)
*基于索引的网页内容提取框架的完整流程*

### 索引构建

该框架首先使用BeautifulSoup解析原始HTML，删除CSS和JavaScript等非内容元素，同时保留脚本中可能包含的有用文本信息。清理后的HTML通过DOM树的深度优先搜索（DFS）遍历进行系统分段。

块级元素构成主要的分段单元，而内联元素则根据特定规则进行处理：图像仅在有标题时保留并格式化为标准化字符串；格式标签被保留；超链接标签被剥离，同时保留锚文本；其他内联标签被移除。为了处理内容长度限制，超出最大阈值（$L_{max,block}$）的块会递归地按句子、然后按单词进行分割，以保持文本结构的完整性。

每个处理后的段落都会获得一个唯一的顺序索引，创建一个索引序列 $B = \{b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n\}$，格式为 `[i] <tag>contents</tag>`。这种转换将非结构化的网页内容转换为可寻址的、结构化的格式，适用于判别式处理。

### IndexLM：判别式提取模型

IndexLM模型代表了核心判别组件，它学习一个映射函数 $f(B, Q)$，该函数输出代表相关内容段落的索引区间 $I^* \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$。与逐令牌生成文本的生成方法不同，IndexLM预测相关内容区间的起始和结束索引（例如，`[[1,2], [3,5]]`）。

该模型架构基于Qwen3模型（0.6B、1.7B和4B参数），这些模型因其能力和效率的平衡而被选中。训练涉及使用结合HotpotQA、Natural Questions和MultiHopRAG中的查询相关样本以及Common Crawl中的主要内容提取数据的监督微调。

对于超出上下文窗口的页面，该框架将索引块分成可管理的块，分别处理每个块，并合并生成的索引区间。这种方法在处理任意大小的网页时保持了计算效率。

训练目标遵循标准的监督微调：

$$
L_{SFT}(\theta) = -E_{(P,I) \sim D} [\log E_{\theta}(I | P)]
$$

其中 $P$ 代表包含 URL、标题和索引块的输入提示，而 $I$ 代表格式化为 Python 列表的目标索引区间。

### 后处理和重构

最后阶段从预测索引中重构提取内容。使用其元数据属性重新组装拆分的块，并通过启发式方法恢复因分割而中断的常见父子关系，从而恢复 HTML 结构。重构的内容与原始网页标题结合形成新的 HTML 文档，然后转换为 Markdown 格式，以简化 LLM 的消费。

![方法示例](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-3.jpeg)
*详细示例展示了从原始 HTML 到最终 Markdown 输出的完整提取过程*

## 实验结果与性能分析

评估涵盖了下游 RAG QA 性能和直接提取质量指标，涉及多个数据集和基线。

### RAG 问答系统性能

当集成到 RAG 系统中时，IndexLM 在五个数据集上始终实现了卓越的问答性能。以 Qwen3-4B 作为回答模型，IndexLM-4B 平均 F1 分数为 55.41，优于 Firecrawl Extract (52.72)，并显著超越传统 Chunk-Rerank 方法 (49.44)。以 Gemma3-27B-it 作为回答模型时，也观察到类似的性能优势 (F1: 57.94)。

![上下文长度分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-4.jpeg)
*不同上下文令牌限制下的性能表现，展示了 IndexLM 始终如一的优越性*

值得注意的是，IndexLM 在实现这些结果的同时使用了显著更少的令牌（大约 1900-2000 个），相比于使用完整上下文限制的方法，这表明其在不牺牲相关性的前提下实现了有效的信息提炼。

![扩展上下文分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-5.jpeg)
*高达 30K 令牌的扩展分析，展示了 IndexLM 在不同上下文长度下的鲁棒性*

### 直接提取性能

在主要内容提取方面，IndexLM-4B 的 F1 分数为 87.40，召回率为 92.46，大幅优于 ReaderLM-v2 (F1: 68.89) 和 HtmlRAG (F1: 48.65) 等专用模型。在查询相关提取方面，IndexLM-4B 的 F1 分数为 31.69，超越了包括生成式方法在内的大多数基线。

效率提升显著：IndexLM-0.6B 在主要内容提取方面平均延迟为 0.35 秒，而 IndexLM-4B (0.81 秒) 比使用提示的 Qwen3-4B (17.35 秒) 快约 49 倍，比 ReaderLM-v2 (11.76 秒) 快 33 倍。

![查询示例](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-6.jpeg)
*展示查询相关提取能力的示例，涉及体育相关内容*

### 消融研究

在查询相关数据和主要内容数据上进行联合训练对于模型的通用性至关重要。仅在查询相关数据上训练保持了 QE 性能，但降低了 ME 能力，而仅在主要内容上训练在 QE 任务上几乎失败。此外，即使将训练过的 IndexLM 替换为未经训练的 Qwen3-4B 模型，该框架固有的有效性也通过合理的性能得以证明。

## 意义与影响

这项研究通过将提取延迟与内容长度解耦，同时保持高准确性，解决了 LLM 驱动的 Web 应用程序中的一个根本瓶颈。判别式方法使得能够以前所未有的速度处理大量网络语料库，这对于实时网络代理和大规模 RAG 部署至关重要。

![令牌分布](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.06641v1/img-7.jpeg)
*令牌分布比较，展示了网络内容处理挑战的规模*

从生成到判别的范式转变，在网络提取之外具有更广泛的意义，潜在地适用于文档处理、数据库查询和结构化信息检索任务。小型模型（0.6B-4B参数）所展示的有效性使该方法适用于资源受限的部署，同时保持有竞争力的性能。

## 技术贡献和未来方向

本文的主要贡献包括：(1) 将网络提取重新定义为索引预测而非文本生成，(2) 开发了一个综合框架，用于在分割和重建过程中保留HTML结构，(3) 在不牺牲提取质量的情况下展示了显著的效率提升，以及 (4) 在多项任务和数据集上提供了广泛的实证验证。

该框架的模块化设计以及作者关于将其扩展到网络内容之外的讨论，表明了在不同领域结构化信息提取方面有前景的研究方向。速度、准确性和结构感知能力的结合，使这种方法成为需要高效网络规模信息处理的下一代大型语言模型（LLM）应用的基础技术。

abstract: As web agents (e.g., Deep Research) routinely consume massive volumes of web pages to gather and analyze information, LLM context management -- under large token budgets and low signal density -- emerges as a foundational, high-importance, and technically challenging problem for agentic and RAG pipelines. Existing solutions for extracting relevant content are inadequate: generative extraction models suffer from high latency, rule-based heuristics lack adaptability, and chunk-and-rerank methods are blind to webpage structure. To overcome these issues, we introduce Index-based Web Content Extraction to reframe the extraction process from slow, token-by-token generation into a highly efficient, discriminative task of index prediction, achieving both effectiveness and efficiency. We partition HTML into structure-aware, addressable segments, and extract only the positional indices of content relevant to a given query. This method decouples extraction latency from content length, enabling rapid, query-relevant extraction. We first evaluate our method as a post-retrieval processing component within an RAG QA system and find that it improves QA accuracy. Then we directly measure its match rate with the target content in two scenarios: main content extraction (ME) and query-relevant extraction (QE). Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing works in both accuracy and speed, effectively bridging the gap between LLMs and the vast webpages.

abstract: Recommender Systems (RSs) have become the cornerstone of various applications such as e-commerce and social media platforms. The evolution of RSs is paramount in the digital era, in which personalised user experience is tailored to the user's preferences. Large Language Models (LLMs) have sparked a new paradigm - generative retrieval and recommendation. Despite their potential, generative RS methods face issues such as hallucination, which degrades the recommendation performance, and high computational cost in practical scenarios. To address these issues, we introduce HGLMRec, a novel Multi-LLM agent-based RS that incorporates a hypergraph encoder designed to capture complex, multi-behaviour relationships between users and items. The HGLMRec model retrieves only the relevant tokens during inference, reducing computational overhead while enriching the retrieval context. Experimental results show performance improvement by HGLMRec against state-of-the-art baselines at lower computational cost.

abstract: In recent years, cross-modal retrieval using images and text has become an active area of research, especially in the medical domain. The abundance of data in various modalities in this field has led to a growing importance of cross-modal retrieval for efficient image interpretation, data-driven diagnostic support, and medical education. In the context of the increasing integration of distributed medical data across healthcare facilities with the objective of enhancing interoperability, it is imperative to optimize the performance of retrieval systems in terms of the speed, memory efficiency, and accuracy of the retrieved data. This necessity arises in response to the substantial surge in data volume that characterizes contemporary medical practices. In this study, we propose a novel framework that incorporates dropout voting and mixture-of-experts (MoE) based contrastive fusion modules into a CLIP-based cross-modal hashing retrieval structure. We also propose the application of hybrid loss. So we now call our model MCMFH which is a medical cross-modal fusion hashing retrieval. Our method enables the simultaneous achievement of high accuracy and fast retrieval speed in low-memory environments. The model is demonstrated through experiments on radiological and non-radiological medical datasets.

abstract: Scientists have always used the studies and research of other researchers to achieve new objectives and perspectives. In particular, employing and operating the measured data in previous studies is so practical. Searching the content of other scientists' articles is a challenge that researchers have always struggled with. Nowadays, the use of knowledge graphs as a semantic database has helped a lot in saving and retrieving scholarly knowledge. Such technologies are crucial to upgrading traditional search systems to smart knowledge retrieval, which is crucial to getting the most relevant answers for a user query, especially in information and knowledge management. However, in most cases, only the metadata of a paper is searchable, and it is still cumbersome for scientists to have access to the content of the papers. In this paper, we present a novel method of faceted search \emph{structured content} for comparing and filtering measured data in scholarly knowledge graphs while different units of measurement are used in different studies. This search system proposes applicable units as facets to the user and would dynamically integrate content from further remote knowledge graphs to materialize the scholarly knowledge graph and achieve a higher order of exploration usability on scholarly content, which can be filtered to better satisfy the user's information needs. The state of the art is that, by using our faceted search system, users can not only search the contents of scientific articles, but also compare and filter heterogeneous data.

abstract: The parallelized multi-retrieval architecture has been widely adopted in large-scale recommender systems for its computational efficiency and comprehensive coverage of user interests. Many retrieval methods typically integrate additional cross-scenario samples to enhance the overall performance ceiling. However, those model designs neglect the fact that a part of the cross-scenario samples have already been retrieved by existing models within a system, leading to diminishing marginal utility in delivering incremental performance gains. In this paper, we propose a novel retrieval framework IncRec, specifically for cross-scenario incremental sample learning. The innovations of IncRec can be highlighted as two aspects. Firstly, we construct extreme cross-scenario incremental samples that are not retrieved by any existing model. And we design an incremental sample learning framework which focuses on capturing incremental representation to improve the overall retrieval performance. Secondly, we introduce a consistency-aware alignment module to further make the model prefer incremental samples with high exposure probability. Extensive offline and online A/B tests validate the superiority of our framework over state-of-the-art retrieval methods. In particular, we deploy IncRec in the Taobao homepage recommendation, achieving a 1% increase in online transaction count, demonstrating its practical applicability.

abstract: Interpretability is central to trustworthy machine learning, yet existing metrics rarely quantify how effectively data support an interpretive representation. We propose Interpretive Efficiency, a normalized, task-aware functional that measures the fraction of task-relevant information transmitted through an interpretive channel. The definition is grounded in five axioms ensuring boundedness, Blackwell-style monotonicity, data-processing stability, admissible invariance, and asymptotic consistency. We relate the functional to mutual information and derive a local Fisher-geometric expansion, then establish asymptotic and finite-sample estimation guarantees using standard empirical-process tools. Experiments on controlled image and signal tasks demonstrate that the measure recovers theoretical orderings, exposes representational redundancy masked by accuracy, and correlates with robustness, making it a practical, theory-backed diagnostic for representation design.

abstract: Multimedia information retrieval from videos remains a challenging problem. While recent systems have advanced multimodal search through semantic, object, and OCR queries - and can retrieve temporally consecutive scenes - they often rely on a single query modality for an entire sequence, limiting robustness in complex temporal contexts. To overcome this, we propose a cross-modal temporal event retrieval framework that enables different query modalities to describe distinct scenes within a sequence. To determine decision thresholds for scene transition and slide change adaptively, we build Kernel Density Gaussian Mixture Thresholding (KDE-GMM) algorithm, ensuring optimal keyframe selection. These extracted keyframes act as compact, high-quality visual exemplars that retain each segment's semantic essence, improving retrieval precision and efficiency. Additionally, the system incorporates a large language model (LLM) to refine and expand user queries, enhancing overall retrieval performance. The proposed system's effectiveness and robustness were demonstrated through its strong results in the Ho Chi Minh AI Challenge 2025.

abstract: Existing fine-grained image retrieval (FGIR) methods learn discriminative embeddings by adopting semantically sparse one-hot labels derived from category names as supervision. While effective on seen classes, such supervision overlooks the rich semantics encoded in category names, hindering the modeling of comparability among cross-category details and, in turn, limiting generalization to unseen categories. To tackle this, we introduce LaFG, a Language-driven framework for Fine-Grained Retrieval that converts class names into attribute-level supervision using large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). Treating each name as a semantic anchor, LaFG prompts an LLM to generate detailed, attribute-oriented descriptions. To mitigate attribute omission in these descriptions, it leverages a frozen VLM to project them into a vision-aligned space, clustering them into a dataset-wide attribute vocabulary while harvesting complementary attributes from related categories. Leveraging this vocabulary, a global prompt template selects category-relevant attributes, which are aggregated into category-specific linguistic prototypes. abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) underpins applications in healthcare, rehabilitation, fitness tracking, and smart environments, yet existing deep learning approaches demand dataset-specific training, large labeled corpora, and significant computational resources.We introduce RAG-HAR, a training-free retrieval-augmented framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) for HAR. RAG-HAR computes lightweight statistical descriptors, retrieves semantically similar samples from a vector database, and uses this contextual evidence to make LLM-based activity identification. We further enhance RAG-HAR by first applying prompt optimization and introducing an LLM-based activity descriptor that generates context-enriched vector databases for delivering accurate and highly relevant contextual information. Along with these mechanisms, RAG-HAR achieves state-of-the-art performance across six diverse HAR benchmarks. Most importantly, RAG-HAR attains these improvements without requiring model training or fine-tuning, emphasizing its robustness and practical applicability. RAG-HAR moves beyond known behaviors, enabling the recognition and meaningful labelling of multiple unseen human activities.
title: RAG-HAR: Retrieval Augmented Generation-based Human Activity Recognition

abstract: Security research is fundamentally a problem of resource constraint and consequent prioritization. There is simply too much attack surface and too little time and energy to spend analyzing it all. The most effective security researchers are often those who are most skilled at intuitively deciding which part of an expansive attack surface to investigate. We demonstrate that this problem of selecting the most promising option from among many possibilities can be reframed as an information retrieval problem, and solved using document ranking techniques with LLMs performing the heavy lifting as general-purpose rankers. We present SiftRank, a ranking algorithm achieving O(n) complexity through three key mechanisms: listwise ranking using an LLM to order documents in small batches of approximately 10 items at a time; inflection-based convergence detection that adaptively terminates ranking when score distributions have stabilized; and iterative refinement that progressively focuses ranking effort on the most relevant documents. Unlike existing reranking approaches that require a separate first-stage retrieval step to narrow datasets to approximately 100 candidates, SiftRank operates directly on thousands of items, with each document evaluated across multiple randomized batches to mitigate inconsistent judgments by an LLM. We demonstrate practical effectiveness on N-day vulnerability analysis, successfully identifying a vulnerability-fixing function among 2,197 changed functions in a stripped binary firmware patch within 99 seconds at an inference cost of $0.82. Our approach enables scalable security prioritization for problems that are generally constrained by manual analysis, requiring only standard LLM API access without specialized infrastructure, embedding, or domain-specific fine-tuning. An open-source implementation of SiftRank may be found at https://github.com/noperator/siftrank.
title: Sift or Get Off the PoC: Applying Information Retrieval to Vulnerability Research with SiftRank

abstract: In the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures are gaining significant attention for their ability to ground language generation in reliable knowledge sources. Despite their impressive effectiveness in many areas, RAG systems based solely on semantic similarity often fail to ensure factual accuracy in specialized domains, where terminological ambiguity can affect retrieval relevance. This study proposes an enhanced RAG architecture that integrates a factual signal derived from Entity Linking to improve the accuracy of educational question-answering systems in Italian. The system includes a Wikidata-based Entity Linking module and implements three re-ranking strategies to combine semantic and entity-based information: a hybrid score weighting model, reciprocal rank fusion, and a cross-encoder re-ranker. Experiments were conducted on two benchmarks: a custom academic dataset and the standard SQuAD-it dataset. Results show that, in domain-specific contexts, the hybrid schema based on reciprocal rank fusion significantly outperforms both the baseline and the cross-encoder approach, while the cross-encoder achieves the best results on the general-domain dataset. These findings confirm the presence of an effect of domain mismatch and highlight the importance of domain adaptation and hybrid ranking strategies to enhance factual precision and reliability in retrieval-augmented generation. They also demonstrate the potential of entity-aware RAG systems in educational environments, fostering adaptive and reliable AI-based tutoring tools.
