abstract: Domain adaptive retrieval aims to transfer knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain, enabling effective retrieval while mitigating domain discrepancies. However, existing methods encounter several fundamental limitations: 1) neglecting class-level semantic alignment and excessively pursuing pair-wise sample alignment; 2) lacking either pseudo-label reliability consideration or geometric guidance for assessing label correctness; 3) directly quantizing original features affected by domain shift, undermining the quality of learned hash codes. In view of these limitations, we propose Prototype-Based Semantic Consistency Alignment (PSCA), a two-stage framework for effective domain adaptive retrieval. In the first stage, a set of orthogonal prototypes directly establishes class-level semantic connections, maximizing inter-class separability while gathering intra-class samples. During the prototype learning, geometric proximity provides a reliability indicator for semantic consistency alignment through adaptive weighting of pseudo-label confidences. The resulting membership matrix and prototypes facilitate feature reconstruction, ensuring quantization on reconstructed rather than original features, thereby improving subsequent hash coding quality and seamlessly connecting both stages. In the second stage, domain-specific quantization functions process the reconstructed features under mutual approximation constraints, generating unified binary hash codes across domains. Extensive experiments validate PSCA's superior performance across multiple datasets.

abstract: We report an iterative algorithm to retrieve accurate real space information from gas phase ultrafast diffraction measurements with missing data at low momentum transfer. The algorithm operates in a manner similar to phase retrieval algorithms which transform signals back and forth between the signal domain and the Fourier transform domain and apply constraints to retrieve the missing phase. Our algorithm retrieves missing data that is not accessible experimentally by applying a real-space constraint that requires only an approximate a-priori knowledge of the shortest and longest internuclear distances in the molecule. We demonstrate successful retrieval of the missing data in simulated data and in experimentally measured electron diffraction signals of photo-dissociated iodobenzene molecules.

alphaxiv_detail.title: Retrieving missing data in electron diffraction of gas-phase molecules
alphaxiv_detail.abstract: We report an iterative algorithm to retrieve accurate real space information from gas electron diffraction measurements with missing data at low momentum transfer. The algorithm is similar to phase retrieval algorithms which transform signals back and forth between the signal domain and the Fourier domain and apply constraints to retrieve the missing phase. The difference in our case is that the goal is not retrieval of the phase of the diffraction signal but the missing data at low momentum transfer, which is necessary for generating the real-space pair distribution function. The missing data is a common problem in static and ultrafast gas phase electron diffraction experiments due to experimental constraints. We demonstrated successful restoration of the missing data in simulated data and in experimentally measured diffraction signals of static and photo-dissociated trifluoroiodomethane and iodobenzene molecules.

abstract: AIVisor, an agentic retrieval-augmented LLM for student advising, was used to examine how personalization affects system performance across multiple evaluation dimensions. Using twelve authentic advising questions intentionally designed to stress lexical precision, we compared ten personalized and non-personalized system configurations and analyzed outcomes with a Linear Mixed-Effects Model across lexical (BLEU, ROUGE-L), semantic (METEOR, BERTScore), and grounding (RAGAS) metrics. Results showed a consistent trade-off: personalization reliably improved reasoning quality and grounding, yet introduced a significant negative interaction on semantic similarity, driven not by poorer answers but by the limits of current metrics, which penalize meaningful personalized deviations from generic reference texts. This reveals a structural flaw in prevailing LLM evaluation methods, which are ill-suited for assessing user-specific responses. The fully integrated personalized configuration produced the highest overall gains, suggesting that personalization can enhance system effectiveness when evaluated with appropriate multidimensional metrics. Overall, the study demonstrates that personalization produces metric-dependent shifts rather than uniform improvements and provides a methodological foundation for more transparent and robust personalization in agentic AI.

abstract: Reusing existing neural-network components is central to research efficiency, yet discovering, extracting, and validating such modules across thousands of open-source repositories remains difficult. We introduce NN-RAG, a retrieval-augmented generation system that converts large, heterogeneous PyTorch codebases into a searchable and executable library of validated neural modules. Unlike conventional code search or clone-detection tools, NN-RAG performs scope-aware dependency resolution, import-preserving reconstruction, and validator-gated promotion -- ensuring that every retrieved block is scope-closed, compilable, and runnable. Applied to 19 major repositories, the pipeline extracted 1,289 candidate blocks, validated 941 (73.0%), and demonstrated that over 80% are structurally unique. Through multi-level de-duplication (exact, lexical, structural), we find that NN-RAG contributes the overwhelming majority of unique architectures to the LEMUR dataset, supplying approximately 72% of all novel network structures. Beyond quantity, NN-RAG uniquely enables cross-repository migration of architectural patterns, automatically identifying reusable modules in one project and regenerating them, dependency-complete, in another context. To our knowledge, no other open-source system provides this capability at scale. The framework's neutral specifications further allow optional integration with language models for synthesis or dataset registration without redistributing third-party code. Overall, NN-RAG transforms fragmented vision code into a reproducible, provenance-tracked substrate for algorithmic discovery, offering a first open-source solution that both quantifies and expands the diversity of executable neural architectures across repositories.

abstract: Image captioning has drawn considerable attention from the natural language processing and computer vision fields. Aiming to reduce the reliance on curated data, several studies have explored image captioning without any humanly-annotated image-text pairs for training, although existing methods are still outperformed by fully supervised approaches. This paper proposes TOMCap, i.e., an improved text-only training method that performs captioning without the need for aligned image-caption pairs. The method is based on prompting a pre-trained language model decoder with information derived from a CLIP representation, after undergoing a process to reduce the modality gap. We specifically tested the combined use of retrieved examples of captions, and latent vector representations, to guide the generation process. Through extensive experiments, we show that TOMCap outperforms other training-free and text-only methods. We also analyze the impact of different choices regarding the configuration of the retrieval-augmentation and modality gap reduction components.

abstract: Accurate question answering over real spreadsheets remains difficult due to multirow headers, merged cells, and unit annotations that disrupt naive chunking, while rigid SQL views fail on files lacking consistent schemas. We present SQuARE, a hybrid retrieval framework with sheet-level, complexity-aware routing. It computes a continuous score based on header depth and merge density, then routes queries either through structure-preserving chunk retrieval or SQL over an automatically constructed relational representation. A lightweight agent supervises retrieval, refinement, or combination of results across both paths when confidence is low. This design maintains header hierarchies, time labels, and units, ensuring that returned values are faithful to the original cells and straightforward to verify. Evaluated on multi-header corporate balance sheets, a heavily merged World Bank workbook, and diverse public datasets, SQuARE consistently surpasses single-strategy baselines and ChatGPT-4o on both retrieval precision and end-to-end answer accuracy while keeping latency predictable. By decoupling retrieval from model choice, the system is compatible with emerging tabular foundation models and offers a practical bridge toward a more robust table understanding.

abstract: The atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) plays a critical role in governing turbulent exchanges of momentum, heat moisture, and trace gases between the Earth's surface and the free atmosphere, thereby influencing meteorological phenomena, air quality, and climate processes. Accurate and temporally continuous characterization of the ABL structure and height evolution is crucial for both scientific understanding and practical applications. High-resolution retrievals of the ABL height from vertical velocity measurements is challenging because it is often estimated using empirical thresholds applied to profiles of vertical velocity variance or related turbulence diagnostics at each measurement altitude, which can suffer from limited sampling and sensitivity to noise. To address these limitations, this work employs nonstationary Gaussian process (GP) modeling to more effectively capture the spatio-temporal dependence structure in the data, enabling high-quality -- and, if desired, high-resolution -- estimates of the ABL height without reliance on ad-hoc parameter tuning. By leveraging Vecchia approximations, the proposed method can be applied to large-scale datasets, and example applications using full-day vertical velocity profiles comprising approximately $5$M measurements are presented.

alphaxiv_detail.abstract: The atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) plays a critical role in governing turbulent exchanges of momentum, heat moisture, and trace gases between the Earth's surface and the free atmosphere, thereby influencing meteorological phenomena, air quality, and climate processes. Accurate and temporally continuous characterization of the ABL structure and height evolution is crucial for both scientific understanding and practical applications. High-resolution retrievals of the ABL height from vertical velocity measurements is challenging because it is often estimated using empirical thresholds applied to profiles of vertical velocity variance or related turbulence diagnostics at each measurement altitude, which can suffer from limited sampling and sensitivity to noise. To address these limitations, this work employs nonstationary Gaussian process (GP) modeling to more effectively capture the spatio-temporal dependence structure in the data, enabling high-quality -- and, if desired, high-resolution -- estimates of the ABL height without reliance on ad-hoc parameter tuning. By leveraging Vecchia approximations, the proposed method can be applied to large-scale datasets, and example applications using full-day vertical velocity profiles comprising approximately $5$M measurements are presented.

abstract: In online marketplaces like Airbnb, users frequently engage in comparison shopping before making purchase decisions. Despite the prevalence of this behavior, a significant disconnect persists between mainstream e-commerce search engines and users' comparison needs. Traditional ranking models often evaluate items in isolation, disregarding the context in which users compare multiple items on a search results page. While recent advances in deep learning have sought to improve ranking accuracy, diversity, and fairness by encoding listwise context, the challenge of aligning search rankings with user comparison shopping behavior remains inadequately addressed. In this paper, we propose a novel ranking architecture - Learning-to-Comparison-Shop (LTCS) System - that explicitly models and learns users' comparison shopping behaviors. Through extensive offline and online experiments, we demonstrate that our approach yields statistically significant gains in key business metrics - improving NDCG by 1.7% and boosting booking conversion rate by 0.6% in A/B testing - while also enhancing user experience. We also compare our model against state-of-the-art approaches and demonstrate that LTCS significantly outperforms them.

abstract: Data quality monitoring is a core challenge in modern information processing systems. While many approaches to detect data errors or shifts have been proposed, few studies investigate the mechanisms governing error generation. We argue that knowing how errors were generated can be key to tracing and fixing them. In this study, we build on existing work in the statistics literature on missing values and propose MechDetect, a simple algorithm to investigate error generation mechanisms. Given a tabular data set and a corresponding error mask, the algorithm estimates whether or not the errors depend on the data using machine learning models. Our work extends established approaches to detect mechanisms underlying missing values and can be readily applied to other error types, provided that an error mask is available. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MechDetect in experiments on established benchmark datasets.

en.title: Algorithms for Boolean Matrix Factorization using Integer Programming and Heuristics
en.abstract: Boolean matrix factorization (BMF) approximates a given binary input matrix as the product of two smaller binary factors. Unlike binary matrix factorization based on standard arithmetic, BMF employs the Boolean OR and AND operations for the matrix product, which improves interpretability and reduces the approximation error. It is also used in role mining and computer vision. In this paper, we first propose algorithms for BMF that perform alternating optimization (AO) of the factor matrices, where each subproblem is solved via integer programming (IP). We then design different approaches to further enhance AO-based algorithms by selecting an optimal subset of rank-one factors from multiple runs. To address the scalability limits of IP-based methods, we introduce new greedy and local-search heuristics. We also construct a new C++ data structure for Boolean vectors and matrices that is significantly faster than existing ones and is of independent interest, allowing our heuristics to scale to large datasets. We illustrate the performance of all our proposed methods and compare them with the state of the art on various real datasets, both with and without missing data, including applications in topic modeling and imaging.

summary.summary: Researchers from Université de Mons introduce a suite of algorithms for Boolean Matrix Factorization, combining integer programming-based methods for enhanced solution quality on smaller instances with novel greedy heuristics for scalability on larger datasets. The work also develops a custom C++ `bitmatrix` data structure to significantly accelerate Boolean operations, leading to state-of-the-art performance across various real-world applications including topic modeling and image processing.
originalProblem: Boolean Matrix Factorization (BMF) is an NP-hard problem, making exact solutions computationally intractable for large datasets.
Existing BMF algorithms often struggle with solution quality, getting stuck in local minima, and lack scalability for very large-scale binary matrices.
Efficient execution of Boolean algebra operations on large binary matrices is often hindered by generic linear algebra libraries not optimized for bitwise logic.
solution: Developed new Integer Programming (IP) based algorithms (MS-Comb-AO, Tree BMF) that combine multiple BMF solutions to overcome local minima and improve approximation error.
Introduced novel greedy and local-search heuristics (Greedy-BoolLS, Greedy-Comb, Greedy-TreeBMF) to address scalability limitations for large datasets, providing efficient approximate solutions.

Engineered a custom C++ `bitmatrix` data structure that stores Boolean values as single bits and uses bitwise operations, drastically reducing memory footprint and accelerating Boolean matrix operations.
keyInsights: Combining multiple BMF solutions, either via optimal IP selection (MS-Comb-AO) or heuristic selection (Greedy-Comb), consistently improves approximation quality by escaping local optima.
Well-designed greedy heuristics can achieve competitive reconstruction errors compared to IP-based methods on certain datasets, while offering superior scalability for very large instances.
Low-level optimization of Boolean matrix operations through a custom bit-packed data structure is crucial for achieving high computational efficiency in BMF algorithms, especially for large matrices.
results: Proposed IP-based methods (MS-Comb-AO, Tree BMF) achieved state-of-the-art or superior reconstruction errors on small to medium-sized datasets compared to existing methods.

Greedy heuristics (Greedy-TreeBMF) demonstrated competitive performance on large datasets like NIST tdt2 (98.45% relative error for r=20), where IP methods were computationally prohibitive, and successfully extracted interpretable topics and facial features.
The `bitmatrix` C++ data structure delivered up to a 5x speedup for Boolean matrix multiplication on large matrices (n=20000) compared to standard libraries like Eigen and Armadillo.

en.overview:
## Problem Overview

Boolean Matrix Factorization (BMF) is a specialized variant of low-rank matrix approximation designed specifically for binary data. Unlike traditional matrix factorization methods that use standard arithmetic, BMF employs Boolean algebra operations (OR and AND) to decompose a binary input matrix $X \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ into two smaller binary factor matrices $W \in \{0,1\}^{m \times r}$ and $H \in \{0,1\}^{r \times n}$, where the approximation is given by the Boolean product $W \circ H$.

![Boolean Matrix Factorization Example](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-0.jpeg)

*Figure 1: Example of Boolean Matrix Factorization showing how a binary matrix representing animal characteristics can be decomposed into factor matrices using Boolean operations.*

The fundamental difference between BMF and standard binary matrix factorization lies in the matrix multiplication operation. In BMF, the product $(W \circ H)_{ij} = \bigvee_{k=1}^{r} (W_{ik} \wedge H_{kj})$, where $\vee$ represents logical OR and $\wedge$ represents logical AND. This can be equivalently expressed as $W \circ H = \min(1, WH)$, where $WH$ is the standard matrix product.

## Algorithmic Contributions

The paper presents a comprehensive suite of algorithms addressing both solution quality and scalability challenges in BMF. The approach is two-pronged: sophisticated Integer Programming (IP) based methods for medium-scale problems requiring high accuracy, and efficient greedy heuristics for large-scale datasets where exact methods become computationally prohibitive.

### Integer Programming Approaches

The core IP-based algorithm employs alternating optimization (AO-BMF), which iteratively optimizes one factor matrix while keeping the other fixed. When matrix $W$ is fixed, the problem decomposes into independent Boolean Least Squares (BoolLS) subproblems for each column of $H$. For a given column $x = X(:,j)$ and fixed $W$, the task is to find $h = H(:,j)$ that minimizes $\|x - W \circ h\|^2_2$.

The BoolLS subproblem is reformulated as a quadratic integer program:

$$
\min_{h \in \{0,1\}^r, z \in \{0,1\}^m} \|m \odot (x - z)\|^2_2 \quad \text{subject to} \quad Wh^T \leq z \leq Wh
$$

where $z = \min(1, Wh)$ is represented by auxiliary binary variables, and $m$ is a mask vector handling missing data.

To address the local minima problem inherent in alternating optimization, the authors introduce MS-Comb-AO, which generates multiple independent BMF solutions and then optimally combines their rank-one factors using another IP formulation. The method pools all rank-one factors from multiple solutions and selects the optimal subset that minimizes the approximation error.

### Scalable Heuristic Methods

For large-scale applications, the paper introduces Greedy-BoolLS, a heuristic solution to the BoolLS subproblem. Starting with an all-zero vector, the algorithm iteratively selects the entry that yields the greatest error reduction when set to one. This is enhanced with a local search strategy that explores neighboring solutions within a small Hamming distance.

The greedy approach is extended to solution combination through Greedy-Comb, which heuristically selects the best rank-one factors from a pool generated by multiple runs. This is further enhanced by Greedy-TreeBMF, which employs a hierarchical combination strategy for improved scalability.

## Technical Innovation: Custom Data Structure

A significant technical contribution is the development of a custom C++ data structure called `bitmatrix` for Boolean vectors and matrices. Standard implementations use excessive memory (8 bits per Boolean value instead of 1), and existing linear algebra libraries use floating-point types that don't leverage bitwise operations.

The `bitmatrix` structure uses integer arrays and bitwise operations to store each Boolean value in a single bit, dramatically reducing memory footprint and enabling faster parallel bitwise operations. Experimental results demonstrate up to 5× speedup compared to general-purpose libraries like Eigen and Armadillo for large matrices.

## Experimental Results and Applications

The algorithms were extensively evaluated on both complete and incomplete datasets from various domains. On small to medium datasets, the proposed methods consistently outperformed state-of-the-art approaches, often achieving better results within much shorter time limits (30 seconds to 5 minutes versus 20 minutes for competing methods).

### Topic Modeling Application

![Overlapping Communities Visualization](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-1.jpeg)

*Figure 2: BMF's ability to model overlapping communities, where entities can belong to multiple groups simultaneously.*

The NIST tdt2 dataset was used to demonstrate scalability in topic modeling applications. On large datasets (10,729 × 8,200 dimensions), only the greedy methods could complete within reasonable time and memory constraints. Greedy-TreeBMF achieved the best relative error (98.45% for rank 20), demonstrating that well-designed heuristics can be highly competitive with exact methods.

The extracted topics showed excellent interpretability, with clear thematic coherence such as "Clinton-Lewinsky scandal," "Israel-Palestine conflict," and "1998 Superbowl," each associated with relevant keywords that clearly define the topic.

![Boolean Logic Interpretation](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-2.jpeg)

*Figure 3: Boolean logic interpretation showing how BMF naturally models logical relationships in binary data.*

### Facial Feature Extraction

![Extracted Facial Features](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-3.jpeg)

*Figure 4: Comparison of facial features extracted by AO-BMF (left) showing more localized features and Greedy-TreeBMF (right) showing more global features.*

On the CBCL facial image dataset, BMF successfully extracted interpretable facial features. Interestingly, different algorithms showed distinct characteristics: AO-BMF extracted more localized features (specific facial regions), while Greedy-TreeBMF extracted more global features, suggesting that initialization strategies can influence the nature of learned representations.

## Significance and Impact

This research significantly advances Boolean Matrix Factorization by providing a comprehensive algorithmic toolkit that bridges the gap between solution quality and computational scalability. The dual-track approach enables practitioners to choose appropriate methods based on their specific requirements: IP-based methods for high-quality solutions on medium-scale problems, and efficient heuristics for large-scale applications.

The custom `bitmatrix` data structure represents a fundamental advancement in computational efficiency for binary data operations, with applications extending beyond BMF to other combinatorial optimization problems involving binary matrices.

The demonstrated success in topic modeling and image analysis, particularly the interpretability of extracted features and topics, positions BMF as a powerful tool for explainable AI applications where understanding the learned representations is crucial. The open-source implementation ensures reproducibility and facilitates adoption by the broader research community.

zh.title: 基于整数规划与启发式算法的布尔矩阵分解算法
zh.abstract: 布尔矩阵分解（BMF）将一个给定的二进制输入矩阵近似分解为两个更小的二进制因子矩阵的乘积。与基于标准算术的二进制矩阵分解不同，BMF在矩阵乘法中采用布尔OR和AND运算，这提高了可解释性并减小了近似误差。它也被应用于角色挖掘和计算机视觉领域。在本文中，我们首先提出了BMF算法，这些算法对因子矩阵执行交替优化（AO），其中每个子问题通过整数规划（IP）求解。接着，我们设计了不同的方法，通过从多次运行中选择秩一因子的最优子集，进一步增强基于AO的算法。为了解决基于IP的方法的可扩展性限制，我们引入了新的贪婪和局部搜索启发式算法。我们还构建了一种新的用于布尔向量和矩阵的C++数据结构，它比现有结构显著更快，并具有独立的价值，使我们的启发式算法能够扩展到大型数据集。我们展示了所有提出的方法的性能，并将其与现有最先进的方法在各种真实数据集（包括有缺失数据和无缺失数据的情况）上进行了比较，涵盖了主题建模和图像处理等应用。

summary.summary: 蒙斯大学的研究人员介绍了一套布尔矩阵分解算法，该算法结合了基于整数规划的方法，以提高小型实例的解决方案质量，并采用了新颖的贪婪启发式算法，以实现大型数据集的可扩展性。这项工作还开发了一个定制的 C++ `bitmatrix` 数据结构，显著加速了布尔运算，从而在主题建模和图像处理等各种实际应用中实现了最先进的性能。
originalProblem: 布尔矩阵分解 (BMF) 是一个 NP-难问题，使得精确解对于大型数据集来说在计算上是不可行的。
现有 BMF 算法通常在解决方案质量方面表现不佳，容易陷入局部最小值，并且缺乏对超大型二进制矩阵的可扩展性。
大型二进制矩阵上布尔代数运算的有效执行通常受到未针对位运算逻辑进行优化的通用线性代数库的阻碍。
solution: 开发了新的基于整数规划 (IP) 的算法（MS-Comb-AO, Tree BMF），它们结合了多个 BMF 解以克服局部最小值并改进近似误差。
引入了新颖的贪婪和局部搜索启发式算法（Greedy-BoolLS, Greedy-Comb, Greedy-TreeBMF），以解决大型数据集的可扩展性限制，提供了高效的近似解。
设计了一个定制的 C++ `bitmatrix` 数据结构，该结构将布尔值存储为单个位，并使用位运算，显著减少了内存占用并加速了布尔矩阵运算。
keyInsights: 通过最优 IP 选择 (MS-Comb-AO) 或启发式选择 (Greedy-Comb) 组合多个 BMF 解，可以一致地通过逃离局部最优解来提高近似质量。
精心设计的贪婪启发式算法在某些数据集上可以达到与基于 IP 的方法相当的重建误差，同时为超大型实例提供卓越的可扩展性。
通过自定义位封装数据结构对布尔矩阵运算进行底层优化，对于实现 BMF 算法（特别是对于大型矩阵）的高计算效率至关重要。
results: 与现有方法相比，所提出的基于 IP 的方法（MS-Comb-AO, Tree BMF）在中小尺寸数据集上实现了最先进或更优的重建误差。
贪婪启发式算法 (Greedy-TreeBMF) 在 NIST tdt2 等大型数据集上表现出有竞争力的性能（r=20 时相对误差为 98.45%），而 IP 方法在计算上是不可行的，并成功提取了可解释的主题和面部特征。
与 Eigen 和 Armadillo 等标准库相比，`bitmatrix` C++ 数据结构在大型矩阵（n=20000）上的布尔矩阵乘法速度提高了多达 5 倍。

zh.overview:
## 问题概述

布尔矩阵分解（Boolean Matrix Factorization, BMF）是一种专门针对二进制数据设计的低秩矩阵近似的变体。与使用标准算术的传统矩阵分解方法不同，BMF 采用布尔代数运算（OR 和 AND）将一个二进制输入矩阵 $X \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ 分解为两个较小的二进制因子矩阵 $W \in \{0,1\}^{m \times r}$ 和 $H \in \{0,1\}^{r \times n}$，其中近似值由布尔积 $W \circ H$ 给出。

![Boolean Matrix Factorization Example](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-0.jpeg)

*图 1：布尔矩阵分解示例，展示了如何使用布尔运算将表示动物特征的二进制矩阵分解为因子矩阵。*

BMF 与标准二进制矩阵分解之间的根本区别在于矩阵乘法运算。在 BMF 中，乘积 $(W \circ H)_{ij} = \bigvee_{k=1}^{r} (W_{ik} \wedge H_{kj})$，其中 $\vee$ 表示逻辑 OR，$\wedge$ 表示逻辑 AND。这可以等价地表示为 $W \circ H = \min(1, WH)$，其中 $WH$ 是标准矩阵乘积。

## 算法贡献

该论文提出了一套全面的算法，解决了 BMF 中解决方案质量和可扩展性方面的挑战。该方法是双管齐下的：针对需要高精度的中等规模问题，采用复杂的基于整数规划（IP）的方法；针对计算成本过高的大规模数据集，采用高效的贪婪启发式算法。

### 整数规划方法

核心的基于 IP 的算法采用交替优化（AO-BMF），该算法在保持一个因子矩阵固定的同时迭代优化另一个因子矩阵。当矩阵 $W$ 固定时，问题分解为 $H$ 的每一列独立的布尔最小二乘（BoolLS）子问题。对于给定的列 $x = X(:,j)$ 和固定的 $W$，任务是找到 $h = H(:,j)$，使其最小化 $\|x - W \circ h\|^2_2$。

BoolLS 子问题被重新表述为一个二次整数规划：

$$
\min_{h \in \{0,1\}^r, z \in \{0,1\}^m} \|m \odot (x - z)\|^2_2 \quad \text{subject to} \quad Wh^T \leq z \leq Wh
$$

其中 $z = \min(1, Wh)$ 由辅助二进制变量表示，而 $m$ 是一个处理缺失数据的掩码向量。

为了解决交替优化中固有的局部最小值问题，作者引入了 MS-Comb-AO，它生成多个独立的 BMF 解决方案，然后使用另一个 IP 公式最佳地组合它们的秩一因子。该方法汇集了来自多个解决方案的所有秩一因子，并选择最小化近似误差的最佳子集。

### 可扩展的启发式方法

对于大规模应用，该论文引入了 Greedy-BoolLS，这是 BoolLS 子问题的一种启发式解决方案。算法从全零向量开始，迭代地选择将某个条目设置为 1 时产生最大误差减小的条目。通过在小汉明距离内探索相邻解决方案的局部搜索策略来增强此方法。

贪婪方法通过 Greedy-Comb 扩展到解决方案组合，Greedy-Comb 启发式地从多次运行生成的池中选择最佳的秩一因子。通过 Greedy-TreeBMF 进一步增强此方法，该方法采用分层组合策略以提高可扩展性。

## 技术创新：自定义数据结构

一项重要的技术贡献是开发了一种名为 `bitmatrix` 的自定义 C++ 数据结构，用于布尔向量和矩阵。标准实现使用了过多的内存（每个布尔值 8 位而不是 1 位），而现有的线性代数库使用浮点类型，无法利用位运算。

`bitmatrix` 结构使用整数数组和位操作将每个布尔值存储在一个比特中，显著减少了内存占用，并实现了更快的并行位操作。实验结果表明，对于大型矩阵，其速度比 Eigen 和 Armadillo 等通用库快达 5 倍。

## 实验结果与应用

这些算法在来自不同领域的完整和不完整数据集上进行了广泛评估。在中小规模数据集上，所提出的方法始终优于最先进的方法，通常在更短的时间限制内（30 秒到 5 分钟，而竞争方法为 20 分钟）获得更好的结果。

### 主题建模应用

![重叠社区可视化](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-1.jpeg)

*图 2：BMF 建模重叠社区的能力，其中实体可以同时属于多个群体。*

NIST tdt2 数据集用于演示主题建模应用的可扩展性。在大型数据集（10,729 × 8,200 维）上，只有贪婪方法能够在合理的时间和内存限制内完成。Greedy-TreeBMF 实现了最佳相对误差（秩为 20 时为 98.45%），表明精心设计的启发式方法可以与精确方法具有高度竞争力。

提取的主题表现出卓越的可解释性，具有清晰的主题连贯性，例如“克林顿-莱温斯基丑闻”、“以色列-巴勒斯坦冲突”和“1998 年超级碗”，每个主题都与明确定义该主题的相关关键词相关联。

![布尔逻辑解释](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-2.jpeg)

*图 3：布尔逻辑解释，展示了 BMF 如何自然地建模二元数据中的逻辑关系。*

### 面部特征提取

![提取的面部特征](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03807v1/img-3.jpeg)

*图 4：AO-BMF（左）提取的局部特征和 Greedy-TreeBMF（右）提取的全局特征的面部特征比较。*

在 CBCL 面部图像数据集上，BMF 成功提取了可解释的面部特征。有趣的是，不同的算法表现出不同的特征：AO-BMF 提取了更多局部特征（特定面部区域），而 Greedy-TreeBMF 提取了更多全局特征，这表明初始化策略可以影响学习表示的性质。

## 意义与影响

这项研究通过提供一个全面的算法工具包，弥合了解决方案质量和计算可扩展性之间的差距，显著推动了布尔矩阵分解的发展。双轨方法使实践者能够根据其特定需求选择合适的方法：基于 IP 的方法适用于中等规模问题的高质量解决方案，而高效启发式方法适用于大规模应用。

自定义的 `bitmatrix` 数据结构代表了二元数据操作计算效率方面的根本性进步，其应用范围超越了 BMF，延伸到涉及二元矩阵的其他组合优化问题。

在主题建模和图像分析中展示的成功，特别是提取特征和主题的可解释性，将 BMF 定位为可解释人工智能应用的强大工具，在这些应用中，理解学习到的表示至关重要。开源实现确保了可重现性，并促进了更广泛研究社区的采用。

abstract: Boolean matrix factorization (BMF) approximates a given binary input matrix as the product of two smaller binary factors. Unlike binary matrix factorization based on standard arithmetic, BMF employs the Boolean OR and AND operations for the matrix product, which improves interpretability and reduces the approximation error. It is also used in role mining and computer vision. In this paper, we first propose algorithms for BMF that perform alternating optimization (AO) of the factor matrices, where each subproblem is solved via integer programming (IP). We then design different approaches to further enhance AO-based algorithms by selecting an optimal subset of rank-one factors from multiple runs. To address the scalability limits of IP-based methods, we introduce new greedy and local-search heuristics. We also construct a new C++ data structure for Boolean vectors and matrices that is significantly faster than existing ones and is of independent interest, allowing our heuristics to scale to large datasets. We illustrate the performance of all our proposed methods and compare them with the state of the art on various real datasets, both with and without missing data, including applications in topic modeling and imaging.

en.title: AR-Med: Automated Relevance Enhancement in Medical Search via LLM-Driven Information Augmentation
en.abstract: Accurate and reliable search on online healthcare platforms is critical for user safety and service efficacy. Traditional methods, however, often fail to comprehend complex and nuanced user queries, limiting their effectiveness. Large language models (LLMs) present a promising solution, offering powerful semantic understanding to bridge this gap. Despite their potential, deploying LLMs in this high-stakes domain is fraught with challenges, including factual hallucinations, specialized knowledge gaps, and high operational costs. To overcome these barriers, we introduce \textbf{AR-Med}, a novel framework for \textbf{A}utomated \textbf{R}elevance assessment for \textbf{Med}ical search that has been successfully deployed at scale on the Online Medical Delivery Platforms. AR-Med grounds LLM reasoning in verified medical knowledge through a retrieval-augmented approach, ensuring high accuracy and reliability. To enable efficient online service, we design a practical knowledge distillation scheme that compresses large teacher models into compact yet powerful student models. We also introduce LocalQSMed, a multi-expert annotated benchmark developed to guide model iteration and ensure strong alignment between offline and online performance. Extensive experiments show AR-Med achieves an offline accuracy of over 93\%, a 24\% absolute improvement over the original online system, and delivers significant gains in online relevance and user satisfaction. Our work presents a practical and scalable blueprint for developing trustworthy, LLM-powered systems in real-world healthcare applications.

summary.summary: The AR-Med framework enhances medical search and recommendation accuracy on online platforms by integrating large language models with retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge distillation, and cross-modal information matching. It achieved over 24% absolute accuracy improvement on an expert-annotated benchmark and positive impacts on online business metrics like conversion rates in real-world deployment.
originalProblem: Traditional medical search systems struggle with semantic comprehension for complex queries, rely on costly expert-curated knowledge bases, and adapt slowly to new information.
Direct deployment of large language models (LLMs) in medical search leads to factual hallucinations and high operational costs, which are unacceptable in a high-stakes healthcare environment.
Online medical platforms face challenges like ambiguous user queries and merchant manipulation (e.g., 'traffic hijacking') with misleading product names.
solution: A retrieval-augmented framework (RAG) grounds LLMs with precise knowledge retrieval from verified medical sources and dynamic expert rules, while enhancing queries and filtering information.
A knowledge distillation scheme transfers expertise from large teacher LLMs to compact, efficient student models, suitable for high-throughput, low-latency online inference.
Cross-modal information matching uses product images to verify attributes and combat merchant fraud, ensuring input reliability for relevance scoring.
Development of LocalQSMed, an expert-annotated benchmark dataset, guides iterative model improvement and evaluates real-world relevance.
keyInsights: Combining LLMs with retrieval-augmented generation and expert-guided rules can effectively mitigate hallucination risks and improve factual accuracy in sensitive domains.
Knowledge distillation enables the efficient deployment of powerful LLM capabilities for real-time, high-volume industrial applications without sacrificing performance.
Integrating multimodal information, like product images, is crucial for combating practical challenges such as merchant fraud and enhancing the robustness of online product search systems.
Domain-specific, expert-annotated benchmarks are essential for aligning offline model evaluation with real-world performance and addressing nuanced, long-tail issues in specialized fields.
results: AR-Med achieved an absolute accuracy improvement of over 24% on the LocalQSMed benchmark compared to the baseline, with Qwen3-4B reaching 92.06% accuracy.

The framework showed significant performance gains in online A/B testing on Meituan's platform, leading to increased UV_CTR, UV_CVR, and UV_CXR, along with a total increase of +4983.0 orders in the medical global scenario.
Knowledge distillation enabled a fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B student model to outperform a larger Llama3.3-70B model in consistency judgment (91.19% vs. 71.49% accuracy), demonstrating efficiency gains.

en.overview:
## Framework Overview

AR-Med (Automated Relevance Enhancement in Medical Search via LLM-Driven Information Augmentation) addresses a critical challenge in online medical delivery platforms: ensuring accurate and reliable search results for pharmaceutical products. Developed by researchers from Meituan Inc. and collaborators, this framework tackles the limitations of traditional search methods while mitigating the risks associated with deploying large language models (LLMs) in high-stakes healthcare environments.

![AR-Med Framework Architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03737v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: Complete AR-Med framework architecture showing the integration of retrieval-augmented processing, expert rule guidance, cross-modal information matching, and knowledge distillation for deployment*

The system operates at the intersection of information retrieval, LLM capabilities, and real-world deployment requirements, processing billions of search requests daily on Meituan's medical delivery platform. Traditional search systems struggle with ambiguous queries, require expensive expert curation, and adapt slowly to new products. While LLMs offer powerful semantic understanding, they suffer from hallucinations and high computational costs that make direct deployment impractical in healthcare settings.

## Core Technical Components

### Retrieval-Augmented Framework

The foundation of AR-Med is a sophisticated retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework designed to ground LLM reasoning in verified medical knowledge. The system begins with precise knowledge retrieval, where user queries are enhanced using instruction-tuned 0.6B LLMs to add category-specific keywords. For example, an ambiguous query like "001" becomes "001 adult product" to improve external search relevance.

Retrieved information undergoes a two-stage filtering process: initial relevance scoring removes low-correlation content, followed by lightweight model consistency checks. This prevents larger LLMs from "overthinking" irrelevant information, reducing both latency and errors. The filtered information is then restructured into core elements including alternative expressions, keywords, topics, hierarchies, and intent judgments.

### Expert Rule Guidance

The framework incorporates domain expertise through dynamic rule application. After query rewriting, named entity recognition (NER) extracts key medical entities such as brand names, dosage forms, ingredients, and regional specifications. These extracted entities trigger tailored relevance rules from a comprehensive medical knowledge base, enabling fine-grained assessments that can distinguish between similar products like "Yunnan Baiyao Aerosol" and "Yunnan Baiyao Ointment" based on their specific dosage forms.

### Cross-Modal Information Matching

To combat merchant fraud through misleading product names, AR-Med incorporates multimodal verification using product images. Multimodal models extract key attributes including name, specifications, type, and usage from product images. These visual attributes are cross-matched against textual Standard Product Unit (SPU) descriptions to detect inconsistencies, standardize product descriptions, and flag fraudulent entries.

## Knowledge Distillation for Deployment

AR-Med addresses the computational challenges of LLM deployment through a sophisticated knowledge distillation scheme. Large teacher models (such as Qwen3-32B) generate diverse inferences via multi-prompt voting to produce stable, high-confidence labels. These outputs are used to train smaller, efficient student models (like Qwen3-0.6B) through supervised learning.

The distillation process uses carefully curated data from Meituan's online traffic, including both accurate matches and challenging cases involving misclassifications or hallucinations. Labels are refined through multi-expert validation to ensure high quality. This approach enables student models to achieve performance comparable to much larger models while significantly reducing inference latency and computational costs.

## LocalQSMed Benchmark

The researchers created LocalQSMed, a specialized benchmark dataset comprising 4,400 query-SPU pairs annotated by 20 professionally trained medical experts. The dataset includes both high-frequency online data and challenging "bad cases" involving ambiguous queries and merchant manipulations. Relevance is categorized as "Highly Relevant" (exact match with identical key attributes), "Less Relevant" (different brand or dosage but overlapping utility), or "Irrelevant" (completely different efficacy or target audience).

## Performance Results

AR-Med demonstrates substantial improvements across multiple evaluation metrics. On the LocalQSMed benchmark, the original online system achieved 69.28% accuracy, while AR-Med with LLM enhancement reached 92.06% accuracy using models like Qwen3-4B, representing an absolute improvement of over 24%.

![Model Performance Across Categories](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03737v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: Overall precision performance across different medical product categories, showing consistent improvements with larger model sizes*

The framework shows particularly strong performance in handling nuanced relevance judgments. Qwen3-32B achieved 68.91% recall in the challenging "Less Relevant" category, demonstrating superior discriminatory ability for ambiguous cases. On a specially constructed "HARD" subset designed to test difficult-to-classify samples, the system achieved 66.11% accuracy, indicating robust performance in real-world scenarios.

![Cross-Modal Matching Results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03737v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: Cross-modal information matching performance showing progressive improvements from baseline to multimodal fusion approaches*

Ablation studies revealed the critical contribution of each component. The "Two-Filter" mechanism combined with other modules boosted accuracy to 93.76% and improved the F1 score for irrelevant cases from 0.2192 to 0.5714. The cross-modal information matching achieved optimal performance with joint expansion using both SPU text and image information, reaching 0.7759 precision and 0.9138 recall.

## Knowledge Distillation Effectiveness

The knowledge distillation approach proved highly effective for practical deployment. The fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B student model achieved 91.19% accuracy in consistency judgment, significantly outperforming a much larger Llama3.3-70B model (71.49%). This demonstrates that domain-specific fine-tuning with compact models can surpass generic large models in specialized tasks while maintaining computational efficiency.

## Real-World Impact

AR-Med was successfully deployed on Meituan's online medical delivery platforms through A/B testing with 25% traffic allocation over 14 days. The system showed positive improvements across key business metrics including UV_CTR (Unique Visitor Click-Through Rate), UV_CVR (Unique Visitor Conversion Rate), and UV_CXR (Unique Visitor Click to Conversion Rate). For the "Medical Global" scenario, AR-Med generated +4983.0 additional orders and a +0.16% increase in UV_CXR, demonstrating measurable business impact and user engagement improvements.

## Significance and Future Directions

AR-Med represents a significant advancement in deploying trustworthy AI systems for healthcare applications. The framework successfully bridges the gap between LLM capabilities and practical deployment requirements by systematically addressing hallucinations, computational costs, and domain specificity. The integration of retrieval-augmented generation, expert knowledge, multimodal verification, and efficient distillation provides a comprehensive solution for high-stakes medical search applications.

The work offers a valuable blueprint for other sensitive domains requiring reliable AI deployment, such as legal services, financial applications, or government systems. The emphasis on expert annotation, rigorous evaluation, and continuous monitoring establishes important precedents for responsible AI implementation in critical applications where accuracy directly impacts user safety and public health.

zh.title: AR-Med：基于大型语言模型驱动信息增强的医疗搜索自动化相关性提升
zh.abstract:
在线医疗平台上的准确可靠搜索对于用户安全和服务效率至关重要。然而，传统方法往往难以理解复杂细致的用户查询，从而限制了其有效性。大语言模型（LLM）提供了一个有前景的解决方案，通过强大的语义理解能力来弥补这一差距。尽管其潜力巨大，但在这一高风险领域部署LLM面临诸多挑战，包括事实性幻觉、专业知识空白和高昂的运营成本。

为了克服这些障碍，我们引入了 \textbf{AR-Med}，这是一种用于**医用搜索自动相关性评估**的新颖框架，并已成功部署在在线医疗服务平台且实现了规模化应用。AR-Med通过检索增强方法，将LLM的推理能力建立在经过验证的医学知识之上，从而确保了高准确性和可靠性。为实现高效的在线服务，我们设计了一种实用的知识蒸馏方案，将大型教师模型压缩成紧凑而强大的学生模型。我们还引入了LocalQSMed，这是一个由多专家标注的基准数据集，旨在指导模型迭代，并确保离线和在线性能之间的高度一致性。

广泛的实验表明，AR-Med的离线准确率超过93%，比原有在线系统绝对提升24%，并显著提升了在线相关性和用户满意度。我们的工作为在真实世界医疗应用中开发值得信赖的、由LLM驱动的系统提供了一个实用且可扩展的蓝图。

summary.summary: AR-Med框架通过整合大型语言模型与检索增强生成、知识蒸馏和跨模态信息匹配，提升了在线平台上医疗搜索和推荐的准确性。它在一个专家标注的基准测试中实现了超过24%的绝对准确率提升，并在实际部署中对在线业务指标（如转化率）产生了积极影响。
originalProblem: 传统医疗搜索系统难以理解复杂查询的语义，依赖于昂贵的专家策划知识库，并且对新信息的适应性缓慢。
直接在医疗搜索中部署大型语言模型（LLMs）会导致事实性幻觉和高昂的运营成本，这在事关重大的医疗环境中是不可接受的。
在线医疗平台面临用户查询模糊和商家操纵（例如，“流量劫持”）误导性产品名称等挑战。
solution: 一个检索增强框架（RAG）通过从经过验证的医疗来源和动态专家规则中精确检索知识来支撑LLMs，同时增强查询和过滤信息。
知识蒸馏方案将大型教师LLMs的专业知识转移到紧凑、高效的学生模型中，适用于高吞吐量、低延迟的在线推理。
跨模态信息匹配利用产品图片验证属性并打击商家欺诈，确保相关性评分的输入可靠性。
开发了LocalQSMed，一个专家标注的基准数据集，用于指导迭代模型改进和评估真实世界的相关性。

知识蒸馏使得强大的LLM能力能够高效部署于实时、高吞吐量的工业应用，而不会牺牲性能。
整合多模态信息（如产品图片）对于应对商家欺诈等实际挑战和增强在线产品搜索系统的鲁棒性至关重要。
领域特定、专家标注的基准对于使离线模型评估与真实世界性能保持一致，并解决专业领域中细微、长尾问题至关重要。

zh.overview:
## 框架概览

AR-Med（通过LLM驱动的信息增强实现医疗搜索的自动化相关性提升）解决了在线医疗配送平台中的一个关键挑战：确保药品搜索结果的准确性和可靠性。该框架由美团公司及其合作者共同开发，旨在应对传统搜索方法的局限性，同时减轻在高风险医疗环境中部署大型语言模型（LLM）所带来的风险。

![AR-Med 框架架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03737v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：完整的AR-Med框架架构，展示了检索增强处理、专家规则指导、跨模态信息匹配和知识蒸馏的集成，以实现部署*

该系统在信息检索、LLM能力和实际部署需求的交叉点上运行，每天处理美团医疗配送平台上数十亿次的搜索请求。传统搜索系统难以处理模糊查询，需要昂贵的专家人工整理，并且对新产品的适应性慢。虽然LLM提供了强大的语义理解能力，但它们存在幻觉和高计算成本的问题，这使得在医疗环境中直接部署不切实际。

## 核心技术组件

### 检索增强框架

AR-Med的基础是一个复杂的检索增强生成（RAG）框架，旨在将LLM的推理建立在经过验证的医学知识之上。系统首先进行精确的知识检索，通过使用指令微调的0.6B LLM来添加类别特定关键词，从而增强用户查询。例如，一个模糊的查询如“001”会变成“001 成人产品”，以提高外部搜索的相关性。

检索到的信息会经过两阶段过滤：首先是初始相关性评分，移除低相关内容；其次是轻量级模型一致性检查。这可以防止大型LLM对不相关信息进行“过度思考”，从而减少延迟和错误。过滤后的信息随后被重构为核心要素，包括替代表达、关键词、主题、层次结构和意图判断。

### 专家规则指导

该框架通过动态规则应用融入了领域专业知识。在查询重写后，命名实体识别（NER）会提取关键的医学实体，如品牌名称、剂型、成分和区域规格。这些提取的实体会触发来自综合医学知识库的定制相关性规则，从而实现细粒度评估，能够根据特定剂型区分“云南白药气雾剂”和“云南白药膏”等相似产品。

### 跨模态信息匹配

为打击商家通过误导性产品名称进行欺诈的行为，AR-Med通过产品图片引入了多模态验证。多模态模型从产品图片中提取关键属性，包括名称、规格、类型和用法。这些视觉属性与文本标准产品单位（SPU）描述进行交叉匹配，以检测不一致性，标准化产品描述，并标记欺诈性条目。

## 知识蒸馏用于部署

AR-Med通过复杂的知识蒸馏方案解决了LLM部署的计算挑战。大型教师模型（如Qwen3-32B）通过多提示投票生成多样化的推断，以产生稳定、高置信度的标签。这些输出用于通过监督学习训练更小、更高效的学生模型（如Qwen3-0.6B）。

蒸馏过程利用了美团在线流量中精心策划的数据，包括准确匹配以及涉及错误分类或幻觉的挑战性案例。标签通过多专家验证进行完善，以确保高质量。这种方法使学生模型能够达到与大得多的模型相当的性能，同时显著降低推理延迟和计算成本。

## LocalQSMed 基准

研究人员创建了 LocalQSMed，这是一个专门的基准数据集，包含 4,400 对由 20 位经过专业培训的医学专家标注的查询-SPU 对。该数据集包括高频在线数据和涉及模糊查询及商家操纵的挑战性“坏案例”。相关性分为“高度相关”（与关键属性完全匹配）、“较不相关”（品牌或剂量不同但用途重叠）或“不相关”（功效或目标受众完全不同）。

## 性能结果

AR-Med 在多项评估指标上均显示出显著改进。在 LocalQSMed 基准上，原始在线系统准确率为 69.28%，而采用 Qwen3-4B 等模型的 AR-Med 经过 LLM 增强后达到 92.06% 的准确率，绝对提升超过 24%。

![Model Performance Across Categories](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03737v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图 2：不同医疗产品类别的总体精确度表现，显示模型尺寸越大，改进越显著*

该框架在处理细致的相关性判断方面表现尤为突出。Qwen3-32B 在具有挑战性的“较不相关”类别中取得了 68.91% 的召回率，展示了对模糊案例卓越的判别能力。在一个专门构建的、旨在测试难以分类样本的“HARD”子集上，系统取得了 66.11% 的准确率，表明在实际场景中性能稳健。

![Cross-Modal Matching Results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03737v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图 3：跨模态信息匹配性能，显示从基线到多模态融合方法的逐步改进*

消融研究揭示了每个组件的关键贡献。“两级过滤”机制与其他模块结合后，将准确率提高到 93.76%，并将不相关案例的 F1 分数从 0.2192 提高到 0.5714。跨模态信息匹配通过 SPU 文本和图像信息联合扩展实现了最佳性能，达到了 0.7759 的精确度和 0.9138 的召回率。

## 知识蒸馏有效性

知识蒸馏方法在实际部署中被证明高效。经过微调的 Qwen3-0.6B 学生模型在一致性判断中达到了 91.19% 的准确率，显著优于大得多的 Llama3.3-70B 模型（71.49%）。这表明，针对特定领域的紧凑模型微调可以在专业任务中超越通用大型模型，同时保持计算效率。

## 实际影响

AR-Med 通过 A/B 测试在美团在线医疗配送平台成功部署，14 天内分配了 25% 的流量。该系统在关键业务指标上显示出积极改进，包括 UV_CTR（独立访客点击率）、UV_CVR（独立访客转化率）和 UV_CXR（独立访客点击到转化率）。对于“医疗全局”场景，AR-Med 额外增加了 4983.0 个订单，UV_CXR 增加了 0.16%，表明可衡量的业务影响和用户参与度提升。

## 意义和未来方向

AR-Med 代表了在医疗健康应用中部署可信赖AI系统的重大进展。该框架通过系统地解决幻觉、计算成本和领域特异性，成功弥合了大型语言模型（LLM）能力与实际部署要求之间的差距。检索增强生成、专家知识、多模态验证和高效蒸馏的集成，为高风险医疗搜索应用提供了一个全面的解决方案。

这项工作为其他需要可靠AI部署的敏感领域提供了宝贵的蓝图，例如法律服务、金融应用或政府系统。对专家标注、严格评估和持续监控的强调，为在准确性直接影响用户安全和公共健康的关键应用中负责任地实施AI树立了重要先例。

abstract: Accurate and reliable search on online healthcare platforms is critical for user safety and service efficacy. Traditional methods, however, often fail to comprehend complex and nuanced user queries, limiting their effectiveness. Large language models (LLMs) present a promising solution, offering powerful semantic understanding to bridge this gap. Despite their potential, deploying LLMs in this high-stakes domain is fraught with challenges, including factual hallucinations, specialized knowledge gaps, and high operational costs. To overcome these barriers, we introduce \textbf{AR-Med}, a novel framework for \textbf{A}utomated \textbf{R}elevance assessment for \textbf{Med}ical search that has been successfully deployed at scale on the Online Medical Delivery Platforms. AR-Med grounds LLM reasoning in verified medical knowledge through a retrieval-augmented approach, ensuring high accuracy and reliability. To enable efficient online service, we design a practical knowledge distillation scheme that compresses large teacher models into compact yet powerful student models. We also introduce LocalQSMed, a multi-expert annotated benchmark developed to guide model iteration and ensure strong alignment between offline and online performance. Extensive experiments show AR-Med achieves an offline accuracy of over 93\%, a 24\% absolute improvement over the original online system, and delivers significant gains in online relevance and user satisfaction. Our work presents a practical and scalable blueprint for developing trustworthy, LLM-powered systems in real-world healthcare applications.
title: AR-Med: Automated Relevance Enhancement in Medical Search via LLM-Driven Information Augmentation

Extensive experiments show AR-Med achieves an offline accuracy of over 93\%, a 24\% absolute improvement over the original online system, and delivers significant gains in online relevance and user satisfaction. Our work presents a practical and scalable blueprint for developing trustworthy, LLM-powered systems in real-world healthcare applications.

en.title: M3DR: Towards Universal Multilingual Multimodal Document Retrieval
en.abstract: Multimodal document retrieval systems have shown strong progress in aligning visual and textual content for semantic search. However, most existing approaches remain heavily English-centric, limiting their effectiveness in multilingual contexts. In this work, we present M3DR (Multilingual Multimodal Document Retrieval), a framework designed to bridge this gap across languages, enabling applicability across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts. M3DR leverages synthetic multilingual document data and generalizes across different vision-language architectures and model sizes, enabling robust cross-lingual and cross-modal alignment. Using contrastive training, our models learn unified representations for text and document images that transfer effectively across languages. We validate this capability on 22 typologically diverse languages, demonstrating consistent performance and adaptability across linguistic and script variations. We further introduce a comprehensive benchmark that captures real-world multilingual scenarios, evaluating models under monolingual, multilingual, and mixed-language settings. M3DR generalizes across both single dense vector and ColBERT-style token-level multi-vector retrieval paradigms. Our models, NetraEmbed and ColNetraEmbed achieve state-of-the-art performance with ~150% relative improvements on cross-lingual retrieval.

summary.summary: M3DR, developed by CognitiveLab, presents a framework for universal multilingual multimodal document retrieval across 22 diverse languages, achieving a 152% relative improvement in cross-lingual retrieval (NDCG@5) over baselines and maintaining strong English performance through synthetic data generation and efficient VLM-based models.
originalProblem: Traditional document retrieval methods are OCR-dependent, losing visual information and performing poorly with diverse scripts, particularly in low-resource languages.
Existing state-of-the-art vision-based document retrieval systems are heavily English-centric, limiting their applicability and fairness in a globally multilingual context.

A fundamental question remained regarding the feasibility of developing universal document retrievers that perform highly across typologically diverse languages without sacrificing English competitiveness.
solution: A scalable pipeline was developed for synthetic multilingual multimodal document data generation, building on the 'Nayana framework' to create a corpus of 1 million document images across 22 languages.
The Nayana-IR benchmark was introduced as the first comprehensive evaluation standard for multilingual multimodal document retrieval, covering 23 datasets and diverse script families.

Two retrieval models were implemented: NetraEmbed (single dense vector) and ColNetraEmbed (ColBERT-style multi-vector), both utilizing Gemma 3 4B-it as the VLM backbone and incorporating Matryoshka representation learning for flexible embedding dimensions.
keyInsights: A simpler 'Positive-Only' training strategy with in-batch negatives significantly outperformed complex hard negative mining in the multilingual multimodal setting due to sufficient batch diversity.
Last token pooling proved dramatically superior to mean pooling for decoder-based Vision-Language Models like Gemma 3, becoming the default pooling strategy.

Matryoshka representation learning successfully enables post-deployment accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, reducing storage requirements by 70% for 768-dimensional embeddings with only a 5% performance drop.
results: NetraEmbed achieved state-of-the-art performance, with a 152% relative improvement in cross-lingual retrieval (0.716 NDCG@5) and an 80% improvement in monolingual tasks (0.738 NDCG@5) over the ColPali-v1.3 baseline.
The system demonstrated consistent high performance across all 22 typologically diverse languages and script families while maintaining competitive English-only retrieval performance (0.554 NDCG@5).

Single dense vector models (NetraEmbed) consistently outperformed ColBERT-style multi-vector models (ColNetraEmbed) in multilingual tasks (e.g., +12.4% NDCG@5 cross-lingual) and offered substantial efficiency benefits, including 250x less storage and faster retrieval speed.

en.overview:
## Introduction

M3DR (Multilingual Multimodal Document Retrieval) addresses a critical limitation in the field of document retrieval: the English-centricity of existing vision-based systems. While recent advances like ColPali have shown promising results by directly encoding document images with vision-language models (VLMs) to bypass OCR errors, these approaches fail dramatically when applied to non-English content. M3DR introduces the first comprehensive framework for universal multilingual multimodal document retrieval, spanning 22 typologically diverse languages across multiple script families.

![M3DR System Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: M3DR system overview showing the offline indexing pipeline and online cross-lingual retrieval. The framework enables querying in any supported language to retrieve semantically relevant documents across all 22 languages in the corpus.*

## Methodology and Architecture

M3DR's approach centers on three core components: scalable synthetic data generation, comprehensive multilingual evaluation, and flexible model architectures supporting both single dense vector and multi-vector retrieval paradigms.

### Synthetic Data Generation Pipeline

The cornerstone of M3DR is its synthetic multilingual parallel corpus generation, building upon the Nayana framework. The pipeline begins with 50,000 diverse English document images, which undergo layout-aware translation using neural machine translation models (NLLB-200 and language-specific models). The process preserves document semantics while maintaining authentic visual appearance through proper typography and layout rules specific to each target language.

![M3DR End-to-End Pipeline](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: Complete M3DR pipeline from synthetic data generation through model architecture to multilingual retrieval, showing the three-stage process of data synthesis, vision-language model training, and cross-lingual document retrieval.*

Query synthesis utilizes state-of-the-art large vision-language models (Llama 3.1 90B Vision, Llama 4 Scout) to generate five distinct query types per document, resulting in approximately 1 million document images with corresponding queries across 22 languages. This comprehensive synthetic approach overcomes the critical data scarcity challenge in multilingual multimodal research.

### Model Architectures

M3DR explores two distinct retrieval paradigms:

**NetraEmbed (Single Dense Vector Model)**: Uses Gemma 3 4B-it as the backbone VLM, processing queries and document images to generate fixed-size dense vectors (2560 dimensions) through last token pooling. The model incorporates Matryoshka Representation Learning, enabling flexible embedding dimensions (768, 1536, 2560) from a single trained model without retraining.

**ColNetraEmbed (ColBERT-Style Multi-Vector Model)**: Retains per-token embeddings (256 visual tokens for documents, variable for queries) to enable fine-grained matching through late interaction via MaxSim, similar to ColPali's approach.

The mathematical formulation for similarity computation in the single dense vector model is:

$$
\text{similarity}(q, d) = \cos(\mathbf{e}_q, \mathbf{e}_d) = \frac{\mathbf{e}_q \cdot \mathbf{e}_d}{||\mathbf{e}_q|| \cdot ||\mathbf{e}_d||}
$$

where $\mathbf{e}_q$ and $\mathbf{e}_d$ are L2-normalized embeddings for query and document respectively.

### Training Strategies and Objectives

The training employs three distinct strategies for dense vector models: positive-only (using in-batch negatives), document-level negatives, and mined hard negatives. Surprisingly, the simplest positive-only strategy with InfoNCE loss substantially outperformed complex hard negative mining approaches in multilingual settings, attributed to sufficient contrastive signal from multilingual batch diversity.

## Experimental Results and Performance

M3DR demonstrates significant advances in multilingual document retrieval performance across both architectural paradigms and diverse linguistic contexts.

### Overall Performance Achievements

NetraEmbed achieved state-of-the-art performance with 0.716 NDCG@5 on cross-lingual retrieval and 0.738 on monolingual tasks, representing a 152% relative improvement over ColPali-v1.3 baseline (0.284 NDCG@5) for cross-lingual tasks. ColNetraEmbed also showed strong performance with 0.637 NDCG@5 cross-lingual and 0.670 monolingual, confirming the framework's generalization across retrieval paradigms.

![Cross-Lingual Performance Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: Comprehensive performance comparison across 22 languages showing NetraEmbed's consistent superiority over existing models. The top panel shows monolingual performance while the bottom panel demonstrates cross-lingual retrieval capabilities.*

### Language-Specific Analysis

M3DR exhibited consistent high performance across all 22 typologically diverse languages spanning Latin, Devanagari, CJK, Arabic, and other script families. This demonstrates robust cross-lingual transfer capabilities without the typical performance degradation seen in existing English-centric models.

![English vs Cross-Lingual Performance](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-3.jpeg)
*Figure 4: Comparative analysis of English (ViDoRe v2) versus cross-lingual performance, showing that M3DR maintains competitive English performance while dramatically improving multilingual capabilities.*

### Efficiency Through Matryoshka Embeddings

The integration of Matryoshka Representation Learning provides crucial flexibility for deployment scenarios with varying computational constraints. The 768-dimensional truncation retains 95.0% of full model performance (0.680 vs. 0.716 NDCG@5) while reducing storage requirements by 70%. The 1536-dimensional representation achieves 98.6% of full performance with 40% storage reduction.

![Matryoshka Performance Trade-offs](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-8.jpeg)
*Figure 5: Matryoshka embedding performance across different dimensions, demonstrating effective accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for various deployment constraints.*

### Architectural Comparison: Dense vs Multi-Vector

The comparison between single dense vector and ColBERT-style multi-vector approaches reveals distinct trade-offs:

**Performance**: NetraEmbed consistently outperformed ColNetraEmbed on multilingual tasks (+12.4% NDCG@5 on cross-lingual), with both achieving similar English performance.

**Efficiency**: Single dense vectors offer substantial computational advantages with ~10 KB per document storage versus ~2.5 MB for multi-vector (250x reduction) and significantly faster retrieval through simpler cosine similarity computation.

**Interpretability**: Multi-vector models provide superior interpretability through token-level attention visualization, validated across languages for ColNetraEmbed.

## Training Insights and Ablation Studies

Critical design insights emerged from comprehensive ablation studies:

![Training Strategy Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-4.jpeg)
*Figure 6: Training progression analysis showing that simple positive-only training with in-batch negatives outperforms complex hard negative mining strategies for multilingual document retrieval.*

**Loss Function Analysis**: BiEncoderLoss (InfoNCE) with in-batch negatives proved most effective, with hybrid approaches showing marginal benefits that don't justify increased complexity.

![Pooling Strategy Comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-6.jpeg)
*Figure 7: Pooling strategy ablation demonstrating the substantial superiority of last token pooling over mean pooling for decoder-based VLMs like Gemma 3.*

**Pooling Strategy Impact**: Last token pooling dramatically outperformed mean pooling for decoder-based VLMs (49.3% vs 35.9% NDCG@5), becoming the default choice.

**Model Scaling Effects**: Performance consistently improved when scaling from 6 to 22 languages, with cross-lingual capabilities showing particularly strong gains (+11.1% NDCG@5).

## Significance and Impact

M3DR represents a fundamental advancement in making document retrieval technologies universally accessible. The framework addresses the critical gap between English-centric AI capabilities and global information needs, demonstrating that inclusive AI systems need not compromise on performance quality.

### Key Contributions

The work makes several crucial contributions: solving English-centricity in vision-based document retrieval, providing a scalable synthetic data generation framework, establishing comprehensive multilingual benchmarks, and releasing production-ready models with flexible deployment options.

### Broader Implications

The societal impact extends to democratizing information access across linguistic communities, enhancing global knowledge management capabilities, and providing tools for cultural heritage preservation. The framework sets new standards for inclusive AI development, demonstrating that multilingual optimization enhances rather than compromises overall system performance.

### Future Directions

While M3DR marks significant progress, future work should address performance optimization for rare language pairs, enhanced handling of complex tabular content with language-specific formatting, extension to passage-level retrieval granularity, and scaling to ultra-low-resource languages with zero-shot transfer capabilities.

The comprehensive evaluation framework, public model releases, and detailed ablation studies provide a strong foundation for continued research in universal document intelligence systems.

zh.title: M3DR: 迈向通用多语言多模态文档检索
zh.abstract:
多模态文档检索系统在对齐视觉和文本内容以进行语义搜索方面取得了显著进展。然而，大多数现有方法仍高度以英语为中心，限制了它们在多语言环境下的有效性。在本文中，我们提出了M3DR（多语言多模态文档检索），这是一个旨在弥合跨语言鸿沟的框架，使其适用于多样化的语言和文化背景。M3DR利用合成多语言文档数据，并可泛化到不同的视觉-语言架构和模型大小，从而实现鲁棒的跨语言和跨模态对齐。

通过对比训练，我们的模型学习了文本和文档图像的统一表示，这些表示可以在不同语言之间有效迁移。我们在22种类型多样的语言上验证了这一能力，展示了跨越语言和文字系统的一致性能和适应性。我们进一步引入了一个全面的基准，捕捉真实世界的多语言场景，并在单语言、多语言和混合语言设置下评估模型。M3DR可泛化到单一稠密向量和ColBERT风格的词元级多向量检索范式。我们的模型NetraEmbed和ColNetraEmbed在跨语言检索方面实现了最先进的性能，取得了约150%的相对改进。

summary.summary: 由CognitiveLab开发的M3DR提出了一种针对22种不同语言的通用多语言多模态文档检索框架，通过合成数据生成和高效的基于VLM的模型，实现了跨语言检索（NDCG@5）相对于基线152%的相对提升，并保持了强大的英语性能。
originalProblem: 传统的文档检索方法依赖于OCR，会丢失视觉信息，并且在处理多样化脚本时表现不佳，特别是在资源匮乏的语言中。
现有最先进的基于视觉的文档检索系统高度以英语为中心，限制了其在全球多语言环境中的适用性和公平性。
一个基本问题仍然存在：开发能够跨越类型学上多样化的语言实现高性能，同时又不牺牲英语竞争力的通用文档检索器是否可行。
solution: 开发了一个可扩展的管道，用于合成多语言多模态文档数据生成，基于“Nayana框架”创建了一个包含22种语言的100万张文档图像语料库。
引入了Nayana-IR基准，作为第一个用于多语言多模态文档检索的综合评估标准，涵盖23个数据集和多样的脚本家族。
实现了两种检索模型：NetraEmbed（单密集向量）和ColNetraEmbed（ColBERT风格多向量），两者都使用Gemma 3 4B-it作为VLM骨干，并结合Matryoshka表示学习以实现灵活的嵌入维度。
keyInsights: 在多语言多模态环境中，由于批次多样性充足，更简单的“仅正例”训练策略（带批内负例）显著优于复杂的困难负例挖掘。
对于Gemma 3等基于解码器的视觉-语言模型，最后标记池化（Last token pooling）被证明比平均池化（mean pooling）优越得多，成为默认的池化策略。
Matryoshka表示学习成功实现了部署后的准确性-效率权衡，对于768维嵌入，存储需求减少了70%，而性能仅下降5%。
results: NetraEmbed实现了最先进的性能，在跨语言检索（0.716 NDCG@5）方面相对ColPali-v1.3基线提升了152%，在单语言任务（0.738 NDCG@5）方面提升了80%。
该系统在所有22种类型学上多样化的语言和脚本家族中表现出持续的高性能，同时保持了具有竞争力的纯英语检索性能（0.554 NDCG@5）。
单密集向量模型（NetraEmbed）在多语言任务中始终优于ColBERT风格的多向量模型（ColNetraEmbed）（例如，跨语言NDCG@5提升12.4%），并提供了显著的效率优势，包括减少250倍的存储空间和更快的检索速度。

zh.overview:
## 简介

M3DR（多语言多模态文档检索）解决了文档检索领域的一个关键限制：现有基于视觉的系统以英语为中心的问题。虽然ColPali等最新进展通过使用视觉-语言模型（VLMs）直接编码文档图像以绕过OCR错误，取得了可喜的成果，但这些方法在应用于非英语内容时却表现不佳。M3DR引入了首个全面的通用多语言多模态文档检索框架，涵盖了22种跨多个文字家族的类型学多样性语言。

![M3DR 系统概述](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：M3DR系统概述，展示了离线索引管道和在线跨语言检索。该框架支持使用任何支持的语言进行查询，以在语料库中的所有22种语言中检索语义相关的文档。*

## 方法论与架构

M3DR 的方法围绕三个核心组件：可扩展的合成数据生成、全面的多语言评估以及支持单稠密向量和多向量检索范式的灵活模型架构。

### 合成数据生成管道

M3DR 的基石是其合成多语言并行语料库的生成，该生成基于 Nayana 框架。该管道首先使用50,000个多样化的英文文档图像，然后通过神经机器翻译模型（NLLB-200和特定语言模型）进行布局感知翻译。此过程在保留文档语义的同时，通过特定于每种目标语言的正确排版和布局规则，保持了真实的视觉外观。

![M3DR 端到端管道](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：完整的M3DR管道，从合成数据生成到模型架构再到多语言检索，展示了数据合成、视觉-语言模型训练和跨语言文档检索的三个阶段过程。*

查询合成利用最先进的大型视觉-语言模型（Llama 3.1 90B Vision, Llama 4 Scout）为每个文档生成五种不同类型的查询，最终在22种语言中产生大约100万个带有相应查询的文档图像。这种全面的合成方法克服了多语言多模态研究中关键的数据稀缺挑战。

### 模型架构

M3DR 探索了两种不同的检索范式：

**NetraEmbed（单稠密向量模型）**：使用 Gemma 3 4B-it 作为骨干 VLM，处理查询和文档图像，通过末尾 token 池化生成固定大小的稠密向量（2560 维度）。该模型整合了套娃表示学习（Matryoshka Representation Learning），使得单个训练模型无需重新训练即可支持灵活的嵌入维度（768、1536、2560）。

**ColNetraEmbed（ColBERT 风格的多向量模型）**：保留每个 token 的嵌入（文档为256个视觉 token，查询可变），通过 MaxSim 进行后期交互，实现细粒度匹配，类似于 ColPali 的方法。

单稠密向量模型的相似度计算公式为：

$$
\text{similarity}(q, d) = \cos(\mathbf{e}_q, \mathbf{e}_d) = \frac{\mathbf{e}_q \cdot \mathbf{e}_d}{||\mathbf{e}_q|| \cdot ||\mathbf{e}_d||}
$$

其中 $\mathbf{e}_q$ 和 $\mathbf{e}_d$ 分别是查询和文档的 L2 范数归一化嵌入。

### 训练策略和目标

训练采用了三种针对稠密向量模型的不同策略：仅正样本（使用批内负样本）、文档级负样本和挖掘的难负样本。令人惊讶的是，在多语言环境中，最简单的仅正样本策略结合 InfoNCE 损失，其性能显著优于复杂的难负样本挖掘方法，这归因于多语言批次多样性提供了足够的对比信号。

## 实验结果和性能

M3DR 在架构范式和多样化的语言环境中，展示了多语言文档检索性能的显著进步。

### 整体性能表现

NetraEmbed 在跨语言检索任务上取得了 0.716 NDCG@5 的最新技术水平性能，在单语言任务上取得了 0.738 的性能，相较于 ColPali-v1.3 基线（0.284 NDCG@5），跨语言任务的相对改进达到了 152%。ColNetraEmbed 也展现了强劲的性能，跨语言 NDCG@5 达到 0.637，单语言达到 0.670，证实了该框架在不同检索范式下的泛化能力。

![跨语言性能比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图3：跨22种语言的综合性能比较，显示NetraEmbed持续优于现有模型。上方面板显示单语言性能，而下方显示跨语言检索能力。*

### 特定语言分析

M3DR 在所有22种具有不同语型的语言（涵盖拉丁语系、天城语系、中日韩语系、阿拉伯语系和其他文字家族）中均表现出持续的高性能。这表明其具有强大的跨语言迁移能力，没有现有以英语为中心的模型中常见的性能下降。

![英语与跨语言性能比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-3.jpeg)
*图4：英语（ViDoRe v2）与跨语言性能的比较分析，显示M3DR在保持有竞争力的英语性能的同时，显著提高了多语言能力。*

### 通过套娃式嵌入提高效率

套娃式表征学习的集成，为具有不同计算约束的部署场景提供了关键的灵活性。768维的截断保留了全模型性能的95.0%（0.680 vs. 0.716 NDCG@5），同时减少了70%的存储需求。1536维的表征实现了全模型性能的98.6%，存储减少了40%。

![套娃式性能权衡](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-8.jpeg)
*图5：不同维度下的套娃式嵌入性能，展示了针对各种部署约束的有效精度-效率权衡。*

### 架构比较：密集型 vs 多向量

单密集向量和ColBERT风格多向量方法的比较揭示了明显的权衡：

**性能**：NetraEmbed 在多语言任务上持续优于 ColNetraEmbed（跨语言 NDCG@5 提高 12.4%），两者在英语性能上表现相似。

**效率**：单密集向量在计算上具有显著优势，每文档存储约10 KB，而多向量约为2.5 MB（减少250倍），并且通过更简单的余弦相似度计算实现显著更快的检索。

**可解释性**：多向量模型通过令牌级注意力可视化提供了卓越的可解释性，这一点在 ColNetraEmbed 的跨语言分析中得到了验证。

## 训练洞察与消融研究

全面的消融研究产生了关键的设计洞察：

![训练策略比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-4.jpeg)
*图6：训练进程分析显示，使用批内负样本的简单正样本训练在多语言文档检索方面优于复杂的硬负样本挖掘策略。*

**损失函数分析**：BiEncoderLoss（InfoNCE）结合批内负样本被证明是最有效的，混合方法只带来了微小的益处，不足以证明其增加的复杂性。

![池化策略比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03514v1/img-6.jpeg)
*图7：池化策略消融实验，展示了对于Gemma 3等基于解码器的VLM而言，末尾标记池化显著优于均值池化。*

**池化策略影响**：对于基于解码器的VLM，末尾token池化显著优于均值池化（NDCG@5分别为49.3% vs 35.9%），并成为默认选择。

**模型扩展效应**：当从6种语言扩展到22种语言时，性能持续提升，其中跨语言能力表现出特别显著的增益（NDCG@5提升11.1%）。

## 意义和影响

M3DR 代表着使文档检索技术普遍可访问的根本性进步。该框架解决了以英语为中心的AI能力与全球信息需求之间的关键差距，证明了包容性AI系统无需牺牲性能质量。

### 主要贡献

这项工作做出了几项关键贡献：解决了基于视觉的文档检索中的英语中心化问题，提供了一个可扩展的合成数据生成框架，建立了全面的多语言基准，并发布了具有灵活部署选项的生产就绪模型。

### 更广泛的影响

其社会影响延伸到民主化跨语言社区的信息获取，增强全球知识管理能力，并提供文化遗产保护工具。该框架为包容性AI开发设定了新标准，表明多语言优化能够增强而非损害整体系统性能。

### 未来方向

尽管M3DR取得了显著进展，但未来的工作应着重于优化稀有语言对的性能，增强对具有特定语言格式的复杂表格内容的处理，扩展到段落级别的检索粒度，以及通过零样本迁移能力扩展到超低资源语言。

全面的评估框架、公开的模型发布以及详细的消融研究为通用文档智能系统的持续研究奠定了坚实基础。

abstract: Multimodal document retrieval systems have shown strong progress in aligning visual and textual content for semantic search. However, most existing approaches remain heavily English-centric, limiting their effectiveness in multilingual contexts. In this work, we present M3DR (Multilingual Multimodal Document Retrieval), a framework designed to bridge this gap across languages, enabling applicability across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts. M3DR leverages synthetic multilingual document data and generalizes across different vision-language architectures and model sizes, enabling robust cross-lingual and cross-modal alignment. Using contrastive training, our models learn unified representations for text and document images that transfer effectively across languages. We validate this capability on 22 typologically diverse languages, demonstrating consistent performance and adaptability across linguistic and script variations. We further introduce a comprehensive benchmark that captures real-world multilingual scenarios, evaluating models under monolingual, multilingual, and mixed-language settings. M3DR generalizes across both single dense vector and ColBERT-style token-level multi-vector retrieval paradigms. Our models, NetraEmbed and ColNetraEmbed achieve state-of-the-art performance with ~150% relative improvements on cross-lingual retrieval.
title: M3DR: Towards Universal Multilingual Multimodal Document Retrieval

abstract: In this study, we more rigorously evaluated our attack script $\textit{TraceTarnish}$, which leverages adversarial stylometry principles to anonymize the authorship of text-based messages. To ensure the efficacy and utility of our attack, we sourced, processed, and analyzed Reddit comments--comments that were later alchemized into $\textit{TraceTarnish}$ data--to gain valuable insights. The transformed $\textit{TraceTarnish}$ data was then further augmented by $\textit{StyloMetrix}$ to manufacture stylometric features--features that were culled using the Information Gain criterion, leaving only the most informative, predictive, and discriminative ones. Our results found that function words and function word types ($L\_FUNC\_A$ $\&$ $L\_FUNC\_T$); content words and content word types ($L\_CONT\_A$ $\&$ $L\_CONT\_T$); and the Type-Token Ratio ($ST\_TYPE\_TOKEN\_RATIO\_LEMMAS$) yielded significant Information-Gain readings. The identified stylometric cues--function-word frequencies, content-word distributions, and the Type-Token Ratio--serve as reliable indicators of compromise (IoCs), revealing when a text has been deliberately altered to mask its true author. Similarly, these features could function as forensic beacons, alerting defenders to the presence of an adversarial stylometry attack; granted, in the absence of the original message, this signal may go largely unnoticed, as it appears to depend on a pre- and post-transformation comparison. "In trying to erase a trace, you often imprint a larger one." Armed with this understanding, we framed $\textit{TraceTarnish}$'s operations and outputs around these five isolated features, using them to conceptualize and implement enhancements that further strengthen the attack.
