en.title: LLM as Explainable Re-Ranker for Recommendation System
en.abstract: The application of large language models (LLMs) in recommendation systems has recently gained traction. Traditional recommendation systems often lack explainability and suffer from issues such as popularity bias. Previous research has also indicated that LLMs, when used as standalone predictors, fail to achieve accuracy comparable to traditional models. To address these challenges, we propose to use LLM as an explainable re-ranker, a hybrid approach that combines traditional recommendation models with LLMs to enhance both accuracy and interpretability. We constructed a dataset to train the re-ranker LLM and evaluated the alignment between the generated dataset and human expectations. Leveraging a two-stage training process, our model significantly improved NDCG, a key ranking metric. Moreover, the re-ranker outperformed a zero-shot baseline in ranking accuracy and interpretability. These results highlight the potential of integrating traditional recommendation models with LLMs to address limitations in existing systems and pave the way for more explainable and fair recommendation frameworks.

summary.summary: Researchers from Carnegie Mellon University developed a hybrid framework utilizing a Large Language Model (LLM) as an explainable re-ranker for recommendation systems. This approach refines initial candidate lists from traditional models, improving ranking accuracy while generating explanations rated at an average of 4.3 for persuasiveness, significantly outperforming zero-shot explanations (3.6 average).
originalProblem: Traditional recommendation systems often lack explainability, operating as "black boxes" which can erode user trust.
Pervasive biases, including popularity bias and position bias, lead to suboptimal and potentially unfair recommendations.
Large Language Models (LLMs) as standalone recommenders frequently struggle with accuracy, order-sensitive tasks, and inherent positional biases.
solution: A hybrid framework employs a fine-tuned LLM (Mistral-7b-Instruct) as an explainable re-ranker to refine initial candidate lists provided by traditional recommendation models.

A two-stage training pipeline incorporates Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with Noisy Layer Fine-Tuning (NEF), followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) combined with Reward-Preference Optimization (RPO) on a GPT-generated dataset.
During inference, candidate list shuffling, bootstrapping, and a self-consistency module are implemented to mitigate popularity and positional biases in the re-ranking process.
keyInsights: LLMs are particularly effective when integrated as re-rankers to refine existing recommendations, rather than serving as standalone primary recommendation generators.
A specialized two-stage training process (SFT with NEF and DPO with RPO) is crucial for enabling LLMs to generate high-quality, persuasive, and context-rich explanations for rankings.
Bias mitigation strategies like candidate shuffling, bootstrapping, and a self-consistency module are essential to counteract inherent LLM biases and produce fair, robust re-rankings.
results: The LLM-generated training dataset was validated to be of comparable quality to human-created data, with a t-test revealing no significant difference (p-value = 0.22).

The SFT-DPO re-ranker significantly improved ranking performance for weak (e.g., NDCG@3 p=0.001) and moderately strong (e.g., Recall@5 p=0.047) base models, though gains diminished for already strong base systems like RippleNet.

Human evaluation confirmed that SFT-DPO generated explanations were significantly more persuasive (average score of 4.3) compared to zero-shot explanations (average score of 3.6), with a p-value < 0.01.

en.overview:
## Understanding the Problem

Recommendation systems power many of the platforms we interact with daily, from Netflix suggesting movies to Amazon recommending products. However, these systems face significant challenges that limit their effectiveness and user acceptance. Traditional recommendation models often operate as "black boxes," providing suggestions without explaining why certain items were recommended. This lack of transparency creates trust issues for users who want to understand the reasoning behind recommendations.

Additionally, these systems suffer from various biases. Popularity bias leads to over-recommendation of widely popular items while neglecting niche content that might better match individual preferences. Position bias causes users to favor items appearing earlier in recommendation lists, regardless of their actual relevance. These limitations have motivated researchers to explore how Large Language Models (LLMs) might address these challenges through their natural language understanding and generation capabilities.

![Dataset Construction Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03439v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: The two-step dataset construction process. Step 1 generates natural language descriptions for movies using LLMs. Step 2 creates positive and negative ranking samples with explanations, where positive samples use correct rankings and negative samples use randomly shuffled rankings.*

## The Hybrid Framework Approach

This research proposes using LLMs as explainable re-rankers rather than standalone recommendation generators. The framework operates on the principle that traditional recommendation models excel at initial candidate generation and filtering, while LLMs provide superior semantic understanding and explanation capabilities. Instead of replacing existing systems entirely, the LLM refines and explains the rankings of candidate items generated by conventional methods.

The approach addresses a key limitation identified in previous research: LLMs struggle with accuracy when used directly for recommendation tasks, particularly in handling sequential preferences and positional biases inherent in their architecture. By positioning the LLM as a re-ranking component, the framework leverages the strengths of both traditional collaborative filtering methods and modern language models.

## Training Pipeline and Methodology

![Training Pipeline](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03439v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: The two-stage training pipeline. Stage 1 uses Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to teach basic ranking skills. Stage 2 applies Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) with Reward-Preference Optimization (RPO) loss to refine preferences between chosen and rejected samples.*

The methodology centers on a sophisticated two-stage training process designed to teach the LLM both ranking capabilities and explanation generation. The training pipeline uses Mistral-7b-Instruct as the base model and employs several advanced techniques:

**Stage 1: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)** focuses on teaching fundamental ranking skills through structured prompts and labeled datasets. The researchers implement Noisy Layer Fine-Tuning (NEF), which introduces controlled noise during training to enhance robustness and prevent overfitting across diverse user profiles and item categories.

**Stage 2: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)** refines the model's ability to distinguish between good and bad rankings. The training uses both DPO loss and Reward-Preference Optimization (RPO) loss. The combined loss function can be expressed as:

$$
L = L_{NLL}(x_i, c_{w_i}, y_{w_i}) + \alpha L_{DPO}(c_{w_i}, y_{w_i}, c_{l_i}, y_{l_i} | x_i)
$$

where $L_{NLL}$ represents the negative log-likelihood loss from SFT, and $L_{DPO}$ represents the preference optimization loss that maximizes the margin between chosen and rejected samples.

The dataset construction process involves generating both movie descriptions and ranking samples using GPT-4-o-mini. Positive samples use correct rankings based on user interaction history, while negative samples employ randomly shuffled rankings. This approach teaches the model to differentiate between appropriate and inappropriate ranking orders while generating user-aligned explanations.

## Bias Mitigation and Inference Strategy

![Inference Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03439v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: The complete inference pipeline showing how user-item interaction graphs feed into recommendation models to generate candidates, which are then re-ranked by the trained LLM using bootstrapping and self-consistency mechanisms.*

During inference, the framework implements several sophisticated bias mitigation strategies. The system addresses positional bias through bootstrapping, where multiple candidate lists with different randomized orders are generated and processed. A self-consistency module then aggregates these results by calculating position indices for each item across all ranked outputs and selecting the ranking with the lowest cumulative position scores.

To combat popularity bias, the initial candidate list undergoes shuffling before being processed by the LLM. This ensures that popular items don't consistently appear in advantageous positions that might influence the model's ranking decisions.

The inference process takes as input a user's historical interactions (sampled to 10 entries) and a list of 15 candidate items generated by traditional recommendation methods. The framework was tested with three different base recommendation approaches: random sampling, collaborative filtering using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and knowledge graph-based recommendations using RippleNet.

## Experimental Results and Performance Analysis

The evaluation focused on two primary dimensions: ranking accuracy and explainability quality. For ranking performance, the researchers compared their SFT-DPO trained model against baseline approaches using standard recommendation metrics including Hit Ratio, Recall, Precision, and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) at various top-N cutoffs.

**Performance with Different Base Models:**

When working with randomly retrieved candidates (representing weak base models), the LLM re-ranker demonstrated substantial improvements across all metrics. For instance, NDCG@3 showed statistically significant gains with p-values consistently below 0.05 (p=0.001 for NDCG@3, p=0.002 for NDCG@5, p=0.008 for NDCG@10). This indicates the re-ranker's strong capability to enhance performance when initial candidate quality is poor.

With moderately strong base models using collaborative filtering, the improvements remained positive but less dramatic. Metrics like Recall@5, Precision@5, and NDCG@10 showed significant improvements (p=0.047 for Recall@5, p=0.001 for NDCG@10), suggesting the framework provides consistent benefits across different base model strengths.

Interestingly, when applied to strong base models like RippleNet (knowledge graph-based), performance gains were marginal and often not statistically significant (p-values between 0.1-0.2). The authors identified this as a "performance degeneration" phenomenon, where the LLM's current architecture cannot fully leverage the rich structural information already processed by sophisticated graph-based models.

**Explainability Assessment:**

Human evaluation involving five participants reviewing 20 samples revealed that the SFT-DPO model achieved an average explanation quality score of 4.3 on a 5-point scale, significantly outperforming the zero-shot baseline's 3.6 score. A paired t-test confirmed statistical significance (p < 0.01). The trained model provided more comprehensive explanations by integrating movie overviews with user history summaries, while zero-shot approaches relied primarily on simplistic genre matching.

## Significance and Future Directions

This research makes several important contributions to the field of recommendation systems. The hybrid integration approach demonstrates that LLMs are most effective when deployed as refinement tools rather than primary recommendation engines. The work provides a practical blueprint for integrating advanced language models into existing recommendation infrastructures without complete system overhauls.

The bias mitigation strategies, particularly the self-consistency mechanism and bootstrapping approach, offer reusable techniques for addressing positional and popularity biases in LLM-based systems. The enhanced explainability capabilities address a critical need for transparency in recommendation systems, potentially increasing user trust and engagement.

However, the research also reveals important limitations that point toward future research directions. The inability to fully leverage structured graph information for strong base models suggests a need for better integration between LLMs and graph-based representations. The authors suggest incorporating graph encoders and mapping layers to feed structured data as prefix tokens to LLMs as a potential solution.

The framework's effectiveness appears inversely related to the strength of the base recommendation model, indicating that future work should focus on developing more sophisticated integration mechanisms that can enhance even the strongest existing systems. Additionally, expanding beyond movie recommendations to other domains and developing more robust evaluation methodologies for explainability remain important areas for investigation.

This work represents a significant step toward more transparent, fair, and user-centric recommendation systems, particularly valuable for platforms seeking to enhance user trust while maintaining recommendation quality.

zh.title: 大语言模型作为推荐系统的可解释重排器
zh.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在推荐系统中的应用近来备受关注。传统的推荐系统常常缺乏可解释性，并存在诸如流行度偏差等问题。此前的研究也表明，LLM作为独立预测器时，无法达到与传统模型相当的准确性。为应对这些挑战，我们提出使用LLM作为可解释的重排序器，这是一种将传统推荐模型与LLM相结合的混合方法，旨在同时提高准确性和可解释性。我们构建了一个数据集用于训练重排序器LLM，并评估了所生成数据集与人类期望之间的一致性。采用两阶段训练过程，我们的模型显著提升了NDCG这一关键排序指标。此外，该重排序器在排序准确性和可解释性方面均超越了零样本基线。这些结果突出了将传统推荐模型与LLM相结合的潜力，有助于解决现有系统中的局限性，并为更具可解释性和公平性的推荐框架铺平道路。

summary.summary: 卡内基梅隆大学的研究人员开发了一种混合框架，利用大型语言模型（LLM）作为推荐系统的可解释重排序器。这种方法优化了传统模型生成的初始候选列表，提高了排序准确性，同时生成了平均说服力评分为4.3的解释，显著优于零样本解释（平均3.6分）。
originalProblem: 传统推荐系统通常缺乏可解释性，以“黑箱”形式运作，这可能会侵蚀用户信任。
普遍存在的偏见，包括流行度偏见和位置偏见，导致次优且可能不公平的推荐。
大型语言模型（LLM）作为独立推荐器，经常在准确性、顺序敏感任务和固有位置偏见方面表现不佳。
solution: 一个混合框架采用了一个经过微调的LLM（Mistral-7b-Instruct）作为可解释的重排序器，以优化传统推荐模型提供的初始候选列表。
一个两阶段训练流程包含带有噪声层微调（NEF）的监督微调（SFT），随后是结合奖励偏好优化（RPO）的直接偏好优化（DPO），并在GPT生成的数据集上进行。
在推理过程中，实施了候选列表洗牌、自举和自洽性模块，以减轻重排序过程中的流行度和位置偏见。
keyInsights: LLM作为重排序器，在优化现有推荐方面特别有效，而不是作为独立的初级推荐生成器。
一个专门的两阶段训练过程（SFT与NEF结合，以及DPO与RPO结合）对于使LLM能够生成高质量、有说服力且上下文丰富的排名解释至关重要。
偏见缓解策略，如候选洗牌、自举和自洽性模块，对于抵消LLM固有的偏见并产生公平、稳健的重排序至关重要。
results: LLM生成的训练数据集被验证与人类创建的数据质量相当，t检验显示无显著差异（p值=0.22）。
SFT-DPO重排序器显著改善了弱（例如，NDCG@3 p=0.001）和中等强度（例如，Recall@5 p=0.047）基础模型的排名性能，尽管对于RippleNet等已经很强的基础系统，增益有所减小。
人工评估证实，与零样本解释（平均3.6分）相比，SFT-DPO生成的解释更具说服力（平均4.3分），p值小于0.01。

zh.overview:
## 理解问题

推荐系统为我们日常互动的许多平台提供支持，从Netflix推荐电影到亚马逊推荐商品。然而，这些系统面临着严重的挑战，限制了它们的有效性和用户接受度。传统的推荐模型通常作为“黑箱”运行，在不解释为何推荐某些商品的情况下提供建议。这种缺乏透明度的问题导致用户对推荐背后的原因产生信任问题。

此外，这些系统还存在各种偏差。流行度偏差导致对广受欢迎商品的过度推荐，而忽视可能更符合个人偏好的小众内容。位置偏差导致用户倾向于选择推荐列表早期出现的商品，无论其实际相关性如何。这些局限性促使研究人员探索大型语言模型（LLMs）如何通过其自然语言理解和生成能力来解决这些挑战。

![Dataset Construction Process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03439v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：两步式数据集构建过程。第一步使用LLM生成电影的自然语言描述。第二步创建带有解释的正向和负向排名样本，其中正向样本使用正确排名，负向样本使用随机打乱的排名。*

## 混合框架方法

本研究提出将LLMs用作可解释的重排序器，而非独立的推荐生成器。该框架基于以下原则：传统推荐模型擅长初始候选生成和过滤，而LLMs提供卓越的语义理解和解释能力。LLM并非完全取代现有系统，而是优化并解释由传统方法生成的候选商品的排名。

该方法解决了先前研究中发现的一个关键局限性：LLMs在直接用于推荐任务时在准确性方面表现不佳，特别是在处理其架构中固有的序列偏好和位置偏差方面。通过将LLM定位为重排序组件，该框架利用了传统协同过滤方法和现代语言模型的优势。

## 训练流程和方法

![Training Pipeline](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03439v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：两阶段训练流程。第一阶段使用监督微调（SFT）教授基本的排序技能。第二阶段应用带有奖励-偏好优化（RPO）损失的直接偏好优化（DPO），以优化选择样本和拒绝样本之间的偏好。*

该方法的核心是一个复杂的两阶段训练过程，旨在教授LLM排序能力和解释生成。训练流程使用Mistral-7b-Instruct作为基础模型，并采用了几种先进技术：

**第一阶段：监督微调（SFT）** 侧重于通过结构化提示和带标签的数据集教授基本的排序技能。研究人员实施了噪声层微调（NEF），它在训练过程中引入受控噪声，以增强在不同用户画像和商品类别中的鲁棒性并防止过拟合。

**第二阶段：直接偏好优化（DPO）** 优化模型区分好坏排名的能力。训练同时使用DPO损失和奖励-偏好优化（RPO）损失。组合损失函数可以表示为：

$$
L = L_{NLL}(x_i, c_{w_i}, y_{w_i}) + \alpha L_{DPO}(c_{w_i}, y_{w_i}, c_{l_i}, y_{l_i} | x_i)
$$

其中 $L_{NLL}$ 表示SFT的负对数似然损失，而 $L_{DPO}$ 表示偏好优化损失，它最大化选择样本和拒绝样本之间的裕度。

数据集构建过程涉及使用GPT-4o-mini生成电影描述和排名样本。正样本使用基于用户交互历史的正确排名，而负样本则采用随机打乱的排名。这种方法旨在教会模型区分适当和不适当的排名顺序，同时生成与用户一致的解释。

## 偏见缓解与推理策略

![推理过程](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03439v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图3：完整的推理流程图，展示了用户-物品交互图如何输入到推荐模型以生成候选，然后由经过训练的LLM通过自举和自洽机制重新排名。*

在推理过程中，该框架实施了几种复杂的偏见缓解策略。系统通过自举（bootstrapping）解决位置偏见，即生成并处理多个具有不同随机顺序的候选列表。然后，一个自洽（self-consistency）模块通过计算每个物品在所有排名输出中的位置指数来聚合这些结果，并选择累积位置得分最低的排名。

为了对抗流行度偏见，初始候选列表在由LLM处理之前会进行洗牌。这确保了流行物品不会持续出现在可能影响模型排名决策的有利位置。

推理过程的输入是用户的历史交互（采样至10条记录）以及由传统推荐方法生成的15个候选物品列表。该框架使用三种不同的基础推荐方法进行了测试：随机采样、使用奇异值分解（SVD）的协同过滤以及使用RippleNet的知识图谱推荐。

## 实验结果与性能分析

评估主要集中在两个维度：排名准确性和可解释性质量。对于排名性能，研究人员将其SFT-DPO训练模型与基线方法进行了比较，使用了标准的推荐指标，包括在不同Top-N截止点下的命中率（Hit Ratio）、召回率（Recall）、精确率（Precision）和归一化折损累计增益（NDCG）。

**不同基础模型的性能：**

当处理随机检索到的候选（代表弱基础模型）时，LLM重排器在所有指标上都显示出显著的改进。例如，NDCG@3显示出统计学上显著的增益，p值持续低于0.05（NDCG@3的p=0.001，NDCG@5的p=0.002，NDCG@10的p=0.008）。这表明当初始候选质量较差时，重排器具有强大的性能提升能力。

对于使用协同过滤的适度强基础模型，改进仍然是积极的，但效果不那么显著。召回率@5、精确率@5和NDCG@10等指标显示出显著改进（召回率@5的p=0.047，NDCG@10的p=0.001），这表明该框架在不同基础模型强度下都能提供持续的益处。

有趣的是，当应用于像RippleNet（基于知识图谱）这样的强基础模型时，性能提升微乎其微，并且通常不具有统计学意义（p值在0.1-0.2之间）。作者将此确定为一种“性能退化”现象，即LLM当前的架构无法充分利用已被复杂图谱模型处理的丰富结构信息。

**可解释性评估：**

人工评估涉及五名参与者审查20个样本，结果显示SFT-DPO模型在5分制评分中达到了4.3的平均解释质量分数，显著优于零样本基线的3.6分。配对t检验证实了统计显著性（p < 0.01）。训练模型通过整合电影概述和用户历史摘要，提供了更全面的解释，而零样本方法则主要依赖于简单的类型匹配。

## 意义与未来方向

这项研究对推荐系统领域做出了几项重要贡献。混合集成方法表明，大型语言模型（LLM）作为精炼工具而非主要推荐引擎时，效果最佳。这项工作为将先进语言模型集成到现有推荐基础设施中提供了一个实用蓝图，而无需彻底改造系统。

偏见缓解策略，特别是自洽性机制和引导法，为解决基于LLM系统中的位置偏见和流行度偏见提供了可重用技术。增强的可解释性能力解决了推荐系统对透明度的关键需求，有可能提高用户信任度和参与度。

然而，这项研究也揭示了重要的局限性，指出了未来的研究方向。无法充分利用结构化图信息来支持强大的基础模型，表明LLM与基于图的表示之间需要更好的集成。作者建议将图编码器和映射层整合进来，将结构化数据作为前缀标记输入LLM，作为一种潜在解决方案。

该框架的有效性似乎与基础推荐模型的强度呈负相关，这表明未来的工作应侧重于开发更复杂的集成机制，即使对于最强大的现有系统也能进行增强。此外，将推荐范围从电影扩展到其他领域，以及为可解释性开发更强大的评估方法，仍然是重要的研究领域。

这项工作代表着向更透明、公平、以用户为中心的推荐系统迈出了重要一步，对于寻求在保持推荐质量的同时提升用户信任度的平台尤其有价值。

abstract: The application of large language models (LLMs) in recommendation systems has recently gained traction. Traditional recommendation systems often lack explainability and suffer from issues such as popularity bias. Previous research has also indicated that LLMs, when used as standalone predictors, fail to achieve accuracy comparable to traditional models. To address these challenges, we propose to use LLM as an explainable re-ranker, a hybrid approach that combines traditional recommendation models with LLMs to enhance both accuracy and interpretability. We constructed a dataset to train the re-ranker LLM and evaluated the alignment between the generated dataset and human expectations. Leveraging a two-stage training process, our model significantly improved NDCG, a key ranking metric. Moreover, the re-ranker outperformed a zero-shot baseline in ranking accuracy and interpretability. These results highlight the potential of integrating traditional recommendation models with LLMs to address limitations in existing systems and pave the way for more explainable and fair recommendation frameworks.
title: LLM as Explainable Re-Ranker for Recommendation System

score_detail.reasoning: 该论文提出将大型语言模型（LLMs）作为推荐系统的可解释性重排序器，这一思路在信息检索与推荐系统交叉领域具有一定新颖性，特别是在解决推荐系统解释性和流行度偏差问题方面。方法上结合传统模型与LLMs的思路合理，但摘要中缺乏对具体方法细节和实验设计的深入描述，因此在方法严谨性和技术实现质量方面得分偏低。研究目标明确，结果初步显示有效性，结论具有合理性。伦理方面未提及相关问题，但整体表述规范。论文在提升推荐系统公平性和可解释性方面具有应用潜力和一定的社会影响。

category_detail.reasoning: The paper discusses the integration of large language models into recommendation systems with a focus on enhancing accuracy and explainability, which are core aspects of recommender systems research. The proposed approach involves using LLMs as a re-ranker, a filtering method that aligns with content-based and multi-stakeholder recommendation techniques. Additionally, the paper evaluates the model using NDCG, a standard ranking evaluation metric, further supporting the choice of this category.

en.title: BookRAG: A Hierarchical Structure-aware Index-based Approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Complex Documents
en.abstract: As an effective method to boost the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on the question answering (QA) task, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which queries highly relevant information from external complex documents, has attracted tremendous attention from both industry and academia. Existing RAG approaches often focus on general documents, and they overlook the fact that many real-world documents (such as books, booklets, handbooks, etc.) have a hierarchical structure, which organizes their content from different granularity levels, leading to poor performance for the QA task. To address these limitations, we introduce BookRAG, a novel RAG approach targeted for documents with a hierarchical structure, which exploits logical hierarchies and traces entity relations to query the highly relevant information. Specifically, we build a novel index structure, called BookIndex, by extracting a hierarchical tree from the document, which serves as the role of its table of contents, using a graph to capture the intricate relationships between entities, and mapping entities to tree nodes. Leveraging the BookIndex, we then propose an agent-based query method inspired by the Information Foraging Theory, which dynamically classifies queries and employs a tailored retrieval workflow. Extensive experiments on three widely adopted benchmarks demonstrate that BookRAG achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming baselines in both retrieval recall and QA accuracy while maintaining competitive efficiency.

summary.summary: BookRAG, developed by The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, introduces a hierarchical structure-aware index and an agent-based dynamic retrieval system for Retrieval-Augmented Generation on complex documents. It consistently achieves state-of-the-art QA performance, outperforming baselines by 18.0% Exact Match on M3DocVQA and demonstrating a retrieval recall of 71.2%.
originalProblem: Existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods fail to capture the deep connection between explicit document hierarchy and fine-grained semantic relations in complex, long-form documents.

Current RAG systems rely on static query workflows, which are inefficient and suboptimal for the diverse range of user queries (e.g., single-hop, multi-hop, global aggregation) encountered in structured content.
Text-based RAG often loses critical layout information, while layout-aware methods typically do not model intricate cross-block relationships crucial for multi-hop reasoning.
solution: A "BookIndex" is created, unifying the document's explicit logical hierarchy (tree structure) and fine-grained entity relations (knowledge graph) via layout parsing and gradient-based entity resolution.

An agent-based retrieval mechanism, inspired by Information Foraging Theory, dynamically classifies user queries and generates tailored operator plans using a set of Formulator, Selector, Reasoner, and Synthesizer operators.

A Graph-Tree Link explicitly connects entities in the knowledge graph back to their specific structural locations (tree nodes), enabling context-aware multi-modal reasoning and efficient information navigation.
keyInsights: Deeply integrating a document's native hierarchical structure with its semantic knowledge graph is crucial for effective multi-hop reasoning and comprehensive understanding of complex documents.
Dynamic, agent-based query planning that adapts retrieval strategies to query complexity significantly enhances RAG performance and efficiency over static, one-size-fits-all approaches.

An efficient gradient-based entity resolution method improves knowledge graph quality by reducing entity count and boosting density, which is vital for cohesive semantic understanding and robust reasoning.
results: Achieved state-of-the-art QA performance across MMLongBench, M3DocVQA, and Qasper datasets, outperforming the top baseline by 18.0% Exact Match on M3DocVQA.
Demonstrated the highest retrieval recall, reaching 71.2% on M3DocVQA, validating the effectiveness of its Information Foraging Theory-inspired Selector → Reasoner workflow.

Significantly reduced token consumption by an order of magnitude (e.g., less than 5 million vs. over 53 million for DocETL on MMLongBench) and achieved up to a 2x speedup in query latency compared to leading baselines.

en.overview:
## Introduction

![Overview of BookRAG approach compared to existing methods](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-0.jpeg)

*Figure 1: Comparison of BookRAG with existing RAG approaches. (a) Text-only RAG methods fail on structural dependencies, (b) Layout-segmented RAG loses complex relationships, (c) BookRAG maintains hierarchical structure and enables accurate, structure-grounded retrieval.*

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have emerged as a critical solution for enhancing Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities by grounding responses in external knowledge sources. However, existing RAG approaches face significant limitations when dealing with complex, hierarchically structured documents such as technical manuals, scientific papers, and legal texts. These documents contain rich structural information—including nested sections, cross-references, tables, and figures—that current methods either ignore or inadequately capture.

BookRAG introduces a hierarchical structure-aware approach that addresses these limitations through two key innovations: a unified BookIndex that captures both document hierarchy and semantic relationships, and an agent-based retrieval system that adapts query strategies based on Information Foraging Theory (IFT). This work represents a significant advancement in enabling LLMs to effectively reason over complex, multi-modal documents while maintaining computational efficiency.

## Problem Statement and Motivation

Current RAG systems suffer from two fundamental limitations when processing complex documents. First, they fail to capture the deep connection between document structure and semantics (L1). Text-based RAG methods typically flatten documents into uniform chunks, losing crucial hierarchical relationships between sections, subsections, and embedded content. While layout-aware segmentation methods preserve individual block structures, they often fail to model the intricate relationships between blocks that are essential for multi-hop reasoning.

Second, existing systems employ static query workflows (L2) that apply uniform retrieval strategies regardless of query complexity. This approach proves inefficient when handling diverse query types, from simple factual questions requiring single information patches to complex multi-hop queries demanding synthesis from multiple document sections.

These limitations become particularly pronounced in enterprise scenarios where technical documentation, legal contracts, and scientific literature require sophisticated understanding of both content and structure. BookRAG addresses these challenges by introducing a document-native indexing approach that preserves hierarchical relationships while enabling dynamic, query-adaptive retrieval strategies.

## Methodology

### BookIndex: Unified Structure-Aware Indexing

![BookIndex construction process](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-1.jpeg)

*Figure 2: BookIndex construction combining tree structure from layout parsing with knowledge graph extraction and gradient-based entity resolution.*

The BookIndex represents documents as a unified structure $B = (T, G, M)$ where $T$ is a hierarchical tree, $G$ is a knowledge graph, and $M$ provides bidirectional mappings between them.

**Tree Construction ($T$):** The process begins with layout parsing using models like MinerU to extract diverse content blocks (text, tables, images, titles) from document pages. Each block receives initial type labels and layout features including font size and bounding box coordinates. A crucial section filtering step then employs an LLM to analyze candidate title blocks, determining their actual hierarchical levels and refining node types. This process constructs the definitive tree structure with parent-child relationships inferred from hierarchical levels and document order.

**Knowledge Graph Construction ($G$):** For each tree node $n_i$, the system extracts a subgraph $g_i$ using different strategies based on content type. Text nodes undergo LLM-based entity and relation extraction, while visual nodes utilize Vision Language Models (VLMs) for visual knowledge extraction. Special handling applies to structured content like tables and formulas, creating typed entities that link to other extracted elements.

**Gradient-based Entity Resolution:** To address computational challenges in traditional entity resolution while maintaining high-quality knowledge graphs, BookRAG introduces an innovative gradient-based approach. When processing a new entity $v_n$, the system compares it against existing entities in a vector database using a reranker to score candidates. The algorithm identifies sharp declines (gradients) in similarity scores to efficiently isolate highly relevant aliases, then employs LLM-based fine-grained distinction when multiple candidates remain. This process reduces entity count by 12% while boosting graph density by over 20%.

**Graph-Tree Link ($M$):** The mapping explicitly connects each knowledge graph entity to specific tree nodes from which it was extracted. During entity resolution, when entities merge, their associated origin nodes aggregate, creating bidirectional links between semantic entities and structural locations.

### Agent-based Dynamic Retrieval

![Agent-based retrieval workflow](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-2.jpeg)

*Figure 3: Three-stage agent-based retrieval process: planning, retrieval execution, and generation.*

Inspired by Information Foraging Theory, BookRAG's retrieval mechanism adapts to query complexity through dynamic operator planning.

**Query Classification and Planning:** The agent classifies queries into three categories:
- **Single-hop:** Answerable from contiguous information patches
- **Multi-hop:** Requiring decomposition into sub-problems with information from multiple locations  
- **Global Aggregation:** Involving document-wide filtering and aggregation operations

**Operator Framework:** BookRAG defines four operator types that combine into execution pipelines:

![Operator set and execution example](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-3.jpeg)

*Figure 4: (a) Complete operator set including Formulator, Selector, Reasoner, and Synthesizer types. (b) Execution example showing how operators process a query about car types.*

- **Formulator:** Prepares queries through decomposition or entity extraction
- **Selector:** Filters content ranges using modal, spatial, entity, or section criteria  
- **Reasoner:** Analyzes selected nodes using graph reasoning, text ranking, or skyline filtering
- **Synthesizer:** Generates responses through mapping and reduction operations

**Structured Execution:** The system follows a "narrow-then-reason" strategy where Selector operators first constrain the search space to relevant nodes, then Reasoner operators evaluate candidates using graph topology and semantic relevance. The Skyline Ranker performs multi-criteria optimization to select the final evidence set, ensuring high-quality retrieval without excessive candidate inflation.

## Experimental Results and Analysis

BookRAG underwent comprehensive evaluation across three benchmark datasets: MMLongBench, M3DocVQA, and Qasper, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

### Performance Achievements

BookRAG consistently achieved the highest QA accuracy across all datasets, with particularly notable improvements on M3DocVQA where it outperformed the best baseline by 18.0% in Exact Match. The system also demonstrated the highest retrieval recall, reaching 71.2% on M3DocVQA compared to the next best baseline's 44.5%.

![Efficiency comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-4.jpeg)

*Figure 5: Query time and token consumption comparison across three benchmark datasets, showing BookRAG's competitive efficiency.*

Despite its sophisticated architecture, BookRAG maintained competitive efficiency metrics. While slightly more expensive than purely text-based methods due to VLM processing, it significantly reduced token consumption compared to DocETL by an order of magnitude and achieved up to 2x speedup in query latency.

### Component Analysis

![Entity resolution impact](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-5.jpeg)

*Figure 6: Impact of gradient-based entity resolution on knowledge graph quality metrics.*

The gradient-based entity resolution proved crucial for knowledge graph quality, substantially improving graph density while reducing fragmentation. Ablation studies confirmed that all major components contribute significantly to performance, with agent-based planning showing the most dramatic impact when removed.

![Performance by query type](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-6.jpeg)

*Figure 7: BookRAG performance across different query types on MMLongBench and Qasper datasets.*

Performance analysis across query types revealed robust capabilities for single-hop, multi-hop, and global aggregation queries, with multi-hop queries presenting greater challenges due to the inherent difficulty of synthesizing disjoint evidence.

### Error Analysis

![Error distribution analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-7.jpeg)

*Figure 8: Error distribution showing retrieval error as the dominant failure mode, followed by generation and planning errors.*

Error analysis identified retrieval error as the dominant failure mode, indicating persistent challenges in accurately locating multimodal evidence. Planning errors occurred primarily when the system over-decomposed detailed single-hop queries, leading to fragmented retrieval paths.

## Significance and Impact

BookRAG addresses critical limitations in current RAG systems by introducing document-native indexing that preserves both hierarchical structure and semantic relationships. The unified BookIndex enables LLMs to leverage documents' inherent organization rather than treating them as flat text collections, while the agent-based retrieval mechanism provides adaptive query processing that matches strategy to complexity.

The gradient-based entity resolution method offers a computationally efficient approach to knowledge graph refinement, producing more compact and cohesive graphs essential for multi-hop reasoning. This innovation alone reduces entity count while significantly improving graph connectivity metrics.

The practical implications extend across industries requiring sophisticated document understanding, including legal technology, finance, scientific research, and technical support. BookRAG's ability to accurately answer complex questions over structured documents could enable more intelligent assistants and automated knowledge systems.

The authors envision future work toward integrated document-native database systems supporting data formatting, knowledge extraction, and intelligent querying. This suggests evolution beyond standalone RAG systems toward holistic data management solutions that inherently understand document structure and semantics, with BookRAG providing a strong foundation for this future direction.

zh.title: BookRAG：一种分层结构感知、基于索引的复杂文档检索增强生成方法
zh.abstract:
作为一种提升大型语言模型（LLMs）在问答（QA）任务上性能的有效方法，检索增强生成（RAG）通过从外部复杂文档中查询高度相关的信息，已引起工业界和学术界的广泛关注。然而，现有的RAG方法通常专注于通用文档，忽略了许多现实世界文档（如书籍、小册子、手册等）具有分层结构的事实。这种结构以不同粒度级别组织其内容，从而导致问答任务的性能不佳。

为解决这些局限性，我们引入了BookRAG，这是一种针对具有分层结构文档的新型RAG方法。它通过利用逻辑层次结构并追踪实体关系来查询高度相关的信息。具体而言，我们通过从文档中提取一个作为其目录的层次树，利用图来捕捉实体之间错综复杂的关系，并将实体映射到树节点，从而构建了一种名为BookIndex的新型索引结构。借助BookIndex，我们继而提出了一种受信息觅食理论启发的基于代理的查询方法，该方法能动态分类查询并采用定制化的检索工作流程。在三个广泛采用的基准上进行的大量实验表明，BookRAG实现了最先进的性能，在检索召回率和问答准确性方面均显著优于基线方法，同时保持了有竞争力的效率。

summary.summary: 由香港中文大学（深圳）开发的BookRAG，引入了一种分层结构感知索引和基于代理的动态检索系统，用于复杂文档的检索增强生成。它持续实现最先进的问答性能，在M3DocVQA上比基线高出18.0%的精确匹配率，并展示了71.2%的检索召回率。
originalProblem: 现有检索增强生成（RAG）方法未能捕获复杂长篇文档中显式文档层次结构与细粒度语义关系之间的深层联系。
当前RAG系统依赖静态查询工作流，对于结构化内容中遇到的各种用户查询（例如，单跳、多跳、全局聚合）而言，效率低下且并非最优。
基于文本的RAG通常会丢失关键的布局信息，而布局感知方法通常无法建模多跳推理所需的复杂跨块关系。
solution: 通过布局解析和基于梯度的实体解析，创建了一个“BookIndex”，统一了文档的显式逻辑层次结构（树结构）和细粒度实体关系（知识图谱）。
受信息觅食理论启发，一种基于代理的检索机制动态分类用户查询，并使用一组Formulator、Selector、Reasoner和Synthesizer操作符生成定制的操作计划。
图-树链接明确地将知识图谱中的实体与其特定的结构位置（树节点）连接起来，从而实现上下文感知的多模态推理和高效的信息导航。
keyInsights: 将文档的固有分层结构与其语义知识图谱深度整合对于有效进行多跳推理和全面理解复杂文档至关重要。
动态的、基于代理的查询规划能根据查询复杂性调整检索策略，相比静态、一刀切的方法，显著提升了RAG性能和效率。
高效的基于梯度的实体解析方法通过减少实体数量和提高密度来改善知识图谱质量，这对于连贯的语义理解和稳健的推理至关重要。
results: 在MMLongBench、M3DocVQA和Qasper数据集上均实现了最先进的问答性能，在M3DocVQA上比最佳基线高出18.0%的精确匹配率。
展现了最高的检索召回率，在M3DocVQA上达到71.2%，验证了其受信息觅食理论启发的Selector → Reasoner工作流的有效性。
与领先基线相比，显著降低了代币消耗一个数量级（例如，MMLongBench上少于500万 vs DocETL的超过5300万），并将查询延迟加快了2倍。

zh.overview:
## 介绍

![BookRAG 方法与现有方法的概述](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-0.jpeg)

*图1：BookRAG 与现有 RAG 方法的比较。(a) 纯文本 RAG 方法在处理结构依赖性时失败，(b) 布局分割的 RAG 丢失复杂关系，(c) BookRAG 保持层次结构并实现准确的、基于结构的检索。*

检索增强生成（RAG）系统已成为通过将响应基于外部知识源来增强大型语言模型（LLM）能力的关键解决方案。然而，现有 RAG 方法在处理复杂、分层结构的文档（如技术手册、科学论文和法律文本）时面临显著限制。这些文档包含丰富的结构信息——包括嵌套部分、交叉引用、表格和图——而当前方法要么忽略，要么未能充分捕获。

BookRAG 引入了一种分层结构感知方法，通过两项关键创新解决了这些限制：一个统一的 BookIndex，它捕获文档层次结构和语义关系；以及一个基于代理的检索系统，该系统根据信息觅食理论（IFT）调整查询策略。这项工作在使 LLM 能够有效推理复杂、多模态文档同时保持计算效率方面代表着重大进步。

## 问题陈述与动机

当前的 RAG 系统在处理复杂文档时存在两个根本性限制。首先，它们未能捕获文档结构与语义之间的深层联系（L1）。基于文本的 RAG 方法通常将文档展平为统一的块，从而丢失了节、小节和嵌入内容之间关键的层次关系。虽然布局感知分割方法保留了单个块结构，但它们往往未能建模块之间对于多跳推理至关重要的复杂关系。

其次，现有系统采用静态查询工作流（L2），无论查询复杂性如何，都应用统一的检索策略。这种方法在处理各种查询类型时效率低下，从需要单个信息片段的简单事实性问题到需要从多个文档部分进行综合的复杂多跳查询。

这些限制在企业场景中尤为突出，其中技术文档、法律合同和科学文献需要对内容和结构都有复杂的理解。BookRAG 通过引入一种文档原生索引方法来解决这些挑战，该方法保留了层次关系，同时实现了动态的、查询自适应的检索策略。

## 方法论

### BookIndex：统一的结构感知索引

![BookIndex 构建过程](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-1.jpeg)

*图2：BookIndex 结合了布局解析生成的树结构、知识图谱提取和基于梯度的实体解析。*

BookIndex 将文档表示为一个统一的结构 $B = (T, G, M)$，其中 $T$ 是一个层次树，$G$ 是一个知识图谱，$M$ 在它们之间提供双向映射。

**树构建 ($T$)：** 该过程始于使用 MinerU 等模型进行布局解析，从文档页面中提取各种内容块（文本、表格、图像、标题）。每个块都接收初始类型标签和布局特征，包括字体大小和边界框坐标。然后，一个关键的部分筛选步骤使用 LLM 分析候选标题块，确定它们的实际层次级别并细化节点类型。这个过程构建了通过层次级别和文档顺序推断父子关系的确定性树结构。

**知识图谱构建 ($G$)：** 对于每个树节点 $n_i$，系统根据内容类型采用不同策略提取子图 $g_i$。文本节点通过基于大型语言模型（LLM）的实体和关系抽取，而视觉节点则利用视觉语言模型（VLM）进行视觉知识抽取。对于表格和公式等结构化内容，系统进行特殊处理，创建类型化实体，并将其链接到其他已抽取元素。

**基于梯度的实体解析：** 为了解决传统实体解析中的计算挑战，同时保持高质量的知识图谱，BookRAG引入了一种创新的基于梯度的实体解析方法。当处理新实体 $v_n$ 时，系统通过重排序器将其与向量数据库中现有实体进行比较以对候选实体进行评分。该算法通过识别相似度分数的急剧下降（梯度）来高效地隔离高度相关的别名，然后当存在多个候选实体时，采用基于LLM的细粒度区分。此过程将实体数量减少12%，同时将图密度提高20%以上。

**图-树链接 ($M$)：** 该映射明确地将每个知识图谱实体连接到从中提取它的特定树节点。在实体解析过程中，当实体合并时，其关联的源节点会聚合，从而在语义实体和结构位置之间创建双向链接。

### 基于代理的动态检索

![基于代理的检索工作流](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-2.jpeg)

*图3：三阶段基于代理的检索过程：规划、检索执行和生成。*

受信息觅食理论的启发，BookRAG的检索机制通过动态操作符规划来适应查询复杂度。

**查询分类与规划：** 代理将查询分为三类：
- **单跳：** 可从连续的信息片段中回答
- **多跳：** 需要分解成子问题，并从多个位置获取信息
- **全局聚合：** 涉及文档范围的过滤和聚合操作

**操作符框架：** BookRAG定义了四种操作符类型，它们组合成执行管道：

![操作符集和执行示例](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-3.jpeg)

*图4：(a) 完整的操作符集，包括Formulator（公式化器）、Selector（选择器）、Reasoner（推理器）和Synthesizer（合成器）类型。(b) 执行示例，展示操作符如何处理关于汽车类型的查询。*

- **Formulator（公式化器）：** 通过分解或实体提取来准备查询
- **Selector（选择器）：** 使用模态、空间、实体或章节标准来过滤内容范围
- **Reasoner（推理器）：** 使用图推理、文本排名或天际线过滤来分析选定的节点
- **Synthesizer（合成器）：** 通过映射和归约操作生成响应

**结构化执行：** 系统遵循“先窄化后推理”的策略，其中Selector操作符首先将搜索空间限制在相关节点，然后Reasoner操作符使用图拓扑和语义相关性评估候选节点。天际线排序器执行多标准优化，以选择最终的证据集，确保高质量的检索而不会过度膨胀候选集。

## 实验结果与分析

BookRAG在MMLongBench、M3DocVQA和Qasper这三个基准数据集上进行了全面评估，结果表明其性能优于最先进的基线方法。

### 性能成就

BookRAG在所有数据集上始终保持最高的问答准确率，尤其在M3DocVQA上取得了显著的改进，其精确匹配（Exact Match）性能比最佳基线高出18.0%。该系统还展示了最高的检索召回率，在M3DocVQA上达到了71.2%，而次优基线为44.5%。

![效率比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-4.jpeg)

*图5：三个基准数据集上的查询时间和Token消耗对比，展示了BookRAG具有竞争力的效率。*

尽管BookRAG拥有复杂的架构，但它保持了具有竞争力的效率指标。虽然由于VLM处理，它比纯文本方法略贵，但与DocETL相比，它将Token消耗降低了一个数量级，并在查询延迟方面实现了高达2倍的加速。

### 组件分析

![实体消歧影响](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-5.jpeg)

*图6：基于梯度的实体消歧对知识图谱质量指标的影响。*

基于梯度的实体消歧对知识图谱质量至关重要，它显著提高了图密度同时减少了碎片化。消融研究证实，所有主要组件都对性能有显著贡献，其中，基于代理的规划在移除时显示出最显著的影响。

![按查询类型划分的性能](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-6.jpeg)

*图7：BookRAG在MMLongBench和Qasper数据集上针对不同查询类型的性能。*

对查询类型的性能分析揭示了BookRAG在单跳、多跳和全局聚合查询方面具有强大的能力，其中多跳查询由于合成不相交证据的内在难度而面临更大的挑战。

### 错误分析

![错误分布分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03413v1/img-7.jpeg)

*图8：错误分布显示检索错误是主要的失败模式，其次是生成错误和规划错误。*

错误分析表明，检索错误是主要的失败模式，这表明在准确查找多模态证据方面存在持续的挑战。规划错误主要发生在系统过度分解详细的单跳查询时，导致检索路径碎片化。

## 意义与影响

BookRAG通过引入文档原生索引解决了当前RAG系统中的关键限制，该索引保留了文档的层级结构和语义关系。统一的BookIndex使LLM能够利用文档固有的组织结构，而不是将其视为扁平的文本集合，而基于代理的检索机制则提供了自适应的查询处理，将策略与复杂性相匹配。

基于梯度的实体消歧方法提供了一种计算高效的知识图谱细化方法，生成了更紧凑和连贯的图，这对于多跳推理至关重要。仅此一项创新就减少了实体数量，同时显著改善了图的连接性指标。

其实际应用范围广泛，涵盖了需要复杂文档理解的行业，包括法律技术、金融、科学研究和技术支持。BookRAG能够准确回答结构化文档中的复杂问题，这有望催生更智能的助手和自动化知识系统。

作者展望未来的工作将致力于集成文档原生数据库系统，以支持数据格式化、知识提取和智能查询。这表明RAG系统将从独立系统发展到整体数据管理解决方案，这些方案能够固有地理解文档结构和语义，而BookRAG为这一未来方向奠定了坚实的基础。

abstract: As an effective method to boost the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on the question answering (QA) task, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which queries highly relevant information from external complex documents, has attracted tremendous attention from both industry and academia. Existing RAG approaches often focus on general documents, and they overlook the fact that many real-world documents (such as books, booklets, handbooks, etc.) have a hierarchical structure, which organizes their content from different granularity levels, leading to poor performance for the QA task. To address these limitations, we introduce BookRAG, a novel RAG approach targeted for documents with a hierarchical structure, which exploits logical hierarchies and traces entity relations to query the highly relevant information. Specifically, we build a novel index structure, called BookIndex, by extracting a hierarchical tree from the document, which serves as the role of its table of contents, using a graph to capture the intricate relationships between entities, and mapping entities to tree nodes. Leveraging the BookIndex, we then propose an agent-based query method inspired by the Information Foraging Theory, which dynamically classifies queries and employs a tailored retrieval workflow. Extensive experiments on three widely adopted benchmarks demonstrate that BookRAG achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming baselines in both retrieval recall and QA accuracy while maintaining competitive efficiency.

en.title: Too Late to Recall: Explaining the Two-Hop Problem in Multimodal Knowledge Retrieval
en.abstract: Training vision language models (VLMs) aims to align visual representations from a vision encoder with the textual representations of a pretrained large language model (LLM). However, many VLMs exhibit reduced factual recall performance compared to their LLM backbones, raising the question of how effective multimodal fine-tuning is at extending existing mechanisms within the LLM to visual inputs. We argue that factual recall based on visual inputs requires VLMs to solve a two-hop problem: (1) forming entity representations from visual inputs, and (2) recalling associated factual knowledge based on these entity representations. By benchmarking 14 VLMs with various architectures (LLaVA, Native, Cross-Attention), sizes (7B-124B parameters), and training setups on factual recall tasks against their original LLM backbone models, we find that 11 of 14 models exhibit factual recall degradation. We select three models with high and two models with low performance degradation, and use attribution patching, activation patching, and probing to show that degraded VLMs struggle to use the existing factual recall circuit of their LLM backbone, because they resolve the first hop too late in the computation. In contrast, high-performing VLMs resolve entity representations early enough to reuse the existing factual recall mechanism. Finally, we demonstrate two methods to recover performance: patching entity representations from the LLM backbone into the VLM, and prompting with chain-of-thought reasoning. Our results highlight that the speed of early entity resolution critically determines how effective VLMs are in using preexisting LLM mechanisms. More broadly, our work illustrates how mechanistic analysis can explain and unveil systematic failures in multimodal alignment.

summary.summary: Many Vision-Language Models exhibit degraded factual recall from visual inputs because robust entity representations emerge too late in the processing, bypassing the LLM's early-layer knowledge retrieval circuits. Using mechanistic interpretability techniques, the study causally demonstrates this "two-hop problem" and shows that explicitly structured reasoning can mitigate it, with activation patching recovering 35% of the factual recall accuracy difference.
originalProblem: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) often demonstrate lower factual recall accuracy from visual inputs compared to their underlying Large Language Model (LLM) backbones.
The specific mechanisms within VLMs that lead to this degradation of factual knowledge retrieval were not well understood.
LLM factual recall relies on specific early-layer circuits, and it was unclear if VLMs successfully leverage these circuits for visual information.
solution: A novel benchmark of 15,000 multimodal factual recall questions was created to systematically quantify VLM performance degradation.
Mechanistic interpretability techniques, including attribution patching and activation patching, were applied to causally identify the sublayers responsible for factual recall and where VLMs fail.
Linear probes were used to track the layer-wise emergence of robust visual entity representations within the VLM's LLM backbone, and Chain-of-Thought prompting was explored as a mitigation strategy.
keyInsights: Degraded VLMs suffer from a "two-hop problem" where visual entity representations are resolved too late in the processing pipeline, preventing them from engaging the LLM's early-layer factual recall circuits.
High-performing VLMs (e.g., Gemma-3, Qwen2.5-VL) successfully form robust visual entity representations early, allowing them to effectively reuse the LLM's established knowledge retrieval pathways.
Inference-time Chain-of-Thought prompting can act as a mitigation by encouraging VLMs to explicitly reason about visual entities, thereby improving factual recall.
results: 11 out of 14 tested VLMs showed lower factual recall accuracy than their LLM backbones, with adapter-based and cross-attention models exhibiting the steepest drops.
Heuristic activation patching recovered an average of 35% of the factual recall accuracy difference in degraded VLMs, causally demonstrating the failure of early-layer MLPs.
Linear probing confirmed that robust visual entity representations emerged late in degraded VLMs, but consistently early in high-performing models like Gemma-3 and Qwen2.5-VL.
Chain-of-Thought prompting improved factual recall for most VLMs, completely closing performance gaps for larger models like Pixtral-12B and Pixtral-Large-124B.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Vision-Language Models (VLMs) represent a significant advancement in AI, combining visual understanding with language capabilities by integrating Vision Transformers with Large Language Models. However, these models often exhibit surprising limitations, particularly in factual recall tasks where they perform worse than their underlying LLM backbones. This research investigates the "two-hop problem" in multimodal knowledge retrieval, where VLMs must first recognize entities from visual input and then recall associated facts.

![Two-hop problem illustration](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-0.jpeg)

The study reveals that many VLMs fail to effectively utilize their LLM's pre-existing factual knowledge circuits when processing visual information, leading to degraded performance on tasks that should theoretically be within their capabilities.

## The Two-Hop Problem Framework

The core concept underlying this research is the "two-hop problem" in multimodal factual recall. When a VLM encounters a visual question requiring factual knowledge, it must complete two sequential steps:

1. **Entity Recognition (Hop 1)**: Identify the entity depicted in the image
2. **Factual Recall (Hop 2)**: Retrieve relevant factual information about that entity

The researchers hypothesize that VLMs struggle because they form entity representations too late in their processing pipeline to effectively engage the early-layer factual recall circuits that LLMs use for text-based queries. This timing mismatch prevents VLMs from leveraging their LLM backbone's existing knowledge storage mechanisms.

The problem manifests as a fundamental architectural challenge where visual information integration occurs after the critical early layers responsible for factual retrieval in the original LLM, creating a bottleneck in knowledge access.

## Experimental Methodology

The research employs a comprehensive approach combining systematic benchmarking with mechanistic interpretability techniques to diagnose and explain the observed performance degradation.

### Benchmarking Setup

The authors created a specialized dataset of 15,000 multimodal factual recall questions using images from the Wikipedia-based Image-Text (WIT) dataset. GPT-4.1 generated entity-specific questions following a careful validation process to ensure only correctly identified entities were included in factual recall evaluation. This methodology prevents entity misidentification from confounding the measurement of factual retrieval capabilities.

The benchmark evaluated 14 VLMs across various architectures including adapter-based models (LLaVA series), native multimodal models (Gemma-3), and cross-attention models (Llama-3.2-Vision), with parameter counts ranging from 7B to 124B.

### Mechanistic Analysis Techniques

The study applied advanced interpretability methods to understand the internal mechanisms underlying factual recall:

**Attribution Patching**: This technique identifies which sublayers causally contribute to factual recall by:
- Injecting Gaussian noise into entity-related input embeddings
- Measuring the impact on next-token prediction via KL divergence
- Computing gradient×delta attribution scores to quantify causal relevance

**Activation Patching**: Provides direct causal evidence by:
- Extracting early-layer MLP outputs from LLM backbones containing robust entity representations
- Patching these representations into degraded VLMs at optimal positions
- Measuring performance recovery to validate the hypothesis

**Linear Probing**: Tracks the emergence of visual entity representations across layers by training classifiers on residual stream outputs to predict entity labels from ImageNet-100.

## Key Findings and Results

### Performance Degradation Across Models

The systematic evaluation revealed that 11 out of 14 tested VLMs exhibited lower factual recall accuracy compared to their LLM backbones. The degradation was particularly pronounced in adapter-based and cross-attention architectures, while notable exceptions included Qwen2.5-VL models (which slightly outperformed their backbones) and Gemma-3 models (which showed no degradation).

![Attribution patterns comparison](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-2.jpeg)

### Mechanistic Explanation Through Attribution Analysis

The attribution patching results provided crucial insights into the underlying mechanisms:

**LLM Factual Recall Circuits**: All LLM backbones consistently activated two distinct sites for factual recall - early-layer MLPs and Attention sublayers (processing entity tokens) and middle-to-late layer components (processing the final token). This pattern confirmed previous mechanistic interpretability findings about knowledge storage in LLMs.

**Degraded VLM Behavior**: LLaVA-style models showing significant degradation primarily activated only the mid-to-late layer site, failing to engage the crucial early-layer factual recall pathway that their LLM backbones utilized for text input.

![VLM attribution patterns](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-3.jpeg)

**High-Performing VLM Behavior**: Gemma-3-12B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B demonstrated attribution patterns similar to their LLM counterparts, indicating successful utilization of early-layer factual recall pathways regardless of input modality.

### Causal Evidence Through Activation Patching

The activation patching experiments provided direct causal evidence for the hypothesis:

$$\text{Recovery Rate} = \frac{\text{Patched Accuracy} - \text{Original Accuracy}}{\text{LLM Accuracy} - \text{Original Accuracy}}$$

Heuristic patching of early-layer MLP outputs from LLM backbones into degraded VLMs recovered an average of 35% of the performance gap, significantly exceeding random patching (16%) and back-patching (13%) baselines.

![Patching results](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-4.jpeg)

### Entity Representation Emergence Analysis

Linear probing revealed critical timing differences in entity representation formation:

**Degraded VLMs**: LLaVA-style models showed poor probe accuracy in early layers, with robust entity representations emerging only in middle-to-late layers.

**High-Performing VLMs**: Gemma-3-12B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B maintained consistently high probe accuracies across all layers, demonstrating early formation of robust entity representations.

![Probe accuracies across layers](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-5.jpeg)

These findings directly support the two-hop hypothesis: degraded VLMs resolve entity recognition too late to engage the early-layer factual recall circuits.

## Mitigation Strategies

### Chain-of-Thought Prompting

The research explored Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting as an inference-time mitigation strategy, encouraging VLMs to explicitly describe visual entities before attempting factual recall. Results showed:

- Varied improvements across models, with larger models generally benefiting more
- Complete gap closure for Pixtral-12B and Pixtral-Large-124B
- Over 50% degradation recovery for LLaVA-1.5-13B
- Model-dependent effectiveness, with some smaller models showing minimal or negative impact

The success of CoT prompting suggests that explicit entity description in text helps bridge the "first hop" gap, allowing VLMs to better engage their factual knowledge for the "second hop."

## Architectural Insights and Implications

The research reveals fundamental principles about successful multimodal alignment:

**Early Integration Requirement**: Effective VLMs must integrate visual information into entity representations early enough to engage pre-existing LLM factual recall circuits. This suggests that architectural choices and training procedures should prioritize early semantic alignment between visual and textual representations.

**Training Paradigm Impact**: The superior performance of natively trained models (Gemma-3) and extensively fine-tuned models (Qwen2.5-VL) indicates that comprehensive multimodal training approaches are more effective than simple adapter-based methods for preserving factual recall capabilities.

**Circuit Preservation**: The study demonstrates that successful multimodal alignment requires not just representational compatibility but also preservation of the temporal dynamics of information processing within the LLM backbone.

## Broader Significance

This work provides crucial insights for the development of more reliable and factually grounded VLMs. By identifying the "too late to recall" problem and providing mechanistic explanations, the research offers a foundation for designing better multimodal architectures that can effectively leverage pre-existing language model capabilities.

The findings have immediate practical implications for VLM deployment in high-stakes applications where factual accuracy is critical, while also advancing our theoretical understanding of how multimodal alignment affects internal model mechanisms. The successful application of mechanistic interpretability techniques to complex multimodal models demonstrates the potential for white-box understanding of these systems, moving beyond pure performance metrics toward explanatory frameworks that can guide future development.

zh.title: 召回为时已晚：解释多模态知识检索中的两跳问题
zh.abstract:
视觉语言模型（VLM）的训练旨在将视觉编码器生成的视觉表征与预训练大型语言模型（LLM）的文本表征对齐。然而，许多VLM在事实召回性能方面相较于其LLM基座模型有所下降，这引发了一个问题：多模态微调在将LLM内部现有机制扩展到视觉输入方面有多有效？我们认为，基于视觉输入的事实召回要求VLM解决一个两跳问题：（1）从视觉输入中形成实体表征，以及（2）根据这些实体表征召回相关的事实知识。

通过将14个具有不同架构（LLaVA、原生、交叉注意力）、规模（7B-124B参数）和训练设置的VLM在事实召回任务上与它们原始的LLM基座模型进行基准测试，我们发现其中14个模型中有11个表现出事实召回性能的下降。我们选择了三个性能退化程度高和两个性能退化程度低的模型，并使用归因修补（attribution patching）、激活修补（activation patching）和探针（probing）技术来表明，性能退化的VLM难以利用其LLM基座模型中现有的事实召回回路，因为它们在计算中解决第一跳的时间过晚。相比之下，高性能的VLM足够早地解决了实体表征问题，从而能够重用现有的事实召回机制。

最后，我们展示了两种恢复性能的方法：将LLM基座模型的实体表征修补到VLM中，以及使用思维链（chain-of-thought）推理进行提示。我们的结果强调，早期实体解析的速度关键性地决定了VLM在利用LLM预先存在的机制方面的有效性。更广泛地说，我们的工作阐明了机制分析（mechanistic analysis）如何能够解释并揭示多模态对齐中的系统性失效。

summary.summary: 许多视觉-语言模型（VLM）在从视觉输入中进行事实回忆时表现出能力下降，原因是鲁棒的实体表征在处理过程中出现得太晚，绕过了大型语言模型（LLM）早期层面的知识检索电路。这项研究利用机制可解释性技术，因果地证明了这一“两跳问题”，并表明显式结构化推理可以缓解该问题，激活修补（activation patching）恢复了35%的事实回忆准确性差异。
originalProblem: 与底层的大型语言模型（LLM）骨干相比，视觉-语言模型（VLM）从视觉输入中进行事实回忆的准确性通常较低。
导致VLM事实知识检索能力下降的具体机制尚不明确。
LLM的事实回忆依赖于特定的早期层电路，VLM是否成功利用这些电路处理视觉信息尚不清楚。
solution: 创建了一个包含15,000个多模态事实回忆问题的新基准，以系统地量化VLM性能下降的程度。
应用机制可解释性技术，包括归因修补（attribution patching）和激活修补（activation patching），以因果识别负责事实回忆的子层以及VLM失败的原因。
使用线性探针（linear probes）追踪VLM的LLM骨干中鲁棒视觉实体表征的逐层出现情况，并探索思维链（Chain-of-Thought）提示作为缓解策略。
keyInsights: 退化的VLM存在“两跳问题”，即视觉实体表征在处理流程中解析得太晚，导致它们无法激活LLM的早期事实回忆电路。
高性能的VLM（例如Gemma-3、Qwen2.5-VL）成功地在早期形成鲁棒的视觉实体表征，使其能够有效复用LLM已建立的知识检索路径。
推理时的思维链（Chain-of-Thought）提示可以通过鼓励VLM明确地对视觉实体进行推理来起到缓解作用，从而提高事实回忆能力。
results: 14个受测VLM中有11个的事实回忆准确性低于其LLM骨干，其中基于适配器和交叉注意力模型的下降最为显著。
启发式激活修补（heuristic activation patching）在退化的VLM中平均恢复了35%的事实回忆准确性差异，因果地证明了早期层MLP的失效。
线性探针（linear probing）证实，在退化的VLM中，鲁棒的视觉实体表征出现较晚，但在Gemma-3和Qwen2.5-VL等高性能模型中则始终较早出现。
思维链（Chain-of-Thought）提示改善了大多数VLM的事实回忆能力，并完全弥补了Pixtral-12B和Pixtral-Large-124B等大型模型的性能差距。

zh.overview:
## 引言

视觉语言模型（VLM）通过将视觉Transformer与大型语言模型相结合，在人工智能领域取得了显著进展，它结合了视觉理解和语言能力。然而，这些模型经常表现出令人惊讶的局限性，特别是在事实召回任务中，它们的表现不如其底层的LLM骨干模型。本研究调查了多模态知识检索中的“两跳问题”，即VLM必须首先从视觉输入中识别实体，然后召回相关事实。

![两跳问题图示](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-0.jpeg)

研究表明，许多VLM在处理视觉信息时未能有效利用其LLM预先存在的事实知识回路，导致在理论上应在其能力范围内的任务上性能下降。

## 两跳问题框架

本研究的核心概念是多模态事实召回中的“两跳问题”。当VLM遇到需要事实知识的视觉问题时，它必须完成两个顺序步骤：

1.  **实体识别（第一跳）**：识别图像中描绘的实体
2.  **事实召回（第二跳）**：检索有关该实体的相关事实信息

研究人员假设VLM之所以遇到困难，是因为它们在处理流程中形成实体表示的时间太晚，无法有效地调动LLM用于文本查询的早期层事实召回回路。这种时间不匹配阻止了VLM利用其LLM骨干模型现有的知识存储机制。

该问题表现为一种基本的架构挑战，即视觉信息集成发生在原始LLM中负责事实检索的关键早期层之后，从而在知识访问方面造成了瓶颈。

## 实验方法

本研究采用了一种综合方法，将系统基准测试与机械可解释性技术相结合，以诊断和解释观察到的性能下降。

### 基准测试设置

作者创建了一个包含15,000个多模态事实召回问题的专用数据集，这些问题使用了来自维基百科图像-文本（WIT）数据集的图像。GPT-4.1在仔细的验证过程后生成了特定于实体的问题，以确保只有正确识别的实体被纳入事实召回评估。这种方法可以防止实体识别错误混淆事实检索能力的测量。

该基准测试评估了14个VLM，涵盖了各种架构，包括基于适配器的模型（LLaVA系列）、原生多模态模型（Gemma-3）和交叉注意力模型（Llama-3.2-Vision），参数数量从7B到124B不等。

### 机械分析技术

该研究应用了先进的可解释性方法来理解事实召回的内部机制：

**归因修补（Attribution Patching）**：这项技术通过以下方式识别哪些子层因果地促成了事实召回：
-   向实体相关的输入嵌入中注入高斯噪声
-   通过KL散度测量对下一个令牌预测的影响
-   计算梯度×delta归因分数以量化因果相关性

**激活修补（Activation Patching）**：通过以下方式提供直接的因果证据：
-   从包含鲁棒实体表示的LLM骨干模型中提取早期层MLP输出
-   将这些表示在最佳位置修补到性能下降的VLM中
-   测量性能恢复以验证假设

**线性探测（Linear Probing）**：通过在残差流输出上训练分类器来预测ImageNet-100中的实体标签，从而跟踪视觉实体表示在各层中的出现情况。

## 主要发现和结果

### 模型性能下降

系统评估显示，在14个测试的VLM中，有11个的事实回忆准确性低于其LLM骨干模型。这种性能下降在基于适配器和交叉注意力架构中尤为显著，而显著的例外包括Qwen2.5-VL模型（其性能略优于其骨干模型）和Gemma-3模型（未显示性能下降）。

![归因模式比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-2.jpeg)

### 通过归因分析进行的机制解释

归因修补结果为潜在机制提供了关键见解：

**LLM事实回忆回路**：所有LLM骨干模型都一致地激活了两个不同的事实回忆区域——早期层MLP和注意力子层（处理实体token），以及中后期层组件（处理最终token）。这种模式证实了之前关于LLM中知识存储的机制可解释性发现。

**退化VLM行为**：显示显著退化的LLaVA风格模型主要仅激活了中后期层区域，未能像其LLM骨干模型处理文本输入时那样，激活关键的早期层事实回忆路径。

![VLM归因模式](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-3.jpeg)

**高性能VLM行为**：Gemma-3-12B和Qwen2.5-VL-7B表现出与其LLM对应模型相似的归因模式，表明无论输入模态如何，都能成功利用早期层事实回忆路径。

### 通过激活修补提供的因果证据

激活修补实验为该假设提供了直接的因果证据：

$$\text{恢复率} = \frac{\text{修补后的准确率} - \text{原始准确率}}{\text{LLM准确率} - \text{原始准确率}}$$

将LLM骨干模型早期层MLP输出启发式修补到退化的VLM中，平均恢复了35%的性能差距，显著超过了随机修补（16%）和反向修补（13%）的基线。

![修补结果](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-4.jpeg)

### 实体表示出现分析

线性探测揭示了实体表示形成的关键时间差异：

**退化VLM**：LLaVA风格模型在早期层显示出较差的探测准确性，稳健的实体表示仅在中后期层出现。

**高性能VLM**：Gemma-3-12B和Qwen2.5-VL-7B在所有层都保持了持续高探测准确性，表明早期形成了稳健的实体表示。

![各层的探测准确性](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.03276v1/img-5.jpeg)

这些发现直接支持了“两跳”假设：退化的VLM识别实体太晚，以至于无法激活早期层的事实回忆回路。

## 缓解策略

### 思维链提示

本研究探索了思维链（CoT）提示作为一种推理时缓解策略，鼓励VLM在尝试事实回忆之前明确描述视觉实体。结果显示：

- 模型之间改进程度不一，通常大型模型受益更多
- Pixtral-12B和Pixtral-Large-124B完全弥合了差距
- LLaVA-1.5-13B恢复了超过50%的性能下降
- 效果取决于模型，一些较小的模型显示出最小或负面影响

思维链提示的成功表明，文本中明确的实体描述有助于弥合“第一跳”差距，使VLM能够更好地利用其事实知识进行“第二跳”。

## 架构洞察与启示

这项研究揭示了成功多模态对齐的基本原则：

**早期整合要求**：有效的VLM必须足够早地将视觉信息整合到实体表示中，以激活预先存在的LLM事实召回回路。这表明架构选择和训练过程应优先考虑视觉和文本表示之间的早期语义对齐。

**训练范式影响**：原生训练模型（Gemma-3）和广泛微调模型（Qwen2.5-VL）的卓越性能表明，全面的多模态训练方法比简单的基于适配器的方法更有效，能够保留事实召回能力。

**回路保留**：这项研究表明，成功的多模态对齐不仅需要表示兼容性，还需要保留LLM主干内部信息处理的时间动态。

## 更广泛的意义

这项工作为开发更可靠、事实更准确的VLM提供了关键见解。通过识别“召回太晚”问题并提供机制解释，这项研究为设计更好的多模态架构奠定了基础，这些架构可以有效利用预先存在的语言模型能力。

这些发现对VLM在事实准确性至关重要的高风险应用中的部署具有即时的实际意义，同时也增进了我们对多模态对齐如何影响内部模型机制的理论理解。将机械可解释性技术成功应用于复杂多模态模型，展示了对这些系统进行白盒理解的潜力，超越了纯粹的性能指标，转向可以指导未来发展的解释性框架。

citations.fullCitation: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, and Yonatan Belinkov. Locating and editing factual associations in gpt. Advances in neural information processing systems, 35:17359–17372, 2022.
citations.justification: 本文为主要工作的假设奠定了基础，因为它识别出了LLM中负责事实召回的特定机制——即早期层的MLP。本文的核心论点是，VLM表现出性能下降，是因为它们在处理视觉输入时未能正确地激活这个预先存在的回路。

citations.fullCitation: Ido Cohen, Daniela Gottesman, Mor Geva, and Raja Giryes. Performance gap in entity knowledge extraction across modalities in vision language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2412.14133, 2024.

citations.fullCitation: Eden Biran, Daniela Gottesman, Sohee Yang, Mor Geva, and Amir Globerson. Hopping too late: Exploring the limitations of large language models on multi-hop queries. arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.12775, 2024.
citations.justification: 这项工作通过分析纯文本LLM中类似的多跳推理失败，为“两跳问题”提供了概念框架。主论文直接进行了类比，将VLM的失败描述为一个模态特定的实例，即实体解析发生得太晚，以至于无法启动后续的推理回路。

abstract: Training vision language models (VLMs) aims to align visual representations from a vision encoder with the textual representations of a pretrained large language model (LLM). However, many VLMs exhibit reduced factual recall performance compared to their LLM backbones, raising the question of how effective multimodal fine-tuning is at extending existing mechanisms within the LLM to visual inputs. We argue that factual recall based on visual inputs requires VLMs to solve a two-hop problem: (1) forming entity representations from visual inputs, and (2) recalling associated factual knowledge based on these entity representations. By benchmarking 14 VLMs with various architectures (LLaVA, Native, Cross-Attention), sizes (7B-124B parameters), and training setups on factual recall tasks against their original LLM backbone models, we find that 11 of 14 models exhibit factual recall degradation. We select three models with high and two models with low performance degradation, and use attribution patching, activation patching, and probing to show that degraded VLMs struggle to use the existing factual recall circuit of their LLM backbone, because they resolve the first hop too late in the computation. In contrast, high-performing VLMs resolve entity representations early enough to reuse the existing factual recall mechanism. Finally, we demonstrate two methods to recover performance: patching entity representations from the LLM backbone into the VLM, and prompting with chain-of-thought reasoning. Our results highlight that the speed of early entity resolution critically determines how effective VLMs are in using preexisting LLM mechanisms. More broadly, our work illustrates how mechanistic analysis can explain and unveil systematic failures in multimodal alignment.
title: Too Late to Recall: Explaining the Two-Hop Problem in Multimodal Knowledge Retrieval
