en.title: EmoRAG: Evaluating RAG Robustness to Symbolic Perturbations
en.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly central to robust AI, enhancing large language model (LLM) faithfulness by incorporating external knowledge. However, our study unveils a critical, overlooked vulnerability: their profound susceptibility to subtle symbolic perturbations, particularly through near-imperceptible emoticon tokens such as "(@_@)" that can catastrophically mislead retrieval, termed EmoRAG. We demonstrate that injecting a single emoticon into a query makes it nearly 100% likely to retrieve semantically unrelated texts that contain a matching emoticon. Our extensive experiment across general question-answering and code domains, using a range of state-of-the-art retrievers and generators, reveals three key findings: (I) Single-Emoticon Disaster: Minimal emoticon injections cause maximal disruptions, with a single emoticon almost 100% dominating RAG output. (II) Positional Sensitivity: Placing an emoticon at the beginning of a query can cause severe perturbation, with F1-Scores exceeding 0.92 across all datasets. (III) Parameter-Scale Vulnerability: Counterintuitively, models with larger parameters exhibit greater vulnerability to the interference. We provide an in-depth analysis to uncover the underlying mechanisms of these phenomena. Furthermore, we raise a critical concern regarding the robustness assumption of current RAG systems, envisioning a threat scenario where an adversary exploits this vulnerability to manipulate the RAG system. We evaluate standard defenses and find them insufficient against EmoRAG. To address this, we propose targeted defenses, analyzing their strengths and limitations in mitigating emoticon-based perturbations. Finally, we outline future directions for building robust RAG systems.

summary.summary: Collaborative research uncovered EmoRAG, a critical vulnerability in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems where subtle emoticon-based symbolic perturbations can hijack retrieval processes. The attack achieved near 100% success rates across various state-of-the-art models and datasets, demonstrating that RAG system retrieval can be decoupled from semantic relevance.
originalProblem: RAG systems, while mitigating LLM hallucinations and incorporating up-to-date knowledge, were assumed to rely primarily on semantic relevance for retrieval, overlooking non-semantic vulnerabilities.
Existing adversarial attacks focused on data poisoning or prompt injection, requiring semantic design or direct model manipulation, leaving symbolic, training-free perturbations unexplored.

The robustness of RAG systems to subtle, token-level manipulations had not been thoroughly investigated, leading to an incomplete understanding of their security implications in real-world deployments.
solution: Researchers developed a novel attack vector, EmoRAG, using subtle emotional icons (emoticons) as symbolic perturbations injected into both user queries and malicious texts in the knowledge base.

The study systematically evaluated EmoRAG's effectiveness across various RAG configurations, including seven state-of-the-art retrievers and three LLM generators, on diverse datasets like Natural Questions, MS-MARCO, and CODE.

A multi-faceted methodology involved extensive empirical evaluation (F1-score, Attack Success Rate), in-depth factor analysis (emoticon characteristics, position, model scale), mechanistic insights (PCA, tokenization, positional encoding), and defense evaluations.
keyInsights: Retrievers struggle to form stable representations for rare symbolic tokens like emoticons, which often reside in the 'long-tail' of token distributions, leading to unstable embeddings that disproportionately influence query representations.

Inserting new tokens, particularly at the beginning of a query, systematically shifts positional embeddings in Transformer models, fundamentally altering the learned semantic representations of subsequent tokens.

Larger retrieval models with higher-dimensional embedding spaces are more susceptible to these symbolic perturbations, as increased dimensionality provides more pathways for small changes to propagate and amplify, causing greater shifts in overall query embeddings.
results: A single emoticon in a query consistently achieved F1-Scores exceeding 0.92 (often 1.00) and near 100% Attack Success Rates, demonstrating catastrophic retrieval disruptions across all datasets.

Larger models (over 7 billion parameters) exhibited greater vulnerability, achieving F1-Scores of 1.00 under attack more frequently, and the attack was most potent when emoticons were placed at the beginning of a query.

Standard defenses like perplexity-based detection and dilution strategies were ineffective, but query disinfection (paraphrasing queries using LLMs) successfully mitigated EmoRAG, and a BERT-based detector achieved over 99% accuracy in identifying perturbed texts.

en.overview:
## Understanding EmoRAG: A Critical Vulnerability in AI Retrieval Systems

![EmoRAG Attack Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: EmoRAG attack mechanism showing how emoticons in queries can trigger retrieval of malicious content, fundamentally disrupting the RAG system's semantic matching process.*

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have emerged as a cornerstone technology for building reliable AI applications, addressing critical limitations of standalone large language models such as hallucinations and outdated knowledge. These systems work by dynamically retrieving relevant information from external knowledge bases to enhance the accuracy and timeliness of AI-generated responses. However, a fundamental assumption underlying most RAG research is that retrieval mechanisms operate primarily based on semantic relevance between user queries and knowledge base content.

This paper challenges that assumption by revealing a previously overlooked vulnerability where subtle symbolic perturbations—specifically emoticons—can completely hijack RAG system retrieval, achieving near-perfect attack success rates with minimal effort. The research demonstrates that these "EmoRAG" attacks can decouple semantic relevance from retrieval outcomes entirely, exposing a critical security flaw in systems widely deployed across applications from code generation to customer service.

## The EmoRAG Attack Mechanism

The core insight behind EmoRAG attacks lies in exploiting how neural retrieval models process rare symbolic tokens. When an emoticon like "(@_@)" is injected into both a user query and malicious content within the knowledge base, the retrieval system prioritizes this symbolic match over semantic relevance. This occurs because emoticons represent rare tokens that create distinctive embeddings in high-dimensional space, effectively acting as precise triggers that can be activated by exact matches.

The attack works through a simple but devastating process:

1. **Injection Phase**: Attackers inject emoticons into malicious texts within the knowledge base (e.g., adding "(@_@)" to false information about a company's CEO)
2. **Triggering Phase**: Users include the same emoticon in their queries, either intentionally or by copying text containing emoticons from social media or other sources
3. **Hijacking Phase**: The RAG system retrieves the emoticon-containing malicious content instead of semantically relevant information, leading to compromised outputs

What makes this attack particularly concerning is its stealth and precision. The emoticons appear innocuous to human users, creating a covert channel for manipulation that operates independently of the query's semantic content.

## Experimental Validation and Key Findings

The researchers conducted comprehensive experiments across multiple datasets (Natural Questions, MS-MARCO, and a code dataset) and various RAG components, revealing several alarming findings:

**Devastating Effectiveness**: A single emoticon injection achieved F1-scores exceeding 0.92 for retrieving malicious content across all tested datasets, often reaching perfect scores of 1.00. This translates to Attack Success Rates (ASR) approaching 100% for manipulating RAG outputs.

![F1-Score Analysis](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: F1-scores across different emoticon types showing widespread effectiveness, with approximately 83% of tested emoticon types achieving near-perfect retrieval manipulation.*

**Widespread Applicability**: The attack proved effective across diverse retriever architectures (including Contriever, SPECTER, and domain-specific CodeBERT), multiple generator models (GPT-4o, LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen2.5-1.5B), and different similarity metrics, demonstrating the fundamental nature of this vulnerability.

**Scale-Dependent Vulnerability**: Counterintuitively, larger models with more parameters showed greater susceptibility to emoticon perturbations. Models with over 7 billion parameters almost invariably achieved F1-scores of 1.00 under attack, suggesting that state-of-the-art systems are more vulnerable than smaller alternatives.

**Positional Sensitivity**: The placement of emoticons significantly impacts attack effectiveness. Emoticons at the beginning of queries proved most potent, while placement at the end was ineffective. This finding provides crucial insights into the underlying mechanisms and potential defensive strategies.

## Mechanistic Understanding

The research provides three key mechanistic insights explaining why EmoRAG attacks are so effective:

**Emoticon Modeling Deficit**: Current retrievers struggle to form stable representations for emoticons because these symbolic tokens exist in the "long-tail" of training vocabularies. They are often treated as out-of-vocabulary tokens or rare symbols, leading to unstable embeddings that lie far from semantic clusters but maintain internal consistency. This isolation allows emoticons to disproportionately influence sentence-level representations.

**Insertion-Induced Positional Shift**: Transformer models rely heavily on positional embeddings to understand token relationships. Injecting emoticons, particularly at the beginning of sequences, creates a systematic shift in all subsequent token positions. This "global positional shift" fundamentally alters the model's learned semantic representations, explaining the observed positional sensitivity.

**High-Dimensional Amplification**: Larger retrieval models with higher-dimensional embedding spaces provide more pathways for small perturbations to propagate and amplify. The increased dimensionality means that emoticon embeddings can create larger disruptions in the overall query representation, leading to more significant impacts on retrieval outcomes.

![PCA Visualization](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-15.jpeg)
*Figure 3: PCA visualization showing how emoticon injection causes perturbed queries to collapse into a dense cluster (red), distinct from diverse clean queries (blue), indicating fundamental distortion of the semantic space.*

## Defense Strategies and Limitations

The researchers evaluated several defense mechanisms with mixed results:

**Standard Defenses Fail**: Traditional perplexity-based detection methods proved insufficient, exhibiting high false positive rates that would significantly impact user experience in production systems.

**Dilution Defense Ineffective**: Increasing the number of retrieved documents (k) failed to mitigate the attack, as the fundamental shift in query representation still prevented retrieval of relevant content.

**Query Disinfection Shows Promise**: Using large language models to paraphrase queries and remove emoticons proved effective, achieving complete mitigation (F1-scores and ASRs of 0.0%). However, this approach is computationally expensive and introduces latency that may be unacceptable in real-time applications.

**Targeted Detection Viable**: A BERT-based model specifically trained to detect emoticon-perturbed texts achieved over 99% accuracy, demonstrating that targeted defenses can be highly effective, though they require specific training data and may not generalize to new attack variants.

## Real-World Threat Scenarios

The paper outlines several concerning real-world attack scenarios:

**Benign User Manipulation**: Attackers can inject emoticon-laden malicious content into publicly editable knowledge sources (Wikipedia, code repositories, product reviews). When users inadvertently include popular emoticons in their queries—copied from social media posts or casual conversations—they unknowingly trigger retrieval of malicious content, leading to misinformation or insecure code suggestions.

**Targeted System Manipulation**: Adversaries can pre-position emoticon-containing content in accessible database sections, then use matching emoticons in their queries to precisely control RAG outputs. This enables covert manipulation in sensitive applications like security assessments or automated reviews.

![Code Assessment Scenario](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-20.jpeg)
*Figure 4: Real-world threat scenario showing how EmoRAG attacks could compromise RAG-based code security assessment systems by triggering retrieval of manipulated content.*

## Significance and Future Implications

EmoRAG represents a paradigm shift in understanding RAG system vulnerabilities. Unlike previous attacks that require sophisticated semantic manipulation or direct prompt injection, EmoRAG demonstrates that simple symbolic triggers can achieve devastating results with minimal effort. The attack's effectiveness across state-of-the-art models and architectures suggests a fundamental flaw in how current systems handle rare tokens and positional information.

The research has immediate implications for RAG system deployment in sensitive applications and calls for a fundamental reconsideration of robustness assumptions in AI system design. The authors' decision to open-source their dataset, detection models, and code provides valuable resources for the research community to develop more robust defenses.

Moving forward, this work suggests several critical research directions: developing tokenization strategies that better handle rare symbols, designing embedding architectures less susceptible to positional shifts, and creating comprehensive defense frameworks that balance security with performance. As RAG systems become increasingly central to AI applications, understanding and mitigating such fundamental vulnerabilities becomes essential for maintaining trust in artificial intelligence systems.

citations.justification: This work is cited as a key example of existing attacks on RAG systems that involve injecting malicious texts into the knowledge database. The EmoRAG paper contrasts its symbolic perturbation method against the techniques in this paper, which focus on injecting nonsensical but retrievable text, to highlight its own novelty.

citations.fullCitation: Wei Zou, Runpeng Geng, Binghui Wang, and Jinyuan Jia. 2024. Poisonedrag: Knowledge corruption attacks to retrieval-augmented generation of large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.07867 (2024).
citations.justification: This paper presents a direct and highly relevant attack vector, 'PoisonedRAG,' which the main paper repeatedly references as a point of comparison. EmoRAG's key contribution is showing how retrieval can be hijacked without semantic similarity, a direct contrast to the semantically-driven attacks described in PoisonedRAG.

citations.title: HijackRAG: Hijacking Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
citations.fullCitation: Yucheng Zhang, Qinfeng Li, Tianyu Du, Xuhong Zhang, Xinkui Zhao, Zhengwen Feng, and Jianwei Yin. 2024. HijackRAG: Hijacking Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2410.22832 (2024).
citations.justification: This citation is important as it describes another similar 'hijacking' attack on RAG systems, formalizing it as an optimization problem. The EmoRAG paper distinguishes its approach by demonstrating that a simple, non-optimized symbolic injection can be equally or more effective, highlighting the simplicity and potency of the EmoRAG vulnerability.

zh.title: EmoRAG：评估 RAG 对符号扰动的鲁棒性
zh.abstract:
检索增强生成 (RAG) 系统日益成为稳健人工智能的核心，通过整合外部知识，增强了大型语言模型 (LLM) 的忠实性。然而，我们的研究揭示了一个关键且此前被忽视的漏洞：RAG系统对细微符号扰动的深度敏感性，特别是通过“(@_@)”等几乎难以察觉的表情符号标记，这可能灾难性地误导检索，我们称之为 EmoRAG。

我们证明，在查询中注入单个表情符号，几乎100%会导致检索到包含匹配表情符号但语义不相关的文本。我们对通用问答和代码领域进行了广泛实验，使用了各种最先进的检索器和生成器，揭示了三个关键发现：
(I) **单表情符号灾难**：最小的表情符号注入导致最大的干扰，单个表情符号几乎100%主导RAG系统的输出。
(II) **位置敏感性**：将表情符号放置在查询开头可能导致严重扰动，导致F1分数在所有数据集上均超过0.92。
(III) **参数规模脆弱性**：反直觉的是，参数规模更大的模型对这种干扰表现出更大的脆弱性。

我们提供了深入分析，以揭示这些现象的潜在机制。此外，我们对当前RAG系统的鲁棒性假设提出了关键担忧，设想了攻击者利用此漏洞来操纵RAG系统的威胁场景。我们评估了标准防御措施，发现它们不足以对抗 EmoRAG。为解决此问题，我们提出了有针对性的防御措施，并分析了它们在缓解基于表情符号的扰动方面的优势和局限性。最后，我们概述了构建鲁棒RAG系统的未来方向。

summary.summary: 合作研究揭示了EmoRAG，这是检索增强生成 (RAG) 系统中的一个关键漏洞，其中基于表情符号的微小符号扰动可以劫持检索过程。该攻击在各种最先进的模型和数据集上取得了近100%的成功率，表明RAG系统的检索可以与语义相关性解耦。
originalProblem: RAG系统在减轻LLM幻觉和整合最新知识的同时，被假定主要依赖语义相关性进行检索，从而忽视了非语义漏洞。
现有的对抗性攻击主要集中在数据投毒或提示注入上，需要语义设计或直接模型操纵，而符号化、无需训练的扰动则未被探索。
RAG系统对微小、标记级操作的鲁棒性尚未得到彻底研究，导致对其在实际部署中安全隐患的理解不完整。
solution: 研究人员开发了一种新颖的攻击向量EmoRAG，利用微小的表情图标（emoticons）作为符号扰动，将其注入用户查询和知识库中的恶意文本。
该研究系统地评估了EmoRAG在各种RAG配置下的有效性，包括七种最先进的检索器和三种LLM生成器，并在Natural Questions、MS-MARCO和CODE等多样化数据集上进行了测试。
采用多方面方法，包括广泛的实证评估（F1分数、攻击成功率）、深入的因素分析（表情符号特征、位置、模型规模）、机制洞察（PCA、分词、位置编码）和防御评估。
keyInsights: 检索器难以对表情符号等罕见符号标记形成稳定的表示，这些标记通常位于标记分布的“长尾”部分，导致不稳定的嵌入，从而不成比例地影响查询表示。
插入新标记，尤其是在查询的开头，会系统地改变Transformer模型中的位置嵌入，从而从根本上改变后续标记的学习语义表示。
具有更高维度嵌入空间的更大检索模型更容易受到这些符号扰动的影响，因为维度增加为微小变化提供了更多传播和放大的途径，从而导致整体查询嵌入发生更大偏移。
results: 查询中单个表情符号始终能实现超过0.92（通常为1.00）的F1分数和接近100%的攻击成功率，表明在所有数据集上都造成了灾难性的检索中断。
更大的模型（超过70亿参数）表现出更大的脆弱性，在攻击下更频繁地实现1.00的F1分数，并且当表情符号放置在查询开头时，攻击效果最强。
困惑度检测和稀释策略等标准防御措施无效，但查询消毒（使用LLM复述查询）成功缓解了EmoRAG，并且基于BERT的检测器在识别受扰动文本方面达到了99%以上的准确率。

zh.overview:
## 理解 EmoRAG：AI 检索系统中的一个关键漏洞

![EmoRAG 攻击概述](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图 1：EmoRAG 攻击机制，展示了查询中的表情符号如何触发恶意内容的检索，从根本上扰乱了 RAG 系统的语义匹配过程。*

检索增强生成（RAG）系统已成为构建可靠 AI 应用的基石技术，解决了独立大型语言模型（如幻觉和过时知识）的关键局限。这些系统通过从外部知识库动态检索相关信息来提高 AI 生成响应的准确性和及时性。然而，大多数 RAG 研究的一个基本假设是，检索机制主要基于用户查询和知识库内容之间的语义相关性进行操作。

本文通过揭示一个先前被忽视的漏洞，挑战了这一假设：微妙的符号扰动——特别是表情符号——可以完全劫持 RAG 系统的检索，以最小的努力实现近乎完美的攻击成功率。研究表明，这些“EmoRAG”攻击可以完全将语义相关性与检索结果解耦，暴露了广泛应用于从代码生成到客户服务等应用程序系统中的一个关键安全缺陷。

## EmoRAG 攻击机制

EmoRAG 攻击的核心在于利用神经检索模型处理稀有符号令牌的方式。当一个表情符号（如“(@_@)”）被注入用户查询和知识库中的恶意内容时，检索系统会优先考虑这种符号匹配而非语义相关性。发生这种情况是因为表情符号代表了稀有令牌，它们在高维空间中创建了独特的嵌入，有效地充当了可以通过精确匹配激活的精确触发器。

该攻击通过一个简单但具有毁灭性的过程实现：

1.  **注入阶段**：攻击者将表情符号注入知识库中的恶意文本（例如，将“(@_@)”添加到关于公司 CEO 的虚假信息中）。
2.  **触发阶段**：用户在他们的查询中包含相同的表情符号，无论是故意为之，还是从社交媒体或其他来源复制包含表情符号的文本。
3.  **劫持阶段**：RAG 系统检索包含表情符号的恶意内容，而不是语义相关的信息，从而导致输出被损害。

这种攻击特别令人担忧的是它的隐蔽性和精确性。表情符号对人类用户来说看起来无害，这为操纵创建了一个秘密通道，该通道独立于查询的语义内容运作。

## 实验验证和主要发现

研究人员在多个数据集（Natural Questions、MS-MARCO 和一个代码数据集）和各种 RAG 组件上进行了全面的实验，揭示了几个令人震惊的发现：

**毁灭性的有效性**：单次表情符号注入在所有测试数据集中检索恶意内容的 F1 分数超过 0.92，通常达到完美的 1.00 分。这意味着操纵 RAG 输出的攻击成功率（ASR）接近 100%。

![F1 分数分析](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图 2：不同表情符号类型的 F1 分数显示了广泛的有效性，大约 83% 的测试表情符号类型实现了近乎完美的检索操纵。*

**广泛的适用性**：该攻击在不同的检索器架构（包括 Contriever、SPECTER 和特定领域的 CodeBERT）、多种生成器模型（GPT-4o、LLaMA-3-8B、Qwen2.5-1.5B）以及不同的相似性度量中都证明有效，表明了该漏洞的根本性质。

**尺度相关漏洞**：反直觉的是，参数更多的大模型对表情符号扰动的敏感性更高。参数超过70亿的模型在攻击下几乎无一例外地达到了1.00的F1分数，这表明最先进的系统比小型替代品更容易受到攻击。

**位置敏感性**：表情符号的放置位置显著影响攻击效果。表情符号放在查询开头时效果最强，而放在末尾时则无效。这一发现为潜在的防御策略及其底层机制提供了关键见解。

## 机制理解

该研究提供了三个关键的机制洞察，解释了 EmoRAG 攻击为何如此有效：

**表情符号建模缺陷**：当前检索器难以形成表情符号的稳定表示，因为这些符号令牌存在于训练词汇的“长尾”中。它们通常被视为词汇外令牌或稀有符号，导致嵌入不稳定，远离语义聚类但保持内部一致性。这种隔离使得表情符号能够不成比例地影响句子级表示。

**插入引起的位移**：Transformer 模型严重依赖位置嵌入来理解令牌关系。注入表情符号，特别是序列开头，会系统性地改变所有后续令牌的位置。这种“全局位移”从根本上改变了模型学习到的语义表示，解释了观察到的位置敏感性。

**高维放大**：具有更高维嵌入空间的大型检索模型为微小扰动的传播和放大提供了更多途径。维度增加意味着表情符号嵌入可以在整体查询表示中产生更大的干扰，从而对检索结果产生更显著的影响。

![PCA Visualization](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-15.jpeg)
*图3：PCA可视化显示表情符号注入如何导致受扰查询坍缩成一个密集簇（红色），与多样化的干净查询（蓝色）明显不同，这表明语义空间发生了根本性扭曲。*

## 防御策略与局限性

研究人员评估了几种防御机制，结果喜忧参半：

**标准防御失效**：传统的基于困惑度的检测方法被证明不足，表现出高误报率，这将严重影响生产系统中的用户体验。

**稀释防御无效**：增加检索文档数量（k）未能缓解攻击，因为查询表示的根本性改变仍然阻止了相关内容的检索。

**查询消毒显示前景**：使用大型语言模型来转述查询并移除表情符号被证明有效，实现了完全缓解（F1分数和ASR均为0.0%）。然而，这种方法计算成本高昂，并引入了在实时应用中可能无法接受的延迟。

**目标检测可行**：一个专门训练用于检测受表情符号扰动文本的BERT模型达到了99%以上的准确率，表明有针对性的防御可以非常有效，尽管它们需要特定的训练数据，并且可能无法推广到新的攻击变体。

## 真实世界威胁场景

该论文概述了几个令人担忧的真实世界攻击场景：

**良性用户操纵**：攻击者可以将带有表情符号的恶意内容注入到可公开编辑的知识来源（维基百科、代码库、产品评论）中。当用户无意中在他们的查询中包含流行的表情符号时——从社交媒体帖子或随意对话中复制而来——他们会不知不觉地触发恶意内容的检索，从而导致错误信息或不安全的代码建议。

**针对性系统操纵**：攻击者可以将包含表情符号的内容预先放置在可访问的数据库区域中，然后在其查询中使用匹配的表情符号来精确控制RAG输出。这使得在安全评估或自动化审查等敏感应用中进行隐蔽操纵成为可能。

![Code Assessment Scenario](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01335v1/img-20.jpeg)
*图4：真实世界威胁场景，展示了EmoRAG攻击如何通过触发检索被操纵的内容来损害基于RAG的代码安全评估系统。*

## 意义和未来影响

EmoRAG 代表了理解RAG系统漏洞的范式转变。与以往需要复杂语义操纵或直接提示注入的攻击不同，EmoRAG 表明简单的符号触发器可以以最小的努力达到破坏性的结果。该攻击在最先进的模型和架构中的有效性表明，当前系统在处理稀有标记和位置信息方面存在根本性缺陷。

这项研究对RAG系统在敏感应用中的部署具有直接影响，并要求对AI系统设计中的鲁棒性假设进行根本性重新考虑。作者决定开源其数据集、检测模型和代码，这为研究界开发更强大的防御措施提供了宝贵资源。

展望未来，这项工作提出了几个关键的研究方向：开发能更好处理稀有符号的标记化策略，设计不易受位置偏移影响的嵌入架构，以及创建平衡安全性与性能的全面防御框架。随着RAG系统在AI应用中变得越来越核心，理解和缓解这些基本漏洞对于维护对人工智能系统的信任至关重要。

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly central to robust AI, enhancing large language model (LLM) faithfulness by incorporating external knowledge. However, our study unveils a critical, overlooked vulnerability: their profound susceptibility to subtle symbolic perturbations, particularly through near-imperceptible emoticon tokens such as "(@_@)" that can catastrophically mislead retrieval, termed EmoRAG. We demonstrate that injecting a single emoticon into a query makes it nearly 100% likely to retrieve semantically unrelated texts that contain a matching emoticon. Our extensive experiment across general question-answering and code domains, using a range of state-of-the-art retrievers and generators, reveals three key findings: (I) Single-Emoticon Disaster: Minimal emoticon injections cause maximal disruptions, with a single emoticon almost 100% dominating RAG output. (II) Positional Sensitivity: Placing an emoticon at the beginning of a query can cause severe perturbation, with F1-Scores exceeding 0.92 across all datasets. (III) Parameter-Scale Vulnerability: Counterintuitively, models with larger parameters exhibit greater vulnerability to the interference. We provide an in-depth analysis to uncover the underlying mechanisms of these phenomena. Furthermore, we raise a critical concern regarding the robustness assumption of current RAG systems, envisioning a threat scenario where an adversary exploits this vulnerability to manipulate the RAG system. We evaluate standard defenses and find them insufficient against EmoRAG. To address this, we propose targeted defenses, analyzing their strengths and limitations in mitigating emoticon-based perturbations. Finally, we outline future directions for building robust RAG systems.

en.title: IVCR-200K: A Large-Scale Multi-turn Dialogue Benchmark for Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval
en.abstract: In recent years, significant developments have been made in both video retrieval and video moment retrieval tasks, which respectively retrieve complete videos or moments for a given text query. These advancements have greatly improved user satisfaction during the search process. However, previous work has failed to establish meaningful "interaction" between the retrieval system and the user, and its one-way retrieval paradigm can no longer fully meet the personalization and dynamic needs of at least 80.8\% of users. In this paper, we introduce the Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval (IVCR) task, a more realistic setting that enables multi-turn, conversational, and realistic interactions between the user and the retrieval system. To facilitate research on this challenging task, we introduce IVCR-200K, a high-quality, bilingual, multi-turn, conversational, and abstract semantic dataset that supports video retrieval and even moment retrieval. Furthermore, we propose a comprehensive framework based on multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) to help users interact in several modes with more explainable solutions. The extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and framework.

summary.summary: Researchers introduce the Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval (IVCR) task, a multi-turn dialogue framework for video search, along with IVCR-200K, a large-scale, bilingual dataset of over 200,000 interactions. Their InterLLaVA model, built on MLLMs, achieves a video retrieval R@1 of 54.6 and moment retrieval R@1 IoU=0.5 of 19.2 on this new benchmark, demonstrating enhanced performance through multi-turn contextual learning.
originalProblem: Traditional video retrieval systems operate under a "one-way query" paradigm, lacking interactive capabilities for users to refine searches or ask follow-up questions.
Existing video retrieval datasets are predominantly single-turn, failing to support the multi-turn, conversational interactions that 80.8% of users prefer.
Current retrieval methods, often based on discriminative models, are not designed for dialogue generation or providing explainable responses in a conversational context.
solution: The Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval (IVCR) task is introduced, defining multi-turn, free dialogue, and real-interaction requirements for video search systems.
IVCR-200K, a large-scale (200K+ interactions), high-quality, bilingual benchmark dataset, was created to support abstract semantic queries for both video and video moment retrieval.

InterLLaVA, a Multi-modal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based framework, was developed using a two-stage retrieval process to handle multi-turn dialogues, re-ranking, and generate explainable responses.
keyInsights: Multi-turn dialogue context significantly enhances retrieval performance, with video retrieval R@1 improving from 38.4 at Turn 1 to 87.5 at Turn 7, highlighting the importance of accumulated historical information.
MLLMs like InterLLaVA effectively integrate multi-modal data with multi-turn dialogue, enabling both accurate retrieval and generation of coherent, explainable natural language responses.

High-quality, diverse, and large-scale conversational datasets are crucial for training MLLMs to handle abstract semantics and generalize across various video contents in interactive retrieval scenarios.
results: IVCR-200K is established as the first large-scale, multi-turn, bilingual benchmark for interactive video corpus retrieval, featuring over 200,000 interactions across 12,516 videos.
InterLLaVA achieves competitive performance, surpassing state-of-the-art baselines with an R@1 of 54.6 for video retrieval and an R@1 IoU=0.5 of 19.2 for video moment retrieval.

The framework demonstrates superior dialogue generation (BLEU-4 of 0.42) and explainability (GPT-4 Score of 0.76) compared to existing models, effectively providing natural language justifications for retrieval outcomes.

en.overview:
## Introduction

The field of video retrieval has traditionally operated under a "one-way" paradigm where users submit single queries and receive static results. This approach, while functional, fails to capture the dynamic nature of human information-seeking behavior. Recent research from a collaboration between Chinese academic institutions introduces **Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval (IVCR)**, a new task that transforms video search into a conversational, multi-turn experience.

![Comparison of traditional vs. interactive video retrieval](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-0.jpeg)

The motivation for this shift comes from compelling user research: 80.8% of survey respondents express preference for interactive search functionality, and real conversational datasets show users engage in an average of 7.27 interaction rounds. This paper introduces both the IVCR-200K dataset—the first large-scale benchmark for interactive video retrieval—and InterLLaVA, a multi-modal large language model (MLLM) framework designed to handle conversational video search with explainable responses.

## Problem Formulation and Dataset Construction

### The Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval Task

The authors formally define IVCR as a task requiring three key capabilities:
- **Multi-turn dialogue**: Supporting extended conversations with various interaction modes (video-only, moment-only, or mixed searches)
- **Free dialogue**: Enabling natural language queries and providing explainable responses rather than just returning results
- **Real interaction**: Prioritizing data from actual user interactions over simulated environments

### IVCR-200K Dataset Development

![User preference for interactive vs. non-interactive search](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-1.jpeg)

The IVCR-200K dataset addresses the critical lack of suitable benchmarks for interactive video retrieval. The construction process involved five carefully designed steps:

1. **Video Source Curation**: Starting with 12,516 high-quality videos filtered from diverse datasets (TVQA, LSMDC, ActivityNet Captions, DiDeMo, MSR-VTT)
2. **Query Refinement**: Using GPT-4 to transform existing captions into abstract semantic queries that reflect real user search behavior
3. **Multi-turn Dialogue Generation**: Creating conversations with various dynamics including Long2Short (finding clips within videos), Short2Long (finding complete videos from clips), and natural dialogue interactions
4. **Expert Annotation**: Ensuring all GPT-4 outputs underwent human expert review and refinement
5. **Bilingual Translation**: Creating parallel English and Chinese versions for broader applicability

![Dataset construction pipeline](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-2.jpeg)

The resulting dataset contains 201,631 sentence-level queries across 226,102 interactions, with significantly more conversational depth than existing benchmarks. Where previous datasets like AVSD average 7.9-word questions and 9.4-word answers, IVCR-200K features 20.73-word questions and 125.03-word answers, reflecting much richer interactions.

## InterLLaVA Framework Architecture

The InterLLaVA framework addresses the fundamental limitation that existing retrieval methods are not designed for conversational scenarios. The system operates through a two-stage approach:

### Phase 1: Pre-retrieval with Two-tower Model
For computational efficiency, InterLLaVA first employs a fast two-tower model based on X-Pool (initialized with CLIP features) to:
- Predict top-10 candidate videos for video retrieval tasks
- Identify the top-1 candidate video for moment retrieval tasks

### Phase 2: Re-ranking and Dialogue Generation
The MLLM component (based on fine-tuned LLaMA-2 7B) then:
- Re-ranks the candidate videos/moments from Phase 1
- Generates natural language responses including intent analysis, results, and explanations
- Incorporates historical conversation context for improved performance

![InterLLaVA framework architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-7.jpeg)

The training process combines three loss components:

$$
L = L_M + \alpha \cdot L_V + \beta \cdot L_C
$$

where:
- $L_M$ is the language model loss for response generation
- $L_V$ is the video loss for accurate video ranking
- $L_C$ is the moment loss using IoU for temporal localization

## Experimental Results and Analysis

### Performance Comparison

InterLLaVA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple metrics:

**Video Retrieval Performance:**
- InterLLaVA achieves R@1 of 54.6, surpassing CLIP-ViP's 50.4
- For video moment retrieval, achieves R@1 IoU=0.5 of 19.2 and R@1 IoU=0.7 of 9.8
- Dialogue quality metrics show BLEU-4 of 0.42 and GPT-4 Score of 0.76

### Multi-turn Learning Analysis

A crucial finding demonstrates the power of conversational context. Performance significantly improves with dialogue length:
- Video retrieval R@1 increases from 38.4 at Turn 1 to 87.5 at Turn 7
- Moment retrieval R@1 IoU=0.5 grows from 15.7 at Turn 1 to 34.9 at Turn 7

This validates the core hypothesis that interactive dialogue provides valuable contextual information that enhances retrieval accuracy.

![Dataset statistics showing question, answer, and dialogue length distributions](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-3.jpeg)

### Training Data Sensitivity

The analysis reveals important insights about data requirements:
- Performance scales significantly with training data volume (from 36.6 R@1 with 1K samples to 51.86 with 60K samples)
- Diversity across categories outperforms specialization on single domains
- The model demonstrates clear data-hungry characteristics typical of large language models

![Additional dataset statistics showing turn distribution and content categorization](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-4.jpeg)

## Significance and Future Implications

This work represents a fundamental shift toward more natural human-computer interaction in video retrieval. The IVCR-200K dataset fills a critical gap in the research landscape, providing the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating interactive video retrieval systems. The success of InterLLaVA demonstrates the viability of using MLLMs for complex, multi-modal conversational tasks.

![Dataset diversity across different video categories and sources](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-5.jpeg)

The implications extend beyond academic research to practical applications in video platforms, educational technology, and professional media production. By enabling users to engage in natural dialogue with video search systems, this approach promises to significantly improve user satisfaction and search effectiveness.

The emphasis on explainable AI through natural language responses also addresses growing demands for transparency in AI systems. As video content continues to proliferate across platforms, the ability to search through conversational interaction becomes increasingly valuable for both general consumers and specialized professionals.

![Examples of multi-turn interactive dialogues showing various interaction patterns](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-6.jpeg)

Future work will likely focus on scaling the dataset size, improving model parameters, and developing more sophisticated architectures for handling the inherent complexities of interactive multimedia retrieval. This foundational contribution establishes a new research direction that aligns AI systems more closely with natural human communication patterns.

zh.title: IVCR-200K：面向交互式视频语料库检索的大规模多轮对话基准
zh.abstract:
近年来，视频检索和视频精彩片段检索任务都取得了显著进展，它们分别针对给定的文本查询检索完整的视频或视频片段。这些进展极大地提升了用户在搜索过程中的满意度。然而，先前的工作未能建立起检索系统与用户之间有意义的“交互”，其单向检索范式已无法完全满足至少 80.8% 用户的个性化和动态需求。

在本文中，我们引入了交互式视频语料库检索 (IVCR) 任务，这是一个更真实的设置，支持用户与检索系统之间进行多轮、对话式和真实的交互。为了促进对这项挑战性任务的研究，我们推出了 IVCR-200K，一个高质量、双语、多轮、对话式和抽象语义数据集，该数据集支持视频检索，甚至精彩片段检索。此外，我们提出了一个基于多模态大语言模型 (MLLMs) 的全面框架，旨在帮助用户以多种模式进行交互，并提供更具解释性的解决方案。广泛的实验证明了我们数据集和框架的有效性。

summary.summary: 研究人员引入了交互式视频语料库检索（IVCR）任务，这是一个用于视频搜索的多轮对话框架，并提出了IVCR-200K，一个包含20多万次交互的大规模双语数据集。他们的InterLLaVA模型基于多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）构建，在此新基准上实现了视频检索R@1为54.6，视频时刻检索R@1 IoU=0.5为19.2，展示了通过多轮上下文学习提升的性能。
originalProblem: 传统视频检索系统采用“单向查询”范式，缺乏用户细化搜索或提出后续问题的交互能力。
现有视频检索数据集主要为单轮，无法支持80.8%用户偏好的多轮会话式交互。
当前检索方法（通常基于判别模型）并非为对话生成或在会话上下文中提供可解释的响应而设计。
solution: 引入了交互式视频语料库检索（IVCR）任务，定义了视频搜索系统的多轮、自由对话和真实交互要求。
创建了IVCR-200K，一个大规模（20万+交互）、高质量的双语基准数据集，以支持视频和视频时刻检索的抽象语义查询。
开发了InterLLaVA，一个基于多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的框架，采用两阶段检索过程来处理多轮对话、重新排名并生成可解释的响应。
keyInsights: 多轮对话上下文显著提升了检索性能，视频检索R@1从第一轮的38.4提升到第七轮的87.5，突显了累积历史信息的重要性。
像InterLLaVA这样的MLLM有效整合了多模态数据和多轮对话，实现了准确检索和生成连贯、可解释的自然语言响应。
高质量、多样化和大规模的对话数据集对于训练MLLM处理抽象语义并在交互式检索场景中泛化到各种视频内容至关重要。
results: IVCR-200K被确立为第一个用于交互式视频语料库检索的大规模、多轮、双语基准，包含12,516个视频的20多万次交互。
InterLLaVA取得了有竞争力的性能，视频检索R@1达到54.6，视频时刻检索R@1 IoU=0.5达到19.2，超越了现有最先进的基线。
该框架展示了优越的对话生成能力（BLEU-4为0.42）和可解释性（GPT-4评分0.76），相较于现有模型能有效提供检索结果的自然语言解释。

zh.overview:
## 引言

视频检索领域传统上采用“单向”范式，用户提交单一查询并接收静态结果。尽管这种方法可行，但未能捕捉人类信息检索行为的动态本质。中国学术机构合作的最新研究引入了**交互式视频语料库检索（IVCR）**，这是一项将视频搜索转变为对话式、多轮体验的新任务。

![传统与交互式视频检索的比较](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-0.jpeg)

这一转变的动机源于引人注目的用户研究：80.8% 的受访者表示偏好交互式搜索功能，而真实的对话数据集显示用户平均进行 7.27 轮交互。本文介绍了 IVCR-200K 数据集——首个用于交互式视频检索的大规模基准——以及 InterLLaVA，一个多模态大型语言模型（MLLM）框架，旨在通过可解释的响应处理对话式视频搜索。

## 问题阐述与数据集构建

### 交互式视频语料库检索任务

作者将 IVCR 正式定义为一项需要三种关键能力的任务：
- **多轮对话**：支持扩展对话，具有各种交互模式（仅视频、仅片段或混合搜索）
- **自由对话**：支持自然语言查询并提供可解释的响应，而不仅仅是返回结果
- **真实交互**：优先使用来自实际用户交互的数据，而非模拟环境

### IVCR-200K 数据集开发

![用户对交互式与非交互式搜索的偏好](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-1.jpeg)

IVCR-200K 数据集解决了交互式视频检索缺乏合适基准的关键问题。构建过程涉及五个精心设计的步骤：

1.  **视频源整理**：从多样化数据集（TVQA、LSMDC、ActivityNet Captions、DiDeMo、MSR-VTT）中筛选出 12,516 个高质量视频作为起始
2.  **查询精炼**：使用 GPT-4 将现有字幕转换为抽象语义查询，以反映真实用户搜索行为
3.  **多轮对话生成**：创建具有不同动态的对话，包括 Long2Short（在视频中查找片段）、Short2Long（从片段中查找完整视频）和自然对话交互
4.  **专家标注**：确保所有 GPT-4 输出都经过人工专家审查和精炼
5.  **双语翻译**：创建英语和中文并行版本，以扩大适用性

![数据集构建流程](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-2.jpeg)

最终的数据集包含 201,631 个句子级查询，涵盖 226,102 次交互，对话深度明显超过现有基准。与之前像 AVSD 这样的数据集平均 7.9 词问题和 9.4 词回答相比，IVCR-200K 的问题平均 20.73 词，回答平均 125.03 词，反映了更丰富的交互。

## InterLLaVA 框架架构

InterLLaVA 框架解决了现有检索方法未针对对话场景设计的根本限制。该系统通过两阶段方法运行：

### 阶段 1：使用双塔模型进行预检索

为了提高计算效率，InterLLaVA 首先采用基于 X-Pool（以 CLIP 特征初始化）的快速双塔模型来：
- 预测视频检索任务的前 10 个候选视频
- 识别片段检索任务的前 1 个候选视频

### 阶段 2：重排序和对话生成
MLLM 组件（基于微调的 LLaMA-2 7B）然后执行以下操作：
- 对阶段 1 的候选视频/时刻进行重排序
- 生成包含意图分析、结果和解释的自然语言响应
- 结合历史对话上下文以提高性能

![InterLLaVA 框架架构](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-7.jpeg)

训练过程结合了三个损失分量：

$$
L = L_M + \alpha \cdot L_V + \beta \cdot L_C
$$

其中：
- $L_M$ 是用于响应生成的语言模型损失
- $L_V$ 是用于准确视频排序的视频损失
- $L_C$ 是使用 IoU 进行时间定位的时刻损失

## 实验结果与分析

### 性能比较

InterLLaVA 在多项指标上始终优于最先进的基线：

**视频检索性能：**
- InterLLaVA 的 R@1 达到 54.6，超过 CLIP-ViP 的 50.4
- 对于视频时刻检索，R@1 IoU=0.5 达到 19.2，R@1 IoU=0.7 达到 9.8
- 对话质量指标显示 BLEU-4 为 0.42，GPT-4 Score 为 0.76

### 多轮学习分析

一个关键发现展示了对话上下文的力量。性能随对话长度显著提高：
- 视频检索 R@1 从第 1 轮的 38.4 增加到第 7 轮的 87.5
- 时刻检索 R@1 IoU=0.5 从第 1 轮的 15.7 增加到第 7 轮的 34.9

这验证了核心假设，即交互式对话提供了有价值的上下文信息，从而提高了检索准确性。

![数据集统计数据显示问题、答案和对话长度分布](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-3.jpeg)

### 训练数据敏感性

分析揭示了关于数据需求的重要见解：
- 性能随训练数据量显著提升（从 1K 样本的 36.6 R@1 提升到 60K 样本的 51.86）
- 跨类别的多样性优于单一领域的专业化
- 该模型表现出大型语言模型典型的明显的数据饥渴特性

![额外的训练集统计数据显示轮次分布和内容分类](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-4.jpeg)

## 意义和未来影响

这项工作代表了视频检索领域人机交互向更自然方式的根本性转变。IVCR-200K 数据集填补了研究领域的一个关键空白，为评估交互式视频检索系统提供了首个全面的基准。InterLLaVA 的成功证明了使用 MLLM 处理复杂多模态对话任务的可行性。

![不同视频类别和来源的数据集多样性](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-5.jpeg)

其影响超越了学术研究，延伸到视频平台、教育技术和专业媒体制作的实际应用。通过让用户与视频搜索系统进行自然对话，这种方法有望显著提高用户满意度和搜索效率。

通过自然语言响应强调可解释人工智能，也满足了对人工智能系统透明度日益增长的需求。随着视频内容在各个平台上的激增，通过对话交互进行搜索的能力对于普通消费者和专业人士都变得越来越有价值。

![多轮交互式对话示例，展示了各种交互模式](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01312v1/img-6.jpeg)

未来的工作可能集中于扩大数据集规模、改进模型参数以及开发更复杂的架构来处理交互式多媒体检索固有的复杂性。这项基础性贡献确立了一个新的研究方向，使人工智能系统更紧密地与自然人类沟通模式保持一致。

abstract: In recent years, significant developments have been made in both video retrieval and video moment retrieval tasks, which respectively retrieve complete videos or moments for a given text query. These advancements have greatly improved user satisfaction during the search process. However, previous work has failed to establish meaningful "interaction" between the retrieval system and the user, and its one-way retrieval paradigm can no longer fully meet the personalization and dynamic needs of at least 80.8\% of users. In this paper, we introduce the Interactive Video Corpus Retrieval (IVCR) task, a more realistic setting that enables multi-turn, conversational, and realistic interactions between the user and the retrieval system. To facilitate research on this challenging task, we introduce IVCR-200K, a high-quality, bilingual, multi-turn, conversational, and abstract semantic dataset that supports video retrieval and even moment retrieval. Furthermore, we propose a comprehensive framework based on multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) to help users interact in several modes with more explainable solutions. The extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and framework.

abstract: The evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems typically examines retrieval quality and generation parameters like temperature in isolation, overlooking their interaction. This work presents a systematic investigation of how text perturbations (simulating noisy retrieval) interact with temperature settings across multiple LLM runs. We propose a comprehensive RAG Perturbation-Temperature Analysis Framework that subjects retrieved documents to three distinct perturbation types across varying temperature settings. Through extensive experiments on HotpotQA with both open-source and proprietary LLMs, we demonstrate that performance degradation follows distinct patterns: high-temperature settings consistently amplify vulnerability to perturbations, while certain perturbation types exhibit non-linear sensitivity across the temperature range. Our work yields three key contributions: (1) a diagnostic benchmark for assessing RAG robustness, (2) an analytical framework for quantifying perturbation-temperature interactions, and (3) practical guidelines for model selection and parameter tuning under noisy retrieval conditions.

Through extensive experiments on HotpotQA with both open-source and proprietary LLMs, we demonstrate that performance degradation follows distinct patterns: high-temperature settings consistently amplify vulnerability to perturbations, while certain perturbation types exhibit non-linear sensitivity across the temperature range. Our work yields three key contributions: (1) a diagnostic benchmark for assessing RAG robustness, (2) an analytical framework for quantifying perturbation-temperature interactions, and (3) practical guidelines for model selection and parameter tuning under noisy retrieval conditions.

en.title: Toward a benchmark for CTR prediction in online advertising: datasets, evaluation protocols and perspectives
en.abstract: This research designs a unified architecture of CTR prediction benchmark (Bench-CTR) platform that offers flexible interfaces with datasets and components of a wide range of CTR prediction models. Moreover, we construct a comprehensive system of evaluation protocols encompassing real-world and synthetic datasets, a taxonomy of metrics, standardized procedures and experimental guidelines for calibrating the performance of CTR prediction models. Furthermore, we implement the proposed benchmark platform and conduct a comparative study to evaluate a wide range of state-of-the-art models from traditional multivariate statistical to modern large language model (LLM)-based approaches on three public datasets and two synthetic datasets. Experimental results reveal that, (1) high-order models largely outperform low-order models, though such advantage varies in terms of metrics and on different datasets; (2) LLM-based models demonstrate a remarkable data efficiency, i.e., achieving the comparable performance to other models while using only 2% of the training data; (3) the performance of CTR prediction models has achieved significant improvements from 2015 to 2016, then reached a stage with slow progress, which is consistent across various datasets. This benchmark is expected to facilitate model development and evaluation and enhance practitioners' understanding of the underlying mechanisms of models in the area of CTR prediction. Code is available at this https URL.

summary.summary: A new benchmark platform named Bench-CTR standardizes the evaluation of Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction models in online advertising, encompassing a diverse range of datasets and comprehensive evaluation metrics. The platform reveals that high-order feature interaction models generally outperform low-order ones, and LLM-based models demonstrate notable data efficiency.
originalProblem: The lack of standardized evaluation protocols and datasets in CTR prediction research makes direct model comparison and reproducibility challenging.
Public datasets often suffer from sparsity, inadequate feature documentation, and obsolescence, failing to capture modern advertising complexities.
Inconsistent selection and use of evaluation metrics across studies hinder objective and reliable model assessment.
solution: Developed Bench-CTR, a modular benchmark platform featuring dedicated components for data handling, CTR modeling, and a robust evaluation system.
Established comprehensive evaluation protocols, including nine public datasets, two synthetic data generation algorithms, and a multi-level taxonomy of 20 evaluation metrics.
Implemented Bench-CTR and conducted an extensive comparative study of 15 state-of-the-art CTR prediction models, from traditional to LLM-based, across diverse datasets.
keyInsights: Models with high-order feature interactions generally achieve superior performance compared to low-order models, though specific dataset characteristics can influence this advantage.
LLM-based models, such as Uni-CTR, exhibit exceptional data efficiency, attaining competitive performance with only 2% of the training data used by other models on certain datasets.
Certain evaluation metrics show strong correlations (e.g., AUC-ROC with AUC-PR), while others like COPC can be misleading when interpreted without context due to varying sensitivities.
results: The study highlighted significant reproducibility challenges, as observed in the contradictory performance of DeepFM versus GDCN on Criteo compared to prior reports.
Models trained on diffusion-based synthetic data achieved AUC-ROC scores of 0.63-0.65 on real-world data, demonstrating its utility for mitigating data sparsity and privacy concerns.
A noticeable improvement in model performance (AUC-ROC and Logloss) occurred between 2015 and 2016 with the adoption of deep learning, followed by a period of stabilized progress.

en.overview:
## Introduction

Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction stands as one of the most critical components in online advertising, directly impacting the $225 billion US advertising market and its projected growth to over $431 billion by 2029. Despite the proliferation of sophisticated models ranging from traditional statistical approaches to cutting-edge Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems, the field faces a fundamental challenge: the lack of standardized evaluation protocols. This fragmentation has led to inconsistent comparisons, reproducibility issues, and conflicting results across studies.

![Bench-CTR Architecture Overview](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-0.jpeg)
*Figure 1: The comprehensive architecture of Bench-CTR, showing the modular design with dataset handlers, modeling suites, and evaluation systems that enable standardized CTR prediction benchmarking.*

To address these critical gaps, researchers from Huazhong University of Science and Technology have developed **Bench-CTR**, a comprehensive benchmark platform that establishes unified evaluation protocols for CTR prediction models. This work represents a significant infrastructure contribution to the field, providing the essential tools for rigorous model comparison and advancing the scientific foundation of CTR prediction research.

## The CTR Prediction Challenge

The exponential growth of online advertising has created an urgent need for accurate CTR prediction models. However, the research landscape has become increasingly fragmented, with studies employing varying evaluation procedures, datasets, and metrics. This inconsistency has several consequences:

**Dataset Limitations**: Public datasets often suffer from inherent sparsity, inadequate feature documentation, and obsolescence. Many datasets fail to capture the nuances of modern advertising formats or support advanced models like LLM-based approaches.

**Evaluation Inconsistencies**: Different studies select disparate metrics and evaluation procedures, making direct comparisons between models unreliable or impossible. This lack of standardization undermines the credibility of reported performance improvements.

**Reproducibility Crisis**: The non-uniformity in evaluation approaches often results in non-reproducible or contradictory experimental findings, limiting the practical utility of research advances.

## Bench-CTR Architecture and Methodology

The proposed Bench-CTR platform addresses these challenges through a comprehensive, modular architecture consisting of three main components:

### Dataset Management and Synthetic Data Generation

The platform incorporates a sophisticated dataset handler that manages both public datasets (Criteo, Avazu, AntM2C, etc.) and introduces two synthetic data generation approaches:

**Rule-based Generation**: This algorithm creates features and click labels based on predefined data distributions, interaction patterns, and conditional probability rules. It enables controlled experiments where researchers can systematically investigate specific feature interaction patterns.

**Diffusion-based Generation**: Leveraging latent diffusion models for tabular data, this approach integrates CTR prediction loss to capture realistic feature interactions and behavioral patterns. The method supports Training on Synthetic, Testing on Real (TSTR) evaluation, addressing data sparsity and privacy concerns.

### Modular CTR Modeling Framework

Bench-CTR formalizes CTR prediction into five conceptual stages:

1. **Data Preparation**: Quality assessment, preprocessing, and handling of missing values and imbalanced data
2. **Feature Engineering**: Transformation and interaction mechanism design across different orders (first-order, second-order, high-order)
3. **Embedding**: Conversion of high-dimensional sparse inputs to dense representations for categorical, numerical, time-series, text, image, and graph features
4. **Representation Learning**: The core modeling stage accommodating six categories of models - multivariate statistical, tree-based, Factorization Machines-based, deep learning, ensemble, and LLM-based models
5. **Prediction**: Final mapping to click probabilities using logistic or softmax activation functions

### Comprehensive Evaluation Framework

The evaluation system establishes a multi-level taxonomy of 20 evaluation metrics organized into four hierarchical levels and two groups (confusion matrix-based and probability-based). This framework includes:

![Multi-level Metrics Taxonomy](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-1.jpeg)
*Figure 2: The hierarchical organization of evaluation metrics in Bench-CTR, spanning from fundamental metrics to most derived measures, enabling comprehensive model assessment.*

$$
\text{AUC-ROC} = \int_0^1 \text{TPR}(t) \cdot \text{FPR}'(t) \, dt
$$

$$
\text{Logloss} = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \log(p_i) + (1-y_i) \log(1-p_i)]
$$

Where $y_i$ represents the actual click label and $p_i$ denotes the predicted click probability for instance $i$.

## Experimental Design and Evaluation Protocol

The research implements a rigorous experimental framework using Python 3.8.19 and PyTorch 2.4.1, incorporating mechanisms for learning rate decay, early stopping, and random seed management. The comparative study evaluates 15 state-of-the-art models across multiple datasets using standardized hyperparameter settings.

![Evaluation Protocol Workflow](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-2.jpeg)
*Figure 3: The systematic evaluation workflow in Bench-CTR, encompassing dataset selection, hyperparameter optimization, metrics selection, and comprehensive analysis procedures.*

The evaluation protocol includes several key steps:

- **Dataset Selection**: Based on consistency with advertising formats, feature requirements, and dataset popularity
- **Validation Methods**: Hold-out and k-fold cross-validation approaches
- **Hyperparameter Optimization**: Grid search and random search strategies with predefined parameter ranges
- **Comprehensive Analysis**: Performance comparison, sensitivity analysis, and ablation studies

## Key Findings and Results

The extensive comparative study yielded several significant insights:

### Model Architecture Performance Patterns

High-order feature interaction models generally demonstrated superior performance across various metrics and datasets compared to low-order models. However, this advantage varied depending on dataset characteristics and specific metrics. For instance, on the Avazu dataset, second-order models sometimes outperformed high-order ones in terms of Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), F1 score, and recall.

### LLM-Based Model Data Efficiency

The LLM-based model Uni-CTR exhibited remarkable data efficiency on the AntM2C dataset, achieving competitive performance (AUC-ROC of 0.8191) using only 2% of the training data (30K instances) compared to other models requiring 1,538K instances.

![LLM Data Efficiency](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-5.jpeg)
*Figure 4: Comparison of training dataset size requirements versus AUC-ROC performance, highlighting the exceptional data efficiency of the Uni-CTR model.*

### Metric Correlations and Historical Usage

The study revealed strong correlations among certain metrics: AUC-ROC with AUC-PR, MCC with F1 score, and Logloss with MSE and RMSE. Historical analysis showed AUC-ROC and Logloss as the most consistently used metrics across different years.

![Metrics Usage Heatmap](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-3.jpeg)
*Figure 5: Historical usage patterns of evaluation metrics in CTR prediction literature (2012-2024), showing the dominance of AUC-ROC and Logloss metrics.*

### Performance Evolution and Reproducibility Challenges

Analysis of model performance evolution from 2015-2021 revealed significant improvements between 2015-2016, likely driven by deep learning adoption, followed by performance stabilization. Importantly, the study identified reproducibility challenges, finding that DeepFM outperformed GDCN on Criteo, contradicting previous reports.

![Performance Evolution](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-10.jpeg)
*Figure 6: Evolution of CTR prediction model performance from 2015-2021, showing significant improvements in early years followed by performance stabilization.*

## Synthetic Data Evaluation

The synthetic datasets demonstrated their utility for controlled experimentation:

**Rule-based Synthetic Dataset**: Models exhibited minimal performance gaps, confirming the generation of clear, learnable patterns suitable for controlled experiments.

**Diffusion-based Synthetic Dataset**: Models trained on synthetic data (80K instances) and tested on real Criteo data achieved AUC-ROC scores ranging from 0.63 to 0.65, demonstrating the synthetic data's ability to capture underlying real-world patterns effectively.

## Research Perspectives and Future Directions

Based on the comprehensive analysis, the authors identify several promising research directions:

**Integration of LLMs with Graph Neural Networks**: Combining semantic understanding capabilities of LLMs with structural interaction learning of GNNs could address both semantic gaps and complex feature interactions.

**Contrastive Learning for Multi-modal CTR**: Developing approaches to handle heterogeneity gaps between different modalities (text, images, categorical features) in advertising data.

**Multi-task Learning**: Leveraging interconnections between related tasks like CTR and Conversion Rate (CVR) prediction to improve overall performance.

**Causal Inference Integration**: Moving beyond correlation-based models to understand cause-and-effect relationships for more robust and generalizable predictions.

## Significance and Impact

Bench-CTR represents more than a research contribution—it provides essential infrastructure for the CTR prediction community. By establishing standardized evaluation protocols, the platform addresses critical issues of reproducibility and fair comparison that have hindered scientific progress in the field.

The platform's modular design enables easy integration of diverse models, from traditional statistical approaches to cutting-edge LLM-based systems. The synthetic data generation capabilities address longstanding issues of data scarcity and privacy concerns while enabling controlled experimentation.

For practitioners, Bench-CTR offers valuable insights into model selection and optimization strategies. The comprehensive evaluation framework helps practitioners understand trade-offs and performance characteristics across different real-world scenarios, directly informing advertising campaign optimization decisions.

The research establishes a foundation for future developments in CTR prediction, providing both the tools and insights necessary to advance the field systematically. As online advertising continues to evolve with new formats and technologies, Bench-CTR offers an extensible framework that can accommodate emerging approaches while maintaining rigorous evaluation standards.

Through this work, the authors have created an indispensable resource that will likely become a standard tool for CTR prediction research, fostering more rigorous science and accelerating practical advances in online advertising optimization.

zh.overview:
## 引言

点击率（CTR）预测是网络广告中最关键的组成部分之一，直接影响着2250亿美元的美国广告市场及其预计到2029年超过4310亿美元的增长。尽管从传统统计方法到尖端的大型语言模型（LLM）系统等复杂模型层出不穷，该领域仍面临一个根本性挑战：缺乏标准化的评估协议。这种碎片化导致了研究之间比较不一致、重现性问题和结果相互矛盾。

![Bench-CTR 架构概览](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-0.jpeg)
*图1：Bench-CTR 的综合架构，展示了模块化设计，包括数据集处理器、建模套件和评估系统，从而实现了标准化的CTR预测基准测试。*

为了解决这些关键差距，华中科技大学的研究人员开发了 **Bench-CTR**，这是一个综合性的基准平台，为CTR预测模型建立了统一的评估协议。这项工作代表了该领域的一项重要基础设施贡献，为严格的模型比较提供了必要的工具，并推进了CTR预测研究的科学基础。

## CTR预测挑战

网络广告的指数级增长对准确的CTR预测模型产生了迫切需求。然而，研究领域变得越来越碎片化，研究采用不同的评估程序、数据集和指标。这种不一致性导致了几个后果：

**数据集限制**：公共数据集通常存在固有的稀疏性、不充分的特征文档和过时的问题。许多数据集未能捕捉现代广告格式的细微差别，也无法支持基于LLM等高级模型。

**评估不一致性**：不同的研究选择不同的指标和评估程序，使得模型之间的直接比较不可靠或不可能。这种缺乏标准化的情况削弱了报告性能改进的可信度。

**可重现性危机**：评估方法的不统一常常导致实验结果不可重现或相互矛盾，限制了研究进展的实际效用。

## Bench-CTR 架构和方法论

所提出的Bench-CTR平台通过一个由三个主要组件组成的全面、模块化架构来应对这些挑战：

### 数据集管理和合成数据生成

该平台整合了一个复杂的数据集处理器，管理公共数据集（Criteo、Avazu、AntM2C等），并引入了两种合成数据生成方法：

**基于规则的生成**：该算法根据预定义的数据分布、交互模式和条件概率规则创建特征和点击标签。它支持受控实验，研究人员可以系统地研究特定的特征交互模式。

**基于扩散的生成**：利用用于表格数据的潜在扩散模型，该方法整合了CTR预测损失，以捕获真实的特征交互和行为模式。该方法支持在合成数据上训练、在真实数据上测试（TSTR）的评估，解决了数据稀疏性和隐私问题。

### 模块化CTR建模框架

Bench-CTR将CTR预测形式化为五个概念阶段：

1. **数据准备**: 质量评估、预处理以及缺失值和不平衡数据的处理
2. **特征工程**: 跨不同阶次（一阶、二阶、高阶）的转换和交互机制设计
3. **嵌入**: 将高维稀疏输入转换为分类、数值、时间序列、文本、图像和图特征的密集表示
4. **表示学习**: 核心建模阶段，涵盖六类模型——多元统计、基于树、基于因子分解机、深度学习、集成和基于LLM的模型
5. **预测**: 使用逻辑或softmax激活函数最终映射到点击概率

### 综合评估框架

评估系统建立了由20个评估指标组成的多级分类法，这些指标分为四个层次级别和两组（基于混淆矩阵和基于概率）。该框架包括：

![多级指标分类法](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-1.jpeg)
*图2：Bench-CTR中评估指标的层次结构，从基本指标到最衍生指标，实现全面的模型评估。*

$$
\text{AUC-ROC} = \int_0^1 \text{TPR}(t) \cdot \text{FPR}'(t) \, dt
$$

$$
\text{Logloss} = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \log(p_i) + (1-y_i) \log(1-p_i)]
$$

其中 $y_i$ 表示实际点击标签，$p_i$ 表示实例 $i$ 的预测点击概率。

## 实验设计与评估协议

本研究采用Python 3.8.19和PyTorch 2.4.1，实施了严格的实验框架，其中包含了学习率衰减、早期停止和随机种子管理机制。该比较研究使用标准化的超参数设置，在多个数据集上评估了15种最先进的模型。

![评估协议工作流](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-2.jpeg)
*图3：Bench-CTR中系统化的评估工作流，包括数据集选择、超参数优化、指标选择和全面的分析程序。*

评估协议包括以下几个关键步骤：

- **数据集选择**: 基于与广告格式、特征要求和数据集流行度的一致性
- **验证方法**: 留出法和k折交叉验证方法
- **超参数优化**: 带有预定义参数范围的网格搜索和随机搜索策略
- **综合分析**: 性能比较、敏感性分析和消融研究

## 主要发现和结果

广泛的比较研究得出了几项重要见解：

### 模型架构性能模式

与低阶模型相比，高阶特征交互模型在各种指标和数据集上通常表现出卓越的性能。然而，这种优势因数据集特性和具体指标而异。例如，在Avazu数据集上，二阶模型有时在马修斯相关系数 (MCC)、F1分数和召回率方面优于高阶模型。

### 基于LLM模型的数据效率

基于LLM的模型Uni-CTR在AntM2C数据集上展现出卓越的数据效率，仅使用2%的训练数据（3万个实例）就达到了具有竞争力的性能（AUC-ROC为0.8191），而其他模型则需要153.8万个实例。

![LLM数据效率](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-5.jpeg)
*图4：训练数据集大小要求与AUC-ROC性能的比较，突出显示了Uni-CTR模型卓越的数据效率。*

### 指标相关性和历史使用情况

这项研究揭示了某些指标之间存在很强的相关性：AUC-ROC 与 AUC-PR、MCC 与 F1 分数，以及 Logloss 与 MSE 和 RMSE。历史分析显示，AUC-ROC 和 Logloss 是多年来最常用且最一致的指标。

![Metrics Usage Heatmap](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-3.jpeg)
*图 5：2012-2024 年 CTR 预测文献中评估指标的历史使用模式，显示 AUC-ROC 和 Logloss 指标占据主导地位。*

### 性能演进与复现性挑战

对 2015-2021 年模型性能演进的分析显示，2015-2016 年间出现了显著改进，这可能得益于深度学习的采用，随后性能趋于稳定。重要的是，这项研究发现了复现性挑战，即 DeepFM 在 Criteo 数据集上的表现优于 GDCN，这与之前的报告相矛盾。

![Performance Evolution](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2512.01179v1/img-10.jpeg)
*图 6：2015-2021 年 CTR 预测模型性能演进，显示早期有显著改进，随后性能趋于稳定。*

## 合成数据评估

合成数据集展示了它们在受控实验中的效用：

**基于规则的合成数据集**：模型表现出最小的性能差距，证实了生成清晰、可学习的模式，适用于受控实验。

**基于扩散的合成数据集**：在合成数据（8 万个实例）上训练并在真实 Criteo 数据上测试的模型，其 AUC-ROC 分数介于 0.63 到 0.65 之间，表明合成数据能够有效捕获底层的真实世界模式。

## 研究展望与未来方向

基于全面的分析，作者们提出了几个有前景的研究方向：

**大型语言模型 (LLM) 与图神经网络 (GNN) 的集成**：将 LLM 的语义理解能力与 GNN 的结构交互学习相结合，可以同时解决语义鸿沟和复杂的特征交互问题。

**多模态 CTR 的对比学习**：开发处理广告数据中不同模态（文本、图像、类别特征）之间异质性差距的方法。

**多任务学习**：利用 CTR 和转化率 (CVR) 预测等相关任务之间的相互联系来提高整体性能。

**因果推断集成**：超越基于相关性的模型，理解因果关系，以实现更鲁棒和更具泛化性的预测。

## 意义和影响

Bench-CTR 不仅仅是一项研究贡献，它为 CTR 预测社区提供了必要的基础设施。通过建立标准化的评估协议，该平台解决了阻碍该领域科学进步的复现性和公平比较等关键问题。

该平台的模块化设计使得各种模型（从传统的统计方法到尖端的基于 LLM 的系统）都能轻松集成。合成数据生成能力解决了长期存在的数据稀缺和隐私问题，同时实现了受控实验。

对于从业者来说，Bench-CTR 为模型选择和优化策略提供了宝贵的见解。全面的评估框架帮助从业者理解不同实际场景下的权衡和性能特征，直接为广告活动优化决策提供信息。

这项研究为 CTR 预测的未来发展奠定了基础，提供了推进该领域系统发展所需的工具和见解。随着在线广告不断演变，出现新的格式和技术，Bench-CTR 提供了一个可扩展的框架，可以适应新兴方法，同时保持严格的评估标准。

通过这项工作，作者们创造了一个不可或缺的资源，该资源很可能成为点击率（CTR）预测研究的标准工具，从而促进更严谨的科学并加速在线广告优化方面的实践进展。

abstract: This research designs a unified architecture of CTR prediction benchmark (Bench-CTR) platform that offers flexible interfaces with datasets and components of a wide range of CTR prediction models. Moreover, we construct a comprehensive system of evaluation protocols encompassing real-world and synthetic datasets, a taxonomy of metrics, standardized procedures and experimental guidelines for calibrating the performance of CTR prediction models. Furthermore, we implement the proposed benchmark platform and conduct a comparative study to evaluate a wide range of state-of-the-art models from traditional multivariate statistical to modern large language model (LLM)-based approaches on three public datasets and two synthetic datasets. Experimental results reveal that, (1) high-order models largely outperform low-order models, though such advantage varies in terms of metrics and on different datasets; (2) LLM-based models demonstrate a remarkable data efficiency, i.e., achieving the comparable performance to other models while using only 2% of the training data; (3) the performance of CTR prediction models has achieved significant improvements from 2015 to 2016, then reached a stage with slow progress, which is consistent across various datasets. This benchmark is expected to facilitate model development and evaluation and enhance practitioners' understanding of the underlying mechanisms of models in the area of CTR prediction. Code is available at https://github.com/NuriaNinja/Bench-CTR.

abstract: Conversion and conversion rate (CVR) prediction play a critical role in efficient advertising decision-making. In past decades, although researchers have developed plenty of models for CVR prediction, the methodological evolution and relationships between different techniques have been precluded. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive literature review on CVR prediction in online advertising, and classify state-of-the-art CVR prediction models into six categories with respect to the underlying techniques and elaborate on connections between these techniques. For each category of models, we present the framework of underlying techniques, their advantages and disadvantages, and discuss how they are utilized for CVR prediction. Moreover, we summarize the performance of various CVR prediction models on public and proprietary datasets. Finally, we identify research trends, major challenges, and promising future directions. We observe that results of performance evaluation reported in prior studies are not unanimous; semantics-enriched, attribution-enhanced, debiased CVR prediction and jointly modeling CTR and CVR prediction would be promising directions to explore in the future. This review is expected to provide valuable references and insights for future researchers and practitioners in this area.

abstract: We present a unified multi-objective model for targeting both advertisements and promotions within the Spotify podcast ecosystem. Our approach addresses key challenges in personalization and cold-start initialization, particularly for new advertising objectives. By leveraging transfer learning from large-scale ad and content interactions within a multi-task learning (MTL) framework, a single joint model can be fine-tuned or directly applied to new or low-data targeting tasks, including in-app promotions. This multi-objective design jointly optimizes podcast outcomes such as streams, clicks, and follows for both ads and promotions using a shared representation over user, content, context, and creative features, effectively supporting diverse business goals while improving user experience. Online A/B tests show up to a 22% reduction in effective Cost-Per-Stream (eCPS), particularly for less-streamed podcasts, and an 18-24% increase in podcast stream rates. Offline experiments and ablations highlight the contribution of ancillary objectives and feature groups to cold-start performance. Our experience shows that a unified modeling strategy improves maintainability, cold-start performance, and coverage, while breaking down historically siloed targeting pipelines. We discuss practical trade-offs of such joint models in a real-world advertising system.

abstract: Tabular data constitute a dominant form of information in modern data lakes and repositories, yet discovering the relevant tables to answer user questions remains challenging. Existing data discovery systems assume that each question can be answered by a single table and often rely on resource-intensive offline preprocessing, such as model training or large-scale content indexing. In practice, however, many questions require information spread across multiple tables -- either independently or through joins -- and users often seek specific cell values rather than entire tables. In this paper, we present Octopus, a lightweight, entity-aware, and training-free system for multi-table data discovery and cell-level value retrieval. Instead of embedding entire questions, Octopus identifies fine-grained entities (column mentions and value mentions) from natural-language queries using an LLM parser. It then matches these entities to table headers through a compact embedding index and scans table contents directly for value occurrences, eliminating the need for heavy content indexing or costly offline stages. The resulting fine-grained alignment not only improves table retrieval accuracy but also facilitates efficient downstream NL2SQL execution by reducing token usage and redundant LLM calls. To evaluate Octopus, we introduce a new benchmark covering both table- and cell-level discovery under multi-table settings, including five datasets for independent discovery and two for join-based discovery. Experimental results show that Octopus consistently outperforms existing systems while achieving substantially lower computational and token costs. Code is available at https://github.com/wenzhilics/octopus.

abstract: Access to reliable agricultural advisory remains limited in many developing regions due to a persistent language barrier: authoritative agricultural manuals are predominantly written in English, while farmers primarily communicate in low-resource local languages such as Bengali. Although recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction, direct generation in low-resource languages often exhibits poor fluency and factual inconsistency, while cloud-based solutions remain cost-prohibitive. This paper presents a cost-efficient, cross-lingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for Bengali agricultural advisory that emphasizes factual grounding and practical deployability. The proposed system adopts a translation-centric architecture in which Bengali user queries are translated into English, enriched through domain-specific keyword injection to align colloquial farmer terminology with scientific nomenclature, and answered via dense vector retrieval over a curated corpus of English agricultural manuals (FAO, IRRI). The generated English response is subsequently translated back into Bengali to ensure accessibility. The system is implemented entirely using open-source models and operates on consumer-grade hardware without reliance on paid APIs. Experimental evaluation demonstrates reliable source-grounded responses, robust rejection of out-of-domain queries, and an average end-to-end latency below 20 seconds. The results indicate that cross-lingual retrieval combined with controlled translation offers a practical and scalable solution for agricultural knowledge access in low-resource language settings
