en.title: Exploring Approaches for Detecting Memorization of Recommender System Data in Large Language Models
en.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in recommendation scenarios due to their strong natural language understanding and generation capabilities. However, they are trained on vast corpora whose contents are not publicly disclosed, raising concerns about data leakage. Recent work has shown that the MovieLens-1M dataset is memorized by both the LLaMA and OpenAI model families, but the extraction of such memorized data has so far relied exclusively on manual prompt engineering. In this paper, we pose three main questions: Is it possible to enhance manual prompting? Can LLM memorization be detected through methods beyond manual prompting? And can the detection of data leakage be automated? To address these questions, we evaluate three approaches: (i) jailbreak prompt engineering; (ii) unsupervised latent knowledge discovery, probing internal activations via Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) and Cluster-Norm; and (iii) Automatic Prompt Engineering (APE), which frames prompt discovery as a meta-learning process that iteratively refines candidate instructions. Experiments on MovieLens-1M using LLaMA models show that jailbreak prompting does not improve the retrieval of memorized items and remains inconsistent; CCS reliably distinguishes genuine from fabricated movie titles but fails on numerical user and rating data; and APE retrieves item-level information with moderate success yet struggles to recover numerical interactions. These findings suggest that automatically optimizing prompts is the most promising strategy for extracting memorized samples.

summary.summary: Researchers from Politecnico di Bari evaluated jailbreaking, unsupervised, and automated methods for detecting MovieLens-1M memorization in LLaMA models. Automatic Prompt Engineering proved most effective for extracting textual item data, achieving up to 26% exact-match accuracy, while all methods struggled to retrieve numerical user and rating information.
originalProblem: Large Language Models (LLMs) integrated into recommender systems are prone to memorizing training data, which poses privacy risks and affects evaluation reliability.
Previous methods for detecting memorization of recommender system datasets, such as MovieLens-1M, relied on labor-intensive and unscalable manual prompt engineering.
LLM memorization of benchmark datasets undermines the validity of recommender system performance evaluations, as models might recall rather than genuinely generalize.
solution: The study enhanced manual prompting by incorporating jailbreak prompt engineering techniques to improve the retrieval of memorized data.

It investigated unsupervised latent knowledge discovery methods, including Contrast
Consistent Search (CCS) and Cluster-Norm, to detect memorized information from internal model activations.
The authors employed Automatic Prompt Engineering (APE) to automate the discovery and refinement of prompts for extracting memorized item, user, and rating data.
keyInsights: Automatic Prompt Engineering (APE) emerges as the most effective and scalable strategy for detecting memorized textual dataset information in LLMs.
LLMs exhibit a stark difference in extractability: semantic textual data (e.g., movie titles) is considerably easier to detect/extract than non-semantic numerical data (e.g., user IDs, ratings).

Unsupervised latent knowledge probes can distinguish real textual data from fabricated entries, but their signals do not conclusively confirm explicit memorization and are ineffective for numerical data.
results: Manual jailbreak prompting was largely impractical for extracting structured data, yielding inconsistent outputs, high hallucination rates, and insufficient reliability.

Unsupervised latent knowledge methods achieved high accuracy (0.92-0.94) in distinguishing real textual movie titles from fake ones, but performed near random (0.51-0.53) for numerical user and rating data.

Automatic Prompt Engineering significantly improved item-level extraction, achieving 18.1% exact-match accuracy for LLaMA-1B and 26% for LLaMA-3B on movie titles, surpassing previous manual methods, but failed to extract numerical user/rating data.

en.overview:
## Research Problem and Context

The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into recommender systems has emerged as a promising direction for enhancing recommendation quality through natural language understanding. However, this integration raises critical concerns about data memorization - the ability of LLMs to reproduce training examples verbatim when appropriately prompted. When benchmark datasets used to evaluate recommender systems are memorized by LLMs, the reported performance metrics become unreliable, as models may simply recall test items rather than demonstrate genuine generalization capabilities.

![Figure 1: Workflow for manual probing with jailbreak prompt engineering. The iterative process involves crafting prompts, querying the LLM, analyzing responses for validity and hallucinations, and refining the approach based on observed issues.](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-0.jpeg)

Previous work by Di Palma et al. identified that the widely-used MovieLens-1M dataset is memorized by popular LLM families, establishing a correlation between memorization and recommender performance. However, their detection methods relied exclusively on labor-intensive manual prompt engineering, which is neither scalable nor robust. This limitation sparked the need for more effective and automated approaches to detect memorized recommender system data in LLMs.

## Methodology and Experimental Design

The researchers investigated three distinct families of techniques for detecting LLM memorization using the MovieLens-1M dataset and LLaMA models (1B and 3B parameters). The dataset comprises user demographics, movie metadata, and rating interactions, providing a comprehensive testbed for memorization detection across different data types.

### Enhanced Manual Prompting with Jailbreak Techniques

The first approach explored whether adversarial prompts designed to bypass LLM safety filters could enhance memorized data retrieval. The researchers adapted jailbreak-style instructions to create a "Context Compliance Attack," involving fabricated conversation histories to prime models for compliance and exact data output. This iterative process involved crafting prompts with few-shot templates, analyzing responses for validity and hallucinations, and refining the approach based on observed issues.

### Unsupervised Latent Knowledge Discovery

The second methodology explored whether memorized knowledge could be detected through the model's internal activations without relying on explicit prompts. Two techniques were employed:

**Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS)** formalizes knowledge discovery as a question-answering task, analyzing hidden activations to identify directions in the activation space corresponding to true statements. The method optimizes consistency over negated pairs to determine if a model "knows" a given sample.

**Cluster-Norm** extends CCS by grouping activations into clusters and normalizing them within each cluster, aiming to reduce spurious correlations and mitigate irrelevant features that could mislead unsupervised probes.

![Figure 2: Workflow for unsupervised latent knowledge discovery using CCS. The process involves creating positive and negative statement pairs, extracting hidden activations, and training linear probes to distinguish true from false statements.](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-1.jpeg)

For evaluation, the researchers constructed datasets of true and false statements about MovieLens-1M content, generating fictitious samples through random bi-gram sampling for negative examples. Performance was measured as classification accuracy on the task of distinguishing real from fabricated data.

### Automatic Prompt Engineering (APE)

The third approach treated prompt design as an optimization problem, allowing an LLM to generate, evaluate, and iteratively refine prompts for memorization detection. The APE framework involved three stages:

1. **Prompt Generation**: An LLM generates 100 candidate prompts bootstrapped with demonstration input-output pairs
2. **Prompt Evaluation**: Each prompt is evaluated on a validation subset using exact-match metrics
3. **Prompt Refinement**: Top-performing prompts are fed back as examples for synthesizing improved prompts

The study investigated the effect of temperature parameters (0.1 to 2.0) during prompt generation to assess whether increased randomness yields more creative and effective prompts.

## Key Findings and Results

The experimental results revealed distinct patterns in memorization detectability across different data types and methodologies.

### Manual Probing Results

Jailbreak prompt engineering yielded limited and inconsistent results. While LLaMA-1B occasionally recalled target records, the majority of outputs consisted of hallucinated movie titles or random numbers for user and rating fields. Even with chain-of-thought phrases and adversarial triggers, improved recall came with increased false positives, making this approach impractical for systematic memorization detection.

### Unsupervised Method Performance

The effectiveness of CCS and Cluster-Norm varied dramatically by data type:

For **textual movie data**, both methods achieved high accuracy (CCS: 0.92, Cluster-Norm: 0.94) in distinguishing genuine movie titles from synthetically generated ones. PCA visualizations confirmed clear separability between representations of real and fabricated movie titles, suggesting the model can implicitly recognize training data items.

![Figure 3: PCA visualization showing clear separation between real and synthetic movie titles, indicating the model's ability to distinguish genuine training data.](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-2.jpeg)

For **numerical data** (user IDs and ratings), accuracies hovered around 0.51-0.53, barely above random guessing. PCA visualizations showed overlapping clusters, indicating no discernible patterns for distinguishing real from synthetic numerical data.

![Figure 4: PCA visualization for numerical data showing overlapping clusters, demonstrating the failure of unsupervised methods to detect patterns in user and rating information.](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-3.jpeg)

### Automatic Prompt Engineering Success

APE demonstrated the most promising results, particularly for item extraction:

$$\text{Item Coverage} = \frac{\text{Correctly Extracted Items}}{\text{Total Items in Test Set}}$$

APE significantly surpassed previous manual prompting results, achieving 18.1% exact-match accuracy for LLaMA-1B (vs. 1.93% manually) and 26% for LLaMA-3B (vs. 2.68% manually). Performance peaked at moderate temperature values (0.7-0.9), confirming that controlled randomness benefits prompt diversity and precision.

However, consistent with other methods, APE struggled with user and rating extraction, yielding near-zero scores across all configurations. The researchers hypothesize that tokenization issues may fragment alphanumeric sequences, stripping them of coherent semantic meaning.

## Significance and Implications

This research provides crucial insights for the reliable evaluation and deployment of LLM-based recommender systems. The identification of Automatic Prompt Engineering as the most effective current strategy for extracting memorized textual data offers practitioners a scalable path forward for auditing LLM training data and understanding potential leakage risks.

The stark divergence in extractability between semantic textual data and non-semantic numerical data reveals fundamental differences in how LLMs process and memorize different information types. This finding suggests that memorization patterns align with models' natural language processing strengths, with implications for developing targeted detection and mitigation strategies.

The work directly impacts the validity of LLM-based recommender system evaluations. If benchmark datasets are memorized, reported performance metrics may reflect recall rather than genuine generalization. The paper's memorization detection mechanisms contribute to developing more rigorous evaluation protocols that ensure meaningful performance assessment.

## Future Research Directions

The authors outline several promising avenues for future investigation:

**Scaling to larger models**: Experimenting with APE on larger open models (e.g., LLaMA-70B) and diverse datasets to assess scalability and generalization across different domains and model sizes.

**Advanced APE methods**: Developing specialized Automatic Prompt Engineering techniques tailored for memorization tasks, with particular focus on overcoming tokenization challenges that hinder numerical data extraction.

**Interpretability enhancement**: Further investigating latent knowledge probes to definitively differentiate between general model knowledge and true memorization, potentially through more sophisticated activation analysis techniques.

This research represents a significant step toward automated, robust detection of data memorization in LLMs used for recommender systems, establishing foundations for more trustworthy and reliable AI applications in recommendation domains.

zh.title: 探索大型语言模型中推荐系统数据记忆化的检测方法
zh.abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）凭借其强大的自然语言理解和生成能力，正越来越多地应用于推荐场景。然而，它们是在内容未公开披露的海量语料库上进行训练的，这引发了对数据泄露的担忧。近期研究表明，MovieLens-1M 数据集已被 LLaMA 和 OpenAI 模型家族所记忆，但此类记忆数据的提取迄今为止一直完全依赖于手动提示工程。在本文中，我们提出了三个主要问题：是否有可能改进手动提示？除了手动提示之外，能否通过其他方法检测 LLM 的记忆化？以及数据泄露的检测能否实现自动化？为解决这些问题，我们评估了三种方法：(i) 越狱提示工程；(ii) 无监督潜在知识发现，即通过对比一致性搜索 (CCS) 和聚类范数 (Cluster-Norm) 探查内部激活；以及 (iii) 自动提示工程 (APE)，它将提示发现视为一个迭代优化候选指令的元学习过程。使用 LLaMA 模型在 MovieLens-1M 数据集上的实验表明，越狱提示并不能改善记忆项目的检索，并且结果不稳定；CCS 能够可靠地区分真实和虚构的电影名称，但在数字用户和评分数据上表现不佳；APE 以中等程度的成功检索了项目级信息，但难以恢复数值交互数据。这些发现表明，自动优化提示是提取记忆样本最有前景的策略。

summary.summary: 巴里理工大学的研究人员评估了越狱、无监督和自动化方法，以检测LLaMA模型中MovieLens-1M数据集的记忆化情况。自动提示工程被证明在提取文本项数据方面最有效，达到了26%的精确匹配准确率，而所有方法在检索数值用户和评分信息时都遇到了困难。
originalProblem: 集成到推荐系统中的大型语言模型（LLM）容易记忆训练数据，这带来了隐私风险并影响评估的可靠性。
以前检测推荐系统数据集（如MovieLens-1M）记忆化的方法依赖于劳动密集且不可扩展的手动提示工程。
LLM对基准数据集的记忆化削弱了推荐系统性能评估的有效性，因为模型可能是在回忆而不是真正地泛化。
solution: 该研究通过结合越狱提示工程技术来增强手动提示，以改进记忆数据的检索。
它研究了无监督的潜在知识发现方法，包括对比一致性搜索（CCS）和聚类范数（Cluster-Norm），以从模型内部激活中检测记忆信息。
作者采用了自动提示工程（APE）来自动化提示的发现和优化，以提取记忆的物品、用户和评分数据。
keyInsights: 自动提示工程（APE）成为检测LLM中记忆的文本数据集信息的最有效和可扩展的策略。
LLM在可提取性方面表现出显著差异：语义文本数据（如电影标题）比非语义数值数据（如用户ID、评分）更容易检测/提取。
无监督的潜在知识探针能够区分真实的文本数据和伪造的条目，但它们的信号不能确凿地证实显式记忆，并且对数值数据无效。
results: 手动越狱提示在提取结构化数据方面很大程度上不切实际，产生了不一致的输出、高幻觉率和可靠性不足。
无监督的潜在知识方法在区分真实文本电影标题和虚假标题方面取得了高准确率（0.92-0.94），但在数值用户和评分数据方面表现接近随机（0.51-0.53）。
自动提示工程显著改善了物品级提取，LLaMA-1B在电影标题上达到了18.1%的精确匹配准确率，LLaMA-3B达到了26%，超越了以前的手动方法，但未能提取数值用户/评分数据。

zh.overview:
## 研究问题与背景

将大型语言模型（LLMs）集成到推荐系统中，已成为通过自然语言理解提升推荐质量的一个有前景的方向。然而，这种集成引发了对数据记忆的关键担忧——即LLMs在被恰当提示时，能够逐字复现训练样本的能力。当用于评估推荐系统的基准数据集被LLMs记忆时，报告的性能指标变得不可靠，因为模型可能仅仅是回忆测试项目，而不是展示真正的泛化能力。

![图1：使用越狱提示工程进行手动探测的工作流程。迭代过程包括制作提示、查询LLM、分析响应的有效性和幻觉，并根据观察到的问题改进方法。](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-0.jpeg)

Di Palma 等人之前的研究发现，广泛使用的MovieLens-1M数据集被流行的LLM家族所记忆，并建立了记忆与推荐器性能之间的相关性。然而，他们的检测方法完全依赖于劳动密集型的手动提示工程，这种方法既不具可扩展性也不够鲁棒。这一局限性促使需要更有效和自动化的方法来检测LLM中被记忆的推荐系统数据。

## 方法论与实验设计

研究人员调查了三种不同的技术家族，用于使用MovieLens-1M数据集和LLaMA模型（1B和3B参数）检测LLM记忆。该数据集包括用户人口统计数据、电影元数据和评分交互，为跨不同数据类型的记忆检测提供了全面的测试平台。

### 增强手动提示与越狱技术

第一种方法探讨了旨在绕过LLM安全过滤器的对抗性提示是否可以增强记忆数据的检索。研究人员改编了越狱风格的指令，创建了一种“上下文合规性攻击”，涉及伪造的对话历史，以促使模型遵守并输出精确数据。这个迭代过程包括使用少样本模板制作提示、分析响应的有效性和幻觉，并根据观察到的问题改进方法。

### 无监督潜在知识发现

第二种方法论探讨了是否可以通过模型的内部激活来检测记忆知识，而无需依赖显式提示。采用了两种技术：

**对比一致性搜索（CCS）** 将知识发现形式化为一个问答任务，分析隐藏激活以识别激活空间中与真实陈述对应的方向。该方法优化了否定对上的一致性，以确定模型是否“知道”给定样本。

**聚类范数（Cluster-Norm）** 扩展了CCS，通过将激活分组到聚类中并在每个聚类内进行归一化，旨在减少虚假相关性并减轻可能误导无监督探测的不相关特征。

![图2：使用CCS进行无监督潜在知识发现的工作流程。该过程包括创建肯定和否定陈述对、提取隐藏激活，以及训练线性探测器以区分真假陈述。](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-1.jpeg)

为了评估，研究人员构建了关于MovieLens-1M内容的真假陈述数据集，通过随机二元语法采样生成虚构样本作为负例。性能以区分真实数据和虚构数据的分类准确率来衡量。

### 自动提示工程（APE）

第三种方法将提示设计视为一个优化问题，允许LLM生成、评估和迭代完善用于记忆检测的提示。APE框架包括三个阶段：

1. **提示生成**：大型语言模型（LLM）通过输入-输出示例对引导生成100个候选提示。
2. **提示评估**：每个提示都在验证子集上使用精确匹配指标进行评估。
3. **提示优化**：表现最佳的提示被作为示例反馈，以合成改进的提示。

该研究调查了提示生成过程中温度参数（0.1到2.0）的影响，以评估增加随机性是否能产生更具创造性和有效性的提示。

## 主要发现和结果

实验结果揭示了不同数据类型和方法在记忆可检测性方面的明显模式。

### 手动探测结果

越狱提示工程的结果有限且不一致。虽然LLaMA-1B偶尔会回忆起目标记录，但大多数输出都是虚构的电影标题或用户和评分字段的随机数字。即使使用思维链短语和对抗性触发器，召回率的提高也伴随着误报的增加，这使得这种方法不适用于系统性的记忆检测。

### 无监督方法性能

CCS和Cluster-Norm的有效性因数据类型而异：

对于**文本电影数据**，两种方法在区分真实电影标题和合成生成标题方面都达到了高准确率（CCS：0.92，Cluster-Norm：0.94）。PCA可视化证实了真实和虚构电影标题表示之间存在清晰的分离，表明模型可以隐式识别训练数据项。

![图3：PCA可视化显示真实和合成电影标题之间存在清晰分离，表明模型能够区分真实的训练数据。](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-2.jpeg)

对于**数值数据**（用户ID和评分），准确率徘徊在0.51-0.53之间，仅略高于随机猜测。PCA可视化显示聚类重叠，表明在区分真实和合成数值数据方面没有可辨别的模式。

![图4：数值数据的PCA可视化显示聚类重叠，表明无监督方法未能检测用户和评分信息中的模式。](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2601.02002v1/img-3.jpeg)

### 自动化提示工程的成功

APE展示了最有希望的结果，特别是对于项目提取：

$$\text{项目覆盖率} = \frac{\text{正确提取的项目数}}{\text{测试集中的总项目数}}$$

APE显著超越了之前的手动提示结果，LLaMA-1B实现了18.1%的精确匹配准确率（手动为1.93%），LLaMA-3B实现了26%（手动为2.68%）。性能在中等温度值（0.7-0.9）时达到峰值，证实了受控随机性有助于提示的多样性和精确性。

然而，与其他方法一致，APE在用户和评分提取方面表现不佳，所有配置下的得分都接近零。研究人员推测，分词问题可能将字母数字序列碎片化，使其失去连贯的语义意义。

## 意义和影响

这项研究为基于LLM的推荐系统的可靠评估和部署提供了关键见解。将自动化提示工程确定为目前提取记忆文本数据最有效的策略，为从业者审计LLM训练数据和了解潜在泄露风险提供了可扩展的途径。

语义文本数据和非语义数值数据之间可提取性上的显著差异揭示了LLM处理和记忆不同信息类型的根本差异。这一发现表明，记忆模式与模型的自然语言处理优势保持一致，对开发有针对性的检测和缓解策略具有重要意义。

这项工作直接影响基于LLM的推荐系统评估的有效性。如果基准数据集被记忆，报告的性能指标可能反映的是召回能力而非真正的泛化能力。该论文提出的记忆检测机制有助于开发更严格的评估协议，以确保有意义的性能评估。

## 未来研究方向

作者概述了几个有前景的未来研究方向：

**扩展到更大的模型**：在更大的开放模型（例如LLaMA-70B）和不同的数据集上试验APE，以评估其在不同领域和模型大小下的可扩展性和泛化能力。

**高级APE方法**：开发专门针对记忆任务的自动化提示工程（APE）技术，特别关注克服阻碍数值数据提取的标记化挑战。

**可解释性增强**：进一步研究潜在知识探测，以明确区分模型的一般知识和真实记忆，可能通过更复杂的激活分析技术来实现。

这项研究代表了在用于推荐系统的LLM中自动化、鲁棒地检测数据记忆方面迈出的重要一步，为推荐领域中更值得信赖和可靠的AI应用奠定了基础。

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in recommendation scenarios due to their strong natural language understanding and generation capabilities. However, they are trained on vast corpora whose contents are not publicly disclosed, raising concerns about data leakage. Recent work has shown that the MovieLens-1M dataset is memorized by both the LLaMA and OpenAI model families, but the extraction of such memorized data has so far relied exclusively on manual prompt engineering. In this paper, we pose three main questions: Is it possible to enhance manual prompting? Can LLM memorization be detected through methods beyond manual prompting? And can the detection of data leakage be automated? To address these questions, we evaluate three approaches: (i) jailbreak prompt engineering; (ii) unsupervised latent knowledge discovery, probing internal activations via Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) and Cluster-Norm; and (iii) Automatic Prompt Engineering (APE), which frames prompt discovery as a meta-learning process that iteratively refines candidate instructions. Experiments on MovieLens-1M using LLaMA models show that jailbreak prompting does not improve the retrieval of memorized items and remains inconsistent; CCS reliably distinguishes genuine from fabricated movie titles but fails on numerical user and rating data; and APE retrieves item-level information with moderate success yet struggles to recover numerical interactions. These findings suggest that automatically optimizing prompts is the most promising strategy for extracting memorized samples.
title: Exploring Approaches for Detecting Memorization of Recommender System Data in Large Language Models

en.title: Exploring Diversity, Novelty, and Popularity Bias in ChatGPT's Recommendations
en.abstract:
ChatGPT has emerged as a versatile tool, demonstrating capabilities across diverse domains. Given these successes, the Recommender Systems (RSs) community has begun investigating its applications within recommendation scenarios primarily focusing on accuracy. While the integration of ChatGPT into RSs has garnered significant attention, a comprehensive analysis of its performance across various dimensions remains largely unexplored. Specifically, the capabilities of providing diverse and novel recommendations or exploring potential biases such as popularity bias have not been thoroughly examined. As the use of these models continues to expand, understanding these aspects is crucial for enhancing user satisfaction and achieving long-term personalization.
This study investigates the recommendations provided by ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 by assessing ChatGPT's capabilities in terms of diversity, novelty, and popularity bias. We evaluate these models on three distinct datasets and assess their performance in Top-N recommendation and cold-start scenarios. The findings reveal that ChatGPT-4 matches or surpasses traditional recommenders, demonstrating the ability to balance novelty and diversity in recommendations. Furthermore, in the cold-start scenario, ChatGPT models exhibit superior performance in both accuracy and novelty, suggesting they can be particularly beneficial for new users. This research highlights the strengths and limitations of ChatGPT's recommendations, offering new perspectives on the capacity of these models to provide recommendations beyond accuracy-focused metrics.

summary.summary: This study evaluates ChatGPT models (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) as recommenders, moving beyond accuracy to quantify their performance on diversity, novelty, and popularity bias across three datasets. It finds that GPT-4 effectively balances these factors and proves particularly robust in challenging user cold-start scenarios.
originalProblem: Most existing research on ChatGPT in recommender systems has focused predominantly on improving recommendation accuracy, neglecting other critical performance dimensions.
A comprehensive understanding of ChatGPT's behavior regarding 'beyond-accuracy' metrics like diversity, novelty, and popularity bias was lacking.
The effectiveness of ChatGPT in challenging user cold-start scenarios across both accuracy and non-accuracy dimensions had not been thoroughly explored.
solution: The authors employed a rigorous methodology using ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) with a refined Role-Playing prompting strategy to generate top-N recommendations.
Recommendations were evaluated against diverse state-of-the-art baselines across three distinct datasets: Facebook Books, MovieLens100k, and Last.FM.

A comprehensive suite of metrics was utilized to assess accuracy (Precision, Recall, nDCG) and 'beyond-accuracy' aspects (diversity, novelty, popularity bias), including a specific analysis of user cold-start performance.
keyInsights: Role-Playing prompting proved the most effective strategy for eliciting consistent and high-quality recommendations from ChatGPT, outperforming Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Chain-of-Thought methods.

ChatGPT models, particularly GPT-4, demonstrate a strong capability to balance diversity and novelty in recommendations, often outperforming many traditional collaborative and content-based filtering baselines.
ChatGPT exhibits a robust ability to provide relevant, diverse, and novel recommendations even in user cold-start scenarios, a challenging problem for traditional recommender systems.
results: ChatGPT-4 consistently outperformed ChatGPT-3.5, achieving higher nDCG on Facebook Books and Last.FM, and generally delivering better diversity (Gini Index, Item Coverage) and novelty (EPC, EFD) across datasets.

In user cold-start scenarios, ChatGPT models, especially GPT-4, achieved the highest nDCG and Recall, demonstrating superior accuracy and maintaining strong beyond-accuracy performance compared to all baselines.

While ChatGPT exhibited some popularity bias (a tendency to recommend popular items), this bias was significantly less pronounced than in explicitly popularity-driven baselines, and it showed a better capability for recommending long-tail items than many traditional methods.

en.overview:
## Background and Motivation

Recommender systems have evolved from simple matrix factorization techniques to sophisticated deep learning architectures, traditionally focusing on accuracy metrics to measure success. However, the field has increasingly recognized that accuracy alone is insufficient for creating truly effective user experiences. Critical "beyond-accuracy" dimensions like diversity, novelty, and fairness have emerged as essential factors for user engagement, long-term satisfaction, and equitable item exposure.

The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly ChatGPT, has introduced a paradigm shift in recommendation approaches. Unlike traditional systems that rely on structured interaction data, LLMs can generate free-form text and leverage vast pre-trained knowledge to potentially offer more nuanced recommendations. While initial explorations have shown promising results in recommendation accuracy, a significant gap exists in understanding how these models perform across the crucial beyond-accuracy dimensions.

This study addresses this critical void by systematically analyzing ChatGPT's recommendation behavior across diversity, novelty, and popularity bias metrics, including challenging user cold-start scenarios where traditional recommenders typically struggle.

## Research Questions and Objectives

The authors formulated four specific research questions to comprehensively evaluate ChatGPT's recommendation capabilities:

- **RQ1**: Are ChatGPT's recommendations diverse? This examines whether ChatGPT provides a wide range of content or concentrates on a narrow set of items.
- **RQ2**: Are ChatGPT's recommendations novel? This investigates ChatGPT's ability to expose users to items they are unlikely to discover independently.
- **RQ3**: Is ChatGPT affected by popularity bias? This explores whether ChatGPT favors items with many interactions over less popular, long-tail items.
- **RQ4**: How effective is ChatGPT in user cold-start scenarios across accuracy and beyond-accuracy dimensions? This probes ChatGPT's performance when users have minimal interaction history.

These objectives collectively aim to provide a multi-dimensional evaluation of ChatGPT's recommendation capabilities, moving beyond the prevalent accuracy-centric view to offer insights vital for responsible deployment in real-world applications.

## Methodology and Experimental Design

The research employed a rigorous methodology to ensure comprehensive evaluation across multiple dimensions and domains.

### Prompt Engineering Strategy

Given the critical role of prompt design in shaping LLM responses, the authors experimented with several prompting techniques:

- **Zero-Shot**: Direct requests for recommendations resulted in incomplete lists and duplicates (~71% contained fewer than 50 items)
- **Few-Shot**: Provided examples to guide the model but still had high duplication rates (~44%)
- **Chain-of-Thought (CoT)**: Explicit step-by-step breakdown generated excessive tokens, hitting context limits
- **Role-Playing (RP)**: ChatGPT impersonated a Recommender System, proving most effective by eliminating duplicates and managing token usage efficiently

The Role-Playing strategy was selected as the primary technique, instructing ChatGPT to "provide only the names of the top 50 recommendations" based on a user's interaction history.

### Datasets and Preprocessing

Three distinct domains were chosen to ensure generalizability:
- **Facebook Books**: Book recommendations
- **MovieLens100k**: Movie recommendations  
- **Last.FM**: Music recommendations

An iterative 10-core filtering strategy was applied to all datasets, ensuring only users and items with at least ten interactions were retained for data quality enhancement.

### Evaluation Framework

The study employed comprehensive metrics across multiple dimensions:

**Accuracy Metrics:**
- Precision and Recall: Measuring relevant items in recommendations and coverage of all relevant items
- Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (nDCG): Evaluating ranking quality with position-sensitive scoring

**Beyond-Accuracy Metrics:**

*Diversity:*
$$\text{Item Coverage (ItemCV)} = \text{Number of unique items recommended across all users}$$

$$\text{Gini Index} = 1 - \frac{2}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(n-i+1)p_i$$

*Novelty:*
- **Expected Free Discovery (EFD)**: Measures ability to recommend relevant long-tail items
- **Expected Popularity Complement (EPC)**: Quantifies discovery of previously unknown content

*Popularity Bias:*
- **Average Popularity of Long-Tail Items (APLT)**: Average popularity of recommended long-tail items
- **Average Rating-based Popularity (ARP)**: Average popularity based on training interactions (lower values indicate less bias)

### Baseline Comparison

ChatGPT's performance was benchmarked against diverse state-of-the-art baselines:
- **Non-Personalized**: Random and Most Popular
- **Collaborative Filtering**: RP3β, LightGCN, ItemKNN, UserKNN, EASER, MF2020, NeuMF
- **Content-Based Filtering**: VSM, AttributeItemKNN, AttributeUserKNN

All evaluations used a Top-N cutoff of 10, following standard practices in recommender systems research.

## Key Findings and Results

### General Recommendation Performance

**Accuracy Performance**: Both ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 demonstrated reasonable accuracy across domains. ChatGPT-4 achieved the highest nDCG on Facebook Books (0.0932) and performed comparably to top collaborative filtering approaches on Last.FM (nDCG=0.2832). While some traditional algorithms outperformed ChatGPT on certain datasets, the models consistently exceeded several baseline approaches.

**Diversity Analysis (RQ1)**: ChatGPT models showed moderate diversity performance. ChatGPT-4 consistently outperformed ChatGPT-3.5 across metrics:
- Facebook Books: Gini Index (0.1050 vs. 0.0713), Item Coverage (1,004 vs. 853 items)
- Last.FM: Similar patterns with GPT-4 showing superior coverage

While not always matching the highest-diversity baselines, ChatGPT demonstrated superior diversity compared to many traditional collaborative and content-based filtering methods.

**Novelty Assessment (RQ2)**: ChatGPT-4 exhibited high novelty across datasets, particularly excelling in Facebook Books (EPC=0.0353, EFD=0.3486) and Last.FM, often exceeding traditional baselines. This suggests a strong ability to recommend less mainstream items based on user interaction history.

**Popularity Bias Evaluation (RQ3)**: ChatGPT showed a tendency toward popular items but significantly less than explicitly popularity-driven baselines:
- Facebook Books: ChatGPT-4 (ARP=40) vs. ChatGPT-3.5 (ARP=46)
- MovieLens: ChatGPT (ARP~90-95) vs. MostPop (ARP=182)

While some bias exists, it remains moderate compared to traditional popularity-focused approaches.

### Cold-Start Scenario Performance

**Accuracy in Data-Sparse Conditions**: ChatGPT proved remarkably effective in cold-start scenarios. ChatGPT-4 achieved the highest nDCG and Recall on Facebook Books and MovieLens, significantly outperforming traditional baselines when user interaction data is minimal.

**Beyond-Accuracy in Cold-Start**: 
- **Diversity**: GPT-4 generally surpassed GPT-3.5 in diversity metrics across datasets
- **Novelty**: ChatGPT's EPC and EFD values consistently exceeded collaborative and content-based filtering baselines
- **Popularity Bias**: Moderate inclination toward popular items, but significantly less than "MostPop" strategies

The cold-start results demonstrate ChatGPT's impressive ability to infer user interests and provide balanced recommendations even with very limited interaction data.

## Significance and Implications

This research establishes the first comprehensive analysis of ChatGPT's performance beyond traditional accuracy metrics in recommender systems. The findings have several significant implications:

**Methodological Contribution**: The study introduces a rigorous framework for evaluating LLM-based recommenders across multiple performance dimensions, challenging the prevailing accuracy-centric evaluation paradigm and encouraging future research to adopt similar multi-dimensional approaches.

**Practical Insights**: The superior performance of Role-Playing prompting provides valuable guidance for practitioners developing LLM-enhanced recommendation systems. The findings suggest that while LLMs can natively generate diverse and novel recommendations, specific strategies may be needed to further reduce popularity bias in certain domains.

**Cold-Start Effectiveness**: The exceptional performance in cold-start scenarios positions LLMs as powerful tools for addressing one of the most challenging problems in recommendation systems, offering personalized suggestions even with minimal user data.

**Future Research Directions**: The study acknowledges a critical limitation regarding LLM memorization, noting that models might have been trained on public datasets like MovieLens. This raises important questions about whether performance improvements reflect true reasoning capabilities or memorized knowledge, highlighting the need for future research to investigate the correlation between recommendation quality and memorization capacity.

The research significantly advances understanding of ChatGPT as a recommendation agent while identifying important challenges and opportunities for developing more robust, fair, and user-centric LLM-driven recommendation technologies.

zh.title: 探索 ChatGPT 推荐中的多样性、新颖性和流行度偏差
zh.abstract:
ChatGPT 作为一种多功能工具崭露头角，在多个不同领域展现出强大的能力。鉴于其取得的成功，推荐系统 (RS) 社区已开始探索其在推荐场景中的应用，但主要侧重于准确性。尽管将 ChatGPT 整合到推荐系统中已获得了广泛关注，但对其在多个维度上的性能进行全面分析却在很大程度上仍未得到充分探索。具体而言，ChatGPT 提供多样化和新颖推荐的能力，以及探索其潜在偏差（如流行度偏差）的能力，尚未得到深入检验。随着这些模型的应用日益普及，理解这些方面对于提升用户满意度并实现长期个性化至关重要。

本研究通过评估 ChatGPT 在多样性、新颖性和流行度偏差方面的能力，对 ChatGPT-3.5 和 ChatGPT-4 提供的推荐进行了调查。我们在三个不同的独立数据集上评估了这些模型，并评估了它们在 Top-N 推荐和冷启动场景中的表现。研究结果表明，ChatGPT-4 在推荐性能上与传统推荐系统持平或超越，展现了在推荐中平衡新颖性和多样性的能力。此外，在冷启动场景中，ChatGPT 模型在准确性和新颖性两方面均表现出卓越的性能，这表明它们对新用户可能特别有益。本研究突出了 ChatGPT 推荐的优势和局限性，为这些模型提供超越以准确性为核心指标的推荐能力提供了新的视角。

summary.summary: 本研究评估了ChatGPT模型（GPT-3.5和GPT-4）作为推荐系统的表现，超越了准确性，量化了它们在三个数据集上在多样性、新颖性和流行度偏差方面的性能。研究发现GPT-4能有效平衡这些因素，并在具有挑战性的用户冷启动场景中表现出特别的鲁棒性。
originalProblem: 现有关于推荐系统中ChatGPT的大多数研究主要集中于提高推荐准确性，而忽视了其他关键的性能维度。
缺乏对ChatGPT在“超越准确性”指标（如多样性、新颖性和流行度偏差）方面的行为的全面理解。
尚未充分探讨ChatGPT在具有挑战性的用户冷启动场景中，在准确性和非准确性维度上的有效性。
solution: 作者采用严谨的方法，使用ChatGPT（GPT-3.5和GPT-4）并结合精细的角色扮演提示策略来生成Top-N推荐。
在Facebook Books、MovieLens100k和Last.FM这三个不同的数据集上，将推荐结果与各种先进的基线进行了评估。
采用了一套全面的指标来评估准确性（精确度、召回率、nDCG）和“超越准确性”的方面（多样性、新颖性、流行度偏差），其中包括对用户冷启动性能的专门分析。
keyInsights: 角色扮演提示被证明是从ChatGPT获取一致且高质量推荐的最有效策略，优于零样本、少样本和思维链方法。
ChatGPT模型，特别是GPT-4，在推荐中展现出平衡多样性和新颖性的强大能力，通常优于许多传统的协同过滤和基于内容的过滤基线。
ChatGPT即使在用户冷启动场景中也表现出提供相关、多样和新颖推荐的强大能力，这是传统推荐系统面临的一个挑战性问题。
results: ChatGPT-4始终优于ChatGPT-3.5，在Facebook Books和Last.FM上实现了更高的nDCG，并且在所有数据集上通常提供了更好的多样性（基尼指数、项目覆盖率）和新颖性（EPC、EFD）。
在用户冷启动场景中，ChatGPT模型，特别是GPT-4，取得了最高的nDCG和召回率，与所有基线相比，展示出卓越的准确性并保持了强大的超越准确性的性能。
尽管ChatGPT表现出一定的流行度偏差（倾向于推荐热门商品），但这种偏差明显低于那些明确以流行度为驱动的基线，并且它在推荐长尾商品方面比许多传统方法表现出更好的能力。

zh.overview:
## 背景与动机

推荐系统已从简单的矩阵分解技术演变为复杂的深度学习架构，传统上侧重于准确性指标来衡量成功。然而，该领域日益认识到，仅凭准确性不足以创造真正有效的用户体验。多样性、新颖性和公平性等关键的“超越准确性”维度已成为用户参与、长期满意度和公平项目曝光的重要因素。

大型语言模型（LLM）的出现，特别是 ChatGPT，给推荐方法带来了范式转变。与依赖结构化交互数据的传统系统不同，LLM 可以生成自由形式的文本，并利用庞大的预训练知识来潜在地提供更细致的推荐。虽然初步探索已在推荐准确性方面显示出有希望的结果，但在理解这些模型在关键的超越准确性维度上的表现方面存在显著差距。

本研究通过系统分析 ChatGPT 在多样性、新颖性和流行度偏差指标方面的推荐行为，包括传统推荐系统通常难以应对的挑战性用户冷启动场景，来弥补这一关键空白。

## 研究问题与目标

作者制定了四个具体的研究问题，以全面评估 ChatGPT 的推荐能力：

- **RQ1**：ChatGPT 的推荐是否多样化？这检查了 ChatGPT 是提供广泛内容还是专注于狭窄的项目集。
- **RQ2**：ChatGPT 的推荐是否新颖？这调查了 ChatGPT 让用户接触到他们不太可能独立发现的项目的能力。
- **RQ3**：ChatGPT 是否受流行度偏差影响？这探讨了 ChatGPT 是否偏爱交互量大的项目，而非不那么受欢迎的长尾项目。
- **RQ4**：ChatGPT 在准确性和超越准确性维度上的用户冷启动场景中效果如何？这探究了当用户交互历史最少时 ChatGPT 的表现。

这些目标共同旨在对 ChatGPT 的推荐能力进行多维度评估，超越普遍以准确性为中心的视角，提供对实际应用中负责任部署至关重要的见解。

## 方法论与实验设计

该研究采用了严谨的方法，以确保在多个维度和领域进行全面评估。

### 提示工程策略

鉴于提示设计在塑造 LLM 响应中的关键作用，作者尝试了几种提示技术：

- **零样本 (Zero-Shot)**：直接推荐请求导致列表不完整和重复（约 71% 的列表包含少于 50 个项目）
- **少样本 (Few-Shot)**：提供示例以引导模型，但仍有高重复率（约 44%）
- **思维链 (Chain-of-Thought, CoT)**：明确的分步分解生成了过多的 tokens，达到了上下文限制
- **角色扮演 (Role-Playing, RP)**：ChatGPT 扮演推荐系统，被证明最有效，消除了重复并高效管理了 token 使用量

角色扮演策略被选为主要技术，指示 ChatGPT 根据用户的交互历史“仅提供前 50 个推荐的名称”。

### 数据集与预处理

选择了三个不同的领域以确保通用性：
- **Facebook Books**：图书推荐
- **MovieLens100k**：电影推荐
- **Last.FM**：音乐推荐

对所有数据集应用了迭代的 10-core 过滤策略，确保只保留至少有十次交互的用户和项目，以提高数据质量。

### 评估框架

该研究采用了跨多个维度的综合指标：

**准确性指标：**
- 精确率和召回率：衡量推荐中相关项目的数量以及所有相关项目的覆盖率
- 归一化折损累计增益 (nDCG)：通过位置敏感评分评估排名质量

**超越准确性的指标：**

*多样性：*
$$\text{项目覆盖率 (ItemCV)} = \text{所有用户推荐的独特项目数量}$$

$$\text{基尼指数} = 1 - \frac{2}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(n-i+1)p_i$$

*新颖性：*
- **预期自由发现 (EFD)**：衡量推荐相关长尾项目的能力
- **预期流行度补足 (EPC)**：量化发现先前未知内容的能力

*流行度偏差：*
- **长尾项目平均流行度 (APLT)**：推荐的长尾项目的平均流行度
- **基于评分的平均流行度 (ARP)**：基于训练交互的平均流行度（值越低表示偏差越小）

### 基线比较

ChatGPT的性能与各种最先进的基线进行了对比：
- **非个性化**：随机和最热门
- **协同过滤**：RP3β, LightGCN, ItemKNN, UserKNN, EASER, MF2020, NeuMF
- **基于内容的过滤**：VSM, AttributeItemKNN, AttributeUserKNN

所有评估均使用Top-N截断为10，遵循推荐系统研究中的标准做法。

## 主要发现和结果

### 一般推荐性能

**准确性表现**：ChatGPT-3.5和ChatGPT-4在各个领域都表现出合理的准确性。ChatGPT-4在Facebook图书上实现了最高的nDCG（0.0932），并在Last.FM上表现与顶级的协同过滤方法相当（nDCG=0.2832）。尽管一些传统算法在某些数据集上优于ChatGPT，但这些模型始终超越了几个基线方法。

**多样性分析 (RQ1)**：ChatGPT模型表现出中等的多样性性能。ChatGPT-4在各项指标上始终优于ChatGPT-3.5：
- Facebook图书：基尼指数（0.1050 vs. 0.0713），项目覆盖率（1,004 vs. 853个项目）
- Last.FM：相似模式，GPT-4显示出卓越的覆盖率

尽管并非总是与多样性最高的基线相匹配，但ChatGPT与许多传统的协同过滤和基于内容的过滤方法相比，展现出卓越的多样性。

**新颖性评估 (RQ2)**：ChatGPT-4在各个数据集上表现出高新颖性，特别是在Facebook图书（EPC=0.0353，EFD=0.3486）和Last.FM上表现出色，经常超过传统基线。这表明它能够根据用户交互历史推荐非主流项目。

**流行度偏差评估 (RQ3)**：ChatGPT表现出对流行项目的偏好，但显著低于明确以流行度为驱动的基线：
- Facebook图书：ChatGPT-4 (ARP=40) vs. ChatGPT-3.5 (ARP=46)
- MovieLens：ChatGPT (ARP~90-95) vs. 最热门 (ARP=182)

尽管存在一些偏差，但与传统的以流行度为重点的方法相比，它仍然是温和的。

### 冷启动场景性能

**数据稀疏条件下的准确性**：ChatGPT在冷启动场景中表现出显著的有效性。在用户交互数据极少的情况下，ChatGPT-4在Facebook图书和MovieLens上实现了最高的nDCG和召回率，显著优于传统基线。

**冷启动中的超越准确性指标**：
- **多样性**：GPT-4在所有数据集的多样性指标上普遍优于GPT-3.5
- **新颖性**：ChatGPT的EPC和EFD值始终超过协同过滤和基于内容的过滤基线
- **流行度偏差**：对流行项目有适度偏好，但显著低于“最热门”策略

冷启动结果表明ChatGPT即使在交互数据非常有限的情况下，也能出色地推断用户兴趣并提供均衡的推荐。

## 意义和启示

这项研究首次全面分析了ChatGPT在推荐系统中超越传统准确性指标的性能。这些发现具有多项重要启示：

**方法论贡献**：本研究引入了一个严谨的框架，用于从多个性能维度评估基于LLM的推荐系统，挑战了当前以准确性为中心的评估范式，并鼓励未来的研究采用类似的多维度方法。

**实践见解**：角色扮演提示的卓越性能为开发LLM增强推荐系统的实践者提供了宝贵的指导。研究结果表明，虽然LLM可以原生生成多样化和新颖的推荐，但在某些领域可能需要特定策略来进一步减少流行度偏差。

**冷启动效能**：在冷启动场景中的出色表现使LLM成为解决推荐系统中最具挑战性问题之一的强大工具，即使在用户数据极少的情况下也能提供个性化建议。

**未来研究方向**：本研究承认LLM记忆方面的一个关键局限性，指出模型可能已经在MovieLens等公共数据集上进行过训练。这引发了关于性能改进是反映了真正的推理能力还是记忆知识的重要问题，强调未来研究需要调查推荐质量与记忆能力之间的相关性。

这项研究显著增进了对ChatGPT作为推荐代理的理解，同时识别了开发更强大、公平和以用户为中心的LLM驱动推荐技术的重要挑战和机遇。

abstract:
ChatGPT has emerged as a versatile tool, demonstrating capabilities across diverse domains. Given these successes, the Recommender Systems (RSs) community has begun investigating its applications within recommendation scenarios primarily focusing on accuracy. While the integration of ChatGPT into RSs has garnered significant attention, a comprehensive analysis of its performance across various dimensions remains largely unexplored. Specifically, the capabilities of providing diverse and novel recommendations or exploring potential biases such as popularity bias have not been thoroughly examined. As the use of these models continues to expand, understanding these aspects is crucial for enhancing user satisfaction and achieving long-term personalization.
  This study investigates the recommendations provided by ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 by assessing ChatGPT's capabilities in terms of diversity, novelty, and popularity bias. We evaluate these models on three distinct datasets and assess their performance in Top-N recommendation and cold-start scenarios. The findings reveal that ChatGPT-4 matches or surpasses traditional recommenders, demonstrating the ability to balance novelty and diversity in recommendations. Furthermore, in the cold-start scenario, ChatGPT models exhibit superior performance in both accuracy and novelty, suggesting they can be particularly beneficial for new users. This research highlights the strengths and limitations of ChatGPT's recommendations, offering new perspectives on the capacity of these models to provide recommendations beyond accuracy-focused metrics.

abstract: Although recent approaches to face normal estimation have achieved promising results, their effectiveness heavily depends on large-scale paired data for training. This paper concentrates on relieving this requirement via developing a coarse-to-fine normal estimator. Concretely, our method first trains a neat model from a small dataset to produce coarse face normals that perform as guidance (called exemplars) for the following refinement. A self-attention mechanism is employed to capture long-range dependencies, thus remedying severe local artifacts left in estimated coarse facial normals. Then, a refinement network is customized for the sake of mapping input face images together with corresponding exemplars to fine-grained high-quality facial normals. Such a logical function split can significantly cut the requirement of massive paired data and computational resource. Extensive experiments and ablation studies are conducted to demonstrate the efficacy of our design and reveal its superiority over state-of-the-art methods in terms of both training expense as well as estimation quality. Our code and models are open-sourced at: https://github.com/AutoHDR/FNR2R.git.

abstract:
In the early 1980s, Open Source Software emerged as a revolutionary concept amidst the dominance of proprietary software. What began as a revolutionary idea has now become the cornerstone of computer science. Amidst OSS projects, AI is increasing its presence and relevance. However, despite the growing popularity of AI, its adoption and impacts on OSS projects remain underexplored.
  We aim to assess the adoption of AI libraries in Python and Java OSS projects and examine how they shape development, including the technical ecosystem and community engagement. To this end, we will perform a large-scale analysis on 157.7k potential OSS repositories, employing repository metrics and software metrics to compare projects adopting AI libraries against those that do not. We expect to identify measurable differences in development activity, community engagement, and code complexity between OSS projects that adopt AI libraries and those that do not, offering evidence-based insights into how AI integration reshapes software development practices.

abstract: Graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search often suffers from performance degradation in high-dimensional spaces due to the ``Euclidean-Geodesic mismatch,'' where greedy routing diverges from the underlying data manifold. To address this, we propose Manifold-Consistent Graph Indexing (MCGI), a geometry-aware and disk-resident indexing method that leverages Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID) to dynamically adapt search strategies to the data's intrinsic geometry. Unlike standard algorithms that treat dimensions uniformly, MCGI modulates its beam search budget based on in situ geometric analysis, eliminating dependency on static hyperparameters. Theoretical analysis confirms that MCGI enables improved approximation guarantees by preserving manifold-consistent topological connectivity. Empirically, MCGI achieves 5.8$\times$ higher throughput at 95\% recall on high-dimensional GIST1M compared to state-of-the-art DiskANN. On the billion-scale SIFT1B dataset, MCGI further validates its scalability by reducing high-recall query latency by 3$\times$, while maintaining performance parity on standard lower-dimensional datasets.
title: MCGI: Manifold-Consistent Graph Indexing for Billion-Scale Disk-Resident Vector Search

abstract:
Background. Defect prediction has been a highly active topic among researchers in the Empirical Software Engineering field. Previous literature has successfully achieved the most accurate prediction of an incoming fault and identified the features and anomalies that precede it through just-in-time prediction. As software systems evolve continuously, there is a growing need for time-sensitive methods capable of forecasting defects before they manifest.
  Aim. Our study seeks to explore the effectiveness of time-sensitive techniques for defect forecasting. Moreover, we aim to investigate the early indicators that precede the occurrence of a defect.
  Method. We will train multiple time-sensitive forecasting techniques to forecast the future bug density of a software project, as well as identify the early symptoms preceding the occurrence of a defect.
  Expected results. Our expected results are translated into empirical evidence on the effectiveness of our approach for early estimation of bug proneness.
title: A Defect is Being Born: How Close Are We? A Time Sensitive Forecasting Approach

abstract:
Claims documents are fundamental to healthcare and insurance operations, serving as the basis for reimbursement, auditing, and compliance. However, these documents are typically not born digital; they often exist as scanned PDFs or photographs captured under uncontrolled conditions. Consequently, they exhibit significant content heterogeneity, ranging from typed invoices to handwritten medical reports, as well as linguistic diversity. This challenge is exemplified by operations at Fullerton Health, which handles tens of millions of claims annually across nine markets, including Singapore, the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mainland China, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Papua New Guinea, and Cambodia. Such variability, coupled with inconsistent image quality and diverse layouts, poses a significant obstacle to automated parsing and structured information extraction.
  This paper presents a robust multi-stage pipeline that integrates the multilingual optical character recognition (OCR) engine PaddleOCR, a traditional Logistic Regression classifier, and a compact Vision-Language Model (VLM), Qwen 2.5-VL-7B, to achieve efficient and accurate field extraction from large-scale claims data. The proposed system achieves a document-type classification accuracy of over 95 percent and a field-level extraction accuracy of approximately 87 percent, while maintaining an average processing latency of under 2 seconds per document. Compared to manual processing, which typically requires around 10 minutes per claim, our system delivers a 300x improvement in efficiency. These results demonstrate that combining traditional machine learning models with modern VLMs enables production-grade accuracy and speed for real-world automation. The solution has been successfully deployed in our mobile application and is currently processing tens of thousands of claims weekly from Vietnam and Singapore.

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a widely adopted approach to enhance Large Language Models (LLMs) by incorporating external knowledge and reducing hallucinations. However, noisy or irrelevant documents are often introduced during RAG, potentially degrading performance and even causing hallucinated outputs. While various methods have been proposed to filter out such noise, we argue that identifying irrelevant information from retrieved content is inherently difficult and limited number of transformer layers can hardly solve this. Consequently, retrievers fail to filter out irrelevant documents entirely. Therefore, LLMs must be robust against such noise, but we demonstrate that standard fine-tuning approaches are often ineffective in enabling the model to selectively utilize relevant information while ignoring irrelevant content due to the structural constraints of attention patterns. To address this, we propose a novel fine-tuning method designed to enhance the model's ability to distinguish between relevant and irrelevant information within retrieved documents. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show that our approach significantly improves the robustness and performance of LLMs.

abstract:
Recent studies have shown that prompting can enable large language models (LLMs) to simulate specific personality traits and produce behaviors that align with those traits. However, there is limited understanding of how these simulated personalities influence critical web search decisions, specifically relevance assessment. Moreover, few studies have examined how simulated personalities impact confidence calibration, specifically the tendencies toward overconfidence or underconfidence. This gap exists even though psychological literature suggests these biases are trait-specific, often linking high extraversion to overconfidence and high neuroticism to underconfidence. To address this gap, we conducted a comprehensive study evaluating multiple LLMs, including commercial models and open-source models, prompted to simulate Big Five personality traits. We tested these models across three test collections (TREC DL 2019, TREC DL 2020, and LLMJudge), collecting two key outputs for each query-document pair: a relevance judgment and a self-reported confidence score.
  The findings show that personalities such as low agreeableness consistently align more closely with human labels than the unprompted condition. Additionally, low conscientiousness performs well in balancing the suppression of both overconfidence and underconfidence. We also observe that relevance scores and confidence distributions vary systematically across different personalities. Based on the above findings, we incorporate personality-conditioned scores and confidence as features in a random forest classifier. This approach achieves performance that surpasses the best single-personality condition on a new dataset (TREC DL 2021), even with limited training data. These findings highlight that personality-derived confidence offers a complementary predictive signal, paving the way for more reliable and human-aligned LLM evaluators.

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for constructing knowledge graphs (KGs) from unstructured clinical narratives. However, existing approaches often rely on structured inputs and lack robust validation of factual accuracy and semantic consistency, limitations that are especially problematic in oncology. We introduce an end-to-end framework for clinical KG construction and evaluation directly from free text using multi-agent prompting and a schema-constrained Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG) strategy. Our pipeline integrates (1) prompt-driven entity, attribute, and relation extraction; (2) entropy-based uncertainty scoring; (3) ontology-aligned RDF/OWL schema generation; and (4) multi-LLM consensus validation for hallucination detection and semantic refinement. Beyond static graph construction, the framework supports continuous refinement and self-supervised evaluation, enabling iterative improvement of graph quality. Applied to two oncology cohorts (PDAC and BRCA), our method produces interpretable, SPARQL-compatible, and clinically grounded knowledge graphs without relying on gold-standard annotations. Experimental results demonstrate consistent gains in precision, relevance, and ontology compliance over baseline methods.

abstract: Global health surveillance is currently facing a challenge of Knowledge Gaps. While general-purpose AI has proliferated, it remains fundamentally unsuited for the high-stakes epidemiological domain due to chronic hallucinations and an inability to navigate specialized data silos. This paper introduces ARIES (Agentic Retrieval Intelligence for Epidemiological Surveillance), a specialized, autonomous multi-agent framework designed to move beyond static, disease-specific dashboards toward a dynamic intelligence ecosystem. Built on a hierarchical command structure, ARIES utilizes GPTs to orchestrate a scalable swarm of sub-agents capable of autonomously querying World Health Organization (WHO), Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and peer-reviewed research papers. By automating the extraction and logical synthesis of surveillance data, ARIES provides a specialized reasoning that identifies emergent threats and signal divergence in near real-time. This modular architecture proves that a task-specific agentic swarm can outperform generic models, offering a robust, extensible for next-generation outbreak response and global health intelligence.

abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often rely on fixed top-k document selection mechanisms that ignore downstream generation quality and impose computational overheads. We propose SRAS (Sparse Reward-Aware Selector), a lightweight document selector trained via reinforcement learning (RL) for edge-native RAG deployment. Unlike prior RL-based retrievers that assume large memory and latency budgets, SRAS learns a compact (~0.76MB) policy using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), guided by a hybrid reward signal combining Relaxed F1 and BERTScore. Our method operates under tight token and compute constraints, maintaining <1s latency on CPU. SRAS outperforms supervised and random selectors on a synthetic QA benchmark, and generalizes to real-world data, achieving BERTScore F1 of 0.8546 on SQuAD v2 without domain-specific tuning. This work is the first to demonstrate that RL-based document selection can be made ultra-lightweight, latency-aware, and effective for on-device RAG pipelines.
title: SRAS: A Lightweight Reinforcement Learning-based Document Selector for Edge-Native RAG Pipelines

abstract: Modern recommender systems trained on domain-specific data often struggle to generalize across multiple domains. Cross-domain sequential recommendation has emerged as a promising research direction to address this challenge; however, existing approaches face fundamental limitations, such as reliance on overlapping users or items across domains, or unrealistic assumptions that ignore privacy constraints. In this work, we propose a new framework, MergeRec, based on model merging under a new and realistic problem setting termed data-isolated cross-domain sequential recommendation, where raw user interaction data cannot be shared across domains. MergeRec consists of three key components: (1) merging initialization, (2) pseudo-user data construction, and (3) collaborative merging optimization. First, we initialize a merged model using training-free merging techniques. Next, we construct pseudo-user data by treating each item as a virtual sequence in each domain, enabling the synthesis of meaningful training samples without relying on real user interactions. Finally, we optimize domain-specific merging weights through a joint objective that combines a recommendation loss, which encourages the merged model to identify relevant items, and a distillation loss, which transfers collaborative filtering signals from the fine-tuned source models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MergeRec not only preserves the strengths of the original models but also significantly enhances generalizability to unseen domains. Compared to conventional model merging methods, MergeRec consistently achieves superior performance, with average improvements of up to 17.21% in Recall@10, highlighting the potential of model merging as a scalable and effective approach for building universal recommender systems. The source code is available at https://github.com/DIALLab-SKKU/MergeRec.
title: MergeRec: Model Merging for Data-Isolated Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been used as relevance assessors for Information Retrieval (IR) evaluation collection creation due to reduced cost and increased scalability as compared to human assessors. While previous research has looked at the reliability of LLMs as compared to human assessors, in this work, we aim to understand if LLMs make systematic mistakes when judging relevance, rather than just understanding how good they are on average. To this aim, we propose a novel representational method for queries and documents that allows us to analyze relevance label distributions and compare LLM and human labels to identify patterns of disagreement and localize systematic areas of disagreement. We introduce a clustering-based framework that embeds query-document (Q-D) pairs into a joint semantic space, treating relevance as a relational property. Experiments on TREC Deep Learning 2019 and 2020 show that systematic disagreement between humans and LLMs is concentrated in specific semantic clusters rather than distributed randomly. Query-level analyses reveal recurring failures, most often in definition-seeking, policy-related, or ambiguous contexts. Queries with large variation in agreement across their clusters emerge as disagreement hotspots, where LLMs tend to under-recall relevant content or over-include irrelevant material. This framework links global diagnostics with localized clustering to uncover hidden weaknesses in LLM judgments, enabling bias-aware and more reliable IR evaluation.
title: Query-Document Dense Vectors for LLM Relevance Judgment Bias Analysis

abstract: Generative search engines are reshaping information access by replacing traditional ranked lists with synthesized answers and references. In parallel, with the growth of Web3 platforms, incentive-driven creator ecosystems have become an essential part of how enterprises build visibility and community by rewarding creators for contributing to shared narratives. However, the extent to which exposure in generative search engine citations is shaped by external attention markets remains uncertain. In this study, we audit the exposure for 44 Web3 enterprises. First, we show that the creator community around each enterprise is persistent over time. Second, enterprise-specific queries reveal that more popular voices systematically receive greater citation exposure than others. Third, we find that larger follower bases and enterprises with more concentrated creator cores are associated with higher-ranked exposure. Together, these results show that generative search engine citations exhibit exposure bias toward already prominent voices, which risks entrenching incumbents and narrowing viewpoint diversity.
title: When Attention Becomes Exposure in Generative Search

abstract: Community search aims to identify a refined set of nodes that are most relevant to a given query, supporting tasks ranging from fraud detection to recommendation. Unlike homophilic graphs, many real-world networks are heterophilic, where edges predominantly connect dissimilar nodes. Therefore, structural signals that once reflected smooth, low-frequency similarity now appear as sharp, high-frequency contrasts. However, both classical algorithms (e.g., k-core, k-truss) and recent ML-based models struggle to achieve effective community search on heterophilic graphs, where edge signs or semantics are generally unknown. Algorithm-based methods often return communities with mixed class labels, while GNNs, built on homophily, smooth away meaningful signals and blur community boundaries. Therefore, we propose Adaptive Community Search (AdaptCS), a unified framework featuring three key designs: (i) an AdaptCS Encoder that disentangles multi-hop and multi-frequency signals, enabling the model to capture both smooth (homophilic) and contrastive (heterophilic) relations; (ii) a memory-efficient low-rank optimization that removes the main computational bottleneck and ensures model scalability; and (iii) an Adaptive Community Score (ACS) that guides online search by balancing embedding similarity and topological relations. Extensive experiments on both heterophilic and homophilic benchmarks demonstrate that AdaptCS outperforms the best-performing baseline by an average of 11% in F1-score, retains robustness across heterophily levels, and achieves up to 2 orders of magnitude speedup.
title: Beyond Homophily: Community Search on Heterophilic Graphs

abstract: While dense retrieval models have become the standard for state-of-the-art information retrieval, their deployment is often constrained by high memory requirements and reliance on GPU accelerators for vector similarity search. Learned sparse retrieval offers a compelling alternative by enabling efficient search via inverted indices, yet it has historically received less attention than dense approaches. In this report, we introduce LACONIC, a family of learned sparse retrievers based on the Llama-3 architecture (1B, 3B, and 8B). We propose a streamlined two-phase training curriculum consisting of (1) weakly supervised pre-finetuning to adapt causal LLMs for bidirectional contextualization and (2) high-signal finetuning using curated hard negatives. Our results demonstrate that LACONIC effectively bridges the performance gap with dense models: the 8B variant achieves a state-of-the-art 60.2 nDCG on the MTEB Retrieval benchmark, ranking 15th on the leaderboard as of January 1, 2026, while utilizing 71\% less index memory than an equivalent dense model. By delivering high retrieval effectiveness on commodity CPU hardware with a fraction of the compute budget required by competing models, LACONIC provides a scalable and efficient solution for real-world search applications.
title: LACONIC: Dense-Level Effectiveness for Scalable Sparse Retrieval via a Two-Phase Training Curriculum

abstract: Evaluating novelty is critical yet challenging in peer review, as reviewers must assess submissions against a vast, rapidly evolving literature. This report presents OpenNovelty, an LLM-powered agentic system for transparent, evidence-based novelty analysis. The system operates through four phases: (1) extracting the core task and contribution claims to generate retrieval queries; (2) retrieving relevant prior work based on extracted queries via semantic search engine; (3) constructing a hierarchical taxonomy of core-task-related work and performing contribution-level full-text comparisons against each contribution; and (4) synthesizing all analyses into a structured novelty report with explicit citations and evidence snippets. Unlike naive LLM-based approaches, \textsc{OpenNovelty} grounds all assessments in retrieved real papers, ensuring verifiable judgments. We deploy our system on 500+ ICLR 2026 submissions with all reports publicly available on our website, and preliminary analysis suggests it can identify relevant prior work, including closely related papers that authors may overlook. OpenNovelty aims to empower the research community with a scalable tool that promotes fair, consistent, and evidence-backed peer review.
title: OpenNovelty: An LLM-powered Agentic System for Verifiable Scholarly Novelty Assessment

abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at visual reasoning but still struggle with integrating external knowledge. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a promising solution, but current methods remain inefficient and often fail to maintain high answer quality. To address these challenges, we propose VideoSpeculateRAG, an efficient VLM-based RAG framework built on two key ideas. First, we introduce a speculative decoding pipeline: a lightweight draft model quickly generates multiple answer candidates, which are then verified and refined by a more accurate heavyweight model, substantially reducing inference latency without sacrificing correctness. Second, we identify a major source of error - incorrect entity recognition in retrieved knowledge - and mitigate it with a simple yet effective similarity-based filtering strategy that improves entity alignment and boosts overall answer accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that VideoSpeculateRAG achieves comparable or higher accuracy than standard RAG approaches while accelerating inference by approximately 2x. Our framework highlights the potential of combining speculative decoding with retrieval-augmented reasoning to enhance efficiency and reliability in complex, knowledge-intensive multimodal tasks.

abstract:
This work investigates the potential of torrent metadata as a source for open-source intelligence (OSINT), with a focus on user profiling and behavioral analysis. While peer-to-peer (P2P) networks such as BitTorrent are well studied with respect to privacy and performance, their metadata is rarely used for investigative purposes. This work presents a proof of concept demonstrating how tracker responses, torrent index data, and enriched IP metadata can reveal patterns associated with high-risk behavior.
  The research follows a five-step OSINT process: source identification, data collection, enrichment, behavioral analysis, and presentation of the results. Data were collected from The Pirate Bay and UDP trackers, yielding a dataset of more than 60,000 unique IP addresses across 206 popular torrents. The data were enriched with geolocation, anonymization status, and flags of involvement in child exploitation material (CEM). A case study on sensitive e-books shows how such data can help detect possible interest in illicit content.
  Network analysis highlights peer clustering, co-download patterns, and the use of privacy tools by suspicious users. The study shows that publicly available torrent metadata can support scalable and automated OSINT profiling.
  This work adds to digital forensics by proposing a new method to extract useful signals from noisy data, with applications in law enforcement, cybersecurity, and threat analysis.
title: Breadcrumbs in the Digital Forest: Tracing Criminals through Torrent Metadata with OSINT

abstract: The availability of structured legal data is important for advancing Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques for the German legal system. One of the most widely used datasets, Open Legal Data, provides a large-scale collection of German court decisions. While the metadata in this raw dataset is consistently structured, the decision texts themselves are inconsistently formatted and often lack clearly marked sections. Reliable separation of these sections is important not only for rhetorical role classification but also for downstream tasks such as retrieval and citation analysis. In this work, we introduce a cleaned and sectioned dataset of 251,038 German court decisions derived from the official Open Legal Data dataset. We systematically separated three important sections in German court decisions, namely Tenor (operative part of the decision), Tatbestand (facts of the case), and Entscheidungsgründe (judicial reasoning), which are often inconsistently represented in the original dataset. To ensure the reliability of our extraction process, we used Cochran's formula with a 95% confidence level and a 5% margin of error to draw a statistically representative random sample of 384 cases, and manually verified that all three sections were correctly identified. We also extracted the Rechtsmittelbelehrung (appeal notice) as a separate field, since it is a procedural instruction and not part of the decision itself. The resulting corpus is publicly available in the JSONL format, making it an accessible resource for further research on the German legal system.

abstract: Recommendation systems often rely on implicit feedback, where only positive user-item interactions can be observed. Negative sampling is therefore crucial to provide proper negative training signals. However, existing methods tend to mislabel potentially positive but unobserved items as negatives and lack precise control over negative sample selection. We aim to address these by generating controllable negative samples, rather than sampling from the existing item pool. In this context, we propose Adaptive Diffusion-based Augmentation for Recommendation (ADAR), a novel and model-agnostic module that leverages diffusion to synthesize informative negatives. Inspired by the progressive corruption process in diffusion, ADAR simulates a continuous transition from positive to negative, allowing for fine-grained control over sample hardness. abstract: Despite notable advancements in remote sensing vision-language models (VLMs), existing models often struggle with spatial understanding, limiting their effectiveness in real-world applications. To push the boundaries of VLMs in remote sensing, we specifically address vehicle imagery captured by drones and introduce a spatially-aware dataset AirSpatial, which comprises over 206K instructions and introduces two novel tasks: Spatial Grounding and Spatial Question Answering. It is also the first remote sensing grounding dataset to provide 3DBB. To effectively leverage existing image understanding of VLMs to spatial domains, we adopt a two-stage training strategy comprising Image Understanding Pre-training and Spatial Understanding Fine-tuning. Utilizing this trained spatially-aware VLM, we develop an aerial agent, AirSpatialBot, which is capable of fine-grained vehicle attribute recognition and retrieval. By dynamically integrating task planning, image understanding, spatial understanding, and task execution capabilities, AirSpatialBot adapts to diverse query requirements. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our approach, revealing the spatial limitations of existing VLMs while providing valuable insights. The model, code, and datasets will be released at https://github.com/VisionXLab/AirSpatialBot

abstract: Hate speech (HS) is a critical issue in online discourse, and one promising strategy to counter it is through the use of counter-narratives (CNs). Datasets linking HS with CNs are essential for advancing counterspeech research. However, even flagship resources like CONAN (Chung et al., 2019) annotate only a sparse subset of all possible HS-CN pairs, limiting evaluation. We introduce FC-CONAN (Fully Connected CONAN), the first dataset created by exhaustively considering all combinations of 45 English HS messages and 129 CNs. A two-stage annotation process involving nine annotators and four validators produces four partitions-Diamond, Gold, Silver, and Bronze-that balance reliability and scale. None of the labeled pairs overlap with CONAN, uncovering hundreds of previously unlabelled positives. FC-CONAN enables more faithful evaluation of counterspeech retrieval systems and facilitates detailed error analysis. The dataset is publicly available.

abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) in mental health counseling faces the dual challenges of hallucinations and lack of empathy. While the former may be mitigated by RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) by anchoring answers in trusted clinical sources, there remains an open question as to whether the most effective model under this paradigm would be one that is fine-tuned on mental health data, or a more general and powerful model that succeeds purely on the basis of reasoning. In this paper, we perform a direct comparison by running four open-source models through the same RAG pipeline using ChromaDB: two generalist reasoners (Qwen2.5-3B and Phi-3-Mini) and two domain-specific fine-tunes (MentalHealthBot-7B and TherapyBot-7B). We use an LLM-as-a-Judge framework to automate evaluation over 50 turns. We find a clear trend: the generalist models outperform the domain-specific ones in empathy (3.72 vs. 3.26, $p < 0.001$) in spite of being much smaller (3B vs. 7B), and all models perform well in terms of safety, but the generalist models show better contextual understanding and are less prone to overfitting as we observe in the domain-specific models. Overall, our results indicate that for RAG-based therapy systems, strong reasoning is more important than training on mental health-specific vocabulary; i.e. a well-reasoned general model would provide more empathetic and balanced support than a larger narrowly fine-tuned model, so long as the answer is already grounded in clinical evidence.

abstract: Embedding-based dense retrieval has become the cornerstone of many critical applications, where approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) queries are often combined with filters on labels such as dates and price ranges. Graph-based indexes achieve state-of-the-art performance on unfiltered ANNS but encounter connectivity breakdown on low-selectivity filtered queries, where qualifying vectors become sparse and the graph structure among them fragments. Recent research proposes specialized graph indexes that address this issue by expanding graph degree, which incurs prohibitively high construction costs. Given these inherent limitations of graph-based methods, we argue for a dual-index architecture and present Curator, a partition-based index that complements existing graph-based approaches for low-selectivity filtered ANNS. Curator builds specialized indexes for different labels within a shared clustering tree, where each index adapts to the distribution of its qualifying vectors to ensure efficient search while sharing structure to minimize memory overhead. The system also supports incremental updates and handles arbitrary complex predicates beyond single-label filters by efficiently constructing temporary indexes on the fly. Our evaluation demonstrates that integrating Curator with state-of-the-art graph indexes reduces low-selectivity query latency by up to 20.9x compared to pre-filtering fallback, while increasing construction time and memory footprint by only 5.5% and 4.3%, respectively.
title: Curator: Efficient Vector Search with Low-Selectivity Filters

abstract: In enterprise search, building high-quality datasets at scale remains a central challenge due to the difficulty of acquiring labeled data. To resolve this challenge, we propose an efficient approach to fine-tune small language models (SLMs) for accurate relevance labeling, enabling high-throughput, domain-specific labeling comparable or even better in quality to that of state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs). To overcome the lack of high-quality and accessible datasets in the enterprise domain, our method leverages on synthetic data generation. Specifically, we employ an LLM to synthesize realistic enterprise queries from a seed document, apply BM25 to retrieve hard negatives, and use a teacher LLM to assign relevance scores. The resulting dataset is then distilled into an SLM, producing a compact relevance labeler. We evaluate our approach on a high-quality benchmark consisting of 923 enterprise query-document pairs annotated by trained human annotators, and show that the distilled SLM achieves agreement with human judgments on par with or better than the teacher LLM. Furthermore, our fine-tuned labeler substantially improves throughput, achieving 17 times increase while also being 19 times more cost-effective. This approach enables scalable and cost-effective relevance labeling for enterprise-scale retrieval applications, supporting rapid offline evaluation and iteration in real-world settings.
title: Fine-tuning Small Language Models as Efficient Enterprise Search Relevance Labelers

To overcome the lack of high-quality and accessible datasets in the enterprise domain, our method leverages on synthetic data generation. Specifically, we employ an LLM to synthesize realistic enterprise queries from a seed document, apply BM25 to retrieve hard negatives, and use a teacher LLM to assign relevance scores. The resulting dataset is then distilled into an SLM, producing a compact relevance labeler. We evaluate our approach on a high-quality benchmark consisting of 923 enterprise query-document pairs annotated by trained human annotators, and show that the distilled SLM achieves agreement with human judgments on par with or better than the teacher LLM. Furthermore, our fine-tuned labeler substantially improves throughput, achieving 17 times increase while also being 19 times more cost-effective. This approach enables scalable and cost-effective relevance labeling for enterprise-scale retrieval applications, supporting rapid offline evaluation and iteration in real-world settings.

abstract: Capturing complex user preferences from sparse behavioral sequences remains a fundamental challenge in sequential recommendation. Recent latent reasoning methods have shown promise by extending test-time computation through multi-step reasoning, yet they exclusively rely on depth-level scaling along a single trajectory, suffering from diminishing returns as reasoning depth increases. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{Parallel Latent Reasoning (PLR)}, a novel framework that pioneers width-level computational scaling by exploring multiple diverse reasoning trajectories simultaneously. PLR constructs parallel reasoning streams through learnable trigger tokens in continuous latent space, preserves diversity across streams via global reasoning regularization, and adaptively synthesizes multi-stream outputs through mixture-of-reasoning-streams aggregation. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that PLR substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining real-time inference efficiency. Theoretical analysis further validates the effectiveness of parallel reasoning in improving generalization capability. Our work opens new avenues for enhancing reasoning capacity in sequential recommendation beyond existing depth scaling.

abstract: The Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system based on Large language model (LLM) has made significant progress. It can effectively reduce factuality hallucinations, but faithfulness hallucinations still exist. Previous methods for detecting faithfulness hallucinations either neglect to capture the models' internal reasoning processes or handle those features coarsely, making it difficult for discriminators to learn. This paper proposes a semantic-level internal reasoning graph-based method for detecting faithfulness hallucination. Specifically, we first extend the layer-wise relevance propagation algorithm from the token level to the semantic level, constructing an internal reasoning graph based on attribution vectors. This provides a more faithful semantic-level representation of dependency. Furthermore, we design a general framework based on a small pre-trained language model to utilize the dependencies in LLM's reasoning for training and hallucination detection, which can dynamically adjust the pass rate of correct samples through a threshold. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves better overall performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines on RAGTruth and Dolly-15k.

abstract: Traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) effectively supports single-hop question answering with large language models but faces significant limitations in multi-hop question answering tasks, which require combining evidence from multiple documents. Existing chunk-based retrieval often provides irrelevant and logically incoherent context, leading to incomplete evidence chains and incorrect reasoning during answer generation. To address these challenges, we propose SentGraph, a sentence-level graph-based RAG framework that explicitly models fine-grained logical relationships between sentences for multi-hop question answering. Specifically, we construct a hierarchical sentence graph offline by first adapting Rhetorical Structure Theory to distinguish nucleus and satellite sentences, and then organizing them into topic-level subgraphs with cross-document entity bridges. During online retrieval, SentGraph performs graph-guided evidence selection and path expansion to retrieve fine-grained sentence-level evidence. Extensive experiments on four multi-hop question answering benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of SentGraph, validating the importance of explicitly modeling sentence-level logical dependencies for multi-hop reasoning.
